features.summary: The Web home page (/) and the two entry pages /agi-work and /agi-code. A signed-out visitor sees a marketing page with Try chat, Sign in and a desktop link. A visitor with a browser session cookie is rewritten to the product (/chat or /code) at the same address.

purpose.what_it_does: Shows the public home page and the Work and Code entry pages to signed-out visitors. For a visitor whose browser holds a session cookie, the web proxy swaps the marketing page for the product page without changing the address bar: / and /agi-work show the chat root, /agi-code shows the cloud code page (apps/web/proxy.ts:124-134, 208-210). It also decides which routes load the browser identity provider, so public pages stay light (apps/web/app/BrowserIdentityBoundary.tsx:8-19).
purpose.why_it_exists: The product must work like the leaders: a returning user lands in the product, a new visitor gets a pitch and a way in. The proxy comment says a signed-in visitor gets the surface instead of the pitch for it (apps/web/proxy.ts:96-104).
purpose.who_uses_it: New visitors on Web, returning signed-in users who type the site address, and search or campaign traffic that lands on /agi-work or /agi-code.
problems_solved: A signed-in user is not shown a sales page when opening the site
A signed-out visitor has a clear route to sign in, try chat or check desktop availability
Public pages do not download the identity script unless the route needs it (apps/web/lib/identity/browser-provider-routes.ts:30-34)
use_cases: A returning user opens the site root and lands in chat
A visitor clicks Try chat on the home page and is sent to /login with a return to /
A visitor on /agi-work clicks Open Work and signs in, then returns to Work mode
A signed-in developer opens /agi-code and sees the cloud code page

working: Rewrite of / and /agi-work to /chat and /agi-code to /code only when the session cookie is present; otherwise the page passes through with a CSP header (apps/web/proxy.ts:105-134)
Cookie test follows Clerk's convention: __client_uat empty or 0 means signed out; if the cookie is absent, a __session cookie counts (packages/platform/identity/src/session-cookie.ts:5-20)
The Work path sets initial Work mode through the x-agi-pathname request header (apps/web/proxy.ts:108-112; apps/web/app/chat/page.tsx:8-20)

The browser identity provider mounts lazily and only for product, auth and listed public prefixes, also when a route is a rewrite target (apps/web/app/BrowserIdentityBoundary.tsx:8-19; apps/web/lib/identity/browser-provider-routes.ts:6-45)
Header reads the cookie after mount and swaps Sign in / Try chat for Open chat (apps/web/shared/components/layout/Header.tsx:11-19)
incomplete: The rewrite decides on cookie presence only; what a visitor sees when the cookie is present but the session is expired or invalid is not established in this review
disconnected_or_disabled: Landing text for Desktop, CLI, Mobile, VS Code and Chrome shows 'Coming soon' because every surface except Web is set to Coming soon in the status registry (apps/web/lib/surface-status.ts:6-13)
not_available: Desktop, Mobile, CLI, VS Code and Chrome apps have no equivalent entry page of their own; they are not part of this feature

steps.what_happens: Browser requests /, /agi-work or /agi-code; the proxy matcher covers these paths
Identity session middleware runs, then the handler checks the cookie
With a cookie the request is rewritten to /chat or /code, with the original path in the x-agi-pathname header; without it the page passes through with a CSP nonce
The page renders; the chat page reads the header to choose Work mode
In the browser the header reads document.cookie and shows the right buttons; the identity provider loads only if the route needs it

features.summary: Public Web pages that explain one capability each: chat (/web and /features/ai-chat), deep research, image generation, video generation and voice. Each ends with a way to start (Open chat) and a link to the plan comparison. Image, video and voice pages exist in code, so the brief's 'missing' is stale.

purpose.why_it_exists: Visitors compare against ChatGPT and Claude page by page; each capability needs a truthful explanation and an entry point (doc: docs/product/competitive-guidance.md section 5.1).
purpose.who_uses_it: Prospective users on Web, search engines, and sales staff who share a link.

purpose.who_uses_it: Prospective users, developers choosing between CLI and editor, and people waiting for the mobile app.

features.summary: The /download page. It reads the release API and offers Mac installers only for architectures that are actually published, detects the visitor's Mac type, shows SHA-256 checksums, and lists CLI archives. Windows and Linux Desktop installers are shown as not published.

purpose.what_it_does: Shows every app's status and, when the release API reports a signed macOS build, a 'Download for Mac' button for the detected architecture plus the other one, the published checksums and verification commands (apps/web/app/download/DownloadSurfaces.tsx:122-186,426-453). The download link goes through our server, which relays the file from the release host (apps/web/app/api/download/route.ts:96-187).
purpose.why_it_exists: A download page must give the right file and never a dead link or an unverified build (doc: docs/product/competitive-guidance.md section 5.1 item 6).
purpose.who_uses_it: Mac users installing Desktop, developers fetching CLI archives, and visitors who want to know which apps exist.
problems_solved: Wrong-architecture installs: the page detects Apple silicon or Intel and offers both
False availability: buttons appear only after the API confirms the architecture (apps/web/app/download/DesktopDownloadAvailability.tsx:74-75)
Tampering doubts: SHA-256 values are published and shown only for the same version
use_cases: A Mac user clicks Download for Mac and gets the right .dmg
A user on an Intel Mac clicks the other-architecture link
A cautious user checks the checksum with shasum
A visitor sees Windows and Linux as not published

where_to_find_it: Web: /download (nav item 'Downloads', apps/web/features/marketing/components/system/nav.ts); Desktop page embeds the same availability block at /desktop#desktop-downloads
Other apps: not applicable; Desktop's own update path is a separate route (apps/web/app/api/releases/desktop-cloud/update)
prerequisites: None; no account needed
screens_and_controls: Hero when a Mac build exists: 'Desktop for Mac', button 'Download for Mac', secondary 'Open <chat name>', and a link 'Download the <architecture> version' for the other Mac (apps/web/app/download/DownloadSurfaces.tsx:122-186)
Hero when none exists: 'Use AGI today, in your browser' with 'Get notified about the apps'

On /desktop: buttons 'Download for Apple silicon' / 'Download for Intel Mac' with '(this Mac)' on the detected one; rows for macOS, Windows, Linux; 'Retry release check' on error (apps/web/app/download/DesktopDownloadAvailability.tsx:41-150)

steps.what_happens: A scheduled job ingests registry sources into a snapshot stored in the server database
The page loads the snapshot, filters by connectable state, listing rules, search text and category, and renders up to 60
For plugins the page reads registry entries through the render cache from the server database
A detail page reads the entry, falls back to the directory snapshot, and reads release history from the versions table
Install or connect clicks go to sign-up or settings; nothing connects from a public page

aliases: Paid upgrade waitlist (the gate in front of checkout)
features.summary: The public /pricing page on the web app lists Free, Basic, Premium, Max and Ultra for individuals and Team (per seat) plus Enterprise for businesses, with a comparison table and usage notes. A signed-in visitor can start Stripe checkout, but new paid purchases are gated behind an upgrade waitlist or access code until the operator opens upgrades.

purpose.what_it_does: Shows what each plan costs and includes, explains how managed (Cloud) usage works in weekly and monthly allowances, links to the credits help article, and lets a visitor start a paid purchase, choose Team seat counts, join the upgrade waitlist, or enter an access code (apps/web/app/pricing/page.tsx:269-1328).
purpose.why_it_exists: Acquisition and honesty: visitors must see real prices and limits before paying, and the page must say that Local and own-key use are free and do not draw on Cloud usage (packages/ui/i18n/locales/en/pricing.json:237). The sales gate is a founder decision (doc: docs/product/commercial.md, Paid Acquisition Gate).
purpose.who_uses_it: Prospective individual buyers, team buyers choosing seats, existing subscribers changing plan, and support or sales staff pointing to plan facts.
problems_solved: Visitor cannot tell which plan fits or what usage limits mean
Team buyer needs per-seat pricing and a seat picker
Operator needs to open or close paid purchasing without a deployment (apps/web/lib/server/billing-waitlist-access.ts:28-45)
Price must show in the visitor's currency where one is sold (apps/web/app/api/pricing/localized/route.ts:9)
use_cases: A signed-out visitor compares Premium and Max in the table, clicks the plan button and is sent to sign-up with a return to /pricing (apps/web/app/pricing/page.tsx:601-608).
A team lead opens the Team and Enterprise view, sets 5 seats and 1 Premium seat and sees the total before starting checkout (page.tsx:1048-1203).
A signed-in Free user whose account is not yet admitted sees plan buttons that join the waitlist, or enter an access code (page.tsx:566-597).
A subscriber on an individual plan clicks a higher plan and is sent to /upgrade/<plan> (page.tsx:650-653).

where_to_find_it: Web: /pricing, linked as Pricing in the footer Product column (apps/web/features/marketing/components/system/nav.ts:165-173). Header nav group wiring for Pricing was not opened: unknown.
Desktop: the public Desktop shows the hosted web app (doc: AGENTS.md section 5), so /pricing is reachable there through the web app [inferred]; not opened.
Mobile: no pricing or purchase screen; Mobile v1 sells nothing in the app (doc: docs/product/commercial.md, Paid Acquisition Gate).
CLI, VS Code, Chrome: none found in the code for this feature.
prerequisites: None to read the page. Starting checkout needs a signed-in account (page.tsx:601-608).
Paid purchase also needs upgrade access: upgrades open, or the account has redeemed an access code (apps/web/lib/server/billing-waitlist-access.ts:42-54).
screens_and_controls: Title and a two-button group: the individual audience button and the business audience button (Team and Enterprise) (page.tsx:1006-1031).

Individual cards: Free, Basic, Premium, Max, Ultra, each with price per month, body text, one action button and a feature list; Ultra carries an asterisk footnote about the missing five-hour cap (page.tsx:880-960).
Free card button is a link to sign-in or home (page.tsx:926-929).

Team band: Monthly / Annual toggle (shown only when yearly checkout is ready), Standard and Premium seat rows, seat count number input, Premium seat count input, running total, Team button, 'Contact sales' link (page.tsx:1048-1206).
Enterprise card: Custom price and Contact sales link to /contact-sales (page.tsx:1213-1226).
Plan button states: Checking account, Update payment, Current plan, Manage billing, a switch-to-plan button, Join <plan> waitlist, Enter access code (page.tsx:494-600).
Comparison table with groups Usage, Models, Research, Projects, Tools, Admin; footnote on Local and BYOK; link to the FAQ (page.tsx:1251-1296).
Dialogs: UpgradeConfirmDialog (Team change), UpgradeWaitlistDialog, DowngradeReviewDialog (page.tsx:1300-1325).
journey: Open /pricing; the individual plans show first.
Optionally switch to the Team and Enterprise view; a #pricing-team-title hash with ?seats=N opens it with N seats (page.tsx:304-326).
For Team, set seats and Premium seats and, if offered, switch Monthly/Annual.
Press the plan button. Signed out: go to sign-up and return to /pricing (page.tsx:601-608).
Signed in and not admitted: the waitlist dialog opens (page.tsx:624-630).

Signed in and admitted: a toast says redirecting to checkout and the browser is handed to the Stripe checkout page (page.tsx:673-700; apps/web/features/billing/services/stripe-payments.ts:208-232). The redirect step itself was not opened [inferred].
After payment Stripe returns to /billing?success=true (apps/web/app/api/checkout/route.ts:501); cancel returns to /pricing (route.ts:502).

An existing Stripe subscriber upgrading a plan goes to /upgrade/<plan>, or confirms a Team change in a dialog, then the page polls up to 6 times, 1 second apart, for the plan to change (page.tsx:167-168, 650-662).
feedback_and_outputs: Notice 'Checkout is temporarily unavailable...' when the web flag is off (apps/web/features/billing/lib/localized-pricing.ts:32-33).
Notices for loading or failed checkout availability, and a region notice per plan (localized-pricing.ts:34-40; page.tsx:960-995).
Alert for a failed payment with a link to Billing (page.tsx:978-987).
Toasts: 'Checkout is temporarily unavailable. Please try again later.', region unavailable, 'Your plan has been upgraded.' (page.tsx:632-640, 1303).
Server message 'Paid-plan checkout is not available yet. Local and BYOK are free.' (apps/web/app/api/checkout/route.ts:178-181).
A 403 with 'Paid upgrades are opening in stages. Join the waitlist or enter an access code to continue.' (billing-waitlist-access.ts:20-21, 56-66).
settings: Settings > Billing handles payment method, portal and plan changes after purchase (page.tsx:980-985, route links). Not opened in detail.
Operator switches: NEXT_PUBLIC_CHECKOUT_ENABLED, STRIPE_CHECKOUT_ENABLED, STRIPE_SECRET_KEY, flag billing.upgrades_open, AGI_BILLING_WAITLIST_OPEN (names only).

working: All plan prices, labels, seat limits and surface visibility come from the shared billing catalog: Free $0, Basic $7, Premium $20, Max $100, Ultra $200 per month, Team $25 per seat monthly or $240 yearly, Team Premium seat $125 or $1200, Enterprise contract-priced (packages/contracts/types/src/billing-catalog.ts:166-231; MIN_PURCHASABLE_SEATS=2 at :157).

Individual plans are sold monthly only; only Team has a yearly option, and the toggle appears only when yearly checkout is ready (page.tsx:1051; apps/web/features/billing/lib/localized-pricing.ts:119). Checkout rejects a yearly interval for a plan that does not sell it (apps/web/lib/validations/checkout.ts:30-36).
Localized prices come from GET /api/pricing/localized using the trusted country header, cached 300 seconds (apps/web/app/api/pricing/localized/route.ts:9-20).

Comparison table cells are computed from catalog functions (canUseBillingPlanCapability, getBillingPlanProductLimits, canAccessModelForSubscriptionTier) and show 'coming soon' for unreleased capabilities (page.tsx:140-215, 745-868).

Usage note: weekly and monthly allowances, Ultra has no five-hour cap, no fixed message count, and a flagship-model share (apps/web/features/billing/lib/plan-card-copy.ts:366-374; page.tsx:1242). Credits, running out, keep-going switch, concurrency and the free lane are explained in the public help article (apps/web/content/support/usage-and-credits.md:9-53).

POST /api/checkout is what the buttons call (apps/web/features/billing/services/stripe-payments.ts:222). It checks CSRF (route.ts:173), the checkout flag and secret key (route.ts:178), a rate limit (route.ts:184), plan-change rules (route.ts:189), trusted-country price (route.ts:231), upgrade access (route.ts:298-309), billing-owner policy (route.ts:312), live-subscription conflicts, trial rules, then creates a Stripe Checkout session requiring terms acceptance and allowing promotion codes (route.ts:517-522) and records a checkout_started audit event.

The route supports Team seats and Premium seats as two line items (route.ts:244-266) and the page offers a real per-seat checkout (test: apps/web/app/pricing/page.test.tsx 'offers Team as a real per-seat checkout instead of a sales hand-off').
incomplete: Whether each table cell matches what the server enforces is not established: cells derive from catalog functions, but the enforcement call sites were not opened. The brief says this was not checked.
The Premium-seat input is hidden for accounts that already hold a paid plan; it points them to settings (page.tsx:1160-1175).
Existing-subscriber Team changes use a dialog while individual changes go to /upgrade/<plan> (page.tsx:650-662).
disconnected_or_disabled: Paid purchase is closed by default for accounts without access: the gate returns 403 until the operator opens upgrades (flag billing.upgrades_open, forced open by AGI_BILLING_WAITLIST_OPEN=1) or the user redeemed a code (beta_redemptions) (apps/web/lib/server/billing-waitlist-access.ts:28-54; doc: docs/product/commercial.md).
Both checkout flags default to on and turn off on 0, false or off (page: localized-pricing.ts:26-30; route.ts:58-62). They must be kept equal by hand (localized-pricing.ts:22-25).
not_available: Desktop, mobile, CLI, VS Code and Chrome have no pricing page of their own (brief: n/a). Mobile has no purchase flow (doc: docs/product/commercial.md).
Local Mode and Local Mode + BYOK are not columns or cards; they are named in a footnote as always free (en/pricing.json:237).

established.statement: A public pricing page lists individual plans with prices and lets a visitor buy one; its plan copy matches enforcement.
A public page shows Team per-seat pricing and lets a buyer choose seats and purchase.
A plan-comparison table lists plans against features and each cell matches enforcement.
Public pages explain how managed usage, allowances and credits work.
Paid checkout code does not open paid purchasing; an access-code or waitlist decision comes before checkout, and clients do not fork the rule.

Public plan names and prices are owned by billing-catalog.ts; changing the audience view does not change account, channel or entitlement; the top tier has no five-hour cap and the card footnote says that is not unlimited use.

steps.what_happens: Browser loads /pricing and renders prices from the catalog; localized prices are fetched.
Page reads the signed-in account, billing and upgrade-access status to choose each button.
Press a paid plan: unauthenticated goes to sign-up; unadmitted opens the waitlist dialog; admitted calls POST /api/checkout.
Server verifies CSRF, flag, key, rate limit, plan-change rules, price, upgrade access, billing owner and existing Stripe state.
Server creates or reuses a Stripe customer, expires older open checkout sessions and creates a new Stripe Checkout session.
Server records a checkout_started audit event and returns the Stripe URL.
Payment happens on Stripe; the subscription webhook later writes the plan. The page polls for the change.

features.summary: Web pages that let a company reach the team: /enterprise describes the Enterprise offer and sends visitors to /contact-sales (an email page); /contact drafts an email; /support lists channels; a dialog stores an Enterprise follow-up email; /partners emails partner applications. Mobile About has support links. The CLI has no contact entry found.

purpose.what_it_does: Presents the Enterprise offering and gives several ways to start a conversation: an email address, a mail-draft composer, a stored email request with consent, and a partner application form that emails the team (apps/web/app/enterprise/page.tsx:64-299; apps/web/app/contact-sales/page.tsx; apps/web/app/partners/PartnerApplicationForm.tsx).
purpose.why_it_exists: Enterprise is contract-priced and not self-serve (packages/contracts/types/src/billing-catalog.ts:219-224), and the company states there is no partner program yet but wants to hear from integrators (apps/web/app/partners/page.tsx:68).
purpose.who_uses_it: Company buyers, security reviewers, integration builders, consultancies, and any visitor needing support.
problems_solved: Buyer needs a sales route for SSO, retention and governance
Partner or plugin builder needs a way to apply
Visitor needs honest support channels and response commitments per plan (apps/web/features/marketing/components/pages/company/support-content.ts:13-36)
Consent for storing an email must be recorded (apps/web/app/api/waitlist/public/route.ts:166)
use_cases: A security lead reads /enterprise, clicks Contact sales and emails the sales inbox with team size and review needs (apps/web/app/contact-sales/page.tsx:43-60).
A visitor on /desktop clicks 'Discuss Enterprise access', enters an email, ticks consent and presses 'Request a follow-up' (apps/web/app/desktop/page.tsx:53-56; WaitlistDialog.tsx:116, 172).
A plugin builder fills the partner form and gets a reference like PA-XXXXXXXXXX (apps/web/app/api/partners/apply/route.ts:21-24).
A logged-in user raises a ticket from Settings > Help rather than email (apps/web/app/support/page.tsx:111).

Desktop, VS Code, Chrome: nothing found.

established.statement: A public page presents the Enterprise offering with a sales path.
A contact or support page lets a visitor reach the company.
A form lets a prospect request an Enterprise conversation and the request is stored.
Partners and developers can submit a listing or partnership application through a form.
Enterprise dialog says a person will contact the visitor about contract-scoped access; consent is required before submit; submit goes through the waitlist client with surface web-waitlist-modal.
Enterprise capabilities are contract scoped and reached through sales; there is no dedicated capacity.

acceptance_criteria: Every Contact sales button on /enterprise and /pricing opens /contact-sales with a working mailto link.
The dialog refuses an invalid email and refuses submit without the required consent, and sends nothing in either case.
A valid dialog submit creates one cloud_managed_waitlist row (idempotent per email and source) and a consent record.
Partner form with fewer than 20 message characters is refused before any request.
A valid partner application returns a PA- reference and an email arrives at the team inbox with reply-to set.
/contact never stores the visitor's text.
Mobile Contact Support is hidden when signed out or in Local mode.
inferred: The stored Enterprise request should be reachable from the Enterprise page to meet 'the request is stored' for S2.36 [inferred].
proposed: [proposed] Open the Enterprise dialog from /enterprise and /pricing, or state that email is the only route.
[proposed] Store partner applications with a status so none is lost if mail fails.

features.summary: The web app publishes a dated list of releases at /changelog and /release-notes (the same page), one page per release at /release-notes/<date-slug>, plus an Atom feed of releases and policy changes. The CLI separately reads a GitHub-based release feed to tell users an update exists and print the install command.

purpose.what_it_does: Lists dated releases with the surfaces reached and a maturity label (generally available, beta or alpha), a forthcoming list, policy changes, and an Atom feed; each release has its own page (apps/web/app/release-notes/ReleaseNotesPage.tsx:89; apps/web/app/release-notes/[slug]/page.tsx:24-93). The CLI compares its version with the newest published CLI release and prints notes and the install command (apps/cli/src/update_check.rs:185-214).
purpose.why_it_exists: Honest, dated product history that states what is released and what is not (ReleaseNotesPage.tsx lede), and a way for CLI users to find updates.
purpose.who_uses_it: Customers, reviewers, people subscribed by feed reader, and CLI users.

features.summary: Four public web pages: /docs indexes guides and reference; /help offers keyword search and browse-by-collection of help articles, each at /help/<slug>; /status shows health checks reused for up to 60 seconds with their age; /trust lists dated security and compliance claims and says which certifications are not held.

purpose.why_it_exists: Self-service answers lower support load, and the status and trust pages must say plainly what is tested and what is not (status metadata: 'A passing check does not verify a model response'; trust lede: no SOC 2 report, ISO 27001 certificate or third-party penetration test).

Search articles without an AI call
See whether the service is up and which dependency fails
Check the security posture with evidence names

features.summary: A public page at /share/<token> shows a conversation that its owner shared. A logged-out visitor sees the title, model label, messages and expiry in read-only form with links to create an account or open it in AGI. Invalid, expired or revoked tokens show the same not-found page. Only chat sessions were found; artifact sharing was not.

purpose.what_it_does: Serves a read-only copy of a shared chat to anyone holding the link when the share is public, and to signed-in workspace members when it is workspace-only (apps/web/app/share/[token]/page.tsx:28-50, 100-122).
purpose.why_it_exists: Lets people show a conversation to others without an account, and brings viewers into the product.
purpose.who_uses_it: The person who shared and any recipient, signed in or not.
problems_solved: Recipient has no account
Link may expire or be revoked and must then stop working
Workspace-only shares must not leak to link holders
use_cases: A recipient opens a link from a chat and reads it.
A workspace member opens an organisation-only share while signed in.
A recipient presses Open in AGI to continue the chat.
A reader reports a shared page with the report link (page.tsx:120).

working: Token must match 24 URL-safe characters or the page returns not found (apps/web/lib/services/org-shared-session-service.ts:25; page.tsx:100-104).

Public read first: a row with visibility 'public' whose owner may still run unattended work (org-shared-session-service.ts:255-270); then a signed-in cookie user gets the workspace read with RLS and admission checks (page.tsx:28-50; service :279-300).
Expired shares are not shown: isLive compares expiry with now and an expired share gives not found (page.tsx:78-80, 105).

features.summary: Lets a person sign in to their AGI account on Web, Desktop, Mobile, CLI, VS Code and Chrome. Web uses one email-first screen; Desktop, CLI, VS Code and Chrome hand off to the web through a browser; Mobile has its own native screen. A session starts only after the account is allowed and Terms are current.

purpose.what_it_does: Authenticates a person to their AGI account and returns a session to the app they started from. On Web the email-first screen at /login and /signup decides sign-in or sign-up from the email typed (apps/web/features/auth/IdentityAuthAdapter.tsx:471-495). Other apps hand the work to the web or, on Mobile, run a native flow (apps/mobile/src/features/auth/components/MobileSignIn.tsx:253-276).
purpose.why_it_exists: Cloud features, sync, limits and account settings need to know who the person is. Local use on Mobile does not need an account (doc: docs/product/requirements.md:481; apps/mobile/app/(auth)/login.tsx:277), so sign-in is for Cloud and account features only [inferred].
purpose.who_uses_it: Anyone with an AGI account or about to create one, on any of the six apps. Reviewers and testers also use it to reach signed-in states.
problems_solved: One account works on all six apps through one identity service (SYS-authentication-and-identity).
A terminal, editor or browser extension has no password field of its own, so a browser approval hands the session back (apps/cli/src/oauth.rs:71-103).
A suspended, locked or deleted account is told why instead of meeting a product that answers 403 on every call (apps/web/app/login/complete/page.tsx:67-79).
A stale browser session no longer loops between /login and /login/complete (apps/web/app/login/complete/page.tsx:55-65; apps/web/app/login/complete/StaleSessionRecovery.tsx:11-14).
use_cases: A returning user opens agiworkforce.com/login, types an email, enters the password and lands in a new chat.
A developer runs agi login in a terminal, approves the code in the browser, and the CLI stores the session.
A Desktop user presses Continue in browser, finishes sign-in in the system browser and the Desktop window signs in by itself.
A Mobile user taps Log in or sign up, types an email, enters an emailed code and returns to the app.

where_to_find_it: Web: /login and /signup render the same screen headed Log in or sign up (apps/web/app/login/page.tsx:1-11; apps/web/app/signup/page.tsx:1-11; apps/web/features/auth/AuthEmailStep.tsx:94). Old paths /sign-in, /sign-up and /register redirect there (apps/web/next.config.ts:153-155).

Desktop: the signed-out window shows a shell-drawn screen titled with the Desktop product name, line Sign in to <brand>, button Continue in browser (apps/desktop/electron/signInScreen.ts:55-63). The web pages Desktop navigates to for sign-in are replaced by that screen (apps/desktop/electron/windowPolicy.ts:102-103).

Mobile: Cloud sign-in screen headed AGI Cloud, inner heading Log in or sign up, reached from the Cloud entry; a close button returns to Local Mode (apps/mobile/app/(auth)/login.tsx:326; apps/mobile/src/features/auth/components/MobileSignIn.tsx:452-453).
CLI: command agi login (apps/cli/src/lib.rs:988-992, 7269-7272).
VS Code: command palette entry Code: Sign In to AGI Cloud (apps/extension-vscode/package.json:157-158; apps/extension-vscode/src/core/commandSetup.ts:1221).

Chrome: the side panel opens a new tab on the web sign-in page with a return to /auth/chrome-extension (apps/extension/src/features/cloud-bridge/clerkAuth.ts:215-223); that page offers Sign in to Cloud (apps/web/app/auth/chrome-extension/page.tsx:50-55).
prerequisites: Web, Desktop, CLI, VS Code, Chrome: network access to the AGI web service.
Desktop: a default system browser that can be opened (apps/desktop/electron/browserSignIn.ts:46-50).

Chrome: the build must carry the identity publishable key and sync host settings, otherwise the extension throws that sign-in is not configured (apps/extension/src/features/cloud-bridge/clerkAuth.ts:61-70).

Mobile: the auth feature flag is on (apps/mobile/lib/v1FeatureFlags.ts:8; apps/mobile/app/(auth)/login.tsx:161); a live identity key is required in preview and production builds (apps/mobile/src/integrations/clerk.ts:7-14).
An account whose status is not locked, recovery pending, suspended, banned or deleted (apps/web/lib/auth/account-status.ts:72-106).
screens_and_controls: Web email step: provider buttons Continue with Google and Continue with GitHub by default, optional passkey button Sign in with a passkey or security key, field Email address, button Continue, small text Last used on the last method, Try again after a retryable failure (apps/web/features/auth/AuthEmailStep.tsx:98-185; apps/web/features/auth/authProviderConfig.ts:7-17).

Web next steps: Enter your password with Forgot password? and Can't reach this email? (apps/web/features/auth/AuthPasswordStep.tsx:53-111); Check your inbox code step with Resend code (apps/web/features/auth/AuthCodeStep.tsx:32-35, 195-197); second-factor step; notice step for rate-limit and similar states (apps/web/features/auth/AuthFlow.tsx:250-258).
Web completion: Finish signing in page with Terms review and Continue, or Continue if current Terms are already accepted (apps/web/app/login/complete/page.tsx:107-146).

Desktop screen buttons: Continue in browser; while waiting Open browser again and Cancel; after expiry or a failed open Try again (apps/desktop/electron/signInScreen.ts:58-84). The web component used inside Desktop also has Continue in your browser and Cancel sign-in (apps/web/features/desktop-host/components/DesktopBrowserSignIn.tsx:29-33, 100).
Browser page for Desktop: Return to Desktop with an Open <Desktop name> button (apps/web/app/auth/desktop/DesktopSignInHandoff.tsx:19-22).

Mobile: provider buttons (Apple on iOS only when the build includes it), Email field, Continue, Use an email code instead, Use a different email, Create an account instead, More sign-in options or Forgot password or try another way, Appeal this suspension (apps/mobile/src/features/auth/components/MobileSignIn.tsx:67-71, 700-780).
CLI: prints a link and a code, and Waiting for authorization (apps/cli/src/oauth.rs:491-517).
VS Code: a notification Signing in to AGI Cloud with Approve code <code> and a Cancel control (apps/extension-vscode/src/features/account-auth/deviceAuth.ts:218-228).
Browser device page: Connect a device with the code, signed-in account, Approve device (packages/ui/i18n/locales/en/auth.json:61-77).
journey: Web: open /login. Type the email and press Continue. The page tries to sign in with that email (apps/web/features/auth/IdentityAuthAdapter.tsx:466-469).

If the account has a password the Enter your password step appears; if it has only an emailed code a code step appears saying the account does not use a password; if an enterprise connection covers the address the page goes to the organization sign-in (IdentityAuthAdapter.tsx:393-402; apps/web/features/auth/AuthCodeStep.tsx:54-60).
If a second factor is needed the second-factor step appears (IdentityAuthAdapter.tsx:376-391).
The session is finished and the browser goes to /login/complete (IdentityAuthAdapter.tsx:308-315).
That page checks the account status, email confirmation, age confirmation and Terms in order, then continues to the destination or the new chat (apps/web/app/login/complete/page.tsx:69-146).

Desktop: choose Continue in browser. The shell opens /auth/desktop in the system browser with a challenge. The person signs in there. The page asks the server for a one-time code and opens the Desktop deep link. Desktop loads the completion page, trades the code for a ticket and signs in (apps/desktop/electron/browserSignIn.ts:36-54; apps/web/app/auth/desktop/DesktopSignInHandoff.tsx:61-84; apps/web/app/auth/desktop/complete/DesktopSignInComplete.tsx:54-81).

Chrome: click sign-in in the side panel, finish web sign-in in the new tab, see Signed in to AGI Cloud, return to the side panel (apps/web/app/auth/chrome-extension/page.tsx:27-45).

Mobile: type email, Continue; the app creates a sign-in attempt, then shows password entry, an emailed code step, an organization sign-in or provider sign-in; on success the app checks Terms and age before opening Cloud (MobileSignIn.tsx:192-215, 253-276; apps/mobile/app/(auth)/login.tsx:161-300).

Notice step with a Try again in <n>s countdown for rate limits and similar (apps/web/features/auth/AuthNoticeStep.tsx:57).

The shell makes a random verifier and sends only its hash; the server issues a 60-second one-time code bound to that hash; redeeming needs the verifier and returns a short-lived sign-in ticket (apps/desktop/electron/browserSignIn.ts:36-54; apps/web/lib/server/desktop-sign-in.ts:7, 33-69; apps/web/app/api/auth/desktop/grant/route.ts:19-51; apps/web/app/api/auth/desktop/redeem/route.ts:23-54).

established.statement: The surface offers a sign-in entry that authenticates the user to their AGI account, in app or by a browser or device handoff that returns a session.
When sign-up or provider sign-in hits an existing account, or sign-in hits none, the user is told and offered the right path (sign in instead, or create).
The user is not forced to sign in for Local mode; Cloud sign-in entry is visible from the Cloud toggle or model picker; failed sign-in gives a helpful error.
Free managed Cloud is available after sign-in.

acceptance_criteria: On /login typing an email with a password account and the right password ends on the new chat after the completion page.
On /login a suspended, locked or deleted account sees the matching notice and no product page.
An already-signed-in browser opening /login is sent to /login/complete.
A wrong password shows an error against the password field; a rate-limit shows a Try again in <n>s notice.
Desktop Continue in browser opens the system browser; approving there signs Desktop in without typing anything in Desktop; Cancel stops the wait.
agi login prints a link and a code; approving in the browser stores a session; a denied or expired code exits with a message ending Run agi login to try again.
On Mobile an unknown email offers Create an account instead (or goes to the sign-up screen); an existing email in sign-up offers Log in instead.
inferred: Web should say clearly when a new account is being created from a typed address, to meet S3.18; today it proceeds without a message [inferred from IdentityAuthAdapter.tsx:479-486 and the Should line].
Sign-in must never be required for Local mode on Mobile or Desktop [inferred from docs/product/requirements.md:481 and the product rule that local inference is free of subscription].
proposed: [proposed] Add a short line on the web password or code step saying whether the address is new, and log the choice for support.
[proposed] Make the account-status lookup failure at the completion page fail closed with a retry rather than allow (apps/web/lib/auth/account-lifecycle.ts:40-48).

steps.what_happens: Web: the browser calls the identity service (hosted by the identity vendor) to create a sign-in attempt for the typed email.
Web: the page reads the allowed first factors and picks enterprise connection, password or emailed code.
Web: the session is finalized and the browser navigates to /login/complete.
Our server reads the account status from the profiles table and the erasure tombstone, then email state, age state and Terms.
Desktop: the shell makes a random verifier, keeps it in memory, sends only its hash in the browser link.
Desktop: the browser page, once signed in, posts the challenge; the server stores a hashed one-time code for 60 seconds.
Desktop: the shell receives the deep link, checks it matches the pending challenge, loads the completion URL with code and verifier in the fragment.
Desktop: the page posts code and verifier; the server marks the grant used if the hash matches and asks the identity service to mint a short sign-in ticket; the page signs in with the ticket.

CLI and VS Code: the app asks for a device code, the person approves it on the web page, the app polls the token endpoint, which re-checks account, Terms and age and returns an access and refresh token.
Mobile: the app talks to the identity service from the device with native calls and, for providers, an in-app browser session.
Mobile: after sign-in the app checks Terms and adult eligibility with our servers before Cloud opens.

features.summary: New people create an account by typing an email on the shared Web screen, then prove the address with a six-digit emailed code. The account is not usable until the address is confirmed. A password is asked for after the code when the account needs one. Mobile has its own sign-up screen with a verify step.

purpose.what_it_does: Creates an AGI account from an email, sends a code to that address, checks the code, and only then opens a session. If creation worked but the address could not be confirmed, the person is told the account exists and to contact support, and is not signed in (apps/web/features/auth/IdentityAuthAdapter.tsx:247-269, 417-434).
purpose.why_it_exists: An unproven email must not own an account or receive a session, and later steps (support replies, recovery) rely on a confirmed address (apps/web/lib/auth/email-confirmation.ts:51-64).
purpose.who_uses_it: New users on any app. CLI, VS Code and Chrome users create the account on the web page those apps open.
problems_solved: Stops sign-in as an address nobody has proven (IdentityAuthAdapter.tsx:421-427).
Gives browsers and password managers a standard one-time-code field so the code can be autofilled (apps/web/features/auth/AuthCodeStep.tsx:154).
Keeps accounts made by older paths with an unconfirmed address from getting in; they are asked for a code at completion (apps/web/app/login/complete/page.tsx:81-87).
use_cases: A person opens /signup, types an email, enters the code from their inbox, sets a password and starts chatting.
A person whose code expired presses Resend code after the cooldown.
A Mobile user taps Create an account, verifies the emailed code and continues to Terms.
A CLI user without an account approves the device on the web page and is first sent through sign-up.

where_to_find_it: Web: /signup shows the same screen as /login, headed Log in or sign up (apps/web/app/signup/page.tsx:1-11; apps/web/features/auth/AuthEmailStep.tsx:94).

Mobile: Create an account heading, reached by Create an account instead or New to AGI? Create an account (apps/mobile/src/features/auth/components/MobileSignUp.tsx:313; apps/mobile/app/(auth)/login.tsx:413-431).
Desktop, CLI, VS Code, Chrome: the browser page the app opens (see F003-01).
prerequisites: A working email address that can receive a code.
Web: browser able to reach the identity service.
The sign-up must need only an email and a password; any other required field makes the page stop with a support message (apps/web/features/auth/IdentityAuthAdapter.tsx:446-449).
screens_and_controls: Email step: Email address, Continue, agreement text beside the button (apps/web/features/auth/AuthEmailStep.tsx:141-169).

Code step: heading Check your inbox, text We sent a code to <email>, field Code (digits only, six), Continue, Resend code or Resend code in <n>s, Edit beside the address (apps/web/features/auth/AuthCodeStep.tsx:32-35, 128-137, 183-198).

features.summary: People can sign in or sign up with Google, GitHub, Microsoft or Apple, and a work email that an organization has set up for single sign-on goes to that organization's login. Signed-in people can connect another provider or remove a linked method in Settings. The server refuses to remove the last way to sign in.

purpose.what_it_does: Offers provider buttons on the sign-in screen, routes enterprise-covered addresses to the organization's sign-in ahead of personal methods, and lists, connects, disconnects and unlinks sign-in methods in Settings (apps/web/features/auth/IdentityAuthAdapter.tsx:31-36, 393-395; apps/web/features/settings/components/Settings/SignInMethodsPanel.tsx:427-513).
purpose.why_it_exists: Many people prefer a provider to a password, organizations require single sign-on, and an account needs more than one way in for safety [inferred].
purpose.who_uses_it: Anyone signing in with a provider; employees of organizations with single sign-on; signed-in users managing sign-in methods.
problems_solved: No new password to remember.
Organizations control authentication for their domain: the enterprise connection outranks personal factors on the same address (IdentityAuthAdapter.tsx:44-46, 393-395).
Account takeover risk: unlinking needs a step-up check, asks first, tells the account holder and records an audit event (apps/web/app/api/settings/identities/route.ts:64-114).
Locked-out by removal: the server refuses to remove the last or the registered sign-in method (identities/route.ts:26-31, 99-101).
use_cases: A user clicks Continue with Google and lands signed in.
An employee types a work email and is sent to the company login.
A user connects GitHub in Settings so either provider works.
A Desktop user presses Continue in browser and signs in with a provider in the system browser.

steps.what_happens: Web: the page asks the identity service to start a provider redirect with return addresses on our site.
The browser goes to the provider (Google, GitHub, Microsoft or Apple), the person signs in, the provider returns to the identity service and to /auth/sso-callback.
Our server runs the completion checks on /login/complete or /signup/complete.
Enterprise: the page finds the enterprise factor for the typed address and redirects to the organization's login.
Desktop: the shell opens the system browser; the browser runs one of the flows above; the handoff of F003-01 returns the session.
Settings unlink: the page calls DELETE with CSRF token and step-up grant; our server removes the identity, audits and notifies.
Settings connect and disconnect run through the identity service client in the browser.

features.summary: A passkey is a device-held login key. On Web a signed-in person can add, rename and remove passkeys in Settings, Security, and sign in with one from the first screen when the deployment turns it on. Mobile lists and removes passkeys but adds them on the web and has no passkey sign-in.

purpose.what_it_does: Registers passkeys and security keys on an account, lists them, renames and removes them, and lets a person sign in with a stored passkey instead of a password or code (apps/web/lib/identity/client.ts:149-176, 253-270; apps/web/features/auth/IdentityAuthAdapter.tsx:620-626).
purpose.why_it_exists: Passkeys resist phishing better than passwords, and the Mobile settings footnote says so (apps/mobile/src/features/settings/account-security/PasskeysSection.tsx:23-24).
purpose.who_uses_it: Security-minded users and anyone who prefers one-tap sign-in.
problems_solved: No password typing or code copying.

Sign-in on a device that holds the passkey without the inbox.

features.summary: A person can turn on an authenticator app as a second sign-in step, is asked for that code (or a backup code) at sign-in, gets one-time backup codes shown once, and can ask a human to restore access after losing a password, email or second factor. Built on web and desktop; mobile challenge partial.

purpose.what_it_does: Lets a signed-in person enrol an authenticator app (QR code or typed setup key, confirmed with a six-digit code), receive one-time backup codes, regenerate them, and turn the factor off. At sign-in the identity provider asks for a second factor and the web sign-in screen offers the factors the account has. People who lost a password, an email address or their second factor can file an account-recovery request that a support person completes. [inferred from the files cited below]
purpose.why_it_exists: A password or email code alone can be stolen. A second factor protects the account, and organizations can require it (workspace MFA policy). Recovery exists so a person who loses the factor is not locked out forever, without letting an attacker talk their way in: a human checks the account is theirs (apps/web/app/recover/page.tsx:25-33).
purpose.who_uses_it: Any signed-in account holder (Settings > Security); workspace members whose organization requires MFA; support staff who complete recovery tickets.
problems_solved: Stolen or guessed passwords alone cannot open the account.
Losing a phone does not permanently lock the account (backup codes, then human recovery).
Organizations can require MFA and refuse requests from members who have not enrolled (apps/web/lib/mfa-policy-gate.ts:91-99).
Enrolment never half-applies: if the identity provider refuses, nothing changes (apps/web/app/api/settings/2fa/verify/route.ts:21-37).
use_cases: A user opens Settings > Security, presses Set up authenticator app, scans the QR code, types the six-digit code, then copies or downloads the backup codes.
A user with 2FA signs in with email and password, is asked 'Confirm it is you', and enters the authenticator code; if the phone is gone they pick 'Use a backup code'.
A user lost both device and backup codes, opens /recover?lost=factor, fills the form, and a support person later removes the second factor.
A member of a workspace that requires MFA is refused until they enrol.

where_to_find_it: Web: Settings > Security page (heading 'Security', 'Sign-in methods, two-factor, passkeys, password and sessions.') with an 'Authenticator app' card (apps/web/features/settings/sections/SecuritySection.tsx:231-250; TwoFactorEnrollment.tsx:485).
Desktop: the same Security page, because the public Desktop window shows the hosted web app (doc: AGENTS.md section 5).
Mobile: Settings account security, section titled 'Two-factor sign-in' (apps/mobile/src/features/settings/account-security/TwoFactorSection.tsx:245).

Recovery: web page /recover titled 'Recover your account' (apps/web/app/recover/page.tsx:25); mobile reset-password screen buttons 'Open Web Account' and 'Lost Your Email or Two-Factor Device?' (apps/mobile/app/(auth)/reset-password.tsx).
CLI, VS Code, Chrome: no screen of their own; the second factor is entered on the web sign-in page [inferred from device sign-in opening the web approval page, see F003-08].
prerequisites: Signed in with a Cloud account.

Server switch AGI_AUTHENTICATOR_ENROLLMENT must be '1' or enrolment endpoints answer 'Authenticator apps and backup codes are temporarily unavailable.' (apps/web/lib/authenticator-enrollment.ts:5-16).
A fresh step-up confirmation (requireStepUp) for enabling, regenerating codes and disabling (setup/route.ts:45, backup-codes/route.ts:39, route.ts:50).
To offer an emailed code as a second factor, the deployment sets AGI_AUTH_MFA_EMAIL_FALLBACK to '1' (apps/web/features/auth/authProviderConfig.ts:8,19).
screens_and_controls: Security > Authenticator app card: button 'Set up authenticator app'; QR image (alt 'QR code containing your two-factor setup key'); 'Copy key'; input with placeholder 123456; buttons 'Verify and enable' and cancel (TwoFactorEnrollment.tsx:611-738).

Backup codes screen: heading 'Save your backup codes', list labelled 'Backup codes', buttons 'Copy codes', 'Download codes' (file agiworkforce-backup-codes.txt), 'Print codes', and a checkbox 'I have saved these backup codes somewhere safe' before it can be dismissed (TwoFactorEnrollment.tsx:530-595, 448).
When on: buttons 'Generate new backup codes' / 'Replace backup codes' and 'Turn off two-factor', each behind a confirm dialog that names the consequence (TwoFactorEnrollment.tsx:366-381,720-728).

Sign-in step: heading 'Confirm it is you', code field, 'Continue', alternative buttons 'Use your authenticator app', 'Text me a code instead', 'Email me a code instead', 'Use a backup code', link 'Lost your device and backup codes?' or 'Lost the device with your codes?' to /recover?lost=factor, and 'Use a different email' (apps/web/features/auth/AuthSecondFactorStep.tsx).

Recovery form: three choices 'My password, and the reset email did not help', 'Access to the email address on the account', 'My two-factor device and backup codes', plus account email, reply email and details fields (AccountRecoveryForm.tsx:18-24).
journey: Enrol: open Settings > Security and press 'Set up authenticator app'; the app may ask you to confirm it is you (step-up).
Scan the QR code or copy the setup key into the authenticator app.
Type the six-digit code and press 'Verify and enable'.
Read and save the backup codes (copy, download or print), tick the acknowledgement box and dismiss. The codes are not shown again.
Sign in later: enter email and password (or email code); the 'Confirm it is you' step asks for the authenticator code; pick a backup code if the phone is gone.
Lost everything: open /recover (also linked from the second-factor step), choose what you lost, fill the form and submit; wait for a person to reply to the address you gave.
feedback_and_outputs: After verify: success state with the one-time backup codes (reason 'enabled'); after regenerate: 'Your previous backup codes have been invalidated.' (TwoFactorEnrollment.tsx:520-527).
Refusal text if the provider will not take the factor: 'Two-factor sign-in cannot be switched on right now. Nothing changed. Try again later or contact support.' (verify/route.ts:33-35).
Wrong code: 401 'Invalid TOTP code'; stale setup (older than 30 minutes): 'Start the authenticator setup again to get a fresh setup key.' (verify/route.ts:65-80).
Print failure: 'The codes could not be sent to the printer. Download or copy the codes instead.' (TwoFactorEnrollment.tsx:47).

Recovery submit: always the same quiet confirmation 'If that address belongs to an account, your request is recorded and a receipt is on its way...' (AccountRecoveryForm.tsx:44-51); a receipt email and a security notice to the account owner follow when a ticket is opened.
settings: Settings > Security > Authenticator app on/off and backup codes.
Workspace policy 'require MFA' (organization policy; read by GET /api/settings/2fa/requirement).
Server environment: AGI_AUTHENTICATOR_ENROLLMENT, AGI_AUTH_MFA_EMAIL_FALLBACK, AGI_AUTH_PROVIDERS (names only; values not read).

working: Web enrolment: POST /api/settings/2fa/setup creates a secret, seals it, stores a pending row (enabled=false) and returns the secret and otpauth URL (apps/web/app/api/settings/2fa/setup/route.ts:57-86).

Web verification: POST /api/settings/2fa/verify checks the code against the pending row (not older than 30 minutes), creates backup codes, registers the factor and codes with the identity provider, deletes the local pending row, records the enrolment, audits and notifies (verify/route.ts:55-100).
Backup-code regeneration replaces the old set at the identity provider, needs step-up, audits and notifies the owner (backup-codes/route.ts:39-75).
Turning off the factor needs step-up and removes it at the identity provider (apps/web/app/api/settings/2fa/route.ts:50-58).

Sign-in challenge on web: the adapter maps provider factors (totp, phone_code, email_code, backup_code) to authenticator, text message, email, backup code and orders them in that priority; the email factor is hidden unless the deployment allows it (IdentityAuthAdapter.tsx:48-65,170-189).

Recovery: POST /api/support/recovery (CSRF, rate limit, bot check) always answers 202; a background job looks up the account by email, opens a support ticket, records an identity security event and emails a receipt (apps/web/app/api/support/recovery/route.ts:19-45; apps/web/lib/support/tickets/recovery.ts:32-100).
Staff completion: completeAccountRecovery removes the second factor or sets a new primary email, ends every other session and writes a critical audit event (recovery.ts:108-175).

Mobile: can enrol, regenerate codes and turn the factor off through the same web endpoints (apps/mobile/src/features/settings/account-security/service.ts:355-392); sign-in handles an emailed second-factor code natively (MobileSignIn.tsx:223-233).
incomplete: Mobile sign-in: only the emailed second-factor code is handled by the app's own screens; any other second factor (authenticator, backup code) hands over to the identity provider's built-in sign-in view through onNativeFallback (apps/mobile/src/features/auth/components/MobileSignIn.tsx:223-230; apps/mobile/app/(auth)/login.tsx:364-385). The brief records that this path is not live-tested and the Clerk Dashboard needs Authenticator and Backup codes enabled (brief S3.14).
The recovery flow is human-completed, so 'restores access' depends on staff action (SupportTicketQueuePanel) and is not instant.
Accounts with Advanced Account Security get no support ticket; the request is only logged as a security event and they must use a recovery key (recovery.ts:51-58,122-127).
disconnected_or_disabled: All enrolment endpoints refuse unless the server switch AGI_AUTHENTICATOR_ENROLLMENT equals '1' (lib/authenticator-enrollment.ts:11-17); the Settings card then says 'Authenticator apps are temporarily unavailable. Password, passkeys and email codes still protect you.' (TwoFactorEnrollment.tsx:494). Whether it is set in production is unknown.
The emailed second factor is off unless AGI_AUTH_MFA_EMAIL_FALLBACK is '1' (authProviderConfig.ts:19-21).
not_available: CLI, VS Code and Chrome have no second-factor screen of their own (no code found in apps/cli/src, apps/extension-vscode/src or apps/extension/src for entering a TOTP code).
Passkey as a second factor: not part of this feature (passkeys are F003-06).

established.statement: A user can enrol an authenticator (QR plus setup key, confirm code, backup codes) and from then on sign-in asks for that second factor.
At sign-in an account with MFA is challenged for its second factor, with alternatives such as backup codes, before a session is issued.
On enabling or regenerating, the user is shown one-time recovery codes once and can copy, print or download them.
A user who lost password, email or second factor can start and complete an account-recovery flow that restores access.
Enrolment is rejected with a clear message if the identity provider refuses it, and nothing changes.
Email is the weakest second factor and is offered beside a stronger one only when the deployment allows it.

acceptance_criteria: With the server switch on, a signed-in web user can complete setup: QR and setup key shown, a valid six-digit code enables the factor and shows backup codes once.
A wrong code returns 'Invalid TOTP code' and leaves 2FA off; a setup older than 30 minutes asks to start again.
If the identity provider rejects the factor, the person sees 'Nothing changed' and 2FA stays off.
Regenerating codes shows a new list and the previous codes no longer work; the owner is notified.
A 2FA account signing in on web must pass the second-factor step before reaching chat; the factor list is ordered authenticator, text message, email (only if allowed), backup code.
Submitting /recover for an unknown address gives the same confirmation as for a known one (no account enumeration) and creates no ticket.
Support completing a recovery ticket ends all other sessions of that account.
With the server switch off, the Settings card says authenticator apps are temporarily unavailable and setup is refused.
inferred: Mobile sign-in must eventually complete authenticator and backup-code challenges inside the app or via the provider view without dead ends [inferred from brief S3.14 'partial'].
The count and format of backup codes should be stated to the user before they are shown [inferred; the exact count was not read from generateBackupCodes].
proposed: [proposed] Add a live end-to-end test that signs in a 2FA account on mobile with authenticator and with a backup code.
[proposed] Show recovery ticket status to the requester so they know progress.

steps.what_happens: Person presses 'Set up authenticator app'; the page calls POST /api/settings/2fa/setup after a step-up check.
Server makes a TOTP secret, seals it, stores a pending row with enabled=false and returns the secret and otpauth URL; the page draws the QR code.
Person types the first code; POST /api/settings/2fa/verify opens the pending row (30-minute window) and checks the code.
Server generates backup codes and registers the secret and codes with the identity provider; if refused, answers 503 and changes nothing.
Server deletes the pending row, caches enrolment for 300 seconds, writes an audit event, notifies the owner, returns codes once.
At sign-in the identity provider reports it needs a second factor; the page orders the offered factors and asks for a code.
Recovery request: form posts to /api/support/recovery; server answers 202 at once and a background task files a ticket.
Support staff completes the ticket; server removes the second factor or sets the new email at the identity provider and ends other sessions.

features.summary: Before using Cloud features a person must accept the current versioned Terms and confirm they are an adult (18 or over). Web, desktop and mobile record acceptance with version and surface; mobile also asks age before anything else, even for Local use. CLI and VS Code tell the person to finish on the web.

purpose.what_it_does: Records, per account, which Terms version was accepted, when, and on which surface; refuses accounts that never accepted; notices (and later requires) newer versions. Separately records an adult-eligibility decision (outcome and minimum age, never the age itself) and refuses under-age accounts. [inferred from terms.ts and adult-eligibility.ts]
purpose.why_it_exists: The service is for adults and runs under versioned Terms. The product needs proof of agreement and a decision that stands in a record, without keeping a birth date (apps/web/lib/server/adult-eligibility.ts comments; packages/contracts/types/src/account-eligibility.ts:41-45).
purpose.who_uses_it: Every new account on web, desktop and mobile; every returning account when a binding Terms revision takes effect; people who sign in from CLI, VS Code and Chrome through the device-approval page.
problems_solved: No account is used without recorded agreement.
A Terms change does not lock out users instantly: older valid versions keep working until a binding date.
Under-age accounts are refused and cannot reopen the question by typing another number (mobile keeps the refusal; server keeps the first decision).
Old builds and API callers are told what to do through a clear refusal code.
use_cases: New web user signs up, ticks the agreement and continues to chat.
Returning user on desktop is shown 'Finish signing in' because they never accepted on record.
Mobile user opens the app for the first time, types their age on the age screen, then continues in Local mode without any account.
CLI user runs 'agi login'; the terminal prints the Terms link and keeps waiting until they accept on the web.

where_to_find_it: Web and Desktop: /login/complete page, heading 'Finish signing in', detail 'Review the details below to continue.' (apps/web/app/login/complete/page.tsx:124-130). Sign-up also has a terms checkbox on /signup (apps/web/app/signup/TermsGate.tsx).
Web age step: AgeConfirmationStep on the same page, field label 'Your age' (account-eligibility.ts:6); refusal page AgeIneligibleNotice.
Mobile age: screen age-gate (apps/mobile/app/(public)/age-gate.tsx), placeholder 'Enter your age', button 'Continue'; shown before onboarding and before Local mode (rootRouting.ts:36-43).

Mobile Terms: on the Cloud sign-in screen (apps/mobile/app/(auth)/login.tsx:188-250), checkbox text 'I agree to the Terms of Service, including the arbitration clause and class-action waiver, and acknowledge the Privacy Policy.' with links 'Read Terms' and 'Read Privacy Policy'.

CLI: terminal line 'Accept the updated terms to finish signing in:' with a link (apps/cli/src/oauth.rs:522-532). VS Code: warning message with the Terms or age link (packages/client/client-runtime/src/deviceAuthorization.ts:120-127).
Chrome: message 'Accept the updated AGI Workforce Terms of Service on agiworkforce.com to keep using AGI Cloud chat.' (apps/extension/src/features/cloud-bridge/freeTrialClient.ts:198-200).
prerequisites: Web: a verified primary email comes first (ConfirmEmailStep), then age, then Terms (login/complete/page.tsx:63-117).
Mobile: nothing for the age screen; Terms need a Cloud sign-in.
screens_and_controls: Web Terms gate: checkbox 'I agree to the ...' with links to Terms and Privacy, button labelled 'Continue', link to sign out (TermsReviewSignOut), and, only at first acceptance for an account with no marketing-email decision, an optional marketing email box (page.tsx:119-122).
Web age step: one numeric field and a submit button; under-18 answers show a notice and block continuing.
Mobile age screen: numeric field (max 3 digits, accessibility label 'Enter your age in years'), 'Continue' disabled until something is typed.
Mobile Terms: checkbox (role checkbox) and a button that calls accept; error state offers retry.
journey: Web or Desktop: sign in; the server checks account status, then email confirmation.
If no age decision is on record the age step appears; answer it.
If the account has never accepted (or a binding revision has passed its date) the Terms gate appears; tick and continue; acceptance is recorded with surface web-login or web-signup.
If the account is on an older valid version it continues straight in with a notice header, and can accept early through ?review=terms.
Mobile: first launch shows the age screen; then onboarding or Local chat; when signing in to Cloud, accept the Terms and (if asked) answer the account age check.
CLI and VS Code: start sign-in, open the web approval page, accept there; the terminal keeps polling (CLI) or shows an error and asks to sign in again (VS Code).
feedback_and_outputs: Under 18: 'You must be at least 18 years old to continue.' (account-eligibility.ts:11).
Notice on every age screen: 'This service is for adults. You must be at least 18 years old to use it.'
Terms changed mid-page: API answers TERMS_VERSION_OUTDATED (409) and the mobile store shows 'The Terms changed. Review the current version before continuing.'
Mobile store error: 'Could not record your agreement. Retry and review the current Terms.'
API refusals for clients: terms_acceptance_required with a link (auth-gate.ts:86-107).
settings: None for the person. Operators: MIN_REQUIRED_TERMS_VERSION and MIN_REQUIRED_TERMS_EFFECTIVE_AT (both null today) and MATERIAL_TERMS_GRACE_DAYS (30) in apps/web/lib/server/terms.ts:20-22; the published Terms version comes from POLICY_LAST_UPDATED.terms.

working: Web terms record: recordTermsAcceptance writes terms_version, terms_accepted_at and terms_accepted_surface on public.profiles; surfaces are web-signup, web-login, mobile-auth (apps/web/lib/server/terms.ts:24,186-212).
Standing logic: no record means 'required'; older version means 'notice' unless a binding revision's date has passed (terms.ts:93-113).

POST /api/terms/accept checks CSRF, version match (409 otherwise), confirmed email, new-account rule for sign-up, adult eligibility, then records, optionally records marketing consent and referral attribution (apps/web/app/api/terms/accept/route.ts:100-195).
GET /api/terms/accept returns currentVersion and accepted = standing is not required (route.ts:198-203). This already reports the standing, so the brief's pending patch note looks superseded.
Adult eligibility: server decision from declared age or OS age signal, stored as outcome plus minimum age; refusal is sticky (apps/web/lib/server/adult-eligibility.ts:70-143).

Web: /login/complete shows the age step and the Terms gate; chat layout, /welcome and the LLM gateway re-check Terms and age (apps/web/app/chat/layout.tsx:62-65; apps/web/app/welcome/page.tsx:18-20; app/api/llm/v1/chat/completions/lib/auth-gate.ts:120-137,279-282).
Device sign-in (CLI, VS Code, Chrome, Desktop browser sign-in): approve and token routes refuse until Terms and age are done (app/api/auth/device/approve/route.ts:164-190; token/route.ts:171-190).

Mobile: age gate before everything (rootRouting.ts), device record in MMKV key age-gate:v1, region rule from device time zone with Brazil and India rules (ageGate.ts:25-66); Terms store verifies, accepts, handles 409 (apps/mobile/src/features/auth/store/termsAcceptanceStore.ts).
incomplete: No Terms revision is binding yet: MIN_REQUIRED_TERMS_VERSION and its date are null, so a new Terms version only produces a notice header and an early-accept link; nobody is re-prompted (terms.ts:20-21,108-113).
Region age rules do not change the threshold: getAgeThreshold uses the larger of the region rule and 18, and Brazil and India are also 18 (ageGate.ts:25-26,69-71).

CLI and VS Code do not show age or Terms screens; they point to the web. CLI keeps polling after printing the link; VS Code stops with an error (oauth.rs:522-532; deviceAuthorization.ts:120-127; deviceAuth.ts:253-256).
Chrome has only a refusal message in the cloud client; acceptance happens on the web.
disconnected_or_disabled: Terms read failures fail open: if acceptance cannot be read the account is let through, logged and counted (terms.ts:148-160). This is deliberate (notice requirement) but means a database outage skips the gate.
not_available: The brief says web and desktop have no age check; the code has one (login/complete/page.tsx:91-104). The brief's age 'missing' status for web and desktop is out of date.
Guest web chat has its own age step (apps/web/features/chat/guest/GuestAgeStep.tsx); see F003-12.

established.statement: Before first use the user reviews and accepts the current Terms (versioned); acceptance is recorded; a Terms change re-prompts.
Where age limits apply the user must confirm age or eligibility before use; under-age users are blocked or restricted.
An account on an older version keeps working until a material revision's effective date, at least MATERIAL_TERMS_GRACE_DAYS (30) after publication.
Accounts that never accepted are refused until they accept.
Acceptance is stored with its version and surface.
The decision keeps that the person met the minimum, never the age or birth date.

acceptance_criteria: A new web account cannot reach /chat or /welcome until age and Terms are done.
Accepting with a stale version returns 409 TERMS_VERSION_OUTDATED and the page reloads the current version.
An under-18 answer shows the refusal and the account stays refused when a higher age is typed later.
After acceptance profiles has the version, time and surface (web-signup, web-login or mobile-auth).
On mobile, the age screen appears before onboarding and before Local chat on a fresh install.
A CLI sign-in for an account that has not accepted prints the Terms link and finishes after acceptance on the web.
A VS Code sign-in in the same state shows a message with the link and does not sign in.
When a binding revision's effective date passes, an account on the old version is refused until it accepts (set the two constants in a test).
inferred: Desktop gets Terms and age because browser sign-in goes through /login then /login/complete [inferred from apps/desktop/electron/browserSignIn.ts and apps/web/app/auth/desktop/DesktopSignInHandoff.tsx:53].
Local mode on mobile needs an age confirmation but no Terms, since Terms are tied to the Cloud account [inferred from rootRouting.ts and the login screen].
proposed: [proposed] Make VS Code keep polling like the CLI so acceptance on the web finishes the sign-in without restarting.
[proposed] Remove the stale 'unfinished' note from brief S3.19 and update the brief's web and desktop age status.

steps.what_happens: After sign-in the web page checks account access, email confirmation, then reads the adult-eligibility decision from profiles.
If undecided, the age step posts declared_age evidence to /api/eligibility; the server judges it with decideAdultEligibility and stores only outcome and minimum age.
The Terms gate shows; on submit the page posts surface and version to /api/terms/accept.
Server writes the acceptance and clears its cached standing.
Every chat turn and device sign-in later re-reads the standing (cached 5 minutes, refusals never cached).
Mobile checks the typed age against the device rule and stores the verdict locally; it reports evidence to the server when the person signs in to Cloud.
CLI and VS Code poll the device token endpoint; the server answers terms_acceptance_required with a link until accepted on the web.

access_and_usage.local_mode: Mobile Local mode needs the age confirmation but no account, no Terms and no payment (rootRouting.ts:36-43; test apps/mobile/__tests__/age-gate-guards-cloud-not-local.test.ts). Desktop Local use outside the hosted app: unknown.

features.summary: First-run setup that asks a preferred name and what the person's work is, offers starter prompts, and leads into a first chat. Web (and desktop through it) has a two-step wizard at /welcome; mobile has a name and work step inside local-first setup; CLI, VS Code and Chrome have setup without a name step.

purpose.what_it_does: Saves a preferred name and a work description to the account so replies can address and tailor to the person, offers starter prompts based on one use-case answer (not saved), then opens chat with the chosen prompt filled in. On other apps it runs a first-run setup that ends in the first chat.
purpose.why_it_exists: A new person should not face an empty box. Telling the assistant a name and work makes early answers fit, and starters show what to try (apps/web/features/onboarding/components/OnboardingWizard.tsx:41-45).
purpose.who_uses_it: New users on web, desktop and mobile; new CLI, VS Code and Chrome installs.
problems_solved: Blank first screen.
Replies that ignore who the person is.
Over-collection: the use-case answer is spent on suggestions and never stored on the account (onboarding-preferences.ts:20-30).
use_cases: A new web user types 'Sam', picks a work description, picks 'Write and debug code' and clicks a starter prompt; chat opens with the prompt in the box.
A new phone user types a name, skips the work question, downloads a local model and starts a private chat.
A developer runs the CLI for the first time and walks the setup to choose a model and permission mode.
A VS Code user opens the 'Get started with AGI Code' walkthrough and resumes it later.

where_to_find_it: Web (and Desktop, which shows the hosted app): page /welcome (apps/web/app/welcome/page.tsx); two steps titled 'What should we call you?' and 'What do you want to do first?'.
Mobile: first-run screens in apps/mobile/app/(public)/onboarding.tsx: intro, 'About you' step with fields 'Your name' and 'What best describes your work?', then device and model screens.
CLI: first run of agi shows 'Welcome to <product>' and the setup steps (apps/cli/src/onboarding.rs:795-1040).
VS Code: Welcome page walkthrough 'Get started with AGI Code' (apps/extension-vscode/package.json:816-890).
Chrome: welcome tab titled 'AGI in Chrome' and a side-panel onboarding prompt (apps/extension/src/welcome.ts; features/onboarding/welcome-page.ts).
prerequisites: Web: signed in, current Terms accepted and adult eligibility confirmed, otherwise /welcome redirects to those pages (welcome/page.tsx:18-20); if onboarding is already completed it redirects to /chat (page.tsx:29-31).
Mobile: age gate done.
CLI: terminal run of agi without a setup marker.
screens_and_controls: Web step 1: input 'Preferred name' (max 60), select 'What best describes your work?' (placeholder 'Select one'), 'Skip for now', 'Continue' (disabled while name is empty).

Web step 2: radio list of use cases (e.g. 'Write and debug code', 'Write and edit', 'Research and analyze'), note 'This picks the suggestions below and nothing else. It is not saved to your account...' with 'Learn more' link, 'Start with one of these' prompt buttons, 'Back', 'Skip for now', 'Finish'.
Web 'How this works' expandable list with three points about model choice, saved history and personalization.
Mobile About you: two text inputs and a continue button (disabled until a name is typed), 'Skip for now' (onboarding.tsx:610-657).
Mobile intro shows three notices: control of settings, where local and cloud chats are kept, 'AI can make mistakes, so check important information.' (onboarding.tsx:61-77).
CLI: menus for trust, sign-in method, model, reasoning, permission mode, a yes/no for the terminal bell, and 'Press Enter to start...'.
journey: Web: land on /welcome after sign-in; type the name; pick the work description; press 'Continue'.
Pick what to do first; click a starter prompt or press 'Finish'.
The page saves the name, the work description and a completion time, then opens /chat; a clicked prompt arrives in the message box (not sent).
Mobile: read the intro; accept the short first-run disclosure; enter name and work or skip; choose or download a local model; arrive in chat.
CLI: confirm the folder is trusted; choose Local model, own key or AGI sign-in; pick a model; pick a permission mode; press Enter; chat starts.
feedback_and_outputs: Errors: 'Failed to save your preferences' or 'Failed to skip setup' in a red alert; the page stays and allows retry (OnboardingWizard.tsx:99-110).
Button text changes to 'Finishing...' while saving.
After finishing, /chat shows the prompt in the composer and the URL parameter is removed (WebChatPage.tsx:1317-1327).
The name appears in model instructions as 'The user's preferred name is ...' (user-identity.ts:186-191).

not_available: Resumable checklist on web, desktop, mobile, CLI, Chrome (brief S3.36); only VS Code has one.

aliases: Import memory from other AI providers
features.summary: Settings that new users meet: choose whether memory is used, import memories from another assistant, review desktop system permissions, and opt in to notifications. Memory and import work on web, desktop and mobile; notifications are optional on each app; a role-based recommended-apps step and recommended plugins were not found.

purpose.what_it_does: Lets a person turn memory on or off, import facts from ChatGPT, Claude, Gemini, Copilot or another assistant after previewing them, see and change what the desktop app may do on their computer, and decide about notifications.
purpose.why_it_exists: Memory, local permissions and notifications each affect privacy and trust, so each is an explicit, changeable choice rather than a hidden default. Importing saves a new user from starting empty.
purpose.who_uses_it: New and existing users on every app; desktop users granting computer control.
problems_solved: Starting with no context.
Unclear what the desktop app is allowed to do.
Notification prompts at the wrong time (mobile spends the one OS prompt only after a primer).
use_cases: A new web user opens Settings > Memory, presses 'Start import', pastes ChatGPT's list and commits the previewed facts.
A Mac user opens Settings > Permissions and presses 'Open System Settings' for Screen Recording.
A phone user turns on notifications from a primer and later changes categories.
A VS Code user follows the walkthrough step 'Decide what AGI remembers'.

established.statement: During setup the user is told about memory, chooses whether and how it is used, and can change it later.
The user can bring memories or history from another assistant through a guided import.
New users are shown a few recommended apps and can connect them in a guided flow.
New users are offered recommended plugins or skills (no app has it).
The app walks the user through the local permissions it needs and records the grants.
Notifications are offered optionally, are declinable and can be changed later.
Imports go through the memory import route and respect workspace memory policy.

Commit over MAX_IMPORT_ITEMS is rejected.

Removing a permission answer makes Desktop ask again next time.
The web notification banner appears at most until dismissed or enabled and never again after (stored flag).
Mobile asks for the OS notification permission only after the person presses 'Turn on notifications'.
CLI bell stays off unless the person answers yes.
inferred: Imported memory should be subject to the same admission rules as typed memory [inferred from memoryWriteAdmission use].
Desktop grants made through ask-on-use are the 'recorded grants' of S3.29 [inferred from DesktopPermissionsSection 'Your answers'].
proposed: [proposed] Add a memory choice to the first-run wizard on web and mobile.
[proposed] Decide whether recommended apps and plugins stay in scope; if not, mark S3.27 and S3.28 not applicable.
[proposed] Turn the permission review into a short guided pass on first desktop launch.
