aliases: Remote Control pairing in VS Code
features.summary: Connects the Chrome extension or a phone to the desktop app. Chrome: Desktop shows an 8-character code in a native dialog and the extension types it in. Phone: Desktop shows a QR (and code) and the phone claims it through the account and a relay. Both can be unpaired. Mobile pairing exists but is switched off in the current mobile build.

purpose.what_it_does: Creates a trusted link between the Desktop app and either the Chrome extension (so chat can read and act in the browser, with approval) or a phone and VS Code (Remote Control: follow and steer coding sessions, approve steps).
purpose.why_it_exists: The extension and phone should act only for the person who owns the computer. A one-time code or QR proves a human at that computer started the pairing.
purpose.who_uses_it: Desktop users who use Chrome automation; paid-plan users who want to follow coding sessions from a phone or VS Code.
problems_solved: Any local program or web page pretending to be the extension.
A stranger's phone joining someone's desktop.
Stale links: pairings expire and can be removed.
use_cases: A user opens the extension side panel, chooses Connect to Desktop, reads the code from Desktop and types it; Chrome can then be used from chat.
A user opens Desktop > Remote Control, presses 'Pair a phone', scans the QR with the phone and allows it in the dialog.
A VS Code user runs 'Code: Remote Control' and scans the panel's QR.
A user unpairs Chrome from Desktop > Chrome.

where_to_find_it: Desktop: Settings pane 'Chrome' (apps/web/features/desktop-host/components/BrowserPairingSection.tsx:14,114) and pane 'Remote Control' (RemoteControlSection.tsx:37).
Chrome extension: side panel 'Connect to Desktop' (as named in the Desktop text, BrowserPairingSection.tsx:17-18).
Mobile: Remote/companion screens, currently unavailable (apps/mobile/app/(app)/settings/remote-control.tsx:131).
VS Code: command 'Code: Remote Control' (package.json:272-274) opening a panel with a QR.
prerequisites: Desktop app running with the local pairing bridge listening; browser host registered (BrowserPairingSection.tsx:21-24).

Remote Control: a paid plan that includes it (RemoteControlSection.tsx:50), workspace policy and the server switch allowing it (remote-control-gate.ts:97-125), and a signed-in phone on the same account (manualPairing.ts claim route).
screens_and_controls: Desktop Chrome pane: 'Install extension' (when nothing asked yet), text 'The code is in a dialog Desktop opened on this Mac. It is never shown on this page.', state 'Paired and answering' or 'Paired, not answering right now', buttons 'Register the browser host again' and 'Unpair'.
Desktop Remote Control pane: 'Pair a phone', dialog 'Pair your phone' with QR and code, 'Cancel pairing', 'Disconnect phone', 'Stop Remote Control', and a copy-link option for a browser.
Native confirm dialog before a phone connects: 'Pairing code ...' with a warning to allow only the phone you just used (remoteControlService.ts:196-210).
journey: Chrome: install the extension; in its side panel choose Connect to Desktop; Desktop opens a native dialog with an 8-character code; type it in Chrome within two minutes (three tries).
Desktop shows 'Paired and answering' and a fingerprint; the browser host is registered so Chrome can reach the app.
Phone: on Desktop open Remote Control and press 'Pair a phone'; on the phone open the pairing scan screen and scan the QR; Desktop asks you to allow that phone; confirm.
To undo: Desktop > Chrome > 'Unpair', or Desktop > Remote Control > 'Disconnect phone'; to pair a different phone stop Remote Control and pair again.
feedback_and_outputs: Wrong code: 'That code does not match the one shown in <Desktop name>.'; after three wrong codes 'Too many wrong codes. Start pairing again from Chrome.' (bridgeServer.ts:341-360).

Phone messages: 'That pairing code is invalid or expired. Generate a new code on Desktop.', 'That pairing code is already connected to a phone.', 'That pairing code belongs to a different account. Sign in as that account on Desktop.' (manualPairing.ts:163-200).
'Remote Control comes with paid plans.' on lower plans (RemoteControlSection.tsx:50).
'Connection lost. Reconnecting so your phone can pick up where it left off.' (RemoteControlSection.tsx:49).
settings: Desktop Settings > Chrome and Remote Control panes.

working: Chrome pairing on Desktop: pending requests expire after 120 seconds, code is 8 characters from a 32-letter alphabet, 3 wrong tries end the request, timing-safe compare, request must come from the extension named in its origin (packages/contracts/types/src/browser-bridge.ts:119-123; apps/desktop/electron/browser/bridgeServer.ts:142-201,324-361,365-395).
On success Desktop saves the pairing and installs the native-messaging host manifest and returns a token and fingerprint (bridgeServer.ts:365-379).
Unpair from Desktop: browser_pairing_unpair removes host and pairing (apps/desktop/electron/runtime/dispatcher.ts:3127-3133).
Extension binds the pairing to the signed-in account locally and drops it if another account signs in (apps/extension/src/features/native-bridge/pairing.ts:119-135,259-290).

Phone claim: POST /api/pair/claim requires a signed-in session, CSRF, rate limit and the Remote Control standing check, then asks the relay to mint a token for that account; the relay refuses another account (apps/web/app/api/pair/claim/route.ts).
The QR carries a secret (scheme agiw3:) and the 12-character code alone no longer secures a connection (apps/mobile/services/manualPairing.ts:10-33; packages/contracts/types/src/pairing.ts:50).
Phone commands are signed with a key derived per session (HMAC, envelope version 3) (apps/mobile/lib/dispatchHmac.ts:18-30).
Desktop and VS Code ask the person to confirm the phone before it connects (remoteControlService.ts:196-210 in both).
VS Code: command opens a webview with the QR and calls /api/pair/initiate (apps/extension-vscode/src/features/remote-control/remoteControlService.ts:154-175).
incomplete: Mobile pairing code is present but turned off: FEATURES.companion and FEATURES.dispatch are false, and the Remote settings screen shows 'FeatureUnavailable' (apps/mobile/lib/v1FeatureFlags.ts:8-16; app/(app)/settings/remote-control.tsx:131). disconnected_or_disabled: Mobile companion and dispatch flags are false (v1FeatureFlags.ts).

not_available: Web: no pairing screen (not applicable).
CLI: not applicable (brief).

established.statement: The browser extension can be paired with the desktop app (or account) through a guided code/confirm step, with a way to unpair.
A phone can be paired with the desktop app by QR or short code, and the pairing is bound to the signed-in account.
A pairing request expires after 120 seconds and allows 3 wrong codes.
The code proves a person at the computer read it; it is never shown on the web page.
A pairing never outlives the reasons that would have refused it (plan, workspace policy, switch).

acceptance_criteria: Starting pairing from Chrome shows a code only in a Desktop dialog; entering it pairs and the Chrome pane shows the fingerprint.
A wrong code three times ends the request; a request older than 120 seconds is gone.
Unpair on Desktop removes the pairing and the extension notices the release.
A pairing made while signed in as account A is rejected when account B signs in to the extension.
On a plan without Remote Control the 'Pair a phone' path says it comes with paid plans and no pairing is created.
A phone signed in as another account gets 'belongs to a different account'.
An older QR without the secret is rejected with the update message.
With mobile flags off, Settings > Remote shows the unavailable notice.
inferred: Desktop pairing with Chrome is local only (loopback bridge) and does not need our servers [inferred from bridgeServer.ts being a local server and the bridge URL being validated as local in pairing.ts].
Remote Control needs our relay and gateway, so it does not work offline [inferred from the claim route and relay URL checks].
proposed: [proposed] Decide the date to turn on mobile companion and update the brief status to disabled until then.
[proposed] Show a pairing expiry countdown in the Desktop dialog.

steps.what_happens: Extension asks the local Desktop bridge for a pairing; Desktop creates a request id and an 8-character code and shows it only in a native dialog.
Person types the code in the extension; the bridge compares it in constant time, counting failures.
On match Desktop installs the native-host manifest, saves the pairing and returns a token and fingerprint; extension stores the token and binds the signed-in account.
Remote Control start on Desktop asks the gateway for a pairing (plan, policy and switch checked) and shows a QR.
Phone scans the QR, then calls /api/pair/claim with its session; the gateway asks the relay to mint a phone token for that account.
Relay refuses if the pairing belongs to another account; Desktop shows a native confirmation naming the pairing code.
Phone and Desktop exchange commands signed with a per-session HMAC key.

aliases: Sync Local Chats to AGI Cloud
features.summary: Lets a person try the product without an account: web guest chat (limited, server-run, behind a switch), mobile Local Mode, CLI local model and VS Code local models. Mobile can copy local chats to Cloud after sign-in. Plan selection and trials are not part of onboarding on any app; trial support lives in billing code.

purpose.what_it_does: Gives a no-account first experience and a path to an account. On web a visitor chats with a managed model under daily limits and is nudged to sign up. On mobile, CLI and VS Code a person can use a local model or their own key without signing in. On mobile, local chats can be copied to the account later.
purpose.why_it_exists: People should see value before registering, and local inference must not need payment or an account (product requirement).
purpose.who_uses_it: Visitors on web; first-time users on mobile, CLI and VS Code who prefer Local mode.
problems_solved: Sign-up wall before any value.
Losing local work when someone signs up (mobile copy tool).
Abuse of free managed chat: per-device, per-IP and global limits.
use_cases: A visitor opens /chat signed out and sends a few messages as a guest.
A phone user presses 'Continue in Local Mode' and chats with a downloaded model.
A CLI user chooses 'Local model, no account required' at first run.
A phone user signs in later and syncs selected local chats to AGI Cloud.

features.summary: The place where a signed-in person starts a fresh chat with a ready composer, or reopens an earlier chat to read it and carry on. On web the same chat page serves /chat, /chat/<id> and, for signed-in people, /agi-work with Work mode on. Mobile, CLI, VS Code and Chrome have their own versions.

purpose.what_it_does: Gives every app one starting point for conversations: an empty chat with a composer, and a way to reopen a saved chat with its transcript so the person can keep going. On web both routes render one component, WebChatRoot, so a link and the sidebar land in the same place (apps/web/app/chat/page.tsx:13, apps/web/app/chat/[sessionId]/page.tsx:13).
purpose.why_it_exists: A chat product must open ready to type and must let people return to past work. Competing products (ChatGPT, Claude) open on an empty composer and list past chats in a sidebar [inferred from the product context given].
purpose.who_uses_it: Every signed-in person on the Web, Desktop (which shows the hosted web app), Mobile, CLI, VS Code and Chrome apps.
problems_solved: No dead end after sign-in: the person always lands on a usable composer.
Past chats can be reopened from a list or from a link.
A deep link can pre-fill a draft or switch on Work mode (q, from, mode parameters).
The browser tab shows the chat title.
use_cases: Open agiworkforce.com signed in and type a first question.
Click an old chat in the sidebar and ask a follow-up.
Follow a link such as /chat?q=... that opens a new chat with a draft in the composer.
Start 'agi' in a terminal for a new session or run 'agi --session <id>' to resume one.

where_to_find_it: Web: /chat for a new chat; /chat/<id> for an old one; clicking a chat in the sidebar goes to /chat/<id>; for a signed-in person /agi-work is rewritten to /chat with Work mode on (apps/web/proxy.ts:128-130, apps/web/proxy.ts:209).
Desktop: the Electron window shows the hosted web app, so it is the same /chat page (AGENTS.md section 5; apps/desktop/electron/config.ts:10-12).

Mobile: drawer row 'New chat' (packages/ui/i18n/locales/en/common.json drawer.newChat; apps/mobile/src/features/drawer/components/DrawerContent.tsx:655) and chats in the drawer list; a chat opens at apps/mobile/app/(app)/chat/[id].tsx.

CLI: 'agi' starts the terminal UI for a new session; '--session <id>' or '-r/--resume <id>' resumes one; '-c/--continue' continues the newest session in the project; 'agi session list' and 'agi session show <id>' (apps/cli/src/lib.rs:246-298, apps/cli/src/lib.rs:1931-1980).

VS Code: commands 'Code: New Conversation' (agi-workforce.newConversation, keybinding ctrl/cmd+n when chat is focused) and 'Code: Open Conversation' (apps/extension-vscode/package.json:192,355,1521-1529).
Chrome: side panel; a new chat shows the label 'New chat' until the first message, after which it is saved on the device or mirrored to the account (apps/extension/src/side_panel.ts:595-615).
prerequisites: Web, Desktop, Mobile cloud mode: a signed-in account (identity session cookie or token).

Mobile Local mode: no account is needed to chat on the device [inferred from Local-mode code paths in apps/mobile/stores/chat/chatViewStore.ts:262-330 that search on-device stores]; sign-in rules for Local are unknown.
CLI: sessions are files on the device; account features need 'agi login'.
screens_and_controls: Web: composer, sidebar list of chats, chat title in the browser tab.

Web error states: error.tsx shows ChatFailureNotice with a retry callback (apps/web/app/chat/error.tsx:12-30); not-found.tsx shows 'Conversation not found' with 'Start a new chat' (apps/web/app/chat/not-found.tsx:21).
Mobile: 'New chat' row, 'Search' icon in the drawer header, 'Recents' and 'Pinned' chat rows.
CLI: start view with key hints, status line, 'Workspace' pane.
journey: 1. Person signs in and opens /chat (web) or taps 'New chat' (mobile).
2. The page loads the chat shell; a loading skeleton shows first (ChatLoadingSkeleton, apps/web/features/chat/components/WebChatRoot.tsx:12-15).
3. If the link carries q, from or mode=agiwork, the draft and Work mode are applied once and the parameters are removed from the address (apps/web/features/chat/hooks/use-new-chat.ts:20-36).
4. Person types in the composer and sends; the app creates the conversation and moves to /chat/<id> [inferred from WebChatPage.tsx:2615-2680 where a conversation id is created and set].

5. To reopen an old chat the person clicks it; the page loads the transcript; if loading fails a toast with the message appears and the app returns to /chat (apps/web/features/chat/pages/WebChatPage.tsx:2369-2384).
6. The person continues the chat with the composer.
feedback_and_outputs: Tab title is the chat title, or a new-chat title for /chat (apps/web/lib/server/conversation-title.ts:32-41; apps/web/app/chat/page.tsx:7).
Toast with the load error and a retry action when a chat cannot be opened (WebChatPage.tsx:2376-2383).
Inline notice for a load failure of the displayed conversation (WebChatPage.tsx:7923).
settings: Mobile: Local or Cloud mode switch in the drawer (DrawerContent.tsx:431-440).
Composer Chat or Work mode toggle (apps/web/features/chat/components/Composer/ChatComposerNew.tsx:314-341).

working: Web /chat and /chat/<id> both render WebChatRoot, which loads WebChatPage with no server render and a skeleton (apps/web/features/chat/components/WebChatRoot.tsx:12-27).

Web page title for /chat/<id> is read server side from web_conversations for the signed-in owner, and returns null if the id is not a UUID or the row is deleted (apps/web/lib/server/conversation-title.ts:11-30).
Signed-in /agi-work is rewritten to /chat and /chat reads the x-agi-pathname header to start in Work mode (apps/web/proxy.ts:112-130, apps/web/app/chat/page.tsx:9-15).
New-chat deep link parameters q, from, mode are parsed and applied once; the draft is cut at 2000 characters (apps/web/features/chat/lib/new-chat-entry.ts:38,69-78; use-new-chat.ts:20-36).
Opening /chat/<id> loads the conversation unless it is already in memory; on failure the person is sent back to /chat with an error toast (WebChatPage.tsx:2357-2384).
Mobile has a 'New chat' row, a chat route, and separate lists for Local and Cloud chats (DrawerContent.tsx:442-457,655).
CLI resumes sessions with --session, --resume and --continue, and lists them with 'agi session list' (apps/cli/src/lib.rs:246-298,5586-5645).
VS Code registers newConversation, openConversation, forkConversation and deleteConversation commands (apps/extension-vscode/src/core/commandSetup.ts:1392-1475,1725).
incomplete: The brief says a missing or deleted chat shows a not-found or error state. The web code instead toasts and redirects to /chat; app/chat/not-found.tsx exists but I did not find what triggers it for a chat id (not-found.tsx:21 vs WebChatPage.tsx:2369-2384).
Chrome status in the brief is 'done' but I did not open the Chrome history list code beyond the sync label function (side_panel.ts:595-615); how a past chat is reopened there is not verified.
disconnected_or_disabled: Marketing page apps/web/app/agi-work/page.tsx is shown only to signed-out visitors; signed-in visitors never see it because of the proxy rewrite (proxy.ts:112-130).
not_available: Desktop has no separate Local chat: the Electron shell treats every chat request as Managed Cloud (apps/desktop/electron/config.ts:10-12).
Web has no Local mode [inferred from the same constraint and from web_conversations being the only store seen].

established.statement: A signed-in user lands on or opens an empty new-chat screen with a ready composer from which a new conversation starts.
Opening a past conversation from the list or a link shows its transcript and lets the user continue it.
Local, own-key and Cloud are separate trust boundaries; nothing may silently route a Local chat to BYOK or managed cloud.
packages/ui/unified-chat is shared by desktop, web, Chrome and VS Code, so it may not assume one surface's routing or billing.

acceptance_criteria: Signed in on web, visiting /chat shows an empty transcript and a focused, usable composer.
Visiting /chat/<id> of an own chat shows its messages and a working composer; the tab title equals the chat title.
Visiting /chat/<id> of a deleted or foreign id does not show the chat, shows an error message and returns the person to /chat.
Signed in, visiting /agi-work shows the /chat page with the composer in Work mode; signed out it shows the marketing page.
A link /chat?q=hello pre-fills the draft once and the q parameter is removed from the address.
Mobile: tapping 'New chat' opens an empty chat; tapping a chat in the drawer opens its transcript.
CLI: 'agi --session <id>' opens the saved session with its history.
inferred: The composer must accept input while an old chat is still loading or must show the loading skeleton [inferred from ChatLoadingSkeleton use].
Mobile Local chats and Cloud chats must stay in separate lists (drawer filters by execution mode, DrawerContent.tsx:449-457).
proposed: [proposed] Decide whether not-found.tsx should be shown for an unknown chat id and update the brief or the code so they agree.
[proposed] Add one test that opens /chat/<unknown uuid> end to end and asserts the exact message and redirect.

features.summary: Find a chat by words from its title or messages, move old chats out of sight into Archived and bring them back, and keep chats you pinned at the top of the list. Web has a search dialog and a Settings page; mobile has a search screen and an Archived chats page; CLI has --search and session pin and archive.

purpose.what_it_does: Lets people find past chats (and projects, files and scheduled tasks on web), hide chats without deleting them, and keep important chats first.
purpose.why_it_exists: Chat history grows; people need search, a way to tidy the list, and a way to keep key chats on top, as in ChatGPT and Claude [inferred from product context].
purpose.who_uses_it: Every signed-in person with many chats, on Web, Desktop, Mobile and CLI; Chrome and VS Code have partial versions.
problems_solved: Finding an old answer without scrolling.
Clearing the sidebar without losing chats.
Reaching key chats fast.
use_cases: Press the search shortcut, type 'invoice', open the matching chat.
Archive a finished chat, later restore it from Settings > Archived chats.
Pin a chat so it stays in the Pinned group.
Run 'agi --search deploy' to find CLI sessions.

where_to_find_it: Web: sidebar 'Search' button showing the shortcut label (packages/ui/ui/src/sidebar/Sidebar.tsx:641-650); the code comment says Cmd+K also works (WebChatPage.tsx:1708); /chat?search=true opens the dialog and removes the parameter (WebChatPage.tsx:1673-1683).

Web: Settings > Archived chats at /settings/archived, which redirects into the settings modal section 'archived' (apps/web/app/settings/archived/page.tsx:5; apps/web/features/settings/components/WebSettingsModal.tsx:200). The sidebar also shows 'Archived (N)' when there are archived chats (Sidebar.tsx:672-694).
Web: pinned chats are listed first in the sidebar (Sidebar.tsx:263).

Mobile: drawer 'Search' icon opens /(app)/search, which is the chats list in search mode (apps/mobile/app/(app)/search.tsx:1-5); filters 'All chats', 'Pinned', 'Unread' (ChatsListScreen.tsx FILTER_LABELS); Settings > Archived chats (apps/mobile/app/(app)/settings/archived-chats.tsx).
CLI: 'agi --search <QUERY>'; 'agi session list [--archived]', 'pin', 'unpin', 'archive', 'unarchive' (apps/cli/src/lib.rs:262,1931-1975).
VS Code: tree of conversations with refresh, delete and fork; no pin or archive command found (commandSetup.ts:1392-1478).
Chrome: no archived list (brief); search of browsing history exists but that is a different feature (side_panel.ts:237-241).
prerequisites: Web and mobile Cloud mode: signed in.
Web search of the 'scheduled' category requires a workspace access check (apps/web/app/api/search/route.ts:283-289).
Search is refused if the workspace data region cannot be confirmed (search/route.ts:130-146).
screens_and_controls: Search dialog: text box 'Search your workspace', category group 'Search category' with All, Artifacts, Sessions, Code, Projects, Scheduled (apps/web/features/chat/lib/global-search-categories.ts:1-8), a role filter 'All messages', 'Clear search' button, 'No results found' text.
Archived chats page: heading 'Archived chats', rows with 'Restore' and 'Delete', 'Load more', 'Delete all archived', 'Retry' on error.
Mobile chats list: search box, recent searches, groups Pinned, Today, Yesterday, This Week, Older.
journey: 1. Person opens the search dialog (button, shortcut or ?search=true).
2. Types words; the dialog calls the search service, which requests /api/search with q, limit and optional category, includeArchived, role and dates (global-search-service.ts:150-165).
3. Results are grouped; the person opens one; the app goes to /chat/<id>?highlightMessage=<id> (WebChatPage.tsx:5089 comment).
4. To archive, the person uses the chat's menu (archive action; PUT sets archived true and clears pinned).
5. To restore, open Settings > Archived chats and click 'Restore'; the chat returns to the sidebar.
6. To remove, click 'Delete' or 'Delete all archived'; a confirm dialog names the consequence; deleted chats move to Recently deleted.
feedback_and_outputs: Loading text 'Loading archived chats…'; error text with 'Retry'; load failure text 'Archived chats could not be loaded' that says it is not the same as having none; empty text 'No archived chats' and 'Chats you archive will appear here.' (ArchivedChatsSection.tsx:98-133).
Status notice line after actions (role=status).
Search spinner 'Searching workspace…' and 'No results found' (GlobalSearchDialog.tsx:670,775).
Mobile toast 'Chat archived. Find it in Settings, Archived chats.' with 'Undo' (useConversationActions.ts:136).
settings: Archived chats page is under the Privacy settings area (a '← Privacy' link, ArchivedChatsSection.tsx).
Mobile recent searches are kept per mode and account (apps/mobile/src/features/search; ChatsListScreen.tsx:243-247).

working: GET /api/search matches chat titles with a case-insensitive contains match (ilike '%q%') and message text the same way, and also returns projects, files and schedules by name (apps/web/app/api/search/route.ts:316-380,470-480).
Archived chats are left out unless includeArchived=true (search/route.ts:326,343,378).
Search also uses an index of documents (indexed search) beside the contains match (search/route.ts:21-31,457-460) [inferred from imports and an 'indexSearch' promise].
The route applies a rate limit named chat-conversation and a region residency check (search/route.ts:246-250).

Conversation list route supports archived=include|only|exclude, deleted=exclude|only, title filter q, cursor paging and pinned-first ordering (apps/web/app/api/chat/conversations/route.ts:53-61,92-100,122-124).
Archiving one chat via PUT sets archived and clears pinned in the same update (apps/web/app/api/chat/conversations/[id]/route.ts:374-380).

Bulk route supports archive_all, delete_all, delete_archived; archive_all clears pinned; deletes are soft and revoke published artifacts and shares (apps/web/app/api/chat/conversations/bulk/route.ts:30-33,59-77,92-115).
Web Archived chats page lists, restores, deletes one or all, with confirmation text that names the 30-day recovery (ArchivedChatsSection.tsx:41-58).
Web sidebar groups pinned first and offers an archived view (Sidebar.tsx:242-290,672-694).
Mobile search runs on the server in Cloud mode and on the device in Local mode (apps/mobile/stores/chat/chatViewStore.ts:244-330).
Mobile archive page lists archived=only with paging and search (apps/mobile/src/features/archived-chats/service.ts:44-84).

CLI search covers titles and message text and PR links, archived sessions stay findable; CLI supports pin, unpin, archive, unarchive (apps/cli/src/sessions.rs:919-940,1707; lib.rs:5646-5648,5765-5776).
incomplete: The brief says CLI pinned is missing, but the CLI has 'agi session pin' and 'unpin' and lists pinned sessions first (apps/cli/src/lib.rs:1940-1945,5586-5600). The brief is stale on this point.
The brief says archived chats can be opened; the web archived page offers only Restore and Delete, no Open button (ArchivedChatsSection.tsx:176-195).
User-typed % and _ in the search text are placed inside the ilike pattern without escaping, so they act as wildcards (search/route.ts:316 builds `%${q}%`) [inferred effect].
Mobile search results for Local mode never reach the server and cover only on-device chats (chatViewStore.ts:279-330).
disconnected_or_disabled: Mobile Settings > Archived chats needs Cloud mode and sign-in; the screen reads appMode and sign-in state (archived-chats.tsx:60-66); the exact message when not signed in was not read.
not_available: Mobile Local chats cannot be archived: 'archived is a column on web_conversations, so archiving only exists for Cloud chats' (useConversationActions.ts:109-112).
Pinned list on VS Code and Chrome: not found in code.
Archived list on Chrome: not found (brief says missing).

established.statement: A search destination takes a keyword and returns past conversations matching titles or message text and opens one.
A destination lists archived conversations and lets the user open, restore or delete them.
Pinned conversations are shown together in a pinned section or filter and open from there.
An agent never destroys user data; chats are archived or moved to Recently deleted; permanent removal only from an explicit user action naming what is lost.
A user action that cannot be undone asks first and names the consequence.

acceptance_criteria: Searching a word that appears only in a message body returns that chat with a snippet.
Searching a word only in an archived chat returns nothing, and returns it when includeArchived is set.
Archive a pinned chat on web: it leaves the sidebar and, after restore, is not pinned.
Archived chats page shows 'No archived chats' when empty, an error with Retry when the request fails.
Delete from the archived page shows a confirmation naming Recently deleted and 30 days, and the chat appears under deleted=only after confirming.
Pinned chats appear first in the sidebar and in the mobile 'Pinned' group.
'agi session archive <id>' hides the session from 'agi session list' and 'agi session list --archived' shows it.
inferred: Search text with % or _ should match literally [inferred from user expectation; code does not escape].
Search results must be limited to the owner and organization scope (scoped DB and clauses at search/route.ts:316-380).
proposed: [proposed] Escape % and _ in the contains pattern.
[proposed] Add an 'Open' action to archived rows or update the brief.
[proposed] Decide whether archived chats should be findable by search in the web UI with a toggle, as the CLI already does.

steps.what_happens: Person types in the search dialog; the client calls GET /api/search.
Server checks rate limit, identity, workspace data region, then runs ilike queries on conversations, messages, projects, files, scheduled tasks, plus an indexed document search.
Server returns results with snippets; the client groups them.
Archive or restore sends PUT to the conversation route; archive sets archived and clears pinned.
Delete moves the chat to Recently deleted by setting deleted_at; shares and published artifacts are revoked.
Mobile Local mode scans on-device messages and titles.
CLI reads session files and filters by title and message text.

features.summary: Projects group chats, files and instructions for one piece of work. People list projects, create one, open it to see its Chats, Artifacts, Work, Sources and Scheduled tabs, and edit its instructions and settings. Web and mobile have full screens; the CLI and VS Code manage projects by commands.

purpose.what_it_does: Keeps related chats, files and instructions together so every chat in the project follows the same instructions and sources.
purpose.why_it_exists: Standing instructions and shared files save retyping; both leading products have projects [inferred from product context].
purpose.who_uses_it: Signed-in people doing repeated work on one topic, on Web, Desktop, Mobile, CLI and VS Code.
problems_solved: Repeating context in every chat.
Losing track of chats about one topic.
Applying team instructions to many chats.
use_cases: Create a 'Quarterly report' project with instructions 'Answer in short bullets' and start chats in it.
Open a project to find all its chats and artifacts.
Change a project's default model.
Run 'agi projects create' from a terminal.

established.statement: A Projects destination lists the user's projects and lets them open or create one.
Opening a project shows its name, description/instructions summary and entry points to chats and files.
Within a project, a list of the project's conversations opens when selected.
A place to view and edit a project's instructions, which then apply to chats in that project.
Do not hardcode plans, limits or quotas that the repository models.
Project allowance comes from plan limits.

A project with 80 or more chats shows the capacity banner.
Opening /chat/projects/<unknown> shows 'Project not found' and a 'Back to projects' button.
On a failing network the list shows an error and Retry reloads it.

steps.what_happens: Opening Projects fetches a page of projects (limit 50) for the signed-in account.
Create checks the plan, inserts a user_projects row and rechecks the limit in the same statement.
Opening a project loads it from the store or by id and lists its chats.
Saving settings sends PUT to /api/projects/<id> with the changed fields.
When a chat in the project is sent, the pipeline reads the project's instructions and applies the account instructions only if the switch is on.
Mobile Local projects are stored on the device; Cloud projects use the same API.
CLI refreshes the account's projects and calls create, edit, archive or delete.

features.summary: Gives a project its own files (Sources), lets an owner share it with people in a team workspace with view or edit rights, keeps what the assistant remembered in a project apart from account memory, and offers a notebook-like Sources tab with notes and a studio. Web and Desktop have all of it; mobile has most; the CLI has file add and project memory.

purpose.what_it_does: Lets a project hold knowledge files that every chat in it can use, controls who can open it, and scopes memory to the project.
purpose.why_it_exists: Project chats need reliable source material, team sharing and memory that does not leak across topics [inferred from the Should lines].
purpose.who_uses_it: People with projects: owners, team members, and anyone adding sources or memories.
problems_solved: Chats cannot see files unless added.
Teams need shared project context with controlled rights.
Account memory should not spill into unrelated work.
use_cases: Upload a style guide to a project's Sources.
Share a project with a teammate as 'Can view'.
Turn off use of memories from outside the project.
Add a project-linked memory from the CLI.

features.summary: AGI Work runs a goal in many steps on our servers. People start it from the chat composer in Work mode, then watch runs on the Work history page (/tasks), open a run to read its activity, and approve or deny a step that waits for them. Mobile shows the same runs in cloud mode; VS Code shows a task tree with approvals.

purpose.what_it_does: Starts long, multi-step work that the assistant carries out with tools, lists every run with its state, shows a run's journal and outputs, and asks the person to approve sensitive tool calls.
purpose.why_it_exists: Long tasks need supervision: a place to follow progress and a safe stop for risky actions (apps/web/app/agi-work/page.tsx approval copy).
purpose.who_uses_it: People on a plan with the agi_work capability (pro and above in code) on Web, Desktop, Mobile, VS Code; Chrome shows a list.
problems_solved: Losing track of long jobs.
Risky tool calls running without consent.
Approvals missed when away from the computer.
use_cases: Give a goal 'Compare these three vendors' and watch it work.
Open the Needs you filter and approve a waiting tool call.
Pause a run and resume with guidance.
Re-run an old goal in a new Work chat.

6. Archive finished runs, or re-run the goal.

established.statement: A home for agentic work where the user states a goal for a multi-step AGI Work run and can reach recent work.
A dashboard lists active or running tasks with live status, filterable from finished ones.
Opening a task shows status, step-by-step activity or transcript, outputs and any pending decision.
An approvals inbox gathers every pending approval across tasks and lets the user approve or reject each.
Mobile gates AGI Work on the cloudTasks flag.
Every subscription capability connects to one AGI Subscription system.

acceptance_criteria: With a plan lacking agi_work, the Work control never renders in the composer.
A new Work run appears in Work history > Active within one refresh and shows live updates every ~4 seconds.
'Needs you' shows runs in awaiting_input, awaiting_approval and paused states and lists them first in 'All'.
Clicking Approve on a pending approval resumes the run; if another device answered first the message 'Another device already answered this approval.' appears.
An expired approval shows 'This approval expired and the task can no longer continue from it.'
Archive and Restore buttons appear on web and not on a host that cannot reach the archive route.
The List/Board choice survives a reload.
Mobile in Local mode shows no AGI Work row.
inferred: The approvals inbox is the Needs you filter; a single cross-task approvals page is not present [inferred from TasksPage structure].
Approving must be idempotent across devices (AlreadyResuming error).
proposed: [proposed] Make the Start Work button visible at all times on /tasks.
[proposed] Use one word (Deny or Reject) on every surface.

features.summary: Run a prompt again on a repeating schedule on our servers and read each run's result. The web page lists schedules, creates them from scratch or a template, and lets people edit, pause, run now, delete and read run history, including approving a run that waits. Mobile, CLI, Chrome and VS Code have their own views.

purpose.what_it_does: Stores a prompt with a cadence, fires it on time in the Cloud, and records each run with status, result and any approval it needs.
purpose.why_it_exists: Recurring jobs such as daily summaries should run without the person present.
purpose.who_uses_it: People on a plan that allows scheduled tasks (3 or more) on Web, Desktop, Mobile, CLI and Chrome; VS Code shows schedule details.
problems_solved: Repeating the same prompt by hand.
Missing results when away.
Unsafe unattended actions (approval stops a run).
use_cases: Every weekday at 9 summarise overnight news.
Run a weekly report now to check it works.
Pause a schedule while on holiday.
Approve a paused run from Run History.

Search 'Search scheduled tasks...', status filter All, Active, Paused, Completed, Failed, Expired; sort 'Next run' or 'Recently created'.

journey: 1. Open Scheduled.
2. Click 'New task' > 'Create from scratch' or 'Start from a template'; fill name, prompt, cadence, model, access; save.
3. The card shows next run and status.
4. Use the card actions: edit, pause or resume, 'Run now', delete (asks first).
5. Open Run History to read each run, load more, retry on failure.
6. If a run needs approval, approve or deny it in Run History.

working: GET /api/schedules lists with limit and offset and optional projectId; POST creates under an advisory lock and quota assert (apps/web/app/api/schedules/route.ts:78-136).
A plan limit of zero is refused before anything else with code schedules_not_in_plan; a full quota gives schedule_limit_reached with an upgrade hint (route.ts:42-52,112-120).
Run now posts to /api/schedules/<id>/runs with an Idempotency-Key header; the server requires the header (schedule-api.ts:274-292; runs/route.ts:74-76).

steps.what_happens: Create posts the schedule; the server checks plan and quota inside a transaction with an advisory lock, then inserts into scheduled_tasks.
A cron calls the run-schedules route, which processes due runs (a batch per sweep).
The scheduled agent executes the prompt with a model and tools; the run is recorded in scheduled_task_runs; a run that needs approval pauses the schedule.
Run now posts with Idempotency-Key; the server rejects a missing header.
Run History reads runs by page and resolves approvals with decision and tool call ids.
Desktop local routines run on the computer through the desktop host bridge.

execution_and_data_flow.models_and_providers: Each scheduled run calls a model through the Cloud pipeline. The schedule stores a model selection, defaulting to automatic (CLI help 'Defaults to the account's automatic selection', lib.rs:1529; MANAGED_CLOUD_DEFAULT_MODEL_SELECTION used in Chrome). Provider choice is by routing (SYS-model-catalog-and-routing, SYS-inference-providers). Prompts are checked for secrets before saving (refuseBlockedSchedulePrompt, route.ts:121).

features.summary: Code lets a signed-in person hand a coding task to an agent that works in an isolated cloud environment, optionally on a Git repository. The person follows the transcript and changes, approves or rejects steps the agent waits on, and types the next instruction. Built on web, desktop (hosted web), mobile, CLI and VS Code; absent in Chrome.

purpose.what_it_does: Lists the account's cloud coding sessions, opens a new one on a repository or an empty environment, runs agent turns inside it, shows the transcript, terminal output and file changes, and lets the person commit, close or share the session. A coding-session workspace shows the transcript, file changes/diffs and a composer to steer the next turn.
Inference and sandbox cost is a design constraint; a stronger model is not a default; subscription capability must come from one entitlement system.
Local, own-key and Cloud are separate trust boundaries; nothing silently routes a Local session to managed cloud.

Creating more active sessions than the plan allows is refused with the limit named.
Closing a session names that the environment is destroyed and uncommitted work is lost, and the transcript stays readable.
The same session id opens on web, phone, CLI and VS Code.

steps.what_happens: Person opens /code or the phone or CLI client; the client reads GET /api/code/sessions to get sessions, availability (deployment ready, plan entitled, plan tier, max sessions) and runtime catalogue.

Create posts repository, network access, runtime, extra hosts; server checks sandbox readiness, kill switch, egress rules, workspace and feature policy, subscription access, then plan gate and active cap, then inserts a session row in state provisioning.
The isolated environment is run by an outside sandbox service (provider key and gate named e2b in code).
A turn is posted with goal, model, mode, step bound and an idempotency key; server checks entitlement, model-on-plan and runs the agent loop up to an 800 second budget.
Model calls for the turn go to the model provider selected from the catalog, through the server's managed route, or a coding agent run inside the sandbox using a proxied or the person's own key.
Client polls the session every 4 seconds while a turn has no stop reason; approvals are read again on load.
Approve or reject posts turnId, stepIndex and decision; an expired approval returns a conflict.

access_and_usage.limits_and_metering: Active sessions capped by plan (max 20 overall) (packages/contracts/types/src/billing-catalog.ts:473); step bounds 12, 24 or 48; goal length limited by CLOUD_CODE_LIMITS.task; turn budget 800 s; workspace spend limit checked (apps/web/lib/services/managed-compute-access.ts:140). features.summary: The signed-in places where a person chooses a model, sees how much of their plan they have used, sees plan, invoices and the overage switch, and changes personal preferences. On web and in Electron they open as sections of one settings dialog. Mobile has its own screens. Mobile billing is off in v1.

purpose.what_it_does: Web: a composer model catalogue (search, filters, upgrade hints, 'Coming soon' rows), a Default model dropdown in Settings > General, a Usage page (plan limits per window, credits, monthly spend limit, history, export) and a Billing page (plan, payment methods, invoices, credit history, overage switch, billing portal). Mobile: its own model picker, Usage and Subscription screens. CLI and VS Code read the same usage endpoint. [inferred] from the code listed in implementation_map.
purpose.why_it_exists: The brief says a person must be able to pick a model they can actually reach, see usage against plan limits and reset times, see and manage billing, and save their own preferences (brief: S4.38, S4.39, S4.40, S4.41). The code comments say the catalogue stops the picker offering a model that cannot answer (apps/web/lib/server/model-catalogue.ts, comment in toCatalogueEntry).
purpose.who_uses_it: Any signed-in person on web, Electron Desktop, mobile, CLI or VS Code. Paid people see meters and billing. Free people see an Upgrade prompt on web usage (apps/web/features/settings/sections/UsageSection.tsx:1224-1328).
problems_solved: A person picks a model their plan or the deployment cannot serve and the turn fails (the server drops models with no configured route and marks fully degraded ones unavailable, apps/web/lib/server/model-catalogue.ts toCatalogueEntry).
A person hits a limit with no idea when it resets (Usage shows windows and reset times, apps/web/features/settings/sections/UsageSection.tsx).
A person cannot find their plan, invoices or how to spend extra credits (BillingSection.tsx).
New chats start on the wrong model (Default model row, GeneralSection.tsx:361-420).
use_cases: On web, open the model picker in the composer, search for a model, and choose it; a model above the plan shows 'Upgrade to use' with the plan name (apps/web/features/chat/components/Composer/ModelCatalogue.tsx:569-577).
Open Settings > Usage on a paid plan to see when the 5-hour or weekly window resets (UsageSection.tsx).
Open Settings > Billing, switch overage on, and see it roll back with an error if saving fails (BillingSection.tsx:301-325).
On the phone open Settings > Usage while signed in to Cloud (apps/mobile/src/features/settings/index.tsx:855-860).

where_to_find_it: Web and Electron Desktop: model picker button in the composer footer opens the catalogue (apps/web/features/chat/components/Composer/ComposerFooter.tsx:1208, ModelCatalogue mounted near :1578).
Web and Electron: settings dialog sections 'general', 'usage', 'billing' (apps/web/features/settings/lib/web-settings-sections.ts WEB_SETTINGS_CONTENT_SECTIONS).

Web direct addresses /settings/general, /settings/usage, /settings/billing each redirect to /chat?<deep-link query> so the dialog opens on that section (apps/web/app/settings/usage/page.tsx; apps/web/features/settings/components/SettingsModalRedirect.tsx).

Mobile: Settings tab rows 'Usage' and the Subscription row; Settings > General has a 'Models' row (apps/mobile/src/features/settings/index.tsx:639,855; apps/mobile/src/features/settings/general/index.tsx:179).

CLI: usage summary (apps/cli/src/usage_summary.rs) and Cloud model list for the app server (apps/cli/src/app_server/account_cloud.rs:104). Exact command names for model and usage are unknown beyond the registry entries 'model' and 'usage' (apps/cli/src/command_registry.rs:381,588).
VS Code: command 'agi-workforce.showAccountUsage' (apps/extension-vscode/src/core/commandSetup.ts:2185).
Chrome extension: reads the managed usage endpoint (apps/extension/src/features/cloud-bridge/freeTrialClient.ts:116); where the person sees it is unknown.
prerequisites: A signed-in account for the Cloud catalogue, usage and billing. On web the catalogue falls back to the anonymous plan tier when the person cannot be resolved (apps/web/app/api/models/catalogue/route.ts resolveViewer).
Mobile usage needs sign-in and Cloud mode, otherwise it shows a sign-in prompt (apps/mobile/src/features/settings/cloud-usage/index.tsx:947-953).
Overage and top-ups only apply to a managed paid plan (BillingSection.tsx canBuyTopUps).
screens_and_controls: Catalogue: search box (placeholder 'Search models'), developer rail tabs, capability filter chips, listbox 'Models', favourite and 'About <model>' buttons, a back button (ModelCatalogue.tsx:623-712).
Settings > General: select 'Default model' with option 'Last used' plus models; locked models read '<name> · Upgrade to use (<plan>)' (GeneralSection.tsx:386-418).

Settings > Usage: heading 'Usage', card 'Plan usage limits' or, on Free, 'Upgrade for higher capacity' with an 'Upgrade' button; 'Billing history' link; retry button 'Try again'; history granularity and export link (UsageSection.tsx:1224-1330,1174).

journey: Web: open the composer model picker. The page calls GET /api/models/catalogue once and keeps the result (apps/web/features/chat/lib/use-model-catalogue.ts).
Search or filter, then click a model. A selectable model becomes the chat model; a plan-locked model calls onUpgradeRequest (ModelCatalogue.tsx:494).
To set a default: open Settings > General, choose from 'Default model'. Choosing a locked model shows an 'Upgrade to use' link instead of saving (GeneralSection.tsx:401-418).
To check usage: open Settings > Usage. Paid people see windows, credits, monthly spend limit and history. Free people see the Upgrade button (UsageSection.tsx:1441-1451).
To manage the plan: Settings > Billing. 'Manage billing' calls POST /api/portal and hands off to the hosted portal (apps/web/features/billing/services/stripe-payments.ts:162-189).
After a top-up checkout, the return address /settings/billing?topup=success shows a toast, then the dialog opens on Billing (SettingsModalRedirect.tsx).
feedback_and_outputs: Catalogue states: loading / error with retry (status prop), 'Coming soon' tag, 'Upgrade to use · <plan>', temporarily-unavailable marker (ModelCatalogue.tsx:37,319-324,555-577).
Usage: status line, bars with used / allowance / left / reset; stale marker '(refresh failed)' on the last-updated label (UsageSection.tsx:1240-1250).
Billing: toast 'Top-up payment received. Your balance updates after payment confirmation.' or 'Top-up checkout was canceled. No balance was added.' (SettingsModalRedirect.tsx).
Overage error text 'Could not update the setting.' under the switch (BillingSection.tsx:321).
settings: Default model preference, stored through the preference client under a default-model namespace (apps/web/features/chat/lib/default-model-preference.ts:63).
Overage switch, stored as subscriptions.overage_enabled (apps/web/app/api/billing/overage/route.ts:72).
Monthly spend limit via /api/settings/spend-limit and auto-reload via /api/billing/auto-reload (UsageSection.tsx:63-67).
Provider training opt-out narrows the catalogue to no-training models (apps/web/app/api/models/catalogue/route.ts:80-86).

working: Server builds the catalogue from the model registry, the managed route list, route health, plan, event promotion and free promotion, and returns it at GET /api/models/catalogue (apps/web/lib/server/model-catalogue.ts buildCatalogueEntries; apps/web/app/api/models/catalogue/route.ts).

A model with no configured executable route is dropped; a model whose routes are all degraded is returned with temporarilyUnavailable; an announced model is a non-selectable 'Coming soon' row (model-catalogue.ts toCatalogueEntry).
The wire entry removes route, provider and provider label so the client never sees suppliers (route.ts toWireEntry).
Free web usage shows only an Upgrade prompt and no meters (UsageSection.tsx:1224,1279-1328,1441-1451); test holds it (apps/web/features/settings/sections/__tests__/UsageSection.test.tsx:249).
Overage switch updates at once, is blocked while saving, and rolls back on failure (BillingSection.tsx:301-325).
Top-up result toast after checkout return (SettingsModalRedirect.tsx; test SettingsModalRedirect.test.tsx:61,74).
Default model row saves through the preference client and toasts on failure (GeneralSection.tsx:401-406).
Usage endpoints exist: /api/usage, /history, /limits, /limit-resets, /export, /discrepancy (apps/web/app/api/usage/*).
CLI reads /api/usage and history (apps/cli/src/usage_summary.rs:15-17) and validates the Cloud catalogue (apps/cli/src/app_server/account_cloud.rs:104-135).
VS Code reads /api/usage and /api/usage/history (apps/extension-vscode/src/utils/api.ts:1545,1555).
incomplete: Billing is 'partial' on web, desktop and mobile; the brief says the live check with a granted test account, Stripe test checkout and migration 0281 is unverified (brief S4.40 Unfinished).

Mobile billing screen: plan summary and store purchase code exist, but the web portal is off and store purchases are off in this build (apps/mobile/lib/v1FeatureFlags.ts:6; apps/mobile/src/features/billing/storePurchases.json).

Mobile model picker reads '/api/models' for provider availability, not '/api/models/catalogue' (apps/mobile/src/features/model-picker/providerAvailabilityStore.ts:5); whether the two agree is unknown.
disconnected_or_disabled: FEATURES.billing = false on mobile, so the portal target is not offered (apps/mobile/lib/v1FeatureFlags.ts:6; apps/mobile/src/features/settings/cloud-billing/index.tsx:199).
Store purchases switched off: nativePurchases false removes purchase, upgrade, top-up and restore controls (apps/mobile/src/features/billing/storePurchases.json; nativePurchaseAvailability.ts:3).
Mobile billing service throws 'billing: cloud billing not available in v1' (apps/mobile/src/features/billing/service.ts:9).
not_available: Web: the brief cites GeneralSection.tsx:1060 for the default model, but that file has 881 lines; the real code is at GeneralSection.tsx:361 (stale brief reference).
Billing management on CLI, VS Code and Chrome: no billing screen listed by the brief (brief S4.40 lists web, desktop, mobile only).
Per-million prices are deliberately not sent to the client (model-catalogue.ts, comment on priceBand).

established.statement: The catalogue lists models the user can reach with capabilities, context and price, and lets them pick one or set a default.
The usage dashboard shows usage against plan limits per window (session, weekly, credits), reset times and recent history.
Billing settings show current plan, renewal, payment method and invoices, and let the user change or cancel the plan.
Personal settings let the signed-in user view and change profile, appearance, personalization and notification preferences and save them.
Free usage screens show only Upgrade, never meters (owner decision, held by the UsageSection test).
One account and entitlement span the suite; a surface must not invent a separate one.
The overage switch is saved at once and rolled back if saving fails; a top-up result is announced after checkout.
Sales of subscriptions on any surface are held until 2027-01-01 and mobile v1 sells nothing.

acceptance_criteria: A model with no configured route never appears in the web catalogue for any plan.
A model whose every route is degraded appears but cannot be selected and is marked unavailable.
A Free account opening Settings > Usage on web sees an Upgrade button and no usage bars.
Toggling overage when PUT /api/billing/overage fails returns the switch to its previous position and shows an error.
Returning from checkout to /settings/billing?topup=success shows the success toast and the Billing section opens.
Saving a default model persists after reload; a saved default not on the plan is shown as 'Last used' with a hint.
On mobile with store purchases off, no Upgrade, top-up or restore control appears on Usage or Subscription.

Local mode on desktop and mobile should list local models without any account [inferred] from the requirement that local inference is free and from the local catalogue in apps/mobile/src/features/model-picker/service.ts.

steps.what_happens: Browser or Electron window opens the picker; hook calls GET /api/models/catalogue.

Server resolves the viewer plan and training opt-out, builds entries from the registry, managed routes, health signals, free pools and promotions, strips supplier fields and replies with a 15-second private cache.
Choosing a locked model calls the upgrade handler; choosing an admitted model changes the chat model.
Saving the default model writes a preference namespace through the preference client.
Usage page fetches the usage summary, limits, history and limit resets with the session; the server reads the usage ledger.
Billing page fetches payment methods, invoices, credit history and overage; invoice data comes from the billing provider through our API.
Manage billing posts to /api/portal and the browser leaves for the hosted portal (outside service).
Overage switch sends PUT /api/billing/overage; server updates subscriptions.overage_enabled.

data.where_stored: Not stored; computed per request and cached 15 s by the browser
Managed cloud preferences store behind the preference client (table name unknown)

data.synced: yes, read by all apps from /api/billing/overage

data.where_stored: managed usage tables read by /api/usage (names not opened here; managed_usage_requests is used by the developer usage service)

execution_and_data_flow.models_and_providers: The catalogue is generated from the model registry and the managed route list; providers are looked up by managed route and availability signals, and only a count of routes reaches the client (model-catalogue.ts). Which model ids exist is data, not hardcoded here. Local models are not in this server catalogue; mobile keeps a local catalogue (apps/mobile/src/features/model-picker/service.ts:97-106). Own-key models: unknown for this page.

access_and_usage.account: Catalogue works without sign-in at the anonymous plan tier on web (route.ts resolveViewer). Usage and Billing need a signed-in account; mobile shows a sign-in prompt otherwise (cloud-usage/index.tsx:947).
access_and_usage.permissions: Overage PUT needs CSRF and a user-scoped database (overage/route.ts:57-60). Billing rows are user-scoped. Workspace-billed plans are managed by an owner or admin [inferred] from planChangeBlockedCopy for 'manual' source (BillingSection.tsx).
access_and_usage.subscription: Admission uses canAccessModelForSubscriptionTier, event promotions and a free-model promotion (model-catalogue.ts). Free sees the Upgrade prompt. Top-ups need a managed paid plan with stripe, apple or google source (BillingSection.tsx canBuyTopUps).
access_and_usage.limits_and_metering: Usage shows session, weekly, flagship weekly, monthly credit windows and a monthly spend limit (UsageSection.tsx:1204-1228). Catalogue route is rate limited under 'model-catalog' (route.ts:48). Usage route uses 'credits-balance' (apps/web/app/api/usage/route.ts:38).
access_and_usage.flags: Mobile FEATURES.billing=false and nativePurchases=false (v1FeatureFlags.ts:6; storePurchases.json). Web has event and free-model promotions as server config (model-catalogue.ts).

aliases: Workspace admin, developer console and help
features.summary: Three web destinations for people who run or build on AGI Workforce. The workspace console lets an owner or admin manage members, roles, identity, policy, sharing, audit, usage and billing. The developer console manages API keys and shows each key's monthly use. Help and feedback links to help pages and sends feedback with an optional screenshot.

purpose.what_it_does: Web: /workspace pages (Overview, Members, Roles, Identity, Policy, Models, Connectors, Code, MCP servers, Plugins, Sharing, Audit, Data, Usage, Billing) shown only to owners and admins; /developers page with API keys, projects, prompts, request logs, webhooks, rate limits and reference links; Help section in settings, account-menu Get help entries, and a feedback dialog that posts to /api/feedback. Mobile has a Report screen and a Help Center row; CLI and VS Code send feedback.
purpose.why_it_exists: Brief S4.42-S4.44: an admin must manage members, roles, invitations and policies; a developer must create and revoke keys and see use per key; a person must reach help and send feedback from inside the product.
purpose.who_uses_it: Workspace owners and admins (console); developers on a plan that includes the managed API (keys); any signed-in person (help and feedback).
problems_solved: Admins cannot control who has access and what they may use.
Developers cannot see which key spends credits (apps/web/lib/services/developer-usage-service.ts).
People cannot report a bug or send a screenshot without leaving the app (ComposerFeedbackDialog.tsx).
use_cases: An admin opens /workspace/people to invite a member with a role (TeamSection.tsx:1017-1024).
A developer creates an API key, then reads 'This month: N requests, X credits' under it (ApiKeys.tsx:77-86).
A person opens Account menu > Get help to reach help and support (AccountMenuItems.tsx:82-100).
A person sends 'Something is broken' feedback with a screenshot (ComposerFeedbackDialog.tsx:22-25,166-195).

established.statement: A workspace administration destination lets an admin manage members, roles, invitations, policies and workspace settings.
A developer console lets the user create and revoke API keys, see API usage per key, read API docs and try requests.
A help-and-feedback destination links to help, docs and status and lets the user send feedback or a bug report.
Feedback needs text and is blocked while sending or while a screenshot is captured.
API usage is counted per key for the current month; admin pages require workspace admin rights.
An action a user cannot undo asks first and names the consequence.

acceptance_criteria: A member with role 'member' opening /workspace sees 'You do not administer this workspace' and the role name.
A person with no workspace sees 'No workspace selected' with a Team settings link.
A database fault while reading membership shows the 'temporarily unavailable' frame with Retry.
A plan without managed API gets 403 code managed_api_plan_required when creating a key.
The 21st active key is refused with the 20-key message.
Each key shows request count and credits for the current UTC month, or 'No requests this month'.
The Send feedback button stays disabled with empty or whitespace text, and while sending or capturing.
A screenshot over 4 MiB or a non PNG/JPEG/WebP file is refused with a message.

Desktop should offer the same console as web because it shows the hosted app [inferred].

steps.what_happens: Browser requests /workspace; server layout reads session, terms, age, account status and organization membership.
Shell decides frame by role; admin pages call their own APIs which re-check rights.
Member changes go to /api/settings/team routes; seat payment may open an outside payment page.
Developer page loads keys and GET /api/developers/usage; server sums settled requests per key for the UTC month.
Creating a key checks CSRF, step-up, plan capability and the 20-key cap, then inserts a key.
Feedback dialog reads a CSRF token and POSTs /api/feedback with metadata (source web, path, version) and an optional data-URL screenshot.
Server inserts a feedback row and puts the screenshot in private object storage; if storage is missing the screenshot is dropped and screenshot_stored is false.

features.summary: The frame around every screen. It decides, by window width, whether navigation sits beside the content, shrinks to an icon rail, or hides behind a drawer opened from a header button. Web and Desktop share one shell. Mobile uses a native drawer. Sidebar resizing and a bottom tab bar do not exist.

purpose.what_it_does: Chooses one of three navigation layouts from the window size and orientation, lets the person collapse and expand the sidebar, opens a slide-in drawer on narrow screens, and shows a thin header on phones. On Web and Desktop this is resolveShellLayout plus WebAppShell and the shared Sidebar. On Mobile it is the Expo drawer with swipe gestures and a hidden tab bar. (apps/web/shared/components/layout/app-shell-layout.ts:5-39) (apps/mobile/src/features/shell/drawerGestures.ts:27-48)
purpose.why_it_exists: Navigation needs 260px to be useful, which does not fit a phone or a portrait tablet. The shell keeps the content readable at every width and keeps the person's collapse choice. [inferred] from the comment in (apps/web/shared/components/layout/app-shell-layout.ts:26-28).
purpose.who_uses_it: Every signed-in person on Web, Desktop and Mobile. CLI, VS Code and Chrome have their own panels and were not traced for this feature.
problems_solved: A phone screen cannot hold a sidebar and a chat column side by side, so the sidebar becomes a drawer.
A tablet in portrait gets an icon rail so the chat column stays readable.
A returning person keeps the sidebar collapsed or expanded as they left it.
Keyboard and screen-reader users cannot tab into the page behind an open drawer (the page is made inert).
use_cases: On a laptop, press Ctrl/Cmd+B to hide the sidebar and give the chat more room.
On a phone browser, tap Open navigation, pick a chat, and the drawer closes by itself.
On a tablet in portrait, keep the icon rail and tap Toggle sidebar to open the full list over the content.
On the phone app, swipe from the left edge to open the drawer.

where_to_find_it: Web and Desktop (Electron window showing the hosted web app): the sidebar on the left; button labelled 'Toggle sidebar' (PanelLeft icon) at the top of the sidebar; on a narrow window a 48px header with a button labelled 'Open navigation' (Menu icon) at its left. (packages/ui/ui/src/sidebar/Sidebar.tsx:578) (apps/web/shared/components/layout/WebAppShell.tsx:641-653) (doc: AGENTS.md section 5 says the public Desktop shows the hosted web app)

CLI, VS Code, Chrome: not traced (unknown).
prerequisites: Web and Desktop: the shell renders for signed-in routes; recents load only after sign-in settles. (apps/web/shared/components/layout/WebAppShell.tsx:244 comment)

screens_and_controls: Sidebar, expanded: default width 260px, 'Toggle sidebar' button with tooltip showing the shortcut (Ctrl+B or the Command key plus B). (packages/ui/ui/src/sidebar/Sidebar.tsx:159, 133-145)
Sidebar, collapsed rail: 52px wide, icon-only buttons (Toggle sidebar, New chat, Code, Search, nav items) with tooltips, plus an account button. (packages/ui/ui/src/sidebar/Sidebar.tsx:115, 485-541)
Narrow header: 'Open navigation' button, the wordmark, and an optional slot a page can fill. (apps/web/shared/components/layout/WebAppShell.tsx:641-663)
Phone drawer on web: a left sheet 280px wide, at most 85% of the viewport, with a hidden title 'Navigation'. (apps/web/shared/components/layout/WebAppShell.tsx:683-720)
Mobile drawer: front drawer on phones; a permanent 280px sidebar when the window is at least 1000 points wide. (apps/mobile/src/shared/hooks/useResponsiveLayout.ts:3-28)
journey: Open the app. On first paint the shell assumes a desktop-sized window, then measures the real window and switches layout. (apps/web/shared/components/layout/app-shell-layout.ts:42-46, 55-71)

Wide window (1024px or more) or a landscape tablet (768px to 1023px): the sidebar sits beside the content. Click 'Toggle sidebar' or press Ctrl/Cmd+B to collapse it to the rail or expand it. (apps/web/shared/components/layout/WebAppShell.tsx:442-453)
Tablet in portrait: the sidebar stays a rail; the toggle and Ctrl/Cmd+B open the full sidebar as a drawer over the content. (apps/web/shared/components/layout/WebAppShell.tsx:626-632)

Under 768px: tap 'Open navigation'. The drawer slides in, the page behind it is inert. Close it with Escape, by tapping outside, by choosing something, or by navigating. (apps/web/shared/components/layout/WebAppShell.tsx:166-171, 639; apps/web/shared/components/layout/WebAppShell.test.tsx:776-880)
Mobile: swipe from the left edge or tap the menu button; the drawer closes when a destination is chosen. (apps/mobile/src/features/drawer/components/DrawerContent.tsx:409-420)
Resize or rotate: the shell re-flows and restores the content scroll position. (apps/web/shared/components/layout/WebAppShell.tsx:204-222)

working: Three-tier layout resolver with 768px and 1024px breakpoints; compact gives a drawer, tablet portrait gives a rail, tablet landscape and regular give a persistent sidebar. (apps/web/shared/components/layout/app-shell-layout.ts:5-39)
Collapse and expand through the toggle button and Ctrl/Cmd+B; on non-persistent layouts both toggle the drawer instead. (apps/web/shared/components/layout/WebAppShell.tsx:442-453, 463)

Collapsed choice is saved and restored on the web; widening the window restores it because it is stored apart from the layout tier. (apps/web/shared/stores/layout-store.ts:113-115) (apps/web/shared/components/layout/WebAppShell.tsx:190-195)

Drawer 280px wide, closes on Escape unless a row menu claims the key, closes on route change, page behind it is inert and aria-hidden. (apps/web/shared/components/layout/WebAppShell.tsx:168-170, 636-639, 690-694)
The web chat page runs its own copy of this layout: in a tablet with a side panel open the sidebar drops to a rail. (apps/web/features/chat/pages/web-chat-layout.ts:36-43)
Desktop menu command 'toggle-sidebar' flips the same store. (apps/web/features/desktop-host/hooks/use-host-commands.ts:26-31)

incomplete: Mobile's permanent-sidebar threshold is 1000 points (280 plus 720), not the web's 768 and 1024 tiers, so the two surfaces differ on a tablet between 768 and 999. (apps/mobile/src/shared/hooks/useResponsiveLayout.ts:3-24)

Chrome, VS Code and CLI layouts: the brief marks them built, but its line references do not match current code and nothing was traced here. (doc: knowledge-base/data/area-briefs/005-application-shell-and-navigation-components.md S5.01)
disconnected_or_disabled: Mobile tab bar: the Tabs layout renders no bar (tabBar returns null, style display none) while still declaring chat and projects tabs, so it is switched off on purpose. (apps/mobile/app/(app)/(tabs)/_layout.tsx:9-17)

The Sidebar accepts a mode prop of local or cloud; Sidebar() does not read it, and the web shells pass 'cloud'. [inferred] from the destructured props at (packages/ui/ui/src/sidebar/Sidebar.tsx:146-205) and (apps/web/shared/components/layout/WebAppShell.tsx:573)

Bottom navigation bar: not built on Web or Mobile. (doc: brief S5.36) (apps/mobile/app/(app)/(tabs)/_layout.tsx:9)

established.statement: Sidebar can be collapsed to a rail or hidden and expanded again.
A drag handle resizes the sidebar and the width persists.
On narrow screens navigation lives in a slide-in drawer opened from a header button, with focus management and dismissal.
On phones a persistent bottom navigation bar switches between main areas.
On tablet widths navigation and content sit side by side (persistent or rail) instead of a phone drawer.
A persistent top header shows where the user is and the primary actions.

acceptance_criteria: At 1280px wide the sidebar is beside the content; Ctrl/Cmd+B collapses it to a 52px rail and again expands it; after a reload the choice is kept.
At 390px wide there is no persistent sidebar; 'Open navigation' opens a 280px drawer; Escape, a tap outside, or choosing a chat closes it and focus returns to the button.
With the drawer open, Tab does not reach the page behind it.
At 834x1112 (portrait tablet) the sidebar is a rail; the toggle opens the drawer; at 1180x820 it is persistent.
Widening the window from phone to desktop restores the person's collapse choice.
On the phone app a left-edge swipe opens the drawer and choosing a chat closes it.
Rotating a tablet keeps the chat scroll position.
inferred: Resize and bottom bar are listed as requirements by the brief but also look like deliberate choices (the bar is explicitly switched off); whether they are still wanted is a product decision. [inferred]
proposed: [proposed] Decide product-wise whether sidebar resize and a bottom bar are required; if not, remove S5.06 and S5.36 from the brief.
[proposed] Align Mobile's persistent-drawer threshold with the web tiers, or document why they differ.
[proposed] Move WebAppShell's and WebChatPage's duplicate drawer wiring into one component.

steps.what_happens: Browser or Electron window loads the shell; first paint assumes a desktop layout.
useShellLayout reads window width and height and re-reads on resize and orientationchange; sets tier, orientation and sidebar mode.
Toggle click or Ctrl/Cmd+B calls handleToggleSidebar: flips the stored collapsed flag on persistent layouts, otherwise opens or closes the drawer.
The stored flag is saved by zustand persist under agi-ui-store; on Desktop it is also sent to the window-state commands.
Mobile: the Expo drawer opens on edge swipe or the menu button; layout class is computed from window size.

features.summary: Controls that move the person between product areas and scopes. Web has a Home and Code switch and a workspace sub-menu (Personal or Enterprise). Mobile has a Local and Cloud toggle in the drawer, a workspace list in Settings, and a Switch account screen when sign-in allows several accounts. CLI, VS Code and Chrome have none found.

purpose.what_it_does: Lets the person change area (Chat or Code on Web and Desktop; Local or Cloud on Mobile), change which workspace owns their chats (Personal or an organisation), and on Mobile change which signed-in account is active. (packages/ui/ui/src/sidebar/Sidebar.tsx:612-641) (apps/web/features/workspaces/components/WorkspaceMenuItems.tsx:114-215) (apps/mobile/src/features/accounts/useDeviceAccounts.ts:118-141)
purpose.why_it_exists: Work and personal content must stay apart. The web menu says personal and enterprise scope differ in who can read content. (apps/web/features/workspaces/components/WorkspaceMenuItems.tsx:78-82)
purpose.who_uses_it: People with a team or enterprise workspace; people using both Chat and Code; Mobile users who run Local and Cloud or hold more than one account.
problems_solved: Pasting company text into a personal chat by mistake.
Reaching the Code area without leaving the sidebar.
Moving between Local on-device chat and Cloud chat on the phone.
Changing account without signing out (Mobile).
use_cases: A consultant switches from Personal to a client's Enterprise workspace before opening chats.
A developer clicks Code in the sidebar to open the Code surface.
A phone user taps Cloud in the drawer to leave on-device chat.
A phone user opens Settings, Switch account, and taps the other account.

steps.what_happens: Person picks a workspace; the hook checks interruptions and may show the confirm panel.
The web sends a PUT with the workspace id (or the personal selector) to the managed workspaces path.
The web re-reads the workspace list and finalizes the switch, clearing scoped caches, then the app reloads in the new scope.
On an error the hook re-reads the list; if the outcome cannot be proven it keeps admission closed and asks for a reload.
Mobile workspace: PUT /api/settings/organization/active, then loads conversations again.
Mobile account: asks the sign-in provider (Clerk) to switch the session, waits until the new account is adopted.
Mobile Local and Cloud toggle changes the app mode on the device; a Cloud switch for a signed-out person goes to sign-in.

features.summary: One-step access to search and to a fresh chat from anywhere in the shell. The sidebar has a Search button (Ctrl/Cmd+Shift+F) that opens a search dialog and a New chat button (Shift+Ctrl/Cmd+O). Mobile puts a search icon and a New chat row in the drawer. CLI, VS Code and Chrome have their own equivalents.

purpose.what_it_does: Opens the global search dialog and starts a new conversation from the sidebar, the rail, the keyboard or the native menu. (packages/ui/ui/src/sidebar/Sidebar.tsx:597-640) (apps/web/shared/components/layout/WebAppShell.tsx:302-320)
purpose.why_it_exists: Finding an old chat and starting a new one are the two most frequent navigation actions. The search shortcut avoids the command palette key. (packages/ui/ui/src/sidebar/searchShortcut.ts:1-2)
purpose.who_uses_it: Everyone who keeps many chats.
problems_solved: Scrolling a long list to find a chat.
Starting new work without hunting for a button.
Keyboard users reaching both actions without a mouse.
use_cases: Press Ctrl/Cmd+Shift+F, type a few words, open the matching chat.
Press Shift+Ctrl/Cmd+O to start a new chat while reading another.
On the phone, tap the search icon at the top of the drawer.
In the Chrome side panel, search recent chats once there are more than ten.

features.summary: One row in the sidebar for each chat or task. It shows the title, which row is open, whether it is a Work task, whether a reply is running, whether it needs the person, and whether it was marked unread. On Web the unread mark is set by hand and stored in the browser; on Mobile it clears when the chat is opened.

purpose.what_it_does: Draws each conversation with state markers and opens it on click or tap. (packages/ui/ui/src/sidebar/SessionItem.tsx:125-200)
purpose.why_it_exists: People run several chats and tasks at once and need to see which one is running, which is waiting for them, and which they have not read.
purpose.who_uses_it: Everyone with more than one chat; people who start long Work tasks.
problems_solved: Missing a task that waits for approval.
Losing track of a running reply in another chat.
Telling a task from a chat (colour alone is not enough, the accessible name says 'Work').
use_cases: Start a task, switch chats, see a pulsing dot on the task row.
See a warning dot where the agent needs approval.
Mark a chat as unread to come back to it.
Ctrl-click a row to open it in a new tab.

features.summary: Lets a person step back and forward through screens, open a shared link to a chat, file, artifact, Work session, research report, schedule or browser task, and see a clear screen when something is loading or cannot be opened. Web relies on the browser; desktop adds menu and title-strip controls; mobile has a go-back hook. Breadcrumbs are not built.

purpose.what_it_does: Moves through screen history, resolves a stable /open/<target>/<id> link to the right screen in AGI Workforce Web (and the Desktop window that shows it), and shows loading, not-found or unavailable screens when a link or route cannot be shown. Mobile has its own back hook and a 404 screen. VS Code can copy a link to a session.
purpose.why_it_exists: People share links to work and expect them to open the right item, or explain why not. They also expect Back and Forward to behave. The brief asks for stable resource links (S5.38), back and forward (S5.25), breadcrumbs (S5.24) and loading or unavailable screens (S5.39).
purpose.who_uses_it: Any signed-in person using Web, Desktop or Mobile; people who receive a link from a notification, a teammate or another app; VS Code users who copy a session link.
problems_solved: A link to a deleted, expired or someone else's item gives a clear reason instead of a blank page.
A signed-out person is sent to sign in and returned to the link afterwards.
A phone screen opened from a link with no history still has a way back.
use_cases: Click a notification that points at a chat: it opens /open/chat/<id>, which redirects to the chat.
Open a link to a schedule that has ended: the page says it has ended and offers Open Scheduled.
On desktop (macOS) press the Back control beside the window buttons to return to the previous screen.
On a phone, open a screen from a link with no history and tap the header back: it goes to the fallback screen.

screens_and_controls: Link-unavailable screen: heading, explanation, and one button whose label depends on the target: 'Back to chats', 'Open Library', 'Open Work history', 'Open Scheduled' (apps/web/features/notifications/components/ProductLinkUnavailable.tsx:15-23).

journey: 1. Someone follows a link of the form /open/<target>/<id>.
2. The server checks the target and id shape; a bad one shows the not-found page (page.tsx:23).
3. If not signed in, the person goes to /login with a return address and comes back after sign in (page.tsx:27-29).
4. The server looks the item up for this person and workspace (product-link-resolver.ts:186-209).
5. If ready, the browser is redirected to the real screen (page.tsx:39).
6. Otherwise the app shell shows the unavailable screen with a way back (page.tsx:41-45).
