features.summary: A keyboard-opened box where a person types to find and run commands or jump to chats and screens, plus a Keyboard shortcuts help dialog. Web and Desktop share one palette (Cmd/Ctrl+K). CLI has a slash-command popup, VS Code uses its own command palette, Chrome has its own side-panel palette. Mobile has neither.

purpose.what_it_does: Searches app actions, chats, preferences and model choices from one text box and runs the chosen one. A separate dialog lists the keyboard shortcuts.
purpose.why_it_exists: Keyboard users and power users reach any command without hunting through menus. The brief asks for a keyboard-invoked palette (S5.26) and a shortcut help view reachable from the app (S5.27).
purpose.who_uses_it: Keyboard-first users on Web, Desktop, CLI, VS Code and Chrome.
problems_solved: Finding a screen or action without remembering where it lives.
Learning which shortcuts exist.
Switching model or theme quickly.
use_cases: Press Cmd+K, type 'settings', press Enter to open Settings.
Press Cmd+K, type a chat title to jump to it.
Open Account menu > Get help > Keyboard shortcuts to read the list.
In the CLI type / to filter slash commands and press Enter to run one.

where_to_find_it: Web and Desktop: press Cmd+K or Ctrl+K anywhere (apps/web/shared/components/CommandPalette/CommandPaletteProvider.tsx:17-29). Its search box placeholder reads 'Search chats and actions' (CommandPalette.tsx:506).

Web and Desktop help: Account menu > 'Get help' > 'Keyboard shortcuts', which shows the '/' shortcut hint (apps/web/shared/components/layout/AccountMenuItems.tsx:80-93). Desktop also has a host command 'show-keyboard-shortcuts' (packages/contracts/local-runtime/src/host-bridge.ts:90).

CLI: slash-command popup titled 'Commands', hint 'Type to filter   ↑↓ navigate   Enter select   Esc cancel' (apps/cli/src/tui/widgets/command_popup.rs:12-14); keybindings include an OpenPalette action (apps/cli/src/keybindings.rs:13-31).
Chrome extension: side-panel palette opened with Cmd/Ctrl+K (apps/extension/src/side_panel.ts:13634-13642).

VS Code: its own Command Palette lists the extension's commands (apps/extension-vscode/package.json contributes commands; line citations in the brief were not matched). A 'Keyboard shortcuts' item in the Help menu opens VS Code's keybindings screen (apps/extension-vscode/src/features/help/helpMenu.ts:25-29).
Mobile: not listed in the brief for either item; none opened.
prerequisites: Web and Desktop: the shell is mounted (palette is mounted once from apps/web/app/AppRuntimeMounts.tsx:17).
Some palette entries depend on workspace policy and sign-in (CommandPalette.tsx imports useDisabledWorkspaceFeatures and useSession).
screens_and_controls: Palette dialog with search box, groups such as 'Quick actions', 'Preferences', 'Recents', 'Actions', 'Search results' and a model submenu with 'Filter models…' (CommandPalette.tsx:129-284, 506).

features.summary: A bell in the Web and Desktop sidebar opens a list of account notifications with an unread count, per-item open and mark-read, and Mark all as read. Mobile has a Notifications screen that merges account and on-device items. CLI, VS Code and Chrome have none.

purpose.what_it_does: Lists the person's account notifications, shows how many are unread (capped at 9+), opens the linked screen and marks items read.
purpose.why_it_exists: Long runs, reports and approvals finish when the person is away; the center tells them what needs attention (S5.28).
purpose.who_uses_it: Signed-in people on Web, Desktop and Mobile.
problems_solved: Missing that a run finished or needs input.
Having to search for the item a notice refers to.
use_cases: See '3' on the bell, open it, click a finished report to go to it.
Click Mark all as read to clear the count.
On a phone, open Notifications to see account items and device alerts together.

where_to_find_it: Web and Desktop: bell button in the sidebar brand row, label 'Notifications' or 'Notifications, N unread' (apps/web/features/notifications/components/NotificationBell.tsx:36-39; apps/web/shared/components/layout/SidebarBrandRow.tsx).
Mobile: screen at apps/mobile/app/(app)/notifications/index.tsx, opened from the drawer (DrawerContent.tsx:560 per brief; not opened).
CLI, VS Code, Chrome: none (brief).
prerequisites: Signed in; signed-out people see no bell (NotificationBell.tsx:101-105).
Mobile account items need the cloud unlock flag from the waitlist store (notifications/index.tsx:219-220).
screens_and_controls: Popover titled 'Notifications'.
Button 'Mark all as read' shown only when there are unread items (NotificationBell.tsx:171-181).
Rows with title, up to two lines of message, relative time and an unread dot; error items show an alert icon.
Error view 'Notifications could not be loaded.' with 'Try again'.
Empty view 'When a run finishes, a report is ready or something needs you, it shows up here.'
Mobile: back button 'Go back', 'Mark all as read', 'Clear notifications on this device', per-row 'Mark as read'.
journey: 1. Click the bell; the feed refreshes.
2. Read the list (newest first from the server).
3. Click an item: it is marked read and, if it has a link, the popover closes and the app goes there.
4. Or click 'Mark all as read'.
5. Close the popover.
feedback_and_outputs: Badge number, or '9+' above 9 (NotificationBell.tsx:13, 117-118).
Red text 'Those notifications could not be marked as read. Try again.' when mark-all fails (NotificationBell.tsx:184-188).
settings: Browser push opt-in is a separate component (WebPushOptIn, mounted in AppRuntimeMounts.tsx:24); its settings were not read.

Optimistic mark read and mark all read with rollback on failure (use-notification-feed.ts:90-125).
GET and PATCH /api/notifications with rate limit, CSRF on PATCH, and user-scoped database (apps/web/app/api/notifications/route.ts:34-100).
Mobile screen merges account and device items, mark-all calls both (notifications/index.tsx:260-263).
incomplete: Individual mark-read failures are swallowed with no message (use-notification-feed.ts:90-98 catch returns undefined).

not_available: CLI, VS Code and Chrome (brief S5.28 status missing).

established.statement: A notification center lists account notifications, shows an unread count, and lets the user open and mark them read.

acceptance_criteria: Signed-out Web shows no bell.
Unread count shows 1-9 as a number and 10 or more as '9+'.
Opening the popover triggers a fresh fetch.
Clicking an item with a link marks it read and navigates.

A failed load shows 'Notifications could not be loaded.' and Try again works.
Empty feed shows the empty text.

features.summary: The Account menu in the Web and Desktop sidebar shows the signed-in email and offers Workspace, Settings, Get help (help, email support, feedback, shortcuts), Upgrade, Learn more and Log out. Upgrade shows only if a higher plan exists, and paid checkout is held behind a billing waitlist unless opened. Mobile uses a Profile page and an About page.

purpose.what_it_does: Gathers who-am-I, account actions, help and the way to a higher plan into one menu.
purpose.why_it_exists: People need a predictable place for settings, support, legal links, sign-out and upgrading (S5.29, S5.30, S5.31).
purpose.who_uses_it: Signed-in people on every app; free people who may upgrade.
problems_solved: Finding help, support and feedback.
Reaching legal and data-rights links after sign in.
Starting an upgrade.
use_cases: Open Account menu > Get help > Send feedback.
Open Account menu > Upgrade to see plans, then join the waitlist or pay.
On a phone, open Profile and tap Log Out.
Open Learn more > Terms and policies.

where_to_find_it: Web and Desktop: account button in the sidebar footer, and a compact trigger in the collapsed rail (apps/web/shared/components/layout/WebAppShell.tsx:507-557; AccountMenuItems.tsx).

Mobile: Profile page (apps/mobile/app/(app)/profile/index.tsx) with rows Chats, Messages, Personalization, Memory, Safety & Security, Data Controls, Subscription, Log Out; About page with Support rows 'Help Center' and 'Service Status' (apps/mobile/app/(app)/about.tsx:257-278).

CLI, VS Code, Chrome: brief says done; VS Code help menu has Documentation, Help center, Keyboard shortcuts, Service status, What’s new, Send feedback (apps/extension-vscode/src/features/help/helpMenu.ts:19-40); VS Code and Chrome show an 'Upgrade' button in the usage banner (extension-vscode webviewContent.ts:3150; Chrome upgrade labels side_panel.ts:736-748). CLI details not opened.
prerequisites: Signed in.
Upgrade: a plan with a higher tier available (hasSelfServeUpgradePath, packages/contracts/types/src/billing-catalog.ts:137-139).
screens_and_controls: Menu order: email label, 'Workspace' submenu, 'Settings', 'Get help' submenu ('Get help', 'Email support', 'Send feedback', 'Keyboard shortcuts'), 'Upgrade' (when shown), 'Learn more' submenu (Data use, Data rights, Terms and policies via translation keys navDataUse, navDataRights, navTermsPolicies), 'Log out' (AccountMenuItems.tsx:57-150; labels from packages/ui/i18n/locales/en/common.json:16,89-113).
Upgrade opens a plan dialog, then either checkout, a confirm dialog for mid-cycle upgrades, or a waitlist dialog (apps/web/features/billing/hooks/useUpgradePlanFlow.ts:60-120).
Mobile paywall bottom sheet (apps/mobile/src/features/chat/components/PaywallBottomSheet.tsx, not opened).
journey: 1. Click the account button.
2. Choose an entry.
3. For Upgrade: pick a plan; if you have an active paid plan, confirm the prorated charge; otherwise start checkout, or join the waitlist or enter an access code.
4. For Log out: signed out and sent to /login.

features.summary: Shows when the device is offline or sync is syncing, queued or failing, and tells Desktop users a new release is ready. Web shows a status bar with Retry on error. Mobile shows an offline banner. CLI shows a connection line in /status. VS Code and Chrome have connection items. Release notices exist on Desktop and CLI only.

purpose.what_it_does: Displays network and sync state, offers Retry when sync fails, and announces a downloaded or available app update.
purpose.why_it_exists: People need to know why a change has not saved and when to update (S5.32, S5.33, S5.34).
purpose.who_uses_it: Everyone on Web, Desktop and Mobile; CLI users running /status.
problems_solved: Wondering whether work is saved while offline.
Not knowing queued changes exist.
Missing a desktop update.
use_cases: Lose Wi-Fi on Web: a bar shows offline, with 'N pending' when changes are queued.
Sync fails: bar shows error and Retry.
Desktop downloads an update: the update row tells the person.
CLI /status shows whether AGI Cloud is reachable.

where_to_find_it: Web and Desktop: status bar at the top centre of the page, label 'Network status indicator' (apps/web/shared/components/OfflineIndicator.tsx:124-134), mounted from apps/web/app/AppRuntimeMounts.tsx:22.

Desktop: menu entry 'Check for Updates…' (apps/desktop/electron/appMenu.ts:136, 574 non-mac) and an update notice and row in the web UI (apps/web/features/desktop-host/components/DesktopUpdateNotice.tsx, DesktopUpdateRow.tsx).

Mobile: banner at the top: 'You're offline. Local chats still work on this device.' (apps/mobile/src/features/edge-cases/components/copy.ts:21; OfflineBanner mounted in apps/mobile/app/_layout.tsx:1006).
CLI: '/status' prints a connectivity line (apps/cli/src/repl/slash_commands.rs:283-286; apps/cli/src/cloud/client.rs:1143).
VS Code and Chrome: brief says connection done, offline missing; not verified here.
prerequisites: Web: nothing; the manager starts on mount.
Desktop update notice: a Desktop shell exposing the update bridge.
screens_and_controls: Bar with icon, message, optional error text, 'Last synced: <time>' when online, a 'Retry' button (error only), '<N> pending' and 'Syncing…' chips.
Mobile banner: icon and text only, no button.
journey: 1. Network drops; the bar appears with the offline message.
2. Changes made offline are queued; the bar shows 'N pending'.
3. Network returns; sync runs and shows 'Syncing…'.
4. If sync fails, error message and Retry appear; click Retry.
5. When all is synced the bar disappears.
feedback_and_outputs: Message text from the sync manager: 'Sync failed - will retry' for error (packages/client/client-runtime/src/offline-sync/index.ts:262) and others for online, offline and syncing.
Error detail 'Sync did not finish. Retry when you are online.' as fallback (OfflineIndicator.tsx:150).
settings: Desktop update check runs about once a day and a dismissed version is remembered (DesktopUpdateNotice.tsx:8-10).
Sync retry timing is set by retryBaseMs and retryMaxMs defaults in the sync manager (offline-sync/index.ts:78-79).

working: Web indicator with visibility rule: always, offline, queued, syncing or error (OfflineIndicator.tsx:60-67).
role=status and aria-live polite (OfflineIndicator.tsx:132-134).
Retry button only in the error state (OfflineIndicator.tsx:176-188).
Sync manager with exponential retry and queue count (packages/client/client-runtime/src/offline-sync/index.ts:123-151).
Desktop update-ready event pushed to the page, with a pending-update query on subscribe (apps/desktop/electron/preload.ts:121-141; main.ts:626, 2455).
Mobile OfflineBanner uses network status and announces politely (OfflineBanner.tsx:9-27).
CLI connectivity line, which says AGI Cloud is not used when the session is not managed (apps/cli/src/cloud/client.rs:1143-1146).
incomplete: When offline and not in error, no reconnect button is shown, which does not meet the brief's 'offers reconnect' (doc: brief S5.32; code OfflineIndicator.tsx:176).
Mobile banner has no retry (OfflineBanner.tsx).
disconnected_or_disabled: none found
not_available: Release indicator on Web and Mobile (brief S5.34).
Offline indicator on CLI, VS Code, Chrome (brief S5.33).

established.statement: A status indicator shows whether the app is connected to its backend/runtime and offers reconnect when not.
When the device loses network, a visible offline indicator appears and clears when back online.
The app tells the user when a new release is available (or just installed) and how to get it.

acceptance_criteria: Going offline on Web shows the bar within a moment and it carries role=status.
Queued changes show '<N> pending'.
Coming online clears the bar once synced.
Sync error shows Retry; clicking it starts a sync.
Mobile airplane mode shows the banner and returning online removes it.
Desktop with a downloaded update shows the update notice with the version.
CLI /status shows a connectivity line.
inferred: An offline bar with a Reconnect action would meet S5.32 better [inferred].
proposed: [proposed] Add a Reconnect button when offline.
[proposed] Add a release notice on Web (new deploy) and Mobile (store update).

features.summary: Every AGI Workforce app paints its page, panels, text, borders, accent and status colours from named role tokens, separately for light and dark. People pick Light, Dark or System, and on web and mobile also an accent colour. VS Code follows the editor's own colours.

purpose.what_it_does: Defines colour once as named roles (page, subtle and elevated surface, primary, secondary, muted text, borders, accent fill, text and on-fill, and success, warning, danger, info) with separate light and dark values, and lets each app switch between them. Web foundation roles live in packages/ui/design-tokens/src/foundation.css (:181 surface-page, :185 text-primary, :193 rule-strong, :210 accent-text, :215-:227 status text) with a separate .dark block (:433).
purpose.why_it_exists: So components never hold their own colour literals, text stays readable (the file states each pair is asserted at 4.5:1 or better against every surface it can land on) and a theme or accent change reaches the whole app at once (doc: packages/ui/design-tokens/src/foundation.css header comment, lines 1-16). The owner decision of 2026-11-19 lists Theme, Accent colour and Contrast as required Appearance settings (doc: docs/product/requirements.md, section on Appearance settings).
purpose.who_uses_it: Anyone who wants a light or dark app, a calmer accent or higher contrast; engineers who build UI from tokens; testers who check contrast.
problems_solved: White flash or wrong theme for people who use a dark OS
Unreadable status text on a coloured background
Each app drifting to its own colours
A theme choice that dies when the app restarts
use_cases: A person on web switches Theme from System to Dark in Settings > Appearance and the page repaints at once.
A person on mobile picks Violet in Settings > Accent Color.
A CLI user runs /theme high-contrast-dark on a dim terminal.
A Chrome extension user forces Light in Options > Appearance while the OS is dark.

Accent colour on mobile is ignored while the OS high-contrast setting is on (apps/mobile/src/ui/theme/useTheme.ts, resolve step: accent is null when isHighContrast).

I found no call from the mobile src or stores folders to /api/settings/preferences, so these choices stay on the device [inferred from a search that returned nothing].

established.statement: Surfaces paint page and panel backgrounds from named semantic tokens per theme, not component literals.
Raised surfaces (cards, menus, popovers, dialogs) use an elevated-surface token distinct from the page ground in each theme.
Primary and muted text use tokens meeting 4.5:1 on every surface they land on, without opacity dilution.
Borders and dividers use named subtle and strong tokens per theme.
Accent and selection have separate fill, text and on-fill roles that each meet contrast.
Success, warning, error and info each have text and fill roles; status text meets 4.5:1 in both themes.
Appearance settings are their own page and include Theme, Accent colour and Contrast.

acceptance_criteria: Switching Theme to Light, Dark or System repaints the whole page without reload on web.
After reload, the chosen theme and accent are still applied on web, mobile, CLI and Chrome.
An invalid stored web theme value resolves to Dark (ThemeConstants.ts:9,13); a missing one resolves to System.
Every status text token reads at 4.5:1 or better on its surfaces in both themes (checked by apps/web/shared/components/__tests__/theme-contrast.test.ts).
With Contrast set to High on web, muted text, borders and the focus ring are visibly stronger in both themes.
In light theme, a dialog or card is visibly distinct from the page behind it.
On desktop, switching the web theme changes native dialog appearance to match.
inferred: A disabled control may dim with opacity, but running text should not [inferred from S6.03 and Button.tsx:9 using disabled:opacity-50].
Mobile accent should apply identically in Local and Cloud modes unless the person chose otherwise [inferred from separate stores].
proposed: [proposed] Give light chat surface-elevated a value different from surface-base, or drop the chat alias and use --surface-elevated.
[proposed] Add a Contrast control to mobile Appearance and a visible Accent control to Chrome and CLI, or record that they are intentionally absent.
[proposed] Make Dialog and AlertDialog draw from the elevated surface token.

steps.what_happens: Person picks a theme in web Settings > Appearance; next-themes sets the class on the page and stores the key 'theme'.
The .dark block swaps every semantic role at once.
When signed in, CloudSettingsSync sends the appearance namespace after a short delay via PUT /api/settings/preferences, stored in user_settings.
On desktop the page's theme attribute is observed and sent over IPC; the main process sets the native theme and saves it.
On mobile, the screen writes themeMode or accentColor to the store for the current app mode; useTheme recomputes colours.
On CLI, set_active_theme changes the palette and the choice is written to the project settings file.

purpose.why_it_exists: Replies are the main thing people read. Even gaps and padding make long answers scannable and stop code and tables from looking cramped.

features.summary: Spaces the conversation: a steady gap between turns, the action toolbar right under a message, padding inside the composer, and page-edge gutters of 16, 24 and 32 pixels that grow with window width. On phones the composer clears the home indicator.

purpose.what_it_does: Web turns sit in .message-row with 6px vertical padding (apps/web/app/globals.css:828-830); the inner column is max-w-3xl with a 16px gutter (:843); the toolbar row has a minimum height and 32px buttons on mouse or 44px on touch (apps/web/features/chat/components/messages/messageActionRow.ts:1-5); the composer adds the iOS safe-area inset (globals.css:1362-1366); list pages use gutters of 16, 24 and 32px at sm and lg widths (apps/web/app/chat/library/page.tsx:11).
purpose.why_it_exists: So the chat reads evenly, toolbars are easy to hit on a phone and the input is never hidden by the home indicator.
purpose.who_uses_it: Everyone who chats; engineers building new pages that need the shared gutters.
problems_solved: Cramped or uneven message gaps
Tiny touch targets on message actions
Composer hidden by the iPhone home bar
Text touching screen edges on narrow windows
use_cases: Scroll a long conversation on web.
Tap a reply on a phone to reveal its toolbar.
Type in the composer on an iPhone with a home indicator.
Open Library on a wide screen and see wider side gutters.

features.summary: Web buttons come from one component in fixed sizes, with a 2px focus ring. Web icons come from one family on a 24px grid with a 2px stroke, but many screens still import another icon set. Mobile has its own button sizes and uses lucide icons. The CLI has none.

purpose.what_it_does: Web: one Button with variants default, destructive, outline, secondary, ghost, link and sizes default h-10, xs h-7, sm h-9, lg h-11, icon h-10 w-10 (packages/ui/ui/src/primitives/Button.tsx:12-28). Icons: createIcon draws every glyph on a 24px grid, stroke 2, round caps and joins (packages/ui/icons/src/grid.ts:1-13; CreateIcon.tsx:11-40).

purpose.who_uses_it: Everyone who clicks; engineers choosing a button size or icon.

features.summary: One shared set of named corner sizes, four named shadow levels (different values for light and dark) and one named stacking ladder, so dialogs, menus, toasts and tooltips sit in a fixed order and look consistent. Web and Desktop share the ladder. Mobile, VS Code and Chrome keep their own smaller copies.

purpose.what_it_does: It gives every surface named values for how round a corner is, how deep a shadow is, and which layer sits on top. Components pick a name such as corner-field, shadow-e3 or z-modal instead of a number. (packages/ui/design-tokens/src/foundation.css:270-279, 318-340, 358-361)
purpose.why_it_exists: Without a shared ladder, each component invents its own number and layers collide (a menu hidden behind a dialog) or corners look uneven. The foundation file says the ladder exists so consumers never invent a numeric rung. (packages/ui/design-tokens/src/foundation.css:315-317)
purpose.who_uses_it: Designers and engineers building UI on all apps that draw their own visuals (Web, Desktop, Mobile, VS Code, Chrome). End users never set it; they only see it. The CLI has no corners, shadows or layers.
problems_solved: Menus and popovers appearing behind dialogs.

features.summary: Named animation speeds and curves (instant 90ms, quick 160ms, moved 260ms, reveal 700ms) shared by the apps, plus a way to calm motion. Web has a Motion setting (System or Reduced). Mobile, VS Code and Chrome follow the device setting. The CLI has a config key and also stops motion in plain mode.

purpose.what_it_does: It defines named durations and easing curves so animations feel the same everywhere, and it stops or slows looping and travelling motion when the person asks for less. (packages/ui/design-tokens/src/foundation.css:341-356)
purpose.why_it_exists: Animation can cause discomfort and can make a hurried flow feel slow. Named values stop random timings. A switch that is decorative is a known failure, so web uses one blanket rule that catches every animation. (apps/web/app/globals.css:1913-1927)
purpose.who_uses_it: People who are sensitive to motion, anyone who prefers a calm interface, and engineers adding animations.
problems_solved: Dizziness or distraction from looping animations.
Animations that escape the reduced-motion switch because someone forgot a variant.
A frozen spinner that looks like a hung screen (design intent: slow it instead). (globals.css:1929-1938)
use_cases: A Web user chooses Reduced in Settings, Appearance, Motion and the sidebar mark stops shining.
A phone user turns on Reduce Motion in iOS and the AGI mark stays still.
A CLI user sets ui.reduced_motion true and the spinner becomes a dot.
A screen-reader or script user runs the CLI with --plain and the spinner is a still dot.

features.summary: What an empty chat looks like and how wide the conversation reads. On web and desktop an empty chat shows a greeting with a centred composer; messages then sit in a narrow centred column. Mobile caps the reading column at 720 points. Tables keep a pinned header row and can open in a larger dialog.

purpose.what_it_does: Shows a start view when a chat has no messages, keeps message text to a readable centred width on wide windows, and lets tables scroll inside the column with a pinned header row or open in a larger dialog (web). Brief status per app is a separate record (doc: knowledge-base/data/area-briefs/007-layout-systems.md).
purpose.why_it_exists: Long lines are hard to read and an empty transcript looks broken. The product contract asks for a transcript with a sticky composer and for dense tables to stay usable (doc: docs/product/experience-contract.md:184, docs/product/experience-contract.md:199).
purpose.who_uses_it: Every person who opens a chat on any of the six apps, and people reading long tables in answers.
problems_solved: Text running edge to edge on a wide monitor.
A blank screen at the start of a chat.
Losing column names while scrolling a long table.
use_cases: Open a new chat on web and type the first message from the centred composer.
Read a long answer on a wide desktop window with text kept to one column.
Scroll a 100-row table in an answer and still see the column names.
Open a wide table in the expanded dialog to read all columns.

established.statement: An empty new chat shows its start view (greeting, prompt entry or suggestions) centred rather than an empty transcript (S7.01).
Message text is limited to a readable column that stays centred when the window is wide (S7.02).
Data work (tables, charts, spreadsheets) can be viewed in a layout that uses the full window width (S7.03).
Table headers stay pinned while a long table scrolls (S7.24).
Dense tables become cards or horizontally scrollable semantic tables.
A conversation layout is a transcript plus a sticky composer.

acceptance_criteria: On web, with no messages, the greeting and the composer are visible and centred on a 1440 pixel window; after sending, the transcript replaces them.
On web, at 1920 pixels wide, assistant text never exceeds the 48rem column and stays centred.
On mobile, on a tablet-width window, rows never exceed 720 points and are centred.
On web, scrolling a table taller than 70 percent of the window keeps the header row visible.
'Expand table' opens a dialog; Escape or the close button returns to the chat with the same scroll position.
On a 320 point wide phone the column is never narrower than the window (apps/mobile/__tests__/content-column.test.ts).
On mobile, CLI, VS Code and Chrome the gaps listed in this page are shown as missing, not as done.
inferred: The reading column on web (48rem) and VS Code (768px) are intentionally the same size [inferred from max-w-3xl and --conversation-width].
Mobile 720 points is chosen for about 80 characters per line (apps/mobile/src/shared/layout/contentColumn.ts:3).
proposed: [proposed] Centre the CLI start view or change the brief status to partial.
[proposed] Add sticky table headers on mobile, VS Code and Chrome, or record why not.
[proposed] Keep the greeting and composer together on mobile, or record the owner decision that they are separate.

features.summary: A panel opens on the right of the conversation for artifacts, research sources or the work session (and project sources). On web and desktop it can be dragged or keyboard resized between 280 and 900 pixels, shares one remembered width, and only one such panel is open at a time. Under 640 or 768 pixels it covers the chat.

purpose.what_it_does: Shows the thing the answer produced or cited beside the transcript so both stay usable, lets the person resize it, and keeps the conversation taking the rest of the width.
purpose.why_it_exists: Viewing an artifact or checking a source should not mean leaving the conversation. The product contract asks for a transcript plus a resizable artifact or file pane on capable desktop and web surfaces, and a full-screen route on phones (doc: docs/product/experience-contract.md:185, docs/product/experience-contract.md:509, docs/product/experience-contract.md:510).
purpose.who_uses_it: People who generate documents, code or research and want to read them while chatting.
problems_solved: Switching away from the chat to see a result.
A panel too narrow for a document or too wide for the chat.
A panel that covers the chat on a phone with no way back.
use_cases: Open an artifact from a message and tweak it while the chat stays visible.
Open the research sources next to an answer and check a citation.
Widen the work session panel to read a long step list.
Resize a panel with the keyboard only.

where_to_find_it: Web and Desktop (hosted web app): the chat page. Panels are the Artifacts panel (title 'Artifacts'), the Research panel (tabs Sources, Report, Library) and the work session panel (apps/web/features/chat/components/artifacts/ArtifactsPanel.tsx:690, apps/web/features/chat/components/research/ResearchPanel.tsx:398, apps/web/features/chat/components/work-session/WorkSessionPanel.tsx:1079).
Resize bar: a thin vertical separator on the panel's left edge with labels 'Resize artifacts panel', 'Resize research panel' and 'Resize <panel label>' (same lines).
VS Code: artifacts open as a read-only editor tab through the editor's own layout (apps/extension-vscode/src/features/artifacts/artifactActions.ts:135).
Mobile: artifacts open full screen (see F007-06); no side panel.
CLI: no panel (brief marks source inspector missing).
prerequisites: A conversation with an artifact, research sources, or a running work session.
Not in compact embed mode: panels render only when the page is not compact (apps/web/features/chat/pages/WebChatPage.tsx:7844).
screens_and_controls: Resize separator: drag with the pointer, or focus it and press Left to widen and Right to narrow by 24 pixels; Home gives the minimum, End the maximum (apps/web/features/chat/components/SidePanelResizeHandle.tsx:10, apps/web/features/chat/components/SidePanelResizeHandle.tsx:45).
Separator exposes aria-valuenow, valuemin and valuemax (apps/web/features/chat/components/SidePanelResizeHandle.tsx:57).
Close controls and a dimmed backdrop under the overlay width (apps/web/features/chat/components/artifacts/ArtifactsPanel.tsx:681).
journey: Open a panel (artifact card, source chip or work toggle).
The panel slides in on the right and the conversation narrows.
Drag the bar or use arrow keys to set the width.
Switch to another panel; it takes the same slot and the same width.
Close the panel; the conversation takes the full width again.
feedback_and_outputs: Panel width changes live while dragging.
On phones the panel covers the chat as a dialog (artifacts, research) or a bottom sheet (work session).
Desktop shell remembers the width across windows and restarts (apps/web/features/desktop-host/hooks/use-shell-layout.ts:21).
settings: None visible. The width is stored in the chat UI store key 'chat-ui-store' on web (packages/ui/unified-chat/src/stores/uiStore.ts:77).

working: Web: one active secondary panel at a time among work, research, artifacts and sources; newly opened research or artifacts takes the slot (apps/web/features/chat/pages/web-chat-layout.ts:19, apps/web/features/chat/pages/WebChatPage.tsx:1203).

Web: three panels render the shared resize handle only when the layout is wide (apps/web/features/chat/components/artifacts/ArtifactsPanel.tsx:690, apps/web/features/chat/components/research/ResearchPanel.tsx:398, apps/web/features/chat/components/work-session/WorkSessionPanel.tsx:1079).

Width is clamped to 280-900 by one shared function (packages/ui/unified-chat/src/stores/uiStore.ts:6, packages/ui/unified-chat/src/stores/uiStore.ts:10) and persisted with the theme and sidebar flag (packages/ui/unified-chat/src/stores/uiStore.ts:77).
Pointer drag sets width to window width minus pointer x (apps/web/features/chat/components/SidePanelResizeHandle.tsx:24).

Overlay: the artifacts and research panels become a modal dialog under 640 pixels (apps/web/features/chat/stores/artifacts-store.ts:38, apps/web/features/chat/components/artifacts/ArtifactsPanel.tsx:273); the work panel becomes a bottom sheet under 768 (apps/web/features/chat/hooks/use-overlay-dialog.ts:5, apps/web/features/chat/components/work-session/WorkSessionPanel.tsx:1069).

Desktop (Electron): the layout hook reads the shell's saved width and sidebar state once on mount and writes each change back (apps/web/features/desktop-host/hooks/use-shell-layout.ts:21, apps/web/features/desktop-host/hooks/use-shell-layout.ts:41, apps/web/features/desktop-host/hooks/use-shell-layout.ts:47).
VS Code: an artifact opens in a preview editor tab from a read-only content provider (apps/extension-vscode/src/features/artifacts/artifactActions.ts:135).
incomplete: Desktop stores the width clamped to 220-720 while the page clamps to 280-900, so a width above 720 is stored as 720 (apps/desktop/electron/windowState.ts:42, apps/desktop/electron/windowState.ts:43, apps/desktop/electron/windowState.ts:104).

The artifacts panel width rule has min 280 and shrink, with md:w-1/2 and lg:w-[480px] classes that the inline width overrides on wide screens (apps/web/features/chat/components/artifacts/ArtifactsPanel.tsx:681).
disconnected_or_disabled: The shared store function openArtifactPanel also collapses the left sidebar (packages/ui/unified-chat/src/stores/uiStore.ts:59). Its callers found are in the internal Tauri desktop code (apps/desktop/src/features/artifacts/openArtifactInChat.ts:60) and a shared hook (packages/ui/unified-chat/src/hooks/useArtifact.ts:11). Web opens the panel through the artifacts store instead, and I did not establish that opening it collapses the left sidebar on web.
The 'work' dock open flag is not persisted; it re-opens per run (apps/web/shared/stores/layout-store.ts:113).
not_available: Source inspector beside the chat on CLI and VS Code (brief: missing).
Resizable panels on mobile, CLI, VS Code and Chrome (brief lists resize for web and desktop only).

steps.what_happens: The person opens a panel; the page sets its flag and resolves which single panel owns the right slot.
The panel reads the shared width and applies it as inline style when the viewport is wide.
A drag or key press calls setArtifactPanelWidth, which clamps to 280-900 and saves it to browser storage.
In the Electron shell the width change is sent to the shell, which stores it in its window state.
The panel content (artifact text, sources) comes from the chat and research features; the artifacts store may sync to the cloud.

features.summary: The Code page shows a coding session with a session list rail, and up to three sessions side by side (tiled) or one above another (stacked). Cmd or Ctrl click a session to add a pane. In VS Code the chat is a sidebar view or an editor tab you can dock with the editor's own tools. The CLI can show git changes beside the chat.

purpose.what_it_does: Lets a person work on several coding sessions in one window and see a session's chat together with its code work (changes, diffs, terminal). VS Code uses the editor's own layout for docking; the CLI shows a workspace pane for git changes.
purpose.why_it_exists: Coding work runs in parallel and needs the conversation next to the code. The contract describes a code workspace with session navigation and draggable chat, diff, terminal, editor and browser panes (doc: docs/product/experience-contract.md:187).
purpose.who_uses_it: Developers using the Code surface on web or desktop, VS Code, or the CLI.
problems_solved: Switching tabs to follow two agent sessions.
Losing the chat while reviewing a diff.
Having the chat only in a side bar when it needs an editor-sized area (VS Code).
use_cases: Compare two running sessions side by side.
Stack three sessions on a wide monitor.
In VS Code open the chat in an editor tab next to the file being changed.
In the CLI show changes since the last commit beside the chat.

where_to_find_it: Web and Desktop (hosted web app): the Code page with the session rail (apps/web/features/code/CloudCodePage.tsx:2423).

Layout toggle labels 'Stack panes' and 'Place panes side by side'; close label 'Close pane'; each extra pane is a region named 'Session pane' (apps/web/features/code/components/CodePanes.tsx:11, apps/web/features/code/components/CodePanes.tsx:14).

VS Code: activity bar container 'AGI Code' with the sidebar view; command 'Code: Open Chat in Editor' and an editor title button (apps/extension-vscode/package.json:953, apps/extension-vscode/package.json:93, apps/extension-vscode/package.json:1036).
CLI: slash command '/diff panel' toggles the workspace pane (apps/cli/src/tui/tui_app.rs:5902).
Mobile and Chrome: not applicable per the brief.
prerequisites: Web: window wider than 900 pixels and not itself a pane (apps/web/features/code/CloudCodePage.tsx:1801, apps/web/features/code/code-surface.ts:83).
Sessions in the rail (cloud sessions, and local sessions on the desktop app).
CLI: a window at least 90 columns wide (apps/cli/src/tui/tui_app.rs:2665).
screens_and_controls: Rail rows: plain click opens a session; Cmd or Ctrl click asks to split (apps/web/features/code/components/CodeRail.tsx:530).
Pane header tools: layout toggle and close button (apps/web/features/code/components/CodePanes.tsx:11).

Keyboard: Cmd or Ctrl plus backslash closes the focused pane, or the main pane if it is focused (apps/web/features/code/hooks/use-code-panes.ts:28, apps/web/features/code/hooks/use-code-panes.ts:105).
VS Code setting 'agiWorkforce.chat.lockEditorGroups' keeps chat editors in their own group (apps/extension-vscode/src/platform/config.ts:235).
journey: Open the Code page and select a session.
Cmd or Ctrl click a second session in the rail; it opens in a new pane.

Use the layout button to switch between side by side and stacked.

Selecting a session that is the main or already open focuses it; split adds a pane when fewer than 3 are open; otherwise a focused extra pane is replaced; otherwise it returns false and the caller opens the session in the main pane (apps/web/features/code/hooks/use-code-panes.ts:73, apps/web/features/code/hooks/use-code-panes.ts:86, apps/web/features/code/hooks/use-code-panes.ts:93, apps/web/features/code/CloudCodePage.tsx:1850).

features.summary: How the app frame adapts to the window. Web has three tiers: phone (drawer), tablet (icon rail in portrait) and wide (permanent sidebar). Mobile uses a permanent drawer from 1000 points, otherwise an overlay drawer. Pickers become bottom sheets on phones, the composer lifts above the keyboard, and no app lets the left sidebar be resized.

purpose.what_it_does: Collapses or reopens the conversation list, turns side panels into overlays and pickers into sheets on small screens, gives tablets a two-column shell, and keeps the composer clear of notches and the on-screen keyboard.
purpose.why_it_exists: One product runs on phones, tablets and wide monitors. The contract says desktop sidebars become modal drawers on narrow screens, modals become full-screen sheets where two columns do not fit, and nothing may cover send controls or safe areas (doc: docs/product/experience-contract.md:197, docs/product/experience-contract.md:202, docs/product/experience-contract.md:203).
purpose.who_uses_it: Everyone, most visibly phone and tablet users and people with narrow browser windows.
problems_solved: A permanent sidebar eating a small screen.
Panels that squeeze the chat unreadably.
A composer hidden by the keyboard or the home indicator.
use_cases: Collapse the conversation list on a laptop to read more.
Open the drawer on a phone by swiping from the left edge.
Hold an iPad in portrait and keep a slim icon rail.
Type on a phone and keep the composer above the keyboard.

On narrow windows side panels stack over the conversation (overlay or sheet) and return beside it when wide (S7.25).
On phones menus and pickers open as bottom sheets (S7.26).
On tablet widths the app shows two columns, navigation plus content (S7.27).
Content and composer stay clear of notches and home indicators and adjust for the keyboard (S7.28).

The composer must not resize or overlap badly on small devices.

At 900 wide in portrait on web the sidebar is a rail; in landscape at 900 wide it is persistent.
At 1100 wide the collapse toggle shrinks and restores the sidebar and the choice survives reload.
On a phone, focusing the composer lifts it above the keyboard and the send button stays visible.
On mobile at 1024 wide the drawer is permanent and the header menu is hidden; at 800 wide it is an overlay.
On iPhone the composer clears the home indicator.
There is no drag handle on the left sidebar on any app (S7.10 stays missing until built).
inferred: The tablet two-column requirement should be satisfied on mobile from 768 points [inferred from the web tier at 768 and the S7.27 wording]; the code starts at 1000.
The sidebar width is fixed by design [inferred from the token and the negative search].
proposed: [proposed] Decide the mobile persistent-drawer threshold against the 768 tablet tier.
[proposed] Add a left sidebar resize handle on web and desktop that reuses SidePanelResizeHandle logic.
[proposed] Record Chrome stacking and collapse results.

aliases: Scrollable transcript independent from side panels
features.summary: The message box stays at the bottom while the transcript scrolls in its own area. The box grows with long text up to a limit. Web expands it in place (not full screen), mobile opens a true full-screen editor, the CLI hands the draft to an external editor, and VS Code and Chrome only grow the box to a set height.

purpose.what_it_does: Keeps typing controls always reachable, grows the input for long prompts, and offers a larger way to edit a long draft without losing the text.
purpose.why_it_exists: Long prompts and pasted text need room, and a composer that scrolls away or hides is unusable. The contract requires a sticky composer and independent transcript scroll (doc: docs/product/experience-contract.md:184, doc: docs/product/experience-contract.md:511).
purpose.who_uses_it: Everyone who writes messages, especially people pasting long text or code.
problems_solved: Composer scrolling off screen.
A one-line box for a ten-paragraph prompt.
Losing a long draft when changing editors.
use_cases: Paste a long document into the composer and see the box grow.
Scroll up through history while the composer stays put.
Open the larger editor on a phone to write a long prompt.
Press Ctrl-E in the CLI to edit a draft in the user's editor.

where_to_find_it: Web and Desktop: the composer at the bottom of the chat; an expand button labelled 'Expand message input' (becomes 'Collapse message input') appears once text is taller than 120 pixels (apps/web/features/chat/components/Composer/ChatComposerNew.tsx:666, apps/web/features/chat/components/Composer/ChatComposerNew.tsx:4720).

Mobile: composer at the bottom; an expand button labelled 'Expand message' appears once text wraps past about 1.5 lines (apps/mobile/src/features/chat/components/ChatInput.tsx:150, apps/mobile/src/features/chat/components/ChatInput.tsx:2149).
CLI: composer box above the status bar; Ctrl-E or Ctrl-G opens the external editor (apps/cli/src/tui/composer_edits.rs:102).
VS Code: composer card in the chat view (apps/extension-vscode/src/features/sidebar-webview/webviewContent.ts:1062).
Chrome: input #sp-input in the side panel (apps/extension/src/side_panel.ts:3853).
prerequisites: A chat open. External editor in the CLI needs VISUAL or EDITOR set, otherwise 'vi' is tried (apps/cli/src/tui/composer_edits.rs:140).
screens_and_controls: Web expand button with aria-expanded; Escape collapses it when no menu is open (apps/web/features/chat/components/Composer/ChatComposerNew.tsx:4703).
Mobile full-screen editor: control 'Collapse editor'; it has its own send button (apps/mobile/src/features/chat/components/ComposerFullScreenEditor.tsx:43).
Web character counter shows near the limit (apps/web/features/chat/components/Composer/ChatComposerNew.tsx:294).
journey: Type or paste text.
The box grows line by line to its limit, then scrolls inside.
Web: choose expand to make the box about 60 percent of the window height; Escape or the button collapses it.
Mobile: tap expand for the full-screen editor; edit; tap 'Collapse editor' to return with the text kept, or send from the editor.
CLI: press Ctrl-E, edit in the editor, save and quit; the text returns to the composer.
feedback_and_outputs: The CLI shows a status notice if the editor fails (apps/cli/src/tui/tui_app.rs:7312).

settings: Web composer rich editor can be chosen by a query parameter or build default (apps/web/features/chat/components/Composer/__tests__/ComposerInput.test.tsx:75). VS Code: none found.

working: Web composer container is sticky at the bottom on small screens and static beneath the scroll area on wide ones (apps/web/features/chat/components/Composer/ChatComposerNew.tsx:4881); the transcript is a separate log region (apps/web/features/chat/components/messages/ChatMessageList.tsx:2112).

Web input grows to 240 pixels (apps/web/features/chat/components/Composer/ChatComposerNew.tsx:665, apps/web/features/chat/components/Composer/ChatComposerNew.tsx:2461), then scrolls; expanded height is min(60dvh, 40rem) (apps/web/features/chat/components/Composer/ComposerInput.tsx:54).

Mobile input has a maximum height of 160 points (apps/mobile/src/features/chat/components/ChatInput.tsx:2107); the full-screen editor is a modal over the whole screen whose text state lives in the composer, so the text is kept (apps/mobile/src/features/chat/components/ChatInput.tsx:2399, apps/mobile/src/features/chat/components/ComposerFullScreenEditor.tsx:60).

CLI input height is 2 border rows plus 1 to 8 content rows (apps/cli/src/tui/tui_app.rs:1995, apps/cli/src/tui/tui_app.rs:3309) as its own layout row beneath the chat (apps/cli/src/tui/tui_app.rs:2003); external editor writes a temp file, runs the editor and reads it back (apps/cli/src/tui/composer_edits.rs:140, apps/cli/src/tui/tui_app.rs:7300).

VS Code: #messages is its own scroll area and the input grows to 140px (apps/extension-vscode/src/features/sidebar-webview/webviewContent.ts:592, apps/extension-vscode/src/features/sidebar-webview/webviewContent.ts:1086).
Chrome: #sp-input grows between 52 and 120 pixels (apps/extension/src/side_panel.ts:3864).
incomplete: Web 'expand' is an in-place taller box, not a full-screen editor (apps/web/features/chat/components/Composer/ComposerInput.tsx:54). The brief lists a full-screen editor as done on web (doc: knowledge-base/data/area-briefs/007-layout-systems.md).
CLI editing leaves the TUI and uses the user's editor; there is no in-app full-screen editor.

VS Code: no dedicated expand control found; 'Open Chat in Editor' gives a larger surface (apps/extension-vscode/package.json:93). The brief marks VS Code full-screen editor done; I did not establish which code it means.
disconnected_or_disabled: Nothing disconnected or switched off was found for this feature.
not_available: Full-screen editor on Chrome (brief: not listed; none found).

established.statement: The composer stays anchored at the bottom while the transcript scrolls above it (S7.20).
The composer grows or opens a larger editor as a long prompt is typed (S7.21).
An editor can take over the whole screen for focused editing and return to the chat (S7.15).
The transcript scrolls in its own region without moving side panels, header or composer (S7.22).
Viewer contract: independent transcript and viewer scroll.

acceptance_criteria: Scroll a 200-message chat: header and composer do not move on any app.
Type 20 lines on web: box grows to 240 pixels then scrolls inside.
On web, expand makes the box taller and Escape returns it with the text intact.
On mobile, expand opens a full-screen editor; collapsing keeps every character.
In the CLI, Ctrl-E opens the editor; saving returns the text; a failing editor shows a notice and keeps the draft.
In the CLI the composer never exceeds 8 content rows.
With the on-screen keyboard open the composer stays visible.
inferred: Web expand was intended as the 'larger editor' option in S7.21 and may not satisfy S7.15 fully [inferred].
Growth limits differ per app by design: 240 web, 160 mobile, 8 rows CLI, 140 VS Code, 120 Chrome [inferred from constants].
proposed: [proposed] Either call the web control 'taller input' in the brief or build a true full-screen web editor.
[proposed] Add a test for the CLI row clamp and external editor failure.
[proposed] Document the VS Code editor path.

features.summary: Long reports, images and artifacts open in views that cover the screen. Web has a full-screen report reader, an image lightbox with zoom and paging, and an artifact toolbar that stays above the scrolling content. Mobile has report screens, a full-screen image viewer and a full-screen artifact view. Chrome has an image viewer. Video viewing was not found.

purpose.what_it_does: Gives long or detailed content the whole screen, with controls that stay visible and a clear way back to the chat.
purpose.why_it_exists: Reports and images are hard to use inside a narrow column. On phones the contract wants a full-screen viewer or native route (doc: docs/product/experience-contract.md:198, doc: docs/product/experience-contract.md:510).
purpose.who_uses_it: People reading research reports, checking generated images, and reviewing artifacts.
problems_solved: Reports cramped in a side panel.
Tiny images in a message.
Losing the copy, download and close controls while scrolling an artifact.
use_cases: Read a long research report full screen with a contents list.
Zoom into a generated image and page through several.
Scroll a long document artifact on a phone with Close always reachable.
View a picture in the Chrome side panel.

features.summary: On Desktop, the Details and Research panels can be opened in their own OS window, and a small always-on-top Quick Ask window (480 by 620) answers a short question from a global shortcut. In Chrome, a round floating launcher opens a small in-page panel on approved sites. Detach is Desktop only; Quick Ask is Cloud only.

purpose.what_it_does: Desktop: a button on the Details panel and the Research panel moves that panel into a separate window and back (apps/web/features/desktop-host/components/PanelWindow.tsx:30-56). Desktop: a global shortcut shows or hides a small frameless window that loads the hosted compact chat page /quick-ask (apps/desktop/electron/quickAsk.ts:6-10, 164-171). Chrome: a 48px launcher button on a page opens a 380px in-page panel that takes one question at a time (apps/extension/src/features/content/in-page-panel/launcher.ts:75-78; panelStyles.ts:16).
purpose.why_it_exists: People want to keep a panel beside other work, ask a quick question without opening the main window, or ask about the page they are reading without leaving it. The code comment says Quick Ask follows the ChatGPT and Claude companion windows (apps/desktop/electron/quickAsk.ts:43-47).
purpose.who_uses_it: Desktop (Electron) users with a signed-in account for detach and Quick Ask. Chrome users on sites they approved, who have the page assistant setting on.
problems_solved: A long research or details panel no longer has to share the main window.
A one-off question does not need the full app, sidebar and panels.
On a web page, a person can ask about the page in place without opening the side panel.
use_cases: Pop the Research panel into a window on a second monitor while writing in the main window.
Press the Quick Ask shortcut from any app, ask one question, press Escape.
Open a conversation from Quick Ask in the main window with Open full chat.
On an approved news page in Chrome, click the launcher and choose a page action chip.

where_to_find_it: Desktop: the window button on the right of the Details panel header and the Research panel header. Its label reads 'Open <panel> in a new window' and, once detached, 'Move <panel> back to the main window'; the research label is 'research panel' (apps/web/features/chat/components/research/ResearchPanel.tsx:29, 455-459; apps/web/features/desktop-host/components/PanelWindow.tsx:39-42). The exact Details label text comes from a panelLabel prop that I did not trace (WorkSessionPanel.tsx:1090-1094).

Desktop: Quick Ask global shortcut. Default chord is the first choice 'Alt+Shift+Space'; alternatives offered are CommandOrControl+Shift+Space and CommandOrControl+Alt+A (packages/contracts/local-runtime/src/host-bridge.ts:162, 170-172). It is also listed in the tray menu as 'Quick Ask' (apps/desktop/electron/tray.ts:174-175) and set in the hosted settings panel under the label 'Quick Ask shortcut' (apps/web/features/desktop-host/__tests__/DesktopSettingsSection.test.tsx:168).

Chrome: launcher button with aria-label 'Open AGI' and tooltip 'Ask AGI' at bottom right of approved http(s) pages (launcher.ts:106-119, 135-136). Shortcut Alt+Shift+K (Command+Shift+K on Mac) is the _execute_action command, labelled 'Open AGI side panel', and opens the side panel, not the in-page panel (apps/extension/manifest.json:67-74; apps/extension/_locales/en/messages.json:2-4).
Chrome setting: 'Page assistant overlay' in the extension settings turns the in-page panel on or off (apps/extension/_locales/en/messages.json:488-491).
prerequisites: Desktop detach: the Electron shell must be present (host not null) and the page must not be the compact Quick Ask page (apps/web/features/desktop-host/hooks/use-detachable-panels.ts:58; apps/web/features/chat/pages/WebChatPage.tsx:1169-1175).
Desktop Quick Ask: signed in, current terms accepted and adult check passed, or the page redirects to sign-in (apps/web/app/quick-ask/layout.tsx:14-25).

Chrome: the site is approved by the person and the page assistant setting is not off (apps/extension/src/background.ts:5568-5573; apps/extension/src/inPagePanel/setup.ts:93-103). The panel only mounts on http or https pages (setup.ts:91).
Chrome: a signed-in AGI account; otherwise the prompt fails with 'Sign in to use AGI Managed Cloud.' (apps/extension/src/background.ts:9135-9137).
screens_and_controls: Detached panel window: 440 by 760, menu bar hidden, minimum 320 by 360, titled 'Details' or 'Research' (apps/desktop/electron/windowPolicy.ts:237-244; apps/web/features/desktop-host/lib/panel-windows.ts:16-19).
Quick Ask window: 480 by 620, no frame, cannot resize, minimise, maximise or go full screen, hidden from the taskbar, always on top, shown on all workspaces (apps/desktop/electron/quickAsk.ts:53-78).
Quick Ask on a conversation shows a small header with 'Open full chat' and a 'New chat' icon (apps/web/features/chat/pages/WebChatPage.tsx:7277-7298).

Chrome in-page panel: provider pill 'Managed Cloud · Auto', buttons 'New question', 'Settings', 'Close panel', page action chips, a prompt box ('Page assistant prompt'), 'Send message', a privacy notice and an 'Open in side panel' link (apps/extension/src/features/content/in-page-panel/panel.ts:72-159).
journey: Detach: open the Details or Research panel, press the window button; the panel closes inline and appears in a new window (use-detachable-panels.ts:63-68).
Work in the detached window; its content is the same React tree drawn into the other window (apps/web/features/desktop-host/components/PanelWindow.tsx:14-28).
Move back: press the button in the detached window, or close the window; the panel reopens inline when moved back with the button (use-detachable-panels.ts:69-75).
Quick Ask: press the shortcut; the window appears centred in the upper part of the screen holding the cursor and takes focus (quickAsk.ts:139-162).
Type one question and read the answer. Clicking outside the window or pressing Escape hides it (quickAsk.ts:81-89).
To continue elsewhere, choose Open full chat; the window hides and the main window opens the route (quickAsk.ts:97-105; apps/desktop/electron/main.ts:1653-1664).
Chrome: click the launcher, pick a chip or type a question, read the streamed answer, press Escape or Close panel; use 'Open in side panel' to continue in the side panel (panel.ts:637-663, 686-688).
feedback_and_outputs: If the browser blocks the pop-out, detachPanel returns false and the panel stays inline; there is no message (panel-windows.ts:115-116; use-detachable-panels.ts:66).
Quick Ask that failed to load while offline reloads on the next shortcut press (quickAsk.ts:152-156).

Chrome shows errors in the response area: 'Sign in to use AGI Managed Cloud.', 'Enter a question or choose a page action.', 'Request cancelled.' (background.ts:9119-9137) and a retryable state on a worker failure (apps/extension/__tests__/in-page-panel-ui.test.ts:278, 368).
Chrome: if opening the side panel fails the response area shows a failure text (panel.ts:651-663).
settings: Desktop: Quick Ask shortcut choice, including none, in the hosted desktop settings (host-bridge.ts:141-172, 446; apps/desktop/electron/main.ts:1982).
Chrome: Page assistant overlay on or off, stored under the key in_page_panel_enabled (apps/extension/src/features/options/preference-rows.ts:10).
Chrome: per-site approval (apps/extension/src/background.ts:5568-5573).

working: Desktop panel detach: window.open with a named window agi-panel-<name>, style sheets copied and kept in sync, panel drawn in by a portal (apps/web/features/desktop-host/lib/panel-windows.ts:56-145; PanelWindow.tsx:14-28).

Desktop window policy lets only about:blank windows named agi-panel-<letters> open as a panel window, locks them from navigating, and closes them when the main window closes (apps/desktop/electron/windowPolicy.ts:246-249, 319-327, 341).
Detached window closes 2 seconds after the panel unmounts, so a quick re-render does not close it (panel-windows.ts:15, 158-173).
Quick Ask window is created, warmed after launch, repositioned on each show, and sends non-Quick-Ask destinations to the main window (apps/desktop/electron/quickAsk.ts:52-188; main.ts:2702-2717).
Quick Ask shortcut registration reports registered, taken, malformed, duplicate or off (apps/desktop/electron/shortcuts.ts:74-110).

Chrome in-page panel mounts only on approved pages, hides while the real side panel is open, and streams answers through the service worker (apps/extension/src/inPagePanel/setup.ts:8-36, 93-114; apps/extension/src/background.ts:9112-9162).
Chrome falls back to a 440 by 860 pop-up window when the browser has no side panel API (apps/extension/src/features/surface/assistantPanel.ts:3-4, 39-73).
incomplete: Detach covers only two panels, 'work' and 'research' (panel-windows.ts:5). Artifacts, Sources and other panels cannot be detached (apps/web/features/chat/pages/WebChatPage.tsx:7843-7896).
Detached window size and position are not remembered; each detach opens at 440 by 760 chosen by the browser features string (panel-windows.ts:13). No saving code found.
When the pop-up is blocked the person gets no message (panel-windows.ts:115-116).
Brief line pointers are stale: windowPolicy.ts:187-230 now holds public page return logic and the panel-window code starts at line 237; manifest.json:78 is now line 83 (checked by opening the files).
Chrome in-page panel is one question and one answer, not a saved chat (apps/extension/_locales/en/messages.json:508-511).
disconnected_or_disabled: Detach is switched off in the compact Quick Ask page (enabled: !compact) and on plain web, because the host bridge is null outside the Electron shell (WebChatPage.tsx:1169-1170; use-detachable-panels.ts:58).
Quick Ask warm-up and shortcut exist only in the Electron app; the retained Tauri build (apps/desktop/src-tauri) was not checked for Quick Ask (unknown).
not_available: Web, Mobile, CLI: no detach and no Quick Ask code found (brief status n/a; no code opened on these surfaces).

VS Code: the extension has no pop-out code of its own; the brief says it relies on the editor's own windowing. I found no pop-out code in apps/extension-vscode/src/providers/chatEditorPanel.ts [inferred].
Chrome has no detach of the in-page panel.

established.statement: A panel of the desktop app can be torn off into its own OS window and used there.
A small always-on-top companion window can float over other apps or pages and be summoned without switching to the main app.
A compact companion mode shows a reduced chat UI (no sidebar or side panels) sized for quick questions.

Detach calls window.open with a named window and copies the style sheets; a blocked pop-up returns false. Quick Ask is a frameless 480 by 620 window loading the hosted /quick-ask page; anything else goes to the main window; detached windows are checked by the desktop window policy.

Quick Ask, Screenshot and Dictation shortcuts take only a chord the shell offers for them, the one already set, or none.

acceptance_criteria: On Desktop, pressing the window button on the Research panel opens a window titled 'Research' and the panel disappears from the main window.
Pressing the button in the detached window, or closing it, returns the panel to the main window or closes it, and no second window for the same panel can exist.
The Quick Ask shortcut shows a 480 by 620 frameless window that cannot be resized and hides on Escape or when focus moves away.
A link inside Quick Ask that leads outside /quick-ask opens in the main window and Quick Ask hides.
In Chrome on an approved site the launcher appears; on an unapproved site, or with the setting off, it does not.
In Chrome the launcher disappears while the side panel is open and returns when it closes.

steps.what_happens: Person presses the detach button; the web page calls window.open with a named about:blank window.
The Electron window policy sees an about:blank request named agi-panel-<letters> and allows it with fixed size options.
The page copies style nodes into the new window and draws the panel there through a portal; the panel's data still comes from the main window's page.
Quick Ask shortcut fires; the main process shows the pre-created window and it loads the hosted /quick-ask page from the cloud app origin.
The hosted layout checks identity, terms and adult eligibility before showing the page.
A question in Quick Ask goes through the same hosted chat page as the main window (compact mode of WebChatPage).
steps.evidence: apps/web/app/quick-ask/page.tsx:6-8; apps/web/app/quick-ask/layout.tsx:27-31. Which model route it uses is unknown.

steps.what_happens: Chrome: the content script asks the service worker if the site is approved and the setting is on, then mounts the launcher.
Chrome: a question is sent over a port to the service worker, which uses the managed account token and streams the answer from Managed Cloud with automatic model selection.

access_and_usage.account: Desktop Quick Ask needs sign-in, current terms and adult check (apps/web/app/quick-ask/layout.tsx:14-25). Chrome in-page panel needs a signed-in AGI account (background.ts:9135-9137). Detach: the host being present; no separate account check found in the detach code.
access_and_usage.permissions: Chrome: per-site approval and the sidePanel permission (manifest.json:17; background.ts:5568-5573). Desktop: windows run sandboxed with context isolation and no Node access (quickAsk.ts:67-73; windowPolicy.ts:237-241). The Quick Ask window does receive the preload bridge (quickAsk.ts:17-23, 72, main.ts:2702-2708); docs/decisions/wire-or-cut.md:706 says it has none, so the document is out of date.
access_and_usage.subscription: none found in the code for detach, the Quick Ask window or the Chrome launcher. What the hosted chat or Managed Cloud does with plans on a question is outside these files (see SYS-subscriptions-entitlements-and-usage).
access_and_usage.limits_and_metering: none found in the code in the files for detach, Quick Ask window or in-page panel. Page text sent from Chrome is bounded by MAX_PAGE_TEXT_CHARACTERS (apps/extension/src/features/content/in-page-panel/panel.ts:50-54).
access_and_usage.flags: Chrome: in_page_panel_enabled (default on unless set to false) (background.ts:5573). Desktop: Quick Ask shortcut can be set to none (host-bridge.ts:141-172). No other flags found.
access_and_usage.model_compatibility: Chrome in-page: automatic selection only, the person cannot pick a model there. Quick Ask: unknown.
access_and_usage.provider_restrictions: Chrome in-page panel is Cloud only (label 'Managed Cloud · Auto'). Quick Ask loads the hosted app; no own-key or local path was found in the Quick Ask files.
access_and_usage.local_mode: Quick Ask needs the hosted page and a signed-in account, so it does not work offline or without signing in (apps/web/app/quick-ask/layout.tsx:19-21; quickAsk.ts:124). Whether the hosted compact page offers Local inference is unknown. Chrome in-page panel has no Local path. Detach is only window handling and is not tied to a mode.

features.summary: The Chrome extension shows the AGI chat in the browser's side panel, so the live page stays visible while the person chats. A toolbar click or Alt+Shift+K (Command+Shift+K on Mac) opens it. Browsers without the side panel API get a pop-up window instead. No other app has a live page beside the chat.

purpose.what_it_does: Opens the extension chat page src/side_panel.html in Chrome's side panel, next to the current tab, and lets the chat read and act on that page with the person's approval (apps/extension/manifest.json:83-85; apps/extension/src/features/surface/assistantPanel.ts:66-73).
purpose.why_it_exists: The brief requires that a live web page is shown beside the conversation so the user can watch or use the page while chatting about it (S7.06).
purpose.who_uses_it: Chrome extension users, signed in to an AGI account.
problems_solved: No tab switching between a page and the chat.
The chat can know which page is in front.
Browsers lacking the side panel still get the chat in a small window.
use_cases: Summarise an article while reading it.
Fill a form while chatting about the fields.
Ask follow-up questions on a product page.
Open the chat from the in-page panel with Open in side panel.

where_to_find_it: Chrome: the extension toolbar button titled 'AGI Extension' (apps/extension/manifest.json:61).
Shortcut: Alt+Shift+K, Command+Shift+K on Mac, labelled 'Open AGI side panel' in chrome://extensions/shortcuts (manifest.json:67-74; _locales/en/messages.json:2-4).
In-page panel footer link 'Open in side panel' (apps/extension/src/features/content/in-page-panel/panel.ts:155-159).
Web, Desktop, Mobile, VS Code: not available.
prerequisites: Chrome version 132 or later (manifest.json:87).
An AGI account for chatting; site approval for the page content to be read (background.ts:5568-5573, 4581-4601 related allowlist code).
The sidePanel permission (manifest.json:17).
screens_and_controls: Side panel page src/side_panel.html with its script src/side_panel.ts (manifest.json:83-85).
Toolbar click and shortcut both go to the same opener (background.ts:7677-7681).
Panel behaviour is set so a toolbar click does not open it automatically; the extension's own click handler opens it (background.ts:1768-1772).
journey: Press the toolbar button or the shortcut.
The service worker calls the side panel open for that tab; if the browser has no side panel API it opens a 440 by 860 pop-up window beside the browser window (assistantPanel.ts:3-4, 39-73).
The side panel connects to the service worker so the page knows the real side panel is open (side_panel.ts:166; background.ts:1812-1835).
Chat while the page stays visible; the in-page launcher hides to avoid two assistants (setup.ts:8-15).
Close the panel; the launcher returns.
feedback_and_outputs: The side panel itself, with the chat and the page context chip.
If opening fails the worker logs a warning; the person sees nothing from the toolbar path (background.ts:7678-7680).
From the in-page panel, a failed open shows a failure text in the response area (panel.ts:651-663).
settings: Keyboard shortcut can be changed in chrome://extensions/shortcuts (the command has a description for this page).
Page assistant overlay setting only affects the in-page panel, not the side panel (setup.ts:93-103).

working: Side panel declared in the manifest with default path src/side_panel.html (apps/extension/manifest.json:83-85).
Opener uses chrome.sidePanel.open for a tab or window and falls back to a pop-up window (assistantPanel.ts:66-73).
The open runs in the synchronous turn of the click to keep Chrome's user gesture rule (apps/extension/src/background.ts:4490-4505).
Presence tracking: the side panel connects on a port; the worker publishes open or closed to the tabs of that window (background.ts:1812-1850; panelPresence.ts:1-17).
Page queries use the right window when the chat lives in the pop-up (assistantPanel.ts:75-90).

features.summary: The app reopens as it was left. Web saves sidebar state and panel width in browser storage. Desktop saves them, and the window frame per display set-up, in its own window-state file, and puts the window back on screen if the monitor changed. VS Code restores its chat editor panel.

purpose.what_it_does: Web: remembers whether the sidebar is collapsed and how wide the side panel is (apps/web/shared/stores/layout-store.ts:101-117; packages/ui/unified-chat/src/stores/uiStore.ts:77-85). Desktop: the shell stores sidebar state, panel width, window frame per display arrangement and the last route (apps/desktop/electron/windowState.ts:27-37).
purpose.why_it_exists: Brief S7.30 and S7.31: layout choices should come back, and the desktop window should reopen at its last size and position and stay on screen when monitors change.
purpose.who_uses_it: Web and Desktop users, and VS Code users who keep a chat editor open.
problems_solved: No need to collapse the sidebar again every visit.
A window never reopens off screen after unplugging a monitor.
A second Desktop window opens on the same layout as the first.
use_cases: Collapse the sidebar on web, reload, still collapsed.
Resize the side panel on Desktop, quit, reopen at that width.
Unplug the external monitor, launch the app, window appears on the laptop screen.
Reload VS Code and see the AGI Chat editor panel return.

where_to_find_it: Web and Desktop: the sidebar collapse control and the draggable edge of the side panel; no separate settings screen was found for layout memory.
Desktop: the window itself (move, resize, maximise).
VS Code: the editor tab titled 'AGI Chat' or 'AGI Chat 2' and so on (apps/extension-vscode/src/providers/chatEditorPanel.ts:66-69).
prerequisites: Web: browser storage available.
Desktop: the Electron shell host; the window-state file in the app's user data folder (apps/desktop/electron/shellWindowStore.ts:15-17).
Window route restore: the same account as when the route was saved (windowState.ts:117-119).
screens_and_controls: Sidebar collapse control (state sidebarCollapsed).
Side panel drag handle (state artifactPanelWidth, default 400).
The OS window frame.
journey: Change the layout: collapse the sidebar, drag a panel edge, resize or move the window.
Close the app.
Reopen it; the stores rehydrate, or on Desktop the hook reads the shell's saved layout once and the main process opens the window at the restored frame.
feedback_and_outputs: The layout appears as left; no message is shown.
Desktop: a restored route that no longer exists sends the window to a new chat (windowState.ts:195-201).
settings: No setting found to turn layout memory on or off or to reset it (not found in the code I opened).

working: Web sidebar flag persisted under 'agi-ui-store', version 2, only sidebarCollapsed (apps/web/shared/stores/layout-store.ts:101-117).
Web chat store persists sidebarCollapsed, themeMode and artifactPanelWidth under 'chat-ui-store' (packages/ui/unified-chat/src/stores/uiStore.ts:77-85); the width is clamped on set (uiStore.ts:63).
Desktop hook adopts the shell's layout once on mount, then writes each change and does not write while adopting (apps/web/features/desktop-host/hooks/use-shell-layout.ts:14-58).
Shell stores layout in window-state.json (shellWindowStore.ts:15-54) and the dispatcher serves read and write (apps/desktop/electron/runtime/dispatcher.ts:2429-2431).
Panel width is clamped to 220-720 in the shell (windowState.ts:42-43, 104-108).
Window frames are kept per display arrangement, keyed by work-area size and position (windowState.ts:62-65; 22-32).
Launch restore picks the frame of an attached display, otherwise pulls the newest frame onto the primary display and clamps it with at least 80 pixels visible (windowState.ts:34-78, 143-164).

A frame is written 400 ms after resize or move, and on close; minimised, full-screen and zoomed windows are not stored as ordinary sizes (apps/desktop/electron/main.ts:1010-1062; windowState.ts:101-111).

features.summary: Print gives a clean paper copy of a whole conversation. On Web and Desktop, the chat menu's Print item turns on a print-only layout that hides app chrome, forces black on white, avoids splitting messages and shows link addresses. On Mobile, the export sheet's Print option sends a styled HTML copy to the printer.

Mobile: the export sheet offers Print and Export as PDF (apps/mobile/src/features/chat/components/ConversationExportSheet.tsx:55-66).
purpose.why_it_exists: Brief S7.32 asks for a print layout without app chrome, with the whole content, paper-friendly colours and sensible page breaks. The code comment says a plain Ctrl+P could only print the rows in the virtual list (WebChatPage.tsx:7403-7406).

problems_solved: Printing a long chat used to print only the visible rows plus chrome (apps/web/app/globals.css:1850-1860).
Dark themes wasted toner.
Links in print had no visible address.
