features.summary: Clickable actions in all six apps: a filled main button, quieter outline and ghost buttons, a red destructive style, icon-only buttons with a spoken name, and grouped buttons. The web and desktop button also has a busy state. A split button (main action plus menu) is not built anywhere.

purpose.what_it_does: Gives every app a consistent way to start an action. The shared web Button has six looks (default, destructive, outline, secondary, ghost, link) and five sizes, can be disabled, and can show a busy state that tells screen readers 'Loading, please wait' (packages/ui/ui/src/primitives/Button.tsx:8-36, :72, :80, :103). Mobile has its own Button with five looks (apps/mobile/components/ui/button.tsx:16-21). The CLI shows approval choices as a row of buttons in a terminal box (apps/cli/src/tui/widgets/approval_overlay.rs:153-160).
purpose.why_it_exists: People must tell the main action from side actions and from risky ones, and people using keyboards or screen readers must be able to use every button. The project contract says every icon-only control has an accessible name (doc: docs/product/experience-contract.md:168) and that touch targets follow platform guidance with a 40 px pointer minimum (doc: docs/product/experience-contract.md:174).
purpose.who_uses_it: Every person on every app (Web, Desktop, Mobile, CLI, VS Code, Chrome). Engineers reuse the shared Button; testers check look, keyboard and screen reader behaviour.
problems_solved: The main action is easy to find.
Risky actions look different from safe ones.
Icon-only buttons are not silent to a screen reader.
A busy button cannot be pressed twice.
use_cases: On web, Continue in onboarding is a default button and Skip for now is a ghost button (apps/web/features/onboarding/components/OnboardingWizard.tsx:199-209).
On mobile, a tool approval row offers Allow once, session and always choices (apps/mobile/src/features/chat/components/CloudToolApprovalControls.tsx:326-345).
In the CLI, a tool approval box offers Yes, No, Allow Session, Always Allow, Deny All, Allow All (apps/cli/src/tui/widgets/approval_overlay.rs:153-160).
On web, a dictation strip groups cancel and send buttons under one label (apps/web/features/chat/components/Composer/DictationStrip.tsx:87-95).

where_to_find_it: Web: everywhere in the chat app, for example the onboarding form buttons Continue and Skip for now (apps/web/features/onboarding/components/OnboardingWizard.tsx:199-209).
Desktop: the public Desktop shows the hosted web app, so it shows the web buttons (doc: AGENTS.md section 5). The internal Tauri build re-exports the same Button (apps/desktop/src/ui/Button.tsx:1).
Mobile: sign-in and settings screens use apps/mobile/components/ui/button.tsx; the tool approval row sits under a tool call in chat.
CLI: the approval box that appears when a tool needs permission, hint line 'Enter confirm Tab note Esc = No' (apps/cli/src/tui/widgets/approval_overlay.rs:173-176).

VS Code and Chrome: sidebar and side panel buttons. Their button styles were not opened in detail; the brief marks them done (doc: knowledge-base/data/area-briefs/008-basic-interactive-elements.md S8.01-S8.04).
prerequisites: None for the buttons themselves. Tool approval controls appear only when an agent asks to run a tool.
screens_and_controls: Web Button looks: default, destructive, outline, secondary, ghost, link; sizes default, xs, sm, lg, icon (Button.tsx:12-29).
Mobile Button looks: primary, secondary, outline, ghost, destructive; sizes sm, md, lg (apps/mobile/components/ui/button.tsx:16-29).
Mobile approval row: one button per scope, label '<scope label>: <summary>' (CloudToolApprovalControls.tsx:340-345), plus a 'Raw JSON' disclosure button (CloudToolApprovalControls.tsx:258-264).
CLI approval buttons in the order Yes, No, Allow Session, Always Allow, Deny All, Allow All (approval_overlay.rs:153-160).
journey: 1. The person sees a view with one filled main button and quieter side buttons.
2. They click, tap, or press Enter or Space on the focused button. Space/Enter activation is native button behaviour [inferred from the use of a real button element at Button.tsx:93].
3. If the action takes time, the web button turns inert and reports busy (Button.tsx:72, :80, :103).
4. In the CLI, they press Left or Right to move the highlight, Enter to confirm, Esc to answer No (approval_overlay.rs:173-176, :244-252).
5. On mobile, a light haptic tap fires when haptics are enabled (apps/mobile/components/ui/button.tsx:57-62).
feedback_and_outputs: Web: pressed look (active:scale-[0.98]), focus ring, dimmed when disabled (Button.tsx:9).
Mobile: pressed colour change; half-opacity when disabled or loading (button.tsx:76-104, :121); label changes to 'Loading...' (button.tsx:135).
CLI: the highlighted choice and a note line; an allowing answer pressed before the detail was read is refused (approval_overlay.rs:259-262).
settings: Mobile: haptics on/off (useSettingsStore hapticsEnabled, apps/mobile/components/ui/button.tsx:54).
None found for web, CLI, VS Code or Chrome in the files read.

working: Web/shared Button with variants, sizes, disabled dimming, loading state with aria-busy and screen-reader text 'Loading, please wait', and a hidden 'Button' fallback name when a non-link button has no text and no aria-label (packages/ui/ui/src/primitives/Button.tsx:8-36, :72, :90-105).

features.summary: On/off and pick-one controls: switches for settings that apply at once, checkboxes for independent choices, radio groups for one visible choice, toggle buttons with a pressed state, and segmented controls of joined options. Web, desktop, mobile and CLI have all; VS Code and Chrome use styled checkboxes and menu items.

purpose.what_it_does: The shared web Switch, Checkbox and RadioGroup wrap Radix components (packages/ui/ui/src/primitives/Switch.tsx:2; Checkbox.tsx:2; RadioGroup.tsx:4). SegmentedControl is a labelled group of buttons with aria-pressed (SegmentedControl.tsx:46-70). Mobile has a Switch that reports checked state (apps/mobile/components/ui/switch.tsx:13-40) and a Local/Cloud ModeToggle (apps/mobile/src/features/chat/components/ModeToggle.tsx:96-135).
purpose.why_it_exists: People need clear on/off and either-or choices that assistive technology can read.
purpose.who_uses_it: Everyone changing settings or modes.
problems_solved: State is announced (checked, pressed, selected).
One choice among visible options is clear.
Mode changes are one tap.

Checkboxes expose checked state.
Radio group has mutually exclusive visible options with checked state exposed.
Switches are immediate on/off settings with switch semantics.

features.summary: Ways to pick values from a list: single-select menus, search-as-you-type comboboxes, multiselect lists and removable chips. Web has all four (chips only in two policy screens); CLI and VS Code have pickers; mobile has a searchable model picker but no multiselect or chips found.

purpose.what_it_does: Lets a person choose one or many values. The shared useCombobox hook wires arrow keys, Enter, Escape and listbox ids for a search box with options (packages/ui/ui/src/primitives/useCombobox.ts:1-106). ChipInput turns typed entries into removable chips with limits and validation (packages/ui/ui/src/primitives/ChipInput.tsx:33-241).
purpose.why_it_exists: Long lists (models, skills, apps) need search; sets of values (policy domains) need add and remove.
purpose.who_uses_it: Everyone choosing models, skills, agents, apps or policy values.
problems_solved: Find an item in a long list by typing.
Pick many items and see what is chosen.
Add several values fast.
use_cases: Search models in the picker (apps/web/features/chat/components/Composer/ModelCatalogue.tsx:340-360).
Choose skills for an agent with a multi-selectable list (apps/web/features/agents/components/AgentSkillSelection.tsx:245-262).
Add allowed values as chips in workspace policy (WorkspacePolicySection.tsx).
Tick tools for a session in a VS Code multi-pick (capabilityManagement.ts:1145).

where_to_find_it: Web: model catalogue in the composer model picker; agent skill selection; refuse-app picker (apps/web/features/desktop-host/components/RefuseAppPicker.tsx:71); workspace policy screens with chips; command palette (CommandPalette.tsx, brief S8.19).
Desktop: web app in the public Desktop [inferred from doc: AGENTS.md section 5].
Mobile: model picker sheet with search (ModelPickerSheet.tsx, brief S8.19).
CLI: model picker with search text, effort picker, elicitation multi-select (model_picker.rs:108-125; elicitation_overlay.rs:60-66).
VS Code: 'Select Model' quick pick and 'Tools for this session' multi-pick (commandSetup.ts:1321-1326; capabilityManagement.ts:1145).
Chrome: menu popovers; combobox missing per brief.
prerequisites: Paid plan affects which model rows are selectable on web and mobile (see access).
screens_and_controls: Web chip input: text field plus chips, each with a remove button named 'Remove <value>' (ChipInput.tsx:174-190).
Web skill list: search field, listbox 'Skills' with aria-multiselectable (AgentSkillSelection.tsx:245-248).
CLI multi-select: Left/Right move, Space toggle (elicitation_overlay.rs:560).
journey: 1. Open the list or focus the search field.
2. Type to filter; Down/Up move, Home/End jump, Enter selects, Escape closes (useCombobox.ts; test at useCombobox.test.tsx).
3. For chips: type a value, press Enter or comma (ChipInput.tsx:131-135), or paste several separated by space, comma or semicolon (ChipInput.tsx:11, :158-164).
4. Remove a chip with its X, or Backspace/Delete on a focused chip (ChipInput.tsx:137-150).
5. Errors show under the field.
feedback_and_outputs: Chip error text with role alert: 'This list holds at most {{count}} entries.' or '{{value}} was not added. {{reason}}' (ChipInput.tsx:76-87, :221-227).
Rejected text stays in the input (ChipInput.tsx:105).
settings: Model favourites and recents on the web catalogue (ModelCatalogue.tsx:335-336).

working: Radix Select wrapper (Select.tsx:4).
useCombobox with IME-safe keys (useCombobox.ts:50).

established.statement: Single-select menu chooses one value from a list.
Searchable combobox filters as typed with listbox semantics or keyboard navigation.
Multiselect shows each selection and lets it be removed.
Token input turns typed entries into removable chips.
Routing weighs capability and cost; routing metadata is central, never inlined at a call site.
Nothing silently routes a Local chat to BYOK or managed cloud; moves are explicit with a visible provider label.

acceptance_criteria: Typing in a combobox narrows the list; Down and Enter pick the active item.
Escape closes the list.
Enter or comma in the chip input adds a chip; the chip's X removes it.
With maxItems set, adding past the limit shows the 'holds at most N entries' text.
An invalid chip value is rejected and stays in the field with a reason.
The model picker never offers a Cloud row as selectable when the plan does not allow it.
Multiselect shows selected items as checked and respects the maximum.

features.summary: Controls for entering a date, a time, a time zone or a colour. Schedule forms on web, desktop, mobile and the Chrome extension use date and time inputs. Web and mobile add a time zone field that starts at the device zone. Web projects and mobile settings offer colour swatches. VS Code has none.

purpose.what_it_does: Lets a person choose a date, a time of day, an IANA time zone (a name such as a city region) or a colour without typing a raw value. The schedule form uses all three of date, time and zone. Colour choice is used for a project accent, the mobile accent colour and desktop theme colours.
purpose.why_it_exists: A schedule that runs at the wrong hour or in the wrong zone is a silent failure, and a free-text date is easy to get wrong. The brief requires pickers wherever a date, time, zone or colour is entered (doc: knowledge-base/data/area-briefs/008-basic-interactive-elements.md, S8.25 to S8.28).
purpose.who_uses_it: Anyone creating or editing a scheduled task or routine, anyone colouring a project, and mobile users changing the accent colour.
problems_solved: Wrong run time because the person typed a date by hand.
Runs landing in the wrong zone: the form starts at the device zone and checks the zone name.
Ambiguous daylight-saving times are rejected with a message instead of running at a surprise hour.
Colour choice stays on a fixed set of accents so contrast stays safe.
use_cases: Create a one-time schedule on web: set Run At, check Time Zone, save.
Create a daily schedule on mobile: tap Choose a time, then pick a zone from the searchable Time zone sheet.
Colour a project on web from the Project colour swatches.
Change the accent colour on mobile under Accent Color.

established.statement: A date picker (calendar or native date control) is used where a date is entered.
A time picker (native or custom) is used where a time is entered.
A time zone picker (searchable list, defaulting to the device zone) is used where schedules take a zone.
A colour picker (swatches or a colour input) is used where the user chooses a colour.

acceptance_criteria: On web, create a One Time schedule: Run At shows a date-time control and saving with an empty value shows a field error.
On web and mobile, a new schedule form shows the device time zone before the person touches it.
On web, typing an invalid zone name and saving shows 'Enter a valid IANA time zone.'.
On mobile, searching 'london' in the Time zone sheet narrows the list and choosing a row closes the sheet and updates the button label.
On mobile Android, the date dialog does not allow a day earlier than today in the selected zone.
On web, choosing a swatch under Project colour sets aria-selected on that swatch only.
On mobile, choosing a colour under Accent Color shows the check on that row and persists after reopening.

Time zone and time values must reach the server unchanged so a schedule runs at the displayed time [inferred from schedule-form.ts converting local input to an ISO time with the chosen zone (lines 303-336)].
proposed: [proposed] Add a zone picker to the retained desktop schedule form or confirm that only the web form is shipped on the Electron Desktop.
[proposed] Update the brief rows for Chrome date, time and zone, and correct stale line references.
[proposed] Offer an exact colour option for projects or say plainly that colours snap to presets.

features.summary: Lets a person attach files to a chat message by choosing them from the device or dragging them onto the chat. Web shows a full-window 'Drop files here' overlay. VS Code and Chrome highlight the composer while files are over it. Mobile uses a picker sheet. The CLI uses an @ file list.

purpose.what_it_does: Gives every app a way to bring files into a message: a file chooser button, and on web, VS Code and Chrome a drop area with a drag-over state.
purpose.why_it_exists: Chat is more useful with documents and images attached, and people expect both a button and drag and drop (doc: knowledge-base/data/area-briefs/008-basic-interactive-elements.md S8.29, S8.30).
purpose.who_uses_it: Anyone attaching a document, image or code file to a message.
problems_solved: Attaching without hunting for a hidden control.
Seeing that a drop will be accepted before releasing.
Being told when files are over the limit rather than losing them silently.
use_cases: Drag two PDFs onto the web chat and send a question about them.
On mobile, tap the add control and pick Photos or File.

purpose.who_uses_it: Every user on every app.

Errors without a way to recover.
Empty lists with no next step.
Long lists that load all at once.

features.summary: Lets a person choose which model answers and attach a file already stored in their library, narrowing long lists as they type. Web and Desktop share one menu; Mobile, CLI, VS Code and Chrome each have their own model picker. Only Web and Desktop have the stored-file picker, and it appears only in AGI Work mode.

purpose.what_it_does: Model picker: lists the models a person may use and switches the chat to the one they pick. A search box narrows the list. Models the plan cannot use are marked and lead to upgrade. Files menu (Web and Desktop only): shows the six most recent library files, searches the library as the person types, and attaches the chosen file to the message, or opens the device file dialog.
purpose.why_it_exists: The product is model agnostic and has hundreds of catalogue entries, so a flat list is unusable. People also reuse files they uploaded or generated earlier and should not have to upload them again. Both pickers must tell the truth about plan limits (brief S9.01, S9.02; doc: docs/product/experience-contract.md:776).
purpose.who_uses_it: Any signed-in or signed-out chat user choosing a model; paid users in AGI Work mode attaching stored files; testers checking plan locking.
problems_solved: Finding one model in a long list without scrolling.
Knowing before sending that a model needs a higher plan, instead of failing after sending.
Re-attaching a stored file without re-uploading it.
Not being told a model 'requires upgrade' while the plan is still loading.
use_cases: On Web, open the model menu in the chat box footer, type part of a name, click a result.
On Mobile, open the model sheet, search, tap an on-device model that is not downloaded and confirm the download.
In the CLI, run /model, type to filter, press Enter.
On Web in AGI Work mode, open Files, type a file name, click it to attach.

where_to_find_it: Web and Desktop (Desktop shows the hosted web app, doc: AGENTS.md section 5): model trigger in the chat box footer (ComposerFooter, heading 'Models') (apps/web/features/chat/components/Composer/ComposerFooter.tsx:206). Files button labelled 'Files' in the work bar under the chat box (apps/web/features/chat/components/Composer/ChatComposerNew.tsx:367, :7113).

established.statement: A picker lists selectable resources (files, projects, models, skills) and narrows the list as the user types a query.
A control lists the available models and switches the conversation to the one the user picks.

Picker eligibility agrees with the server's effective plan, deployment, model and route policy; catalogue failures settle into an error state with bounded retry; closing the picker cancels obsolete work.
Layout and display hacks must not own model facts; the model registry is the source of truth for model, capability, price and rollout.
A model the plan cannot use is shown locked with a label and clicking it opens upgrade (first-draft requirement, confirmed in Web code).

acceptance_criteria: Typing in the Web model search narrows the list and shows 'No models match' when nothing matches.
With the plan still loading, no row is marked locked or labelled 'requires upgrade'.
On a Free plan, clicking a locked model opens the upgrade flow and the selected model does not change.
Web Files search sends one request about 200 ms after typing stops and aborts the earlier request; the query string carries q and limit=6.
If /api/library fails the Files menu shows 'The library could not be loaded.'; if the file fetch fails the error stays in the menu and the menu stays open.
Closing the Files menu or the model menu clears the typed text and any error.
On Mobile, choosing a model from an effort row sets that effort as well as the model.
In the CLI, typing after opening filters rows without pressing '/' first; '/' refocuses search after arrow navigation.
inferred: The CLI should mark locked rows and warn before selecting them, since it keeps them selectable only to avoid an empty picker [inferred from model_picker.rs:199-205].
Silent no-op on a locked Mobile tap when native purchases are unavailable should give a message [inferred from ModelPickerSheet.tsx:466].
proposed: [proposed] Share one filter function between the Web short list and the catalogue so both rank the same way.
[proposed] Add a stored-file picker to Mobile chat that reuses the library picker-scope hook.
[proposed] Give the CLI the same locked-row notice that Web shows before sending.

execution_and_data_flow.models_and_providers: The picker lists models from the generated catalogue and does not name providers itself. Provider availability (degraded notices) is fetched when the picker opens (ComposerFooter.tsx:923-929). Whether a model is allowed depends on the plan through isModelAllowedForTier and getAllowedAutoModesForTier (apps/web/features/chat/lib/model-plan-admission.ts:21-30). Local models on Web/Desktop are chosen through a separate local selection path that says 'nothing leaves this Mac' (ComposerFooter.tsx:1274-1276). Own-key and managed routing is shown in CLI sections 'Your key' and 'Managed' (model_picker.rs:6-12).

access_and_usage.account: Web model picker opens for signed-out visitors too: a signed-out visitor is treated as Free (ComposerFooter.tsx:1038-1042). Files menu needs a signed-in account because /api/library resolves a user-scoped database (apps/web/app/api/library/route.ts:151).
access_and_usage.permissions: Files menu needs the canUseAgiWork capability and AGI Work mode (ChatComposerNew.tsx:1062-1067). /api/library only returns the caller's own files (route.ts:151, :166).
access_and_usage.subscription: Model locks come from the plan tier (modelLock, isModelAllowedForTier). The AGI Subscription decides eligible models; the picker shows a plan label and sends upgrade clicks to the host onUpgradeRequest. Mobile checks tier through useTierStore and the cloud waitlist (ModelPickerSheet.tsx:289-295). Chrome uses allowedAutoModes from managed access (managedModelPicker.ts:268-272).
access_and_usage.limits_and_metering: Library list is rate limited under the 'chat-conversation' bucket (route.ts:149). Attaching a file can be refused with a daily cap or burst limit, shown with the reset time (ComposerFilesMenu.tsx:117-138). Model rows may show a note that a model uses limits faster (ComposerFooter.tsx:692-694).
access_and_usage.flags: Free lane UI (useFreeLaneUiEnabled), free model promotion (useFreeModelPromotion) and free-quota models change what is locked (ComposerFooter.tsx:1049, :1203-1207). Mobile: NATIVE_PURCHASES_AVAILABLE decides whether a locked tap opens a plan screen (ModelPickerSheet.tsx:466).
access_and_usage.model_compatibility: On switch, the Web picker checks the request against the target model and holds the switch behind a notice when something would be dropped (ComposerFooter.tsx:1180-1186). The mobile compatibility notice in the chat input is a separate feature.
access_and_usage.provider_restrictions: VS Code: in own-key mode a model from a different provider than the route's key is locked with 'Add your <provider> key' (modelConstants.ts:182-205). CLI: Local and own-key rows are never tier locked (model_picker.rs:199-205).
access_and_usage.local_mode: Local models are listed and selectable without a paid plan: CLI marks them never locked; Mobile lists on-device models with a download step; Web/Desktop local models use a local selection. Whether sign-in is needed to open the picker in Local mode on Mobile was not established.

features.summary: Lets a person narrow what an answer may use and where it runs. Web research offers a source chooser at plan approval; each app has a way to pick a project; connectors show their linked accounts. In the code the account list is display only, so no account can be picked yet.

purpose.what_it_does: Source picker: during a deep research run on Web (and Desktop, which shows the web app), the person can add sites to include, sites to exclude, their files, or a connected app, as chips under 'Sources for this run'. Project picker: sets the project a chat runs in. Connected-account list: shows the accounts linked to a connector.
purpose.why_it_exists: People want answers drawn only from chosen places, chats filed in the right project, and clarity on which account a connector uses (brief S9.03, S9.04, S9.06).
purpose.who_uses_it: Paid users of research and AGI Work on Web/Desktop; project users on all six apps; connector users on Web and Mobile.
problems_solved: Research that wanders over the whole web when the user wants two sites.
Chats landing in no project, losing instructions and knowledge files.
Not knowing which account a connector is linked to.

features.summary: Lets a person switch between their Personal space and team workspaces (Web, Desktop, Mobile), and pick workspace members by name or email when sharing a project or placing a legal hold (Web, Desktop). CLI, VS Code and Chrome have neither. Web asks first when switching would end running work.

purpose.what_it_does: Workspace switcher: lists 'Personal' (Only you) and an 'Enterprise' group of organization workspaces, marks the active one, and changes it. Member picker: a search field that finds workspace members by name or email, supports one or many, and accepts pasted emails.
purpose.why_it_exists: Personal and enterprise content differ in who can read it, so the switch must be explicit and visible. Sharing and holds need a safe way to name people (brief S9.05, S9.11).
purpose.who_uses_it: Members of team or enterprise workspaces; workspace admins; project owners sharing a project.
problems_solved: Pasting into the wrong workspace.
Losing a half-written reply or unsaved work on a switch.
Typing member ids or emails by hand when sharing.
use_cases: Open the account menu on Web and switch from Personal to an enterprise workspace.

The user can pick the branch a coding session starts from or works on from a list of the repository's branches.

Web repository and branch pickers are partial because the switch is off: set AGI_E2B_EXECUTION=1 and E2B_API_KEY in production and redeploy, then live-check /code; AGI_MANAGED_COMPUTE_PRIVATE_BETA is on when unset and must not be set to 0.
A bad URL or branch shows an error and is not saved (first-draft requirement, confirmed).

acceptance_criteria: With no GitHub installation the first-run panel with two steps is shown.
Search narrows the repository list after about 250 ms and an unfinished earlier request is cancelled.
When more exist, the truncation text shows; when an installation cannot be read its name is listed.
A URL that is not a public https GitHub owner/repository shows the error and keeps the old selection.
A branch name with illegal characters shows the branch error.
Picking a repository fills its default branch.
On Desktop, picking another branch switches the folder to it, or shows 'branch is not in this repository'.
With the server switch off, starting a Web session shows a capability-unavailable message.
inferred: The Web chip list should say why repository choices are unavailable when the switch is off, instead of failing at session start [inferred from cloud-code-session-open.ts:44].
proposed: [proposed] Add a branch picker to the CLI for the current repository.
[proposed] Correct the brief: Mobile has repository and branch pickers.

features.summary: Four related controls: pick the speaker for voice replies (Web, Desktop), choose how far a permission reaches (API key scopes, approval policy), read in words what a connected app or the assistant may do, and approve or deny an action in an inline card or CLI overlay. The microphone cannot be picked.

purpose.what_it_does: Device picker: on Web voice, lists audio output devices and routes sound to the chosen one. Permission-scope picker: API key scopes on Web and the three-way tool approval policy on Mobile and elsewhere. Permission summary: plain sentences on connector scopes and on what the assistant can use. Approval card: shows the action, its request (command text, code or file diff) and offers Allow, Allow for this chat and Deny.
purpose.why_it_exists: People must stay in control of what the assistant may do and must be told in plain words before it acts (brief S9.10, S9.31, S9.32; doc: docs/product/experience-contract.md:397).
purpose.who_uses_it: Everyone who runs tools, connectors or voice; API users making keys.
problems_solved: Granting too much access to an API key.
Approving an action without seeing it.
Not knowing what a connector can do.
Sound playing on the wrong device.
use_cases: Create an API key with only 'Read usage'.
Set action approvals to 'Ask before every action'.
Open a connector and read 'Permissions requested' with Read or Write badges.
See an approval card for a command, read its text, choose 'Allow for this chat'.

established.statement: The user can pick which device is used (microphone, speaker, camera or paired computer) from a list.
When granting access the user chooses how far the permission reaches: capabilities, or once versus always.
One view states in plain language what the assistant or a connected app is allowed to do (scopes, autonomy, allowed sites or tools).
An inline card names the action and offers approve and deny; the choice resumes or stops the run.
High-risk actions do not offer 'approve for chat'; an expired approval shows no buttons.
The approval card is part of the experience contract.

acceptance_criteria: With two or more output devices the Web voice view shows the audio menu; with fewer it shows nothing.
Choosing a device calls setSinkId and marks it checked.

On a high-risk approval 'Allow for this chat' is absent and the high-risk notice is shown.
An expired approval shows the expired message, no Allow or Deny buttons.
Allow resumes the run; Deny stops it and the decision is sent for every pending call.
Mobile 'Skip approvals' is disabled when the workspace forbids it.
The CLI overlay answers No on Esc and High-risk calls are excluded from Allow All.

steps.what_happens: The browser lists output devices and listens for device changes; no server call.
The agent run stops on a tool that needs consent and the card is drawn from the paused tool entry.
A click records the decision, updates the tool entry, then posts run_id and tool_approvals to the resume path and streams the continued answer.
A newer turn marks the paused one expired; decisions on it are ignored.
Action approvals policy is loaded and saved to the account; mobile syncs it.
For desktop-side actions the approval can also arrive on the device ('Approve it if your desktop asks').
CLI shows the overlay locally and returns the choice to the agent loop.

features.summary: Sets how a scheduled task repeats, shows 'Step X of N' in guided flows, and runs first-time setup. Web offers eight frequencies; Mobile and Chrome offer once, daily, weekly and monthly; the CLI takes a cron text. The Web welcome wizard has two steps and saves a name and work description.

purpose.what_it_does: Recurrence editor: a Frequency control with matching fields (time, weekdays, day of month, interval, cron, recurrence rule) that creates a schedule the cloud runs. Stepper: shows the step number out of the total. Setup wizard: ordered first-run steps that save the person's answers.
purpose.why_it_exists: People need to say 'every weekday at nine' without writing cron; first-time users need a short guided start (brief S9.12, S9.22, S9.23; doc: docs/product/experience-contract.md:774, :790).
purpose.who_uses_it: Users of scheduled tasks on Web, Desktop, Mobile, CLI and Chrome; every new user at first sign-in.
problems_solved: Writing cron by hand.
Wrong time zone or daylight-saving errors.
New users not knowing where to start.
use_cases: Create a weekly schedule on Monday and Friday at 08:00.
Create a one-time schedule for a future date on Mobile.
First visit to Web: enter a preferred name and work, continue, pick a starter prompt.
CLI first run: trust the folder, sign in, choose a model, choose a permission mode.

screens_and_controls: Web Frequency options: 'One Time', 'Daily', 'Weekly', 'Monthly', 'Interval', 'Custom Cron', 'Recurrence Rule', 'When An Event Happens' (ScheduleForm.tsx:306-313).

Fields by choice: 'Run At' (one time), 'Repeat Every' and 'Interval Unit' (interval), 'Local Time' (daily, weekly, monthly), 'Days of Week', 'Day of Month', 'Cron Expression', 'Recurrence Rule' (ScheduleForm.tsx:320-480).
Mobile: choose Once, Daily, Weekly or Monthly; weekly needs a day and once needs a future date (apps/mobile/src/features/schedules/components/ScheduleForm.tsx:117-155).

steps.what_happens: Person fills the schedule form; the browser builds the payload and checks fields and time zone.
The server validates the recurrence, builds cron, once, interval, rrule or event timing and computes the first run.
A periodic sweep runs due schedules in the cloud; a run uses managed models and may spend credits.
Welcome page checks identity, terms and onboarding status on the server.
Finishing the wizard reads the stored namespace, removes the use-case field, merges name, work and completed time, and saves it.
CLI writes a local marker file when setup ends.
Mobile onboarding stores the 'onboarding-done' flag on the device; the optional on-device model download in the same flow fetches from the model's download URL (an outside host, not traced further).

steps.what_happens: The person opens Library or changes a tab, sort, query or the deleted toggle; the view builds query parameters limit, sort, surface, kind, origin, q and deleted.
The web wrapper sends GET /api/library with the session cookie.
The server rate-limits, opens a user-scoped database connection, validates the query, reads rows plus one, and maps them to items.
On the first non-deleted page the server also reads the storage meter, the download meter (based on the entitled plan) and the byte breakdown; failures of the meters are logged and skipped.
The client validates the response against the shared schema and shows the items; a stale response is dropped by a sequence counter.
A click opens the viewer; image, video and PDF load from /api/files/<id>; text and tables load a preview; an artifact is fetched and shown if 512 KB or less.
Mobile and CLI call the same endpoint with their own client and render their own list.

features.summary: Compound parts that show and steer work: an activity timeline under answers, a task board by stage, a work-session progress panel, artifact version history with restore, a code diff panel with include and discard, interactive cards inside answers, and a resizable side panel. The docking manager exists only through VS Code itself.

purpose.what_it_does: Shows what a run is doing in time order (packages/ui/unified-chat/src/components/AgentActivityTimeline.tsx:679-905), lays cloud tasks out in stage columns with actions (packages/ui/unified-chat/src/components/tasks/TasksBoard.tsx:46-80), lists artifact versions and restores one (apps/web/features/chat/components/artifacts/ArtifactVersionHistory.tsx:61-183), shows file diffs to include or discard (apps/web/features/code/components/CodeChangesPanel.tsx:39-118), renders cards the person operates inside answers (apps/web/features/chat/components/messages/InteractiveCardBlock.tsx:31-52) and lets the side panel be resized by pointer or keyboard (apps/web/features/chat/components/SidePanelResizeHandle.tsx:14-72).
purpose.why_it_exists: Long agent runs and edits must be visible, reversible and reviewable before the person accepts them (doc: knowledge-base/data/area-briefs/009-compound-interface-components.md S9.19, S9.26, S9.27).
purpose.who_uses_it: Anyone running agent work or editing artifacts and code on Web, the desktop window, Mobile, CLI, VS Code and Chrome.

established.statement: The steps of a run show in time order, each with its state and, where known, how long it took.
Tasks lay out as a board with a column per status.
A running task shows a card with current state and progress that updates while it runs.
The version panel lists saved versions (when, what) and lets the user open or restore one.
Changes show as a diff with added and removed lines marked, readable before accepting.
An answer can embed a widget operated in place; the choice or state feeds back into the conversation.
Two panes can be resized by pointer and by keyboard.
Panels can be moved to left, right, bottom or floating and the layout keeps the arrangement.
An action that cannot be undone asks first and names the consequence.

acceptance_criteria: Run an agent turn: the timeline lists steps in the order they started, and a screen reader hears status changes.
Switch Tasks to Board: each run appears in the column for its state; Queued, Running, Needs approval and Done always show.
On a card in Needs approval, Approve and Deny act on that run and focus stays sensible after it moves.
Edit an artifact twice: Version history shows three versions, newest first, with 'N lines added, M removed'.
Restore Version 1: a confirm dialog appears; after confirm a new latest version holds Version 1's content and versions in between remain.
Open Changes: expanding a file shows added lines and removed lines marked differently; Discard asks before acting.
Focus the resize separator and press Left: the panel widens by 24 px; Home sets 280, End sets 900; aria-valuenow follows.
Operate an interactive card: the choice appears in the conversation as the next input.
inferred: Timeline step durations should show per step when the data has a start and end [inferred from 'where known'].
The board should keep the same stage names on every app [inferred].
proposed: [proposed] Align the VS Code tree group names with the web board stages.
[proposed] Decide whether the docking manager is wanted for Web and desktop, or mark S9.25 not applicable because VS Code supplies it.
[proposed] Add unit tests for ArtifactVersionHistory, SidePanelResizeHandle and CodeChangesPanel; none were found.

steps.what_happens: Chat streaming events build the activity state on the device; the timeline renders it.
The Tasks page loads cloud agent runs and groups them by stage on the device.
Approve, deny, pause, resume, cancel and archive send a request for that run; the board updates when the state changes.
Version history reads the versions held in the artifact store; Restore adds a new latest version and removes the stored draft.
Changes panel receives the diff from the cloud code API, parses it and shows it; discard and commit are requests to that API.
A card choice is sent back to the conversation through the card resume hook or the answer follow-up.
Resize writes the clamped width to the UI store, which saves it in the browser.

access_and_usage.account: Task board and cloud runs need an account; local agent tasks have a separate panel in desktop Local mode (DesktopShellV3.tsx:~614-617).
access_and_usage.permissions: Approve and deny act on tool approvals the run asked for; discard asks first (CodeChangesPanel.tsx:314-319).

access_and_usage.limits_and_metering: Timeline shows a page of steps and lets the person load earlier ones (AgentActivityTimeline.tsx:883-899). Side panel width limited 280 to 900 (uiStore.ts:6-7).

access_and_usage.model_compatibility: Interactive cards depend on the answer carrying a card of a known kind; unknown kinds are not rendered by the registry [inferred] (InteractiveCardBlock.tsx:34-52).
access_and_usage.local_mode: Desktop Local mode uses the 'agent-tasks' panel instead of the cloud board (DesktopShellV3.tsx:~614-617). Timeline and version history work from device state; whether Local mode feeds them was not established.

features.summary: Two checks around an answer. The source inspector shows each source's site, title and excerpt and opens it. The model warning checks the chosen model against the conversation and tells the person, inside the model picker, that images, tools, files or history will not fit, before they switch or send.

purpose.what_it_does: Lets a person open the sources behind an answer through a 'Sources' button or a citation chip (apps/web/features/chat/components/research/ResearchPanel.tsx:596-632; packages/ui/unified-chat/src/components/markdown/CitationChip.tsx:85-150). Before a model is used, it compares the request with the model's catalogue limits and shows plain warnings (apps/web/features/chat/components/Composer/model-compatibility.ts:97-207).
purpose.why_it_exists: People must be able to check where an answer came from, and must not lose images, tools or older messages silently when a model cannot handle them (doc: knowledge-base/data/area-briefs/009-compound-interface-components.md S9.28, S9.34).
purpose.who_uses_it: Anyone reading cited answers or choosing between models on Web, the desktop window and Mobile (Chrome for sources).
problems_solved: Trusting an answer without seeing the source (CitationChip.tsx:85-116).
A model that cannot read images ignoring them without notice (model-compatibility.ts:187-192).
A smaller context model dropping older messages (model-compatibility.ts:181-186).
use_cases: Click 'Sources' under an answer and read each site, title and excerpt.
Hover a citation chip to see the excerpt, click to open the page.
Switch to a model that cannot call tools while web search is on: see 'cannot call tools' and choose Switch anyway or keep the current model.
Attach a PDF while a free quota model is selected: see that Free Auto will answer.

steps.what_happens: The page mounts the hook, which requests /api/usage with the session cookie unless one is already in flight.
The server rate limits, resolves the user and builds the managed usage summary from the subscription system.
The client parses the response with a typed parser and publishes it to every subscriber.
Every five minutes, or when the person becomes active after that time, a background request refreshes; failure sets stale only.
Percent and reset text are computed from the response; a minute timer re-renders reset countdowns.
Use reset sends a request to the limit resets API and refreshes.
The CLI reads a stored sign-in token and requests the account usage; with no credential or bring-your-own-key it prints a local-only note.

steps.what_happens: The bell mounts for a signed-in session and polls the feed every minute while the person is active.
The server lists the user's notifications by keyset cursor with an optional unread filter.
Opening a row updates local state at once and sends PATCH with the id; failure is ignored for single rows.
Mark all sends PATCH with all true; on failure the list rolls back and an alert shows.
The palette shortcut is caught before page handlers, loads the palette code on first use and toggles it.
Typed text filters local commands; after 200 ms and 2 or more characters the palette calls /api/search for 10 results.
Activity: the settings query calls /api/settings/activity with the auth token; the server selects from security_audit_logs for the user.
Connector cards combine the connector catalogue with the account's connections; Connect starts OAuth, Disconnect removes the connection.

features.summary: Lets a signed-in person make a new project and change the title of a chat or project. Web and the Electron desktop share one web implementation. Mobile and CLI have their own. Chrome can rename chats in its history list but no project create was found. VS Code has a New Project command but no session rename was found.

purpose.what_it_does: Creates a project (a named folder for chats, files and instructions) in the account, and saves a new title for an existing chat or project. Create asks for a name. Rename edits the title in place or in a prompt.
purpose.why_it_exists: People need to group work into named projects and fix the auto-generated titles of chats. The brief says create must ask for a name and make the project in the account, and rename must save the new title (doc: knowledge-base/data/area-briefs/010-modal-and-dialog-inventory.md, S10.01 and S10.02).
purpose.who_uses_it: Any signed-in user of web, the Electron desktop, mobile, CLI, VS Code and Chrome. Local-only mobile users can create local projects.
problems_solved: A new topic has no home until a project exists.
Auto titles are often unhelpful and hard to find later.
Developers using the terminal need a way to name projects and sessions without opening the web app.
use_cases: On web, open Projects, choose New project, type a name and create it; the page opens the new project.
In a chat header on web, open the title menu, choose Rename, type, press Enter.
In the CLI, run the projects create command with a name, or /rename with a session id and a new title.
On mobile, long-press a chat, choose Rename, type, save.

established.statement: A create-project dialog or command asks for a name and creates the project in the account.
The user opens rename on a conversation, edits the title in a field or prompt, and the new title is saved.
Chat lifecycle changes must survive reload; failed persistence is visible and recoverable.
Forms keep input on failure (stated for feedback; applied here by analogy).

acceptance_criteria: Creating a project with a valid name adds it to the Projects list on web without a reload.
Creating with an empty name cannot be submitted.
Renaming a chat updates the title in the header and sidebar at once and after reload.
If the save fails, an error is shown; the person can retry without retyping (target; not met today on mobile or web chat).
A project count at the plan limit gives a clear refusal message.
A signed-out or Local-only CLI refuses account project commands with a message naming the mode.
inferred: The brief's rule 'a failed save must keep the typed text' is not met on mobile, where the editor closes first [inferred from useProjectEditor.ts:160-200].
Desktop users get the web behaviour because Electron loads the web app [inferred from main.ts:1065-1067 and AGENTS.md].
proposed: [proposed] Keep the mobile editor open until the first sync acknowledgement or show a visible failed state on the row.
[proposed] Keep the web rename input open with the draft when onRename returns false.
[proposed] Add a session rename command to VS Code that reuses the fork name prompt pattern.

steps.what_happens: Person submits the create dialog on web or Electron desktop.
The client sends POST /api/projects with CSRF token; the server checks rate limit, feature gate and plan limit, inserts the row under a quota guard.
Client adds the returned project to its store and navigates to the project page.
Chat rename: the client shows the new title, then PATCHes the conversation; a false result rolls back the title.

features.summary: Files a chat under a project (or removes it) and makes an independent copy of a chat or project. Web, mobile and Chrome can move a chat. Web branches a chat as a copy and duplicates a project; mobile duplicates a chat; CLI and VS Code fork a session. The brief's 'mobile missing' is wrong in the code.

purpose.what_it_does: Move changes which project a chat belongs to. Duplicate creates a separate copy (a chat branch, a forked session, or a project with its settings and files) so the original is untouched.
purpose.why_it_exists: People reorganise work and want to try a variation without losing the original. The brief requires move to pick a project and file the chat there, and duplicate to create an independent copy and say where it is (doc: knowledge-base/data/area-briefs/010-modal-and-dialog-inventory.md, S10.03, S10.04).

problems_solved: A chat started outside a project cannot otherwise be filed.
Experimenting on a long thread risks the original.

features.summary: Hides a chat in Archived with Undo, or removes a chat or project after a confirmation that names it. Delete on web and mobile Cloud is a soft delete, restorable for 30 days from Recently deleted. A separate permanent-delete command with its own modal exists only for VS Code sessions; CLI uses one confirm.

purpose.what_it_does: Archive moves a chat out of the main list and offers Undo and a way to see archived chats. Delete asks first, naming the item and the consequence, then removes it. Project delete moves its chats out and deletes its source files.
purpose.why_it_exists: People tidy their lists but must not lose data by accident. The brief requires confirmation or undo, a named item, and plain wording about what cannot be undone (doc: knowledge-base/data/area-briefs/010-modal-and-dialog-inventory.md, S10.05 to S10.07). AGENTS.md section 9 requires a named consequence and a Trash or archive step before permanent removal (doc: AGENTS.md).
purpose.who_uses_it: All signed-in users on web, Electron desktop, mobile, Chrome, CLI and VS Code.
problems_solved: Cluttered chat lists.
Accidental deletion.
Leftover project files after a project is dropped.

Delete a chat from the sidebar menu and confirm the named dialog.

established.statement: Archiving asks to confirm, or confirms afterwards with a way to undo, and says where archived items can be found.
Deleting asks for confirmation that names the item before anything is removed.
An irreversible delete says plainly that it cannot be undone and needs an explicit second confirmation.

An action a user cannot undo asks first and the question names the consequence; an agent never destroys data on its own; chats are archived or moved to Recently deleted; permanent removal needs an explicit user action naming what is lost.
Chat lifecycle: archive, restore and delete preserve lineage after reload; failed persistence is visible and recoverable.

acceptance_criteria: Delete never starts without a dialog that names the chat or project, with a plain fallback phrase when untitled.
Cancel leaves the item untouched.
Archive hides the chat, shows Undo and a way to open archived chats, and Undo restores the chat (and its pin).
Deleting a project moves its chats to All Chats and removes its source files, and the copy says so.
On failure the row stays and an error is shown.
Deleted web chats appear in Recently deleted and Restore puts them back within 30 days.
Wording of every delete states the real recoverability (soft or permanent) accurately.
inferred: Because web delete is soft, a second confirmation is only needed for a true purge, which was not found [inferred from DELETE_CONVERSATION_SQL and DeletedChatsSection.tsx:60].
The web 'cannot be undone' wording conflicts with the 30-day restore window [inferred].
proposed: [proposed] Align web delete copy with the 30-day restore window, or add a distinct 'Delete forever' action in Recently deleted with a typed or second confirm.
[proposed] Give CLI and mobile Local deletes a Trash step as AGENTS.md section 9 asks.

steps.what_happens: Person chooses Delete; the shell opens the named confirmation dialog.
On confirm the client calls deleteConversation; the server sets deleted_at, clears the cached compaction summary and returns.
A false result produces a toast 'Could not delete this conversation' and the row stays.
Archive writes archived=true through PATCH; the toast offers Undo that restores and re-pins.
CLI session delete resolves the id, confirms, then removes the local session files.
Chrome delete queues an account deletion message to the background worker and deletes the local copy.

features.summary: Creates a link to a chat snapshot, a file (system share sheet on mobile) or a published artifact page; shows who can open it; and revokes or takes it down. Web chat links last 1, 7 or 30 days and can be public or workspace-only. Mobile manages links in Settings; CLI lists and revokes; Chrome shares from history.

purpose.what_it_does: Chat share publishes a read-only snapshot at a link. Publish puts an artifact (page, app, code, diagram, text) on a live URL. Access controls choose who can open it and when it expires. Revoke or Unpublish makes the link stop working.
purpose.why_it_exists: People need to show a chat or generated page to others and to take it back. The brief requires the dialog to state who can open the link, allow revoke with confirmation, and fail without a half link (doc: knowledge-base/data/area-briefs/010-modal-and-dialog-inventory.md, S10.08 to S10.12).
purpose.who_uses_it: Signed-in users on web, Electron desktop, mobile, CLI and Chrome. Workspace members use the workspace audience.
problems_solved: Sending a conversation to someone without an account copy.
Publishing a generated page.
Withdrawing access that was granted by link.
use_cases: Web: share a chat, choose 7 days and Anyone with the link, copy.
Web: change audience to Everyone in your workspace.
Mobile: Settings, Shared Links, Revoke.
CLI: agi artifacts publish <id> --audience workspace; agi shares revoke <token>.

established.statement: A share dialog creates a link to the conversation, shows it for copying, and states who can open it.
The user can share a file or folder from the library by link or the system share sheet.
An artifact share dialog publishes to a link, lets the user copy it, choose who can open it and take it down.
A publish dialog puts a generated app or page on a live URL and hands back the link.
For a shared link the user can see its access (who, expiry) and change or revoke it.
Public sharing: preview what will be exposed; verify link access signed-out; revocation and expiry stop access; workspace restrictions are enforced on the server.

acceptance_criteria: The dialog states who can open the link before it is copied.
A created chat link opens in a signed-out browser until expiry.
Revoke asks first and, once done, the link no longer opens.
A failed create leaves no link in the list.
Changing audience to workspace-only stops signed-out access to the same URL.
Publish returns a URL and Unpublish makes it stop resolving.
Local-mode mobile cannot create a link and says why.
inferred: A temporary chat cannot be shared [inferred from TEMPORARY_CHAT_SHARE_REFUSAL import in use-share-conversation.ts:23].
Share and publish are cloud-only features, because the server stores the snapshot [inferred from /api/share and /api/artifacts/publish].
proposed: [proposed] Add a take-down control in the artifact preview next to Copy link.
[proposed] Offer an expiry choice on mobile chat share to match web.
[proposed] Add VS Code share and publish commands or record them as out of scope.

steps.what_happens: Web builds a snapshot of the visible messages and artifacts and posts it with the chosen expiry.
The server rate-limits, redacts secrets and local paths, checks the workspace policy, stores the snapshot and returns the token and URL.
A visitor opens the share page; GET /api/share/[token] returns the snapshot if not expired and the audience allows.
Revoke sends DELETE; the old URL stays dead and a new share gets a new URL.
Artifact publish posts the content to /api/artifacts/publish; moderation and outbound-content checks run before storage.
Mobile library share downloads the file then hands it to the operating system share sheet.

features.summary: Lets a workspace admin invite people by email with a role, renew or revoke pending invitations, change a member's role after confirmation, and lets the owner hand ownership to another member after a fresh identity check. Needs a Team or Enterprise plan. Web and mobile have all three; CLI none found.

purpose.what_it_does: Invites people to a workspace, manages pending invitations, changes roles (Viewer, Member, Admin, Owner), and transfers the owner role while the old owner keeps a seat with a chosen lower role.
purpose.why_it_exists: Teams need controlled access. The brief requires invite with email and role, role change with confirmation and server enforcement, and a transfer that checks identity and refuses transfer to self (doc: knowledge-base/data/area-briefs/010-modal-and-dialog-inventory.md, S10.13 to S10.15).
purpose.who_uses_it: Workspace owners and admins on a Team or Enterprise plan.
problems_solved: Adding colleagues safely.
Limiting what each person can do.
Handing over a workspace when the owner leaves.
use_cases: Admin invites a colleague as Member from Team settings.
Admin renews an expired invitation.
Admin changes a Viewer to Admin and confirms.
Owner transfers ownership and becomes Admin.

where_to_find_it: Web: Settings, Team section; cards 'Invite teammate' (description 'Invitations expire after 7 days.'), member list, pending invitations, and 'Workspace ownership' (apps/web/features/settings/sections/TeamSection.tsx:976,1190-1215,1405-1510).
Desktop public window: the same web Team settings (doc: AGENTS.md section 5).
Desktop internal Tauri CloudTeamSection has add-member and role select; not the public window (apps/desktop/src/features/settings/cloud/CloudTeamSection.tsx:45-130).

Mobile: Settings, Workspace screen with 'Invite by email', 'Send invitation', member row role picker 'Role for <name>', 'Remove from workspace?' (apps/mobile/src/features/team/WorkspaceAdministration.tsx:112-200; apps/mobile/src/features/team/RolePickerModal.tsx:60-110; apps/mobile/app/(app)/settings/workspace.tsx:270-320).
prerequisites: Signed in; an admin or owner role in the workspace (TeamSection.tsx canAdminister; workspace.tsx:340-342).
An active Team or Enterprise subscription; otherwise the server answers SUBSCRIPTION_REQUIRED (apps/web/app/api/settings/team/team-admin-access.ts:70-82).
Free seats; web shows 'No seats are available. Revoke an invitation, remove a member, or buy more seats.' (TeamSection.tsx:1040-1046).
Ownership transfer: only the Primary Owner, plus a step-up identity check (apps/web/app/api/settings/organization/transfer-ownership/route.ts:44-80).
screens_and_controls: Web invite form: field labelled 'Invitee email', select 'Invitation role' with Member role, Viewer role, Admin role (TeamSection.tsx:998-1024).
Pending rows: 'Renew invitation for <email>' and 'Revoke invitation for <email>' buttons (TeamSection.tsx:1186-1215).

Member row: role select, then confirm dialog 'Change member role?' with the text '<name> will become <Role>. The workspace must always retain at least one owner.' and button 'Change role' (TeamSection.tsx:1349-1362,1640-1665).
Ownership card: 'New owner' select, 'Your role afterwards' select (Admin, Member, Viewer), button 'Transfer ownership', confirm 'Transfer ownership?' (TeamSection.tsx:1405-1510).
Mobile role picker: radio options with permission list, a warning for ownership, buttons Cancel and 'Save role' or 'Transfer ownership' (RolePickerModal.tsx:70-130).
journey: 1. Admin opens Team settings or the Workspace screen.
2. Enters an email and role and sends the invitation; a link and delivery status are shown (web).
3. Pending invitations list with Renew and Revoke.
4. For a role change, picks a new role and confirms.
5. For ownership, the owner picks a member and their own new role, confirms, and completes a step-up identity check.
6. A success message shows ('Ownership was transferred. Your role is now ...').

Web: invitation link with delivery status and a copy button (TeamSection.tsx:600-625).

Non-admins do not see invite or role controls.

features.summary: Three input choices. Sources: before a research run starts, the person chooses sites, files and connected apps it may use (web and mobile). Upload: Add photos and files opens the device file chooser (all apps). Screen share: Electron shows a picker before any capture; the web composer's live-screen entry was not found mounted.

purpose.what_it_does: Sources limits what a Deep Research run may read. Upload attaches files from the device to the next message. Screen share lets the person pick a screen or window before anything is captured.
purpose.why_it_exists: People want control over where an answer's evidence comes from, need to give the assistant their files, and must stay in control of what the screen capture sees. The brief states these three rules (doc: knowledge-base/data/area-briefs/010-modal-and-dialog-inventory.md, S10.16, S10.17, S10.35).
purpose.who_uses_it: Anyone using chat; research sources apply to Deep Research users.
problems_solved: Research that reads unwanted sites.
Getting a document into a chat.
Accidentally exposing the wrong screen.
use_cases: Restrict a research run to one site and never another.
Attach a PDF and ask a question.
Capture a screenshot for feedback by choosing a window.

features.summary: Lets a signed-in person link outside accounts (connectors), see the linked account, reconnect an expired link, install or update plugins after seeing the permissions they ask for, and import or edit their own skills. Web and Electron Desktop share one directory panel. Mobile and CLI have smaller screens. VS Code and Chrome have none.

purpose.what_it_does: Connectors link an outside service to the AGI account through the service's own sign-in. Plugins add bundles of skills and tools. Skills are saved instructions the assistant can load. This feature covers the dialogs for connecting, reconnecting, showing the linked account, installing or updating a plugin, and importing or editing a skill.
purpose.why_it_exists: The assistant can only act on a person's cloud drive, mail or code host after that person grants access. Plugins and skills extend what it can do, so the person must see what a plugin asks for and must be able to write their own skills.
purpose.who_uses_it: Signed-in people on web, Electron Desktop, mobile and CLI. Workspace admins also control which plugins are allowed.
problems_solved: Granting access to an outside service without sharing a password
Recovering when an access grant expires or is revoked
Knowing what a plugin can do before it is installed
Adding a personal skill without a developer tool
use_cases: Connect a cloud drive, then ask chat to read a file from it
Reconnect Google Drive after the grant is revoked, keeping tool permissions
Install a plugin and read its permission list first
Import a SKILL.md or a zipped skill folder, then edit its description

established.statement: Connect runs the service's real authorization and ends with the account connected.
An expired connection offers reconnect that re-runs authorization and keeps its settings.
When a service has several accounts, a dialog lets the user pick which to use or make default.
Install and update show the permissions a plugin requires and ask the user to accept them.
Skill import ends with a usable skill; edit saves name, description and instructions.
An action a user cannot undo asks first and names the consequence.

acceptance_criteria: Connect a supported connector on web: after approval the connector appears as connected and chat can call one of its tools
Revoke the grant at the service: the connector shows a reconnect action beside Disconnect; reconnecting keeps its tool permissions
With two accounts linked to one service, the person can choose the default account
Installing a plugin that asks for permissions shows each permission before install and installs only after acceptance
Updating to a version with new permissions names the new ones
Importing a zip with SKILL.md in the wrong place shows the layout message and creates nothing
Editing a skill's description and saving shows the new description after reload
Disconnect names what is lost before it runs

features.summary: Warns when a chosen model cannot handle the chat (images, tools, length), warns when a chat nears its context limit, explains a reached usage limit with the reset time and next step, and lets people compare plans, cancel and update a card. Paid purchase is held behind a waitlist. Cancel and card changes open an outside billing portal. Mobile billing is switched off.

purpose.what_it_does: Shows notices and dialogs around model choice, chat length, usage limits and plan billing so the person knows what will happen before it does.
purpose.why_it_exists: Models differ in images, tools and context size. Limits and plans cost money. Silent trimming or silent refusals would confuse people and could bill them without notice.
purpose.who_uses_it: Every signed-in person. Free and paid users see limit notices. Billing controls are for the account owner.
problems_solved: Switching to a model that drops the images or tools in a chat
Chats that exceed the model's window and lose old messages
Not knowing why a request was refused or when it works again
Not knowing when paid access ends after cancelling
use_cases: Switch model in the web composer with images attached and get a warning first
Hit a usage limit and see the limit, reset time and an upgrade or switch option
Compare plans in the upgrade dialog, or join the waitlist while paid upgrades are closed
Cancel a plan from Billing settings

features.summary: Before a sensitive account action, a dialog asks the person to prove who they are again. The server refuses the action without a fresh signed proof. Separately, when a tool could send private chat data to an outside place, the approval card says so and names the destination. CLI has no such approval.

purpose.what_it_does: Step-up asks for a password, email code, passkey or second-factor code and issues a short-lived signed grant that the server demands for listed actions. Data-transfer approval pauses a tool call that could carry private data out and asks the person to allow or deny it.
purpose.why_it_exists: A stolen session should not be able to delete an account or move ownership. A web page or tool result that tricks the model should not be able to send private chat content to a stranger.
purpose.who_uses_it: Account owners, workspace admins, and anyone using tools that reach outside services.
problems_solved: Session theft turning into account takeover
Prompt injection making a tool send private data out
Unattended runs approving risky sends with nobody present
use_cases: Delete the account and be asked to confirm identity
Transfer workspace ownership
Approve a web fetch that could carry private data to a site
Browser assistant stops on a banking site and asks

steps.what_happens: Client sends the sensitive request; server finds no valid grant header and replies 403 STEP_UP_REQUIRED
Dialog collects the factor from the person and verifies it with the identity provider
Client asks /api/auth/step-up for a signed grant
Client replays the request with header x-step-up-token; server verifies action, user and resource
Tool loop evaluates the gate for each tool call and emits an approval-requested event with risk level high
Person answers on the card; answer goes to the approve route and the loop resumes

features.summary: Gives every control in the Web, Desktop, Mobile, VS Code and Chrome apps a spoken name, gives each screen a top heading, and tells a screen reader whether a tool step is running, done, failed or waiting for approval. Approve and Deny buttons carry names. The CLI has its own screen-reader mode (see F011-04 and F011-06).

purpose.what_it_does: Makes controls, headings and tool or approval status readable by a screen reader. Names come from visible text or an aria-label on web-based surfaces, and from accessibilityLabel and accessibilityRole on mobile. Tool steps and approval cards expose their state as text, not only as a colour or icon.
purpose.why_it_exists: Blind and low-vision people cannot use an icon-only button or an unlabelled approval card. The product requires every icon-only control to have an accessible name (doc: docs/product/experience-contract.md:168) and lists screen-reader checks as a release gate (doc: docs/product/experience-contract.md:750).
purpose.who_uses_it: People who use VoiceOver, TalkBack, NVDA, JAWS or other assistive technology, on Web, Desktop (which shows the hosted web app), Mobile, the VS Code extension and the Chrome extension. Also testers and engineers who audit names.
problems_solved: An icon-only button is read as 'button' with no purpose.
A tool run that waits for approval looks idle to someone who cannot see the card.
A screen has no heading to jump to.
use_cases: A screen-reader user reaches Allow and Deny on a tool approval card in web chat and hears their text.
A VoiceOver user on the phone opens the agent activity list and hears 'Show agent activity: <summary>' with an expanded or collapsed state.
A VS Code user tabs through the sidebar and every icon button has a name such as Sessions, Settings, New chat.
A user jumps by heading to the conversation title (web h1).

where_to_find_it: Web and Desktop (Electron shows the hosted web app, CLOUD_APP_ORIGIN) chat: conversation title is an h1 in the shared header, with buttons 'Rename conversation' and 'Conversation options' (apps/web/features/chat/components/ConversationTitleMenu.tsx:119,140; packages/ui/unified-chat/src/components/ConversationHeader.tsx:88-92). WebChatPage also renders an sr-only h1 (apps/web/features/chat/pages/WebChatPage.tsx:7313).

Web and Desktop: the 'Agent activity' section is a button named 'Show agent activity: <summary>' or 'Hide agent activity: <summary>' (packages/ui/unified-chat/src/components/AgentActivityTimeline.tsx:869,877-884). Tool approval buttons read 'Allow', 'Allow for this chat', 'Deny' (packages/ui/unified-chat/src/components/ToolCallCard.tsx:412-436; packages/contracts/types/src/tool-approval-policy.ts:23-32).

Mobile: agent activity row named 'Show agent activity: <summary>' / 'Hide ...'; each step 'title, status'; approvals are 'Approve <tool> action', 'Approve <step>', 'Deny <step>', 'Reject <tool>' (apps/mobile/src/features/chat/components/AgentActivityTimeline.tsx:417-418,1034-1044; apps/mobile/src/shared/components/ApprovalModal.tsx:222; apps/mobile/src/features/companion/components/DispatchTaskReply.tsx:304,313; apps/mobile/src/features/companion/components/CodeSessionParts.tsx:268,293; apps/mobile/src/features/companion/components/AgentDashboard.tsx:422,434).

VS Code sidebar: icon buttons 'Sessions', 'Settings', 'New chat', 'More actions', 'Stop response', 'Send' and a visually hidden h2 'Conversation' above the transcript (apps/extension-vscode/src/features/sidebar-webview/webviewContent.ts:2928-2942,3161,3365-3366).
Chrome side panel: composer controls 'Message AGI', 'Send message', 'Add attachment', 'Voice input' (apps/extension/__tests__/side-panel-a11y.test.ts:19-27 asserts them in source).

Mobile ApprovalModal does not set accessibilityViewIsModal; it is on a pending list of five modal files, so VoiceOver and TalkBack can keep reading the screen behind it (apps/mobile/__tests__/modal-accessibility-semantics.test.ts:13-19; apps/mobile/src/shared/components/ApprovalModal.tsx:110 has <Modal without that prop).
Announcement and many label strings are English literals, not translated (AgentActivityTimeline.tsx:369-384; apps/mobile/src/features/chat/components/AgentActivityTimeline.tsx:1043,1124).

established.statement: Every interactive control exposes an accessible name (visible text, aria-label or platform equivalent) that says what it does.
Each screen has a top heading and sections use nested headings, so screen-reader users can jump by heading.
Tool steps and approval requests expose their state (running, done, failed, waiting for approval) to assistive tech, with labelled approve and deny controls.
Every icon-only control has an accessible name and tooltip where discoverability matters.
Keyboard, screen reader, focus, touch, reduced motion and contrast are verified before release.
Failure of a name shows as a missing name, not as silence (from the draft 'should' list).

acceptance_criteria: With a screen reader on web chat, every button in the header, composer and message actions is announced with a name that states its action; none is announced as just 'button'.
Each web chat page has exactly one h1; jumping by heading reaches the conversation title.
A tool step that needs approval is announced as 'Approval needed' and the Allow and Deny buttons are reachable and named.
On iOS and Android, a swipe through the agent activity list announces each step with its status, and expanded state is spoken.
When the mobile ApprovalModal opens, the screen behind it is not reachable by screen reader (currently fails: pending list).
In the VS Code sidebar and Chrome side panel, no button, tab or menu item is announced without a name.
inferred: Names should be translated with the app language; today many are English literals [inferred from the string literals cited above].
The Desktop public app inherits web behaviour because Electron loads the hosted web app (apps/desktop/electron/main.ts:1065-1067) [inferred].
proposed: [proposed] Add an automated axe sweep over signed-in chat, settings and approval states on web, and record the result in a report like apps/web/reports/a11y-report.json, which today covers only five public pages.
[proposed] Fix the five PENDING mobile modals, starting with ApprovalModal, and shrink the list in modal-accessibility-semantics.test.ts.
[proposed] Move announcement and label strings into the i18n catalogue.

steps.what_happens: The app renders markup with names, roles and headings (web React, mobile React Native props, VS Code and Chrome HTML).
The platform accessibility layer (browser tree, VoiceOver, TalkBack) exposes names to the reader.
Tool and approval state comes from the agent activity state, which the chat turn pipeline fills; the timeline turns it into a label and a live phrase.

steps.what_happens: Approve or Deny calls the onApprove, onApproveForChat or onReject callbacks the host app supplies.

data.what: No data is created by names or headings; approval decisions are created by the callbacks, not by this feature.

features.summary: Lets a keyboard-only person reach every control, use arrow keys, Home, End and Escape in menus, keep Tab inside dialogs, get focus back where it was, and see a focus ring. Shortcut hints show Cmd on Apple and Ctrl elsewhere. Web, Desktop, VS Code, Chrome and the CLI have it; Mobile has dialog semantics only.

purpose.what_it_does: Implements the standard keyboard rules for menus and dialogs as shared hooks, draws focus indicators, and computes the right shortcut label for the platform.
purpose.why_it_exists: People who cannot use a mouse need to operate every control; the product lists keyboard-only checks, focus entering and returning from dialogs and menus that stay operable as a release test (doc: docs/product/experience-contract.md:796).
purpose.who_uses_it: Keyboard-only and switch users, screen-reader users, power users, on Web, Desktop, VS Code, Chrome and CLI.
problems_solved: Arrow keys walking focus out of an open menu into the page behind it.
Focus lost on the page after a dialog closes.
A hint that says Ctrl on a Mac.
use_cases: Open the sidebar conversation menu, press Arrow Down, Home, End, Escape; focus returns to the trigger.
Open a hand-rolled dialog; Tab cycles inside; Escape closes and focus goes back to the button that opened it.
Read 'Cmd K' vs 'Ctrl K' in the desktop sidebar search hint.
In the terminal CLI, press Esc to cancel a popup, arrows to move.

where_to_find_it: Web and Desktop: every menu or dialog built with the shared hooks (packages/ui/ui/src/primitives/useMenuKeyboard.ts, useDialogKeyboard.ts); account menu shows the shortcut for '/' via shortcutLabel (apps/web/shared/components/layout/AccountMenuItems.tsx:112); desktop sidebar search hint uses shortcutLabel('K') (apps/desktop/src/features/v3/Sidebar.tsx:432).
VS Code sidebar: actions menu, plus menu, slash menu, model and controls popovers, sessions sheet (webviewContent.ts:6112-6123,6887,6981-7004).
Chrome side panel: model dropdown and recents sheet (apps/extension/src/side_panel.ts:11440-11470,13064-13085).
CLI: command popup hint 'Type to filter   ↑↓ navigate   Enter select   Esc cancel' (apps/cli/src/tui/widgets/command_popup.rs:17); custom keybindings in config (apps/cli/src/keybindings.rs).
Mobile: modals use accessibilityViewIsModal and onRequestClose (apps/mobile/src/features/companion/components/CompanionDemoWalkthrough.tsx:170-171).
prerequisites: A physical keyboard (or a terminal for the CLI).
On Mobile, a screen reader or hardware keyboard; the app has no keyboard menu code of its own that I found.
screens_and_controls: Menus: Arrow Down, Arrow Up, Home, End, Escape, Tab (closes the menu).
Dialogs: focus enters the first focusable control, Tab and Shift+Tab wrap inside, Escape closes.
Focus ring: a 2px outline on :focus-visible on web (apps/web/app/globals.css:1233-1236); text fields get an inset border instead (globals.css:1249-1252).
Resize handles: Arrow Left and Right, Home and End (apps/web/features/chat/components/SidePanelResizeHandle.tsx:44-55).
journey: Press Tab until the trigger button has the focus ring.
Press Enter or Space to open the menu; the first item is focused.
Use arrow keys, Home or End to move; disabled items are skipped by default.
Press Escape; the menu closes and focus returns to the trigger.
For dialogs: open, Tab around (it wraps), press Escape; focus returns to the opener.
feedback_and_outputs: A visible focus ring.
Shortcut hint text in menus and tooltips.
CLI popup hint line.
settings: High contrast toggle in Appearance changes the focus ring colour via data-contrast (apps/web/shared/components/AppearancePreferences.tsx:39-43; apps/web/app/globals.css:1270-1277).
CLI keybindings configured by name in config (apps/cli/src/keybindings.rs:34-46).

working: useMenuKeyboard: capture-phase listener; Escape closes and refocuses the trigger, Tab closes the menu, arrows, Home, End move with wrap, disabled items skipped (packages/ui/ui/src/primitives/useMenuKeyboard.ts:17-88).

useDialogKeyboard: records the opener, focuses first focusable (or the panel), traps Tab both ways, closes on Escape, restores focus to the opener on close (packages/ui/ui/src/primitives/useDialogKeyboard.ts:29-119).
shortcutLabel and primaryModifierLabel use userAgentData, then navigator.platform, then userAgent to choose the Apple symbol or Ctrl (packages/ui/ui/src/platformKeys.ts:6-32).
Web global focus-visible ring and a main-content exception (apps/web/app/globals.css:1233-1239).

Desktop (Tauri src) uses the hooks in FileTree, ProjectRow, Sidebar, ThemeEditorDialog (apps/desktop/src/features/code/FileTree.tsx:488; features/v3/ProjectRow.tsx:118; features/settings/ThemeEditorDialog.tsx:238) and has a global :focus-visible rule (apps/desktop/src/styles/globals.css:371).
Web side-panel resize handle is keyboard operable with ARIA separator values (SidePanelResizeHandle.tsx:44-70).
VS Code: webview has its own Escape, Arrow and focus-restore code for menus and the sessions sheet; focus-visible rules (webviewContent.ts:547-548,6112-6123,6441-6452).

Chrome: model dropdown handles Escape, Tab, Arrow, Home, End and refocuses the button; recents sheet traps Tab and restores focus to the history button (apps/extension/src/side_panel.ts:11440-11470,13064-13085); focus-visible outlines throughout (side_panel.ts:2061).
CLI: user-configurable keybindings with validation against keys the composer owns (apps/cli/src/keybindings.rs:191-251); command popup navigation hints (command_popup.rs:17).
