features.summary: Tells a screen-reader user, without moving focus, that a reply, tool step, save or connection has finished, and reads a streaming reply in calm whole-word chunks at most every 2 seconds. Web and Desktop do this; Mobile announces only start and outcome; VS Code and Chrome use a plain polite log and are unverified.

purpose.what_it_does: Uses polite live regions (web, VS Code, Chrome) and native announcements (mobile) to speak status changes. On web it has two parts: one short phrase per generation state change, and a per-message announcer that reads streamed text in 2-second word-bounded chunks.
purpose.why_it_exists: Without it, a blind user hears nothing when a reply ends, or hears every token and every repeated word. The comments in the code say a token is not a word and the answer should be read once.
purpose.who_uses_it: Screen-reader users on every app; people who rely on audible feedback.
problems_solved: Silence when a reply finishes.
Token-by-token speech.
The same text read twice.
Focus jumping to the reply.
use_cases: Send a message on web and hear 'Generating response', then the reply in short pieces, then the final tail.
Hear 'Response paused, waiting for your approval'.
On the phone hear 'Responding' then the outcome when the reply ends.
Hear a connector reconnect toast.

where_to_find_it: Web and Desktop chat: invisible; sr-only status paragraph in the message list plus a StreamAnnouncer inside each assistant message (apps/web/features/chat/components/messages/ChatMessageList.tsx:2086-2091; MessageBubble.tsx:2914).
Mobile chat list: system announcement through the screen reader (apps/mobile/src/features/chat/components/MessageList.tsx:246-258).
VS Code sidebar: transcript role=log aria-live=polite; runtime status and follow-up status regions (webviewContent.ts:3122,3167,3360).
Chrome side panel: sp-messages role=log aria-live=polite; thinking status (apps/extension/src/side_panel.ts:6340-6346).

A chat turn in progress.

journey: Send a message.

When the stream ends the remaining text is read once.
The status phrase then says the outcome (for example completed, stopped, finished with errors).
feedback_and_outputs: Spoken phrases only.
Phrases such as 'Response paused, waiting for your approval' (ChatMessageList.tsx:1756-1758); 'Agent activity completed' (AgentActivityTimeline.tsx:383).
Mobile outcome text from turnOutcomeAnnouncement (MessageList.tsx:176).
settings: Chat text size, motion and similar Appearance settings do not alter announcements.
Streaming interval is a parameter, default 2000 ms (StreamAnnouncer.tsx:3).

working: useStreamAnnouncement: each 2 s tick announces only the new text up to the last whitespace, strips markdown, and announces the tail once when streaming ends; says nothing for a message already finished at mount (packages/ui/unified-chat/src/components/markdown/StreamAnnouncer.tsx:3-77).

StreamAnnouncer renders children plus a sr-only role=status aria-live=polite aria-atomic span (StreamAnnouncer.tsx:88-109); used in web MessageBubble (apps/web/features/chat/components/messages/MessageBubble.tsx:2914) and shared MessageBubble (packages/ui/unified-chat/src/components/MessageBubble.tsx:825) and StreamingMarkdownContent.tsx:3.

Web message list: one status phrase per phase (settled, awaiting approval, generating) from a ref guard so it is spoken once; the log itself has aria-live off (ChatMessageList.tsx:1744-1759,2086-2116).
Shared activity timeline announces activity states (AgentActivityTimeline.tsx:369-384,870-872).

Mobile announces 'Responding' when an assistant message starts streaming and an outcome when it ends, via AccessibilityInfo.announceForAccessibility (MessageList.tsx:164,246-258); other mobile screens use accessibilityLiveRegion polite (OfflineBanner.tsx:31, CloudTasksScreen.tsx:324, ServiceNoticesBanner.tsx:91).

Web connector outcomes: ConnectorOutcomeAnnouncer raises toasts for reauthorization and unavailable connectors (apps/web/features/connectors/components/ConnectorOutcomeAnnouncer.tsx:22-52, mounted at apps/web/app/AppRuntimeMounts.tsx:21).
CLI screen reader mode: plain line REPL, 'you:' and 'agi:' labels, bell when input needed, enabled by flag, environment or config (apps/cli/src/lib.rs:442-448,5941-5950).
incomplete: Mobile reads no streamed text, only start and outcome; the brief marks S11.08 mobile as missing.
VS Code and Chrome transcripts are live logs (aria-live polite); whether they chunk or repeat streamed text is unverified (brief S11.08).
Announcement phrases are English literals.

established.statement: When something finishes (a reply, a tool step, a save, a connection), a screen reader hears a short announcement without moving focus.
A streaming reply is announced calmly (word-bounded chunks or once when done), never token by token and never twice.
Streamed text is announced at most every 2 seconds, in whole-word pieces, and the final tail once when streaming ends.
established.source: task brief for F011-04; matches StreamAnnouncer.tsx:3

established.statement: Status changes use a polite live region and never move focus.
Mobile announces only the start and the outcome of a reply, not the streamed text.

acceptance_criteria: On web with a reader, a 30-second streamed reply is spoken in pieces no more often than every 2 seconds.
No spoken piece ends mid-word.
The last words are spoken once after streaming ends.
The reply is not read twice (not by the message log and again by the announcer).
Focus stays where it was throughout.
On the phone the reader says a start phrase and an outcome phrase and no streamed text.
A paused turn waiting for approval is announced as waiting for approval.
inferred: Mobile having no chunking is by design per the task brief, but the brief marks it 'missing' [inferred conflict].
VS Code and Chrome may double-announce, since the log is polite and receives appended nodes [inferred, unverified].
proposed: [proposed] Reuse the StreamAnnouncer algorithm in VS Code and Chrome.
[proposed] Translate announcement phrases.

features.summary: Keeps text readable at larger sizes: a Chat text size setting on web, device text size on Mobile, browser zoom reflow to one column on web, and long or translated labels that wrap or truncate. Web, Desktop and Mobile are partial and unverified at 200 and 400 percent; the CLI and Chrome are marked done.

purpose.what_it_does: Lets people enlarge text (app setting, browser zoom, OS text size) without clipping. The web shell switches to a drawer layout on narrow viewports, which is what 400% zoom produces. Mobile caps scaling at set multipliers and stacks rows when text is large.
purpose.why_it_exists: Low-vision users need larger text, and translated strings are longer than English.
purpose.who_uses_it: Low-vision users and people using translated interfaces, on all apps.
problems_solved: Clipped or overlapping text at large sizes.
Horizontal scrolling at high zoom.
Long German or Arabic labels breaking layout.
use_cases: Set Chat text size to Large on web.
Zoom the browser to 400 percent and use the app in one column.
Raise phone text size and read settings rows stacked.
Read a long label truncated cleanly in the Chrome model button.

features.summary: Stops or softens looping and moving animation when the operating system asks for less motion. Web and Desktop also have an in-app Motion setting that can only reduce motion. Mobile reads the device setting and listens for changes. VS Code and Chrome follow the OS. The CLI uses plain mode or a reduced-motion config.

purpose.what_it_does: Collapses animation and transition durations, stops infinite loops, replaces moving spinners, and lets the person choose Reduced in the app even when the OS says nothing.
purpose.why_it_exists: Moving and looping animation can cause dizziness and distraction. The code comment states overriding an OS reduced-motion request is the one harmful direction, so there is no 'full motion' option.
purpose.who_uses_it: People with vestibular conditions, distraction sensitivity, or who prefer calm interfaces.
problems_solved: Spinners and pulses that never stop.
Smooth scroll jumps.
Animations added later that escape a per-class rule.
use_cases: Turn on OS Reduce Motion and open web chat.
Set Settings, Appearance, Motion to Reduced without changing the OS.
On the phone, toggle Reduce Motion and see toasts stop animating.
Run the CLI with plain mode to remove spinners.

where_to_find_it: Web and Desktop: Settings, Appearance, row 'Motion' with buttons 'System' and 'Reduced' and hint 'Less animation in replies and the interface. System follows your device.' (apps/web/features/settings/sections/AppearanceSection.tsx:115-140).
Mobile: device Settings, Accessibility, Reduce Motion (no in-app control; doc: docs/decisions/2026-11-13-founder-decisions.md:80-82).
CLI: --plain flag, AGI_PLAIN, or ui.reduced_motion in config (apps/cli/src/lib.rs:439-440; apps/cli/src/config.rs:155).
VS Code and Chrome: OS setting only.
prerequisites: None for the OS path; Motion row needs the web settings page.
screens_and_controls: Motion group with two buttons using aria-pressed and names 'System motion' and 'Reduced motion' (AppearanceSection.tsx:130-137).
journey: Choose Reduced (or set the OS option).
The html element gets data-motion='reduced' (AppearancePreferences.tsx:48-50).
One blanket CSS rule shrinks durations to 0.01ms and iteration to 1 (globals.css:1935-1946).
Spinners slow rather than freeze: animate-spin runs at 3s under the OS media query (globals.css:1949-1953).
feedback_and_outputs: Animations visibly stop or jump to end state.
Setting persists and syncs.
settings: motion: system or reduced (web-settings-store.ts:36,120,142).
ui.reduced_motion in CLI config (config.rs:155,1572-1575).
--plain / AGI_PLAIN / --screen-reader on the CLI.

working: Web: in-app Motion stored as 'system' or 'reduced'; only 'reduced' sets data-motion; deliberately no full-motion option (apps/web/shared/components/AppearancePreferences.tsx:44-50; web-settings-store.ts:36).
Web CSS: one blanket rule for data-motion='reduced' plus separate prefers-reduced-motion blocks (apps/web/app/globals.css:1935-1946,1949-1953).
Web e2e checks public stylesheet geometry transitions under reduced motion (apps/web/e2e/public-reduced-motion.spec.ts:10-33).
Shared hook useReducedMotion reads the media query and listens for changes (packages/ui/unified-chat/src/hooks/useReducedMotion.ts).

Desktop Tauri stylesheet has three prefers-reduced-motion blocks and a test that requires broad rules (apps/desktop/src/styles/globals.css:474,509,1305; apps/desktop/src/__tests__/reducedMotionPolicy.test.ts); Electron shows hosted web.

Mobile: store reads AccessibilityInfo.isReduceMotionEnabled once at first subscribe and listens for 'reduceMotionChanged'; keeps the last value on unmount (apps/mobile/src/ui/theme/useReduceMotion.ts:20-82); used by Toast, ImageFullScreen, ShimmerText, AgiMark; a test forbids opting out and requires core Animated surfaces to read it (accessibilityPreferenceCoverage.test.ts:70-86).

CLI: plain output or ui.reduced_motion = true sets motion::set_reduced; plain mode swaps the spinner for text printed once (apps/cli/src/tui/tui_app.rs:7122-7124; apps/cli/src/tui/motion.rs:9-15; apps/cli/src/output.rs:244-248).
VS Code webview: prefers-reduced-motion block collapses durations (webviewContent.ts:2774-2781).
Chrome side panel: same rule (apps/extension/src/side_panel.ts:4618-4631).
incomplete: VS Code, Chrome and Mobile do not offer the in-app Motion setting; they follow the OS only (by decision for Mobile).
CLI does not read an OS setting; it needs the flag, environment variable or config.
Web keeps spinning at 3s rather than stopping (by design comment).

not_available: In-app motion option on Mobile, VS Code and Chrome.

established.statement: With the OS or app reduced-motion preference on, looping and travelling animation stops or is replaced.
The in-app setting can only reduce motion, never add it, because an override of an OS request is treated as harmful.
On mobile the preference is read once at start and updated when the OS changes it.
Mobile apps follow the device for reduced motion.
The CLI plain mode removes animation.

acceptance_criteria: With OS reduce motion on, web chat shows no infinite animation; spinners are slow or static.
Choosing Motion: Reduced on web sets data-motion='reduced' on html and shrinks transitions.
There is no way in the web UI to force full motion when the OS asks for reduced.
On iOS or Android, flipping Reduce Motion while the app runs updates toasts and shimmer without restart.
CLI --plain shows no spinner frames; ui.reduced_motion=true uses the still spinner glyph.
VS Code and Chrome panels respect the OS media query.
inferred: Desktop users get web's Motion row via the hosted app [inferred].
proposed: [proposed] Add an e2e test that runs a signed-in chat page under reduced motion and asserts no running infinite animations.
[proposed] Let the CLI read common OS or terminal hints.

features.summary: Live voice conversations show what is said as on-screen text on Web, Desktop (the Electron window shows the hosted web app) and Mobile, and each finished turn is saved as a chat message. The CLI has no live captions: its push-to-talk /voice shows the transcribed words and sends them as a normal message.

purpose.what_it_does: Shows the words of a spoken (live voice) conversation as text while it happens, labelled by speaker, and keeps each finished spoken turn in the chat so it can be read later. Web adds a toggle and a waiting message; Mobile shows a scrolling caption list; the CLI shows the recognised words after each recording.
purpose.why_it_exists: People who are deaf, hard of hearing, in a noisy place or unable to listen need the words as text, and the brief wants a readable record kept with the chat (brief S11.15, S11.16).
purpose.who_uses_it: Signed-in users of live voice on Web, Desktop and Mobile who want text; screen-reader users; CLI users who dictate with /voice.
problems_solved: Spoken words vanish unless they are also text.
A voice call would leave no record in the chat history.
Screen-reader users would hear every partial phrase twice if the captions panel announced itself (web sets aria-live off).
use_cases: A user in a meeting turns on Captions in a web voice call and reads the assistant instead of listening.
A mobile user scrolls the live captions during a call and selects a line to copy.
After a call, a web user opens the chat and reads the saved You and Assistant turns.
A CLI user runs /voice, reads 'You said:' and presses Enter to send.

where_to_find_it: Web and Desktop (hosted web app): enter voice mode from the composer, open the voice chat dock menu, section 'Call', item 'Captions' (a checkbox item) (apps/web/features/chat/components/Voice/VoiceChatDock.tsx:122-131).
Mobile: the live voice bar header has a captions button labelled 'Hide captions' or 'Show captions' (apps/mobile/src/features/voice/components/LiveVoiceBar.tsx:78-79, :309-313).
CLI: the /voice slash command (and /dictate) in builds with the voice feature (apps/cli/src/lib.rs:81-103).
VS Code and Chrome: not applicable (brief status n/a).
prerequisites: Web/Desktop: a managed (Cloud) chat, not a Local or own-key model, with the canUseVoice capability (apps/web/features/chat/pages/WebChatPage.tsx:5905-5922).
A plan whose tier policy allows voice; otherwise the session start returns 403 (apps/web/app/api/voice/live/sessions/route.ts:311-317).
Mobile: Cloud execution mode and sign-in; Local mode stays turn based (apps/mobile/src/features/voice/services/liveVoiceAvailability.ts:17-25).
CLI: a build with the voice feature, a microphone, and a speech-to-text backend (apps/cli/src/voice.rs:101-140).
screens_and_controls: Web: 'Voice captions' region (role log) with lines labelled 'You' or 'Assistant'; waiting text 'Captions will appear here as soon as someone speaks.' (apps/web/features/chat/components/Voice/VoiceCaptions.tsx:7-12, :23-29).
Mobile: scrolling list with labels YOU and AGI, text is selectable (apps/mobile/src/features/voice/components/LiveVoiceBar.tsx:438-461).
CLI: line 'You said: <text>' then '[ENTER to send, e to edit, r to re-record, ESC to discard]' (apps/cli/src/voice.rs:1219-1221, :236-240).
journey: Web: start a voice session from a Cloud chat.
Open the voice chat dock menu and choose Captions; the waiting message shows until someone speaks.
Speak; your line appears and is replaced in place as the partial text grows, then the assistant line appears.
Only the last four lines stay on screen.
Leave the call; the finished turns are in the chat as messages.
Mobile: start live voice; captions are on by default; press 'Hide captions' to hide them while the call continues.
CLI: run /voice, press the key to record, read 'You said:', then Enter, e, r or Esc.
feedback_and_outputs: Web: caption lines with data-role and data-final attributes; error toast 'Part of this voice conversation could not be saved to your history.' if saving a turn fails (apps/web/features/chat/pages/WebChatPage.tsx:6779).
Mobile: transcript appears in the chat list as user and assistant messages (apps/mobile/stores/chat/chatMessageStore.ts:1161-1200).
CLI: '(no speech detected)', 'Transcription failed' messages (apps/cli/src/voice.rs:213-222).
settings: Web: Captions toggle state is local component state, off at the start of each voice surface (apps/web/features/chat/components/Voice/VoiceModeSurface.tsx:208).
Mobile: captionsShown starts true (LiveVoiceBar.tsx:214).
CLI: --voice-lang flag sets the speech language (apps/cli/src/lib.rs:5951-5956).

working: Web: caption lines are built from live transcript turns; a partial turn replaces its line in place (same turnId), empty text is ignored, and only the last 4 lines are kept (apps/web/features/chat/components/Voice/voice-captions.ts:3, :15-33).

Web: the panel is role=log with aria-live=off so partial phrases are not announced (VoiceCaptions.tsx:23-24); a separate polite status region announces call state (apps/web/features/chat/components/Voice/voice-announcements.ts:1-40).
Web: every transcript turn also goes to the chat store and, when final, is POSTed to /api/chat/conversations/:id/messages with skipLlm (apps/web/features/chat/pages/WebChatPage.tsx:6739-6788).

Mobile: turns are shown while live and final turns are written to the chat store, and marked for cloud sync when the conversation is Cloud (apps/mobile/src/features/voice/hooks/useLiveVoiceSession.ts:204-222; apps/mobile/stores/chat/chatMessageStore.ts:1161-1200).
CLI: recorded audio is transcribed, shown as 'You said:' and sent to the agent as a normal user message (apps/cli/src/voice.rs:204-290).
incomplete: Mobile captions have no waiting message and render nothing until a turn exists (LiveVoiceBar.tsx:438).
CLI has no live captions and no spoken assistant output: it is record, then transcribe, then confirm, so 'captions' means the post-recording text only (apps/cli/src/voice.rs:1-9, :204-290).

Caption labels on Web ('You', 'Assistant', waiting text, region name) and on Mobile (YOU, AGI, Hide captions, Show captions) are English literals, not translated (VoiceCaptions.tsx:7-12; LiveVoiceBar.tsx:78-79, :450).
disconnected_or_disabled: CLI voice is off by default: the Cargo feature 'voice' must be enabled, and Linux release builds leave it out (apps/cli/Cargo.toml:126-132; .github/workflows/release-cli.yml:227-229).
Web/Desktop live voice is not offered when the chat is Local or own-key (voiceManaged false hides onEnterVoiceMode) (WebChatPage.tsx:5907-5911, :7672).
not_available: VS Code and Chrome have no voice captions (brief n/a).
Mobile Local mode has no live voice, so no live captions (liveVoiceAvailability.ts:17-25).

established.statement: Spoken audio (voice conversations) can be shown as live captions. Web, desktop, mobile and CLI are marked done.
A voice conversation leaves a readable text transcript kept with the chat. Web, desktop, mobile and CLI are marked done.
Captions show a waiting message until someone speaks; the captions region does not announce every partial phrase because the transcript carries the same words.
Voice: permission denied, absent microphone, transcription failure, mute, interruption and exit all have recoverable states; speech and text refer to the correct turn.
Do not claim realtime audio behaviour for a completed-text-to-speech path.
Transcript/edit-before-send exists for dictation.

acceptance_criteria: On Web, with captions off, no element with test id voice-captions exists; after choosing Captions the toggle reports aria-checked true and the waiting text shows.
Emit a partial then a final turn with the same turnId: exactly one caption line shows the final text, labelled You or Assistant.
After five different turns only the last four caption lines remain.
The captions region has aria-live off and role log.
After a final turn, a POST to the conversation messages endpoint is made and the turn is in the chat list; a failed POST shows the toast.
On Mobile, 'Hide captions' removes the transcript and keeps the call status 'Listening'; 'Show captions' brings back every turn.
On the CLI, a recording with no speech prints '(no speech detected)' and nothing is sent.
inferred: A caption line shows both user and assistant speech because the same turn feed drives it [inferred from deliverTranscript, use-voice-session.ts:456-462].
Desktop users see the Web behaviour because the public Desktop window shows the hosted web app (AGENTS.md section 5) [inferred].
proposed: [proposed] Give Mobile captions a waiting message and a live-region role to match Web.
[proposed] Move caption labels into the translation catalog.
[proposed] Re-state the brief's CLI status as 'push-to-talk dictation text', since the CLI has no live captions.

steps.what_happens: Web: the user enters voice mode in a managed chat; the page asks the server to start a live session.
The server checks sign-in, plan voice permission and the usage budget, then asks the managed voice provider to open a session.
The browser streams microphone audio and receives transcript delta events from the session.
The client groups deltas into user and assistant turns and emits each (partial or final).
Each turn is sent to the caption sink (foreground only) and to the transcript sink.
Final turns are POSTed to the conversation messages route and stored.
Mobile: same event feed; final turns are written to the on-device chat store, and queued for sync when the conversation is Cloud.
CLI: audio is captured and written to a temporary WAV file, transcribed by the chosen backend (AGI account, OpenAI API key, or a local program), shown, then sent.

data.retained_or_deleted: Lost when the voice surface unmounts (apps/web/features/chat/components/Voice/VoiceModeSurface.tsx:209)

data.what: Voice transcript turns as chat messages
data.where_stored: Web chat store and server conversation messages; Mobile on-device chat store (store:chat messages) and Cloud sync for Cloud chats
data.synced: Web: via POST when final; Mobile: only Cloud conversations are marked for sync
data.retained_or_deleted: Follows normal chat retention; no voice-specific rule found

data.where_stored: A temporary recordings folder created with owner-only permissions, with a sweep of stale recordings

execution_and_data_flow.models_and_providers: Web and Mobile live voice runs on a managed voice backend chosen by plan from the model catalog; the route refuses to start if the backend is not a live model (apps/web/app/api/voice/live/sessions/route.ts:319-322). The provider's transcript events feed captions. The CLI transcribes through the AGI account, an OpenAI key or a local program, and a Local session may not use the cloud OpenAI path without AGIWORKFORCE_VOICE_ALLOW_CLOUD=1 (apps/cli/src/voice.rs:455-482).

access_and_usage.account: Web and Mobile live voice need a signed-in account (route uses getClerkAuthUser, apps/web/app/api/voice/live/sessions/route.ts:10). CLI managed transcription needs the AGI account; the OpenAI and local backends do not.
access_and_usage.permissions: Microphone permission is needed on every surface; Mobile shows an alert on denial (apps/mobile/src/features/voice/components/voicePermissionAlert.ts).
access_and_usage.subscription: Live voice needs a plan whose tier policy has allowVoice, else 403 with a not-in-plan message; free plans have a metered free allowance in seconds (apps/web/app/api/voice/live/sessions/route.ts:311-317, :344-358; apps/web/lib/voice/free-voice-allowance.ts:47). CLI managed transcription checks the voice capability from the tier cache (apps/cli/src/voice.rs:960-966).
access_and_usage.limits_and_metering: Voice seconds are metered per session and the budget can end the session (apps/web/app/api/voice/live/sessions/lib/voice-session-budget.ts). Exact quotas per plan: unknown.
access_and_usage.flags: The route asserts a capability flag 'canUseVoice' (route.ts:296-300); the web client also reads useCapability('canUseVoice') (WebChatPage.tsx:5905).
access_and_usage.model_compatibility: Live voice is available only when the selected chat model resolves to a managed provider mode (ManagedGateway or ManagedNative) (WebChatPage.tsx:5907-5911).
access_and_usage.provider_restrictions: The route refuses voice when the user opted out of training and a model may train on inputs (route.ts:324-340).
access_and_usage.local_mode: No live voice, so no live captions, on Web and Mobile in Local mode (WebChatPage.tsx:5907-5911; liveVoiceAvailability.ts:17-25). The CLI Local session can only use the on-device program unless the user opts in to cloud egress (voice.rs:455-482).

features.summary: A chart in a chat answer or artifact gets a hidden text summary (title, kind, series, first, last, lowest and highest values, pie shares) and a collapsible data table, so people who cannot see the graphic can read the values. The brief wrongly lists the table as missing: it exists on Web and Desktop. Mobile charts have neither.

purpose.what_it_does: Pairs each drawn chart with a screen-reader summary and a real HTML table of the plotted values, plus a PNG download and a text fallback if drawing fails.
purpose.why_it_exists: A drawn chart is invisible to a screen reader and hard to read for low-vision users; the brief asks for a description and a table alternative (brief S11.17, S11.18).
purpose.who_uses_it: Screen-reader users, low-vision users, and anyone who wants exact numbers.
problems_solved: Chart values locked in a picture.
A crashed chart leaving a blank hole (fallback shows the data text).
Missing exact values when hovering is not possible.
use_cases: A screen-reader user focuses a revenue chart and hears the summary.
A user opens 'View chart data' to copy values.
A user downloads the chart as PNG for a report.
A chart with broken data shows the raw content instead of nothing.

where_to_find_it: Web and Desktop (hosted web app): chart artifacts in the artifact preview, library, slides and chart blocks in answers, drawn by ChartArtifact (apps/web/features/chat/components/artifacts/ArtifactPreview.tsx:1979; apps/web/features/chat/components/artifacts/presentation/SlideView.tsx:140).
Web: inline interactive answer charts (AnswerUiChart) with a disclosure labelled 'Data table' (packages/ui/unified-chat/src/lib/answer-ui.ts:10).
Mobile: ChartArtifactView in artifact full screen, no summary or table (apps/mobile/src/features/chat/components/ArtifactFullScreen.tsx:1887).
prerequisites: A chart artifact or chart block with valid JSON data.
screens_and_controls: Figure with accessible name = chart name, described by the hidden summary (ChartArtifact.tsx:132-137).
Header showing kind, '<n> points · <n> series' (ChartArtifact.tsx:147-155).
Button 'PNG' with label 'Download <chart name> as PNG' (ChartArtifact.tsx:169).
Disclosure 'View chart data' containing a table labelled '<chart name> data' with column and row headers (ChartArtifact.tsx:212-240).
Fallback panel with the raw content and a reason (ChartArtifact.tsx:81-103).
journey: Open a chat that has a chart.
Focus the chart; a screen reader reads its name and the summary.
Optionally open 'View chart data' and read the table by row.
Optionally press PNG to download.
If data was cut at the row cap, read the note about the first points.
feedback_and_outputs: Summary text such as 'Revenue. Bar chart of 4 points, month on the horizontal axis... Sales: starts at ..., lowest ..., highest ....' (chart-spec.ts:127-183).
PNG file named from the chart title (ChartArtifact.tsx:28-34).
Error text role=alert if PNG export fails (ChartArtifact.tsx:175-179).
Truncation note 'Plotting the first 500 of N points. Download the JSON for the full data.' (ChartArtifact.tsx:248-253).
settings: Reduced motion turns off chart animation (ChartArtifact.tsx uses useReducedMotion, animate={!reducedMotion}).
Light/dark theme changes chart colours.

working: The summary names the chart, the kind, the axes, and per series the first, last, lowest and highest value; pies give total, largest and smallest; donuts give each share (packages/ui/unified-chat/src/components/artifact-components/chart-spec.ts:127-183).

The data table disclosure exists in the shared chart component, with column and row headers and a name (ChartArtifact.tsx:212-240), and a test opens it (packages/ui/unified-chat/src/components/artifact-components/__tests__/ChartArtifact.draw.test.tsx:110-120).
AnswerUiChart has its own summary and a 'Data table' disclosure with a caption and a fallback line naming the table (apps/web/features/chat/components/messages/cards/answer-ui/AnswerUiChart.tsx).
If the chart cannot be parsed or drawn, a fallback shows the reason and raw data (ChartArtifact.tsx:81-103, :189-197).
Point and series counts use plural-aware translation (ChartArtifact.tsx:147-155; packages/ui/i18n/locales/ar/chat.json:465-476).
incomplete: Summary sentence frames ('Bar chart of', 'starts at', 'lowest', 'highest', 'Showing the first') and 'View chart data' are English literals; only the point and series counts are translated (chart-spec.ts:134-183; ChartArtifact.tsx:213).
Table cell numbers are written raw (row[entry.dataKey]) while the summary uses toLocaleString, so formatting differs (ChartArtifact.tsx:235; chart-spec.ts:109).
The truncation note tells the user to 'Download the JSON for the full data' but ChartArtifact has no JSON download control; whether the artifact host offers one: unknown (ChartArtifact.tsx:251).
Whether the drawn recharts surface itself is hidden from or exposed to assistive tech in ChartArtifact: unknown (ChartSpecView hides it with aria-hidden, ChartArtifact does not).
disconnected_or_disabled: ChartSpecView (used by AnswerUiChart) wraps the canvas in aria-hidden, so the summary and table carry all the meaning there (packages/ui/unified-chat/src/components/artifact-components/ChartSpecView.tsx:57).
not_available: Mobile ChartArtifactView has no summary and no table; it only sets an alert role for errors (apps/mobile/src/features/chat/components/ChartArtifactView.tsx:35).
CLI, VS Code and Chrome: brief says n/a; not checked further.

established.statement: A chart comes with a text description (title, what is plotted, key values) that assistive tech can read. Web and desktop done.
A chart can be viewed as a data table (or its data read in order) as an alternative to the graphic. The brief lists web and desktop as missing.
Controls have accessible names; focus, keyboard, zoom, reduced motion and screen reader are verified for core flows.

acceptance_criteria: A valid line chart renders role=figure with an accessible name equal to the title.
The hidden summary contains the title, kind, series name, lowest and highest values.
A pie summary lists total, largest and smallest; a donut lists each share, with under 1 percent shown as '<1%'.
Opening 'View chart data' shows one row per plotted point with a header for each series.
A malformed JSON chart shows the fallback with the raw text instead of throwing.
Data above 500 rows shows the truncation note and the summary says it shows the first N of M.
The PNG button downloads a file named from the chart title.
inferred: Web and Desktop share the chart code because the public Desktop window shows the hosted web app [inferred from AGENTS.md section 5].
The brief's 'missing' for S11.18 is out of date [inferred from ChartArtifact.tsx:212-240 and its test].
proposed: [proposed] Translate the summary sentences and the disclosure label.
[proposed] Format table cells with the same locale formatter as the summary.
[proposed] Give Mobile charts a summary and a table, or mark the brief item 'Mobile missing'.
[proposed] Fix the truncation note or add the JSON download.

steps.what_happens: A chart artifact or chart block arrives in the chat as JSON text.
The component parses the JSON, caps rows and series, and builds the spec.
It writes the summary into a hidden paragraph and the data into a table.
The graphic loads lazily and draws; an error boundary swaps in the fallback if it throws.
PNG download clones the drawn SVG, paints it on a canvas and downloads it.

access_and_usage.model_compatibility: Any model that emits valid chart JSON; the renderer is model-agnostic.
access_and_usage.local_mode: Works fully on device in Local mode because rendering and summary need no network.

scenarios.name: Screen reader summary

features.summary: Web sets the page direction from the language table and lets message text and the composer pick their own direction. Mobile sets native layout direction. Enter is ignored while an input method is composing on Web, VS Code and Chrome; Mobile's composer never sends on Enter. Today only English and Spanish are selectable, so no right-to-left language can be chosen.

purpose.what_it_does: Mirrors the layout for right-to-left languages, aligns each message by its own text direction, and stops Enter from sending while an input method (Japanese, Chinese, Korean) is confirming characters.
purpose.why_it_exists: Arabic and Hebrew readers need correct direction; Japanese, Chinese and Korean typists would otherwise send half-typed messages (brief S11.19-S11.21).
purpose.who_uses_it: Users of right-to-left languages and of input methods, on every typing surface.
problems_solved: Arabic text laid out left to right.
Half-composed text sent by the Enter that confirms a candidate.
Mixed-language drafts aligned the wrong way.
use_cases: A user switches the display language to a right-to-left language and the page flips (when such a language becomes selectable).
A Japanese typist presses Enter to confirm characters and nothing is sent.
A user pastes Arabic into the composer and it aligns right.
A VS Code user types Korean in the sidebar chat.

features.summary: Counted phrases pick the right plural form through shared plural-aware helpers, and common error messages go through the translation catalog. Only English and Spanish are selectable on Web and Desktop; Mobile language choice is switched off; VS Code uses all twelve catalogs; Chrome ships English only; the CLI has no translation.

purpose.what_it_does: Looks up counted phrases by language plural category (one, few, many and so on) and shows error messages from the language catalog instead of fixed English text.
purpose.why_it_exists: An English 's' suffix is wrong in many languages, and error text in the wrong language is hard to act on (brief S11.24, S11.25; decision D-2026-09-15-03 on complete catalogs only).
purpose.who_uses_it: Non-English users and the translators who maintain catalogs.

Half-translated screens (decision hides incomplete languages).

features.summary: Dates, times, numbers and prices are formatted with the browser or phone locale, using the Intl API, and money uses the currency's own minor-unit digits with a fixed two-digit fallback. The locale comes from the device, not the app's chosen language. The CLI shows credits and a fixed date format, not currency.

purpose.what_it_does: Formats billing amounts, invoice and device dates, usage counts and prices so they read the way the person's device expects.
purpose.why_it_exists: A fixed US format confuses people and wrong currency digits misstate prices (brief S11.22, S11.23).
purpose.who_uses_it: Everyone who sees billing, usage, devices or pricing, on every app.
problems_solved: US-style dates and number separators for everyone.
Wrong number of decimals for currencies with none or three.
Missing currency symbol or code.
use_cases: A user opens invoices and sees dates and amounts in their locale.
A user reads the pricing page in their local currency where available.
A user reads 'Last seen' on linked devices.
A VS Code user sees account dates in the host locale.

where_to_find_it: Web and Desktop (hosted web app): Billing invoices list (apps/web/app/billing/invoices/InvoiceList.tsx:25-31), payment history (apps/web/features/billing/components/BillingPaymentHistory.tsx), pricing page (apps/web/app/pricing/page.tsx:290-349), Settings linked devices and passkeys panels.
Desktop Tauri pricing cards and upgrade dialog (apps/desktop/src/features/pricing/PlanCard.tsx:35-91; DesktopUpgradeConfirmDialog.tsx:139), retained code.
Mobile: Settings, plans and cloud usage (apps/mobile/src/features/settings/plans/index.tsx:30-33; apps/mobile/src/features/settings/cloud-usage/index.tsx:75-221).
VS Code: account and artifact presentation; Chrome: side panel usage text; CLI: credits text.
prerequisites: For localized prices on Web: the localized pricing catalog loaded from the server (apps/web/app/pricing/page.tsx:290).
screens_and_controls: Plain text amounts and dates; no controls. Pricing shows server-localized prices with a fixed en-US format before the page mounts (apps/web/app/pricing/page.tsx:148, :291).
journey: Open Billing, invoices or Pricing.
Read the amount with the symbol and decimals of its currency.
Read dates such as 'Linked' and 'Last seen' in the device's date style.
feedback_and_outputs: Money such as a currency symbol plus amount; whole units can drop decimals (packages/contracts/types/src/money-format.ts:14-31).
Unknown currency prints '<amount with two digits> <CODE>' (money-format.ts:29-31).
Renewal text like '<price>/month plus tax' (apps/web/features/billing/lib/billing-format.ts:41-48).
settings: None in the app: the locale is the runtime default (Intl with undefined locale), not the Display Language setting (money-format.ts:21; billing-format.ts:23).

working: formatBillingMoney converts minor units using the currency's digit count, formats with Intl, and falls back to a fixed 2-digit amount with the currency code on error (packages/contracts/types/src/money-format.ts:1-31).
formatUsdAmount formats US dollars with the runtime locale (money-format.ts:33-40).
Billing dates use Intl.DateTimeFormat with the runtime locale (apps/web/features/billing/lib/billing-format.ts:8-24).
Plan price amounts use a locale argument and narrow currency symbols (apps/web/features/billing/lib/localized-pricing.ts:44-70).

Devices and passkeys panels use toLocaleString and toLocaleDateString with undefined locale (apps/web/features/settings/components/LinkedDevicesPanel.tsx:63-70; apps/web/features/settings/components/Settings/PasskeysPanel.tsx:22-27).
Mobile uses toLocaleDateString, toLocaleTimeString and Intl.NumberFormat with undefined locale (apps/mobile/src/features/settings/cloud-usage/index.tsx:75, :205-221, :898; plans/index.tsx:30-33).
Chrome side panel uses Intl relative time and date formatting with undefined locale (apps/extension/src/side_panel.ts:1133, :11669, :12497, :12561).
incomplete: The locale comes from the runtime, not from the chosen Display Language, so a user who picks Spanish in a US browser still sees US formatting (money-format.ts:21; billing-format.ts:23) [inferred from Intl undefined-locale behaviour].

Mobile plan prices come from the plan catalog label (getBillingPlanPricing(...).label) and store prices, not from formatBillingMoney (apps/mobile/src/features/settings/plans/index.tsx:89, :118; apps/mobile/src/features/billing/storePricing.ts:9-14).
Web pricing first renders with a fixed en-US locale to match the server, then switches after mount (apps/web/app/pricing/page.tsx:148, :291).

VS Code citations in the brief (artifactPresentation.ts:83, commandSetup.ts:398) do not hold date code; other date code exists in accountPresentation.ts (apps/extension-vscode/src/features/account-auth/accountPresentation.ts:18).
Helper words '/month', '/year', 'plus tax', 'including' are English (billing-format.ts:32-48).
disconnected_or_disabled: Some web billing flows depend on checkout flags such as NEXT_PUBLIC_CHECKOUT_ENABLED; that affects whether prices are actionable, not their format (apps/web/features/billing/lib/localized-pricing.ts:19-26).
not_available: CLI shows credits through format_usd_as_credits and a fixed '%Y-%m-%d %H:%M' date; no currency symbol or locale formatting (apps/cli/src/cost_ledger.rs:50-52; apps/cli/src/agents.rs:1365-1368).
The brief says currency formatting is done on CLI; the code shows credits, not currency.

established.statement: Dates, times and numbers are formatted for the user's locale rather than a fixed US format. Done on web, desktop, mobile, VS Code; CLI missing; Chrome unverified.
Prices and money amounts show the right currency symbol and the user's number format. Done on web, desktop, mobile, CLI.
The pricing display uses a deployment country header and configured price currency options; it never trusts a browser-supplied currency.
Public clients must not receive private internal allowance units, ledger cents or the internal unit-to-currency conversion.

acceptance_criteria: formatBillingMoney(1999, 'usd') shows a dollar amount with two decimals in the runtime locale.
A zero-decimal currency amount shows no decimals.
An unknown currency code shows a two-digit amount followed by the code.
Invoice dates and amounts change when the browser locale changes.
Linked devices and passkeys dates follow the browser locale.
Mobile cloud usage dates follow the phone locale.
The CLI prints credits and a fixed date; no currency is shown.
inferred: Using Intl with an undefined locale follows the runtime locale; therefore the formatting does not follow the Display Language [inferred].
Desktop gets Web behaviour through the hosted web app [inferred].
proposed: [proposed] Decide whether formatting should follow the Display Language or the device; then pass that locale to every formatter.
[proposed] Translate the billing helper words.
[proposed] Either mark the CLI done as 'credits' or add locale formatting.

steps.what_happens: The server sends amounts as minor units with a currency code (invoices, previews, localized plan prices).
The client divides by 10 to the currency's digit count and formats with Intl using the runtime locale.
On a formatting error the client prints a fixed two-digit amount plus the code.
Dates are formatted by Intl on the device from ISO strings.
Pricing page uses a fixed en-US locale for the first render, then the runtime locale after mount.

features.summary: The CLI has a plain mode for screen-reader users: no colour, no spinners, no rules, and the line-based REPL instead of the full-screen interface. It turns on with --plain, any non-empty AGI_PLAIN, or screen reader mode. NO_COLOR alone only removes colour. Screen reader mode adds speaker labels, numbered menus and a bell.

purpose.what_it_does: Switches the CLI to output that a screen reader can read line by line: no colour, one-time progress text instead of animated spinners, no decorative rules, and the classic REPL. A stronger screen reader mode labels lines you: and agi:.
purpose.why_it_exists: An animated spinner repainting eight times a second is spoken eight times a second by a screen reader (comment in apps/cli/src/output.rs:30-36).
purpose.who_uses_it: Screen-reader users, people who dislike colour, and scripts that want quiet output.
problems_solved: Spinner noise in screen readers.
Box-drawing rules read aloud.
Colour that the user cannot or does not want to see.
use_cases: A blind developer sets AGI_PLAIN=1 in the shell profile.
A user runs agi --screen-reader for a labelled transcript.
A user sets NO_COLOR to drop colour but keep the full-screen interface.
A user sets ui.screen_reader in the config file.

where_to_find_it: CLI flag --plain (global) (apps/cli/src/lib.rs:436-440).
CLI flag --screen-reader (global) (apps/cli/src/lib.rs:442-448).
Environment variables AGI_PLAIN, AGI_SCREEN_READER and NO_COLOR (apps/cli/src/output.rs:56-60, :83-85, :99-101).
Config file key ui.screen_reader (apps/cli/src/lib.rs:5943-5948).
prerequisites: The agi CLI installed.
screens_and_controls: Line-based prompt 'you: ' with a bell in screen reader mode, '> ' otherwise (apps/cli/src/output.rs:274-280).
Numbered menus answered by typing a number (output.rs:340-350, :375-390).
Assistant lines prefixed 'agi: ' and tool lines 'tool: <name> <detail>' (output.rs:398-408, :462-478).
journey: Set AGI_PLAIN, pass --plain, or pass --screen-reader.
Start agi; the line-based REPL opens instead of the full-screen TUI.
Type a prompt at 'you: '.
Hear 'agi: ...' lines and 'tool: ...' lines; progress is announced once in text.
Answer questions by typing the menu number.
feedback_and_outputs: Progress text printed once to stderr, then silence (output.rs:263-270).
Prompts with labels and a bell in screen reader mode.
settings: --plain, --screen-reader flags.
AGI_PLAIN, AGI_SCREEN_READER, NO_COLOR environment variables (names only).
ui.screen_reader and ui.reduced_motion in config (apps/cli/src/lib.rs:5946; apps/cli/src/tui/tui_app.rs:7123).

working: Plain output policy is set once at startup before anything prints: flag, AGI_PLAIN non-empty, or screen reader mode turn it on (apps/cli/src/lib.rs:5943-5951).
In plain mode colour is forced off, the colour level reports None, and spinners become a single announcement line (apps/cli/src/output.rs:38-48, :89-95, :258-264).
Plain mode selects the classic REPL instead of the TUI (apps/cli/src/lib.rs:8295).
The TUI also reads plain mode to enable reduced motion (apps/cli/src/tui/tui_app.rs:7122-7124).
NO_COLOR with any value turns colour off but does not enable plain mode (output.rs:30-34, :99-101); a test sets NO_COLOR and checks the level (output.rs:1700-1716).
AGI_PLAIN empty means off, any non-empty means on (output.rs:56-60; test output.rs:1676-1695).
Screen reader mode: labels on every transcript line, numbered menus, bell prompts, tool labels, only for the interactive REPL (output.rs:62-79, :274-280, :340-350, :398-408, :462-478; lib.rs:5980).
TUI icons fall back to ASCII when NO_COLOR is set or TERM is dumb (apps/cli/src/tui/icons.rs:33-35).
incomplete: detect_color_level has no caller outside output.rs, so the colour level it computes is not used elsewhere (search in apps/cli/src found none) [inferred: colour is controlled through the colored crate override instead].
Whether the full-screen TUI colours honour NO_COLOR is not shown in the code; only icons do (apps/cli/src/tui/icons.rs:33-35).
The doc comment on screen_reader_requested_by_environment says it follows AGI_PLAIN but it reads AGI_SCREEN_READER, which can mislead (output.rs:81-85).
disconnected_or_disabled: The screen reader label mode is only on for the interactive REPL; scripted modes keep stdout free of labels by design (output.rs:62-66; lib.rs:5974-5980).
not_available: Other apps have no plain-mode equivalent (brief S11.28 lists CLI only).

established.statement: The CLI offers a plain output mode for screen readers (no colour, spinners or redraws) and honours NO_COLOR everywhere. CLI done.
Plain mode removes colour, animation and redraws, not just colour; NO_COLOR alone turns off colour but is not plain mode; any non-empty AGI_PLAIN turns plain mode on.
With reduced motion on, looping and travelling animation stops or is replaced (CLI done).
Keyboard, screen reader, focus, reduced motion and contrast are verified for core flows.

acceptance_criteria: agi --plain starts the line-based REPL with no ANSI colour in output.
AGI_PLAIN=1 does the same; AGI_PLAIN='' does not.
With plain mode on, a long operation prints its progress message once and no spinner frames.
NO_COLOR=1 alone removes colour but the full-screen interface still opens.
agi --screen-reader prefixes the prompt with 'you: ' and assistant lines with 'agi: '.
In screen reader mode a yes or no question shows a numbered menu Yes 1, No 2 and accepts the number.
A one-shot prompt run (agi -p) keeps stdout free of labels.
inferred: Screen reader mode implies plain mode because the plain flag is computed with the OR of the screen reader value (lib.rs:5949-5951) [inferred].
proposed: [proposed] Confirm that TUI colours honour NO_COLOR when plain is off, with a test.
[proposed] Fix the doc comment on screen_reader_requested_by_environment.
[proposed] Document the three switches in the CLI help text.

features.summary: The screen a person sees when a new chat opens: no messages, a ready composer and, on Web, Mobile, Desktop and the signed-in Chrome panel, a time-of-day greeting that uses the person's first name when one is known and not opted out. CLI shows a welcome panel instead. VS Code shows a neutral heading.

purpose.what_it_does: Shows an empty conversation with a ready composer. On Web, Desktop (hosted web), Mobile and the signed-in Chrome side panel it adds a greeting that changes with the time of day and may include the person's first name. CLI shows a start panel with version, model, mode and folder. VS Code shows 'Start a conversation'.
purpose.why_it_exists: A new chat needs a calm, obvious starting point. A short personal greeting makes the product feel owned by the person, and a neutral fallback protects people who do not want their name shown (doc: AGENTS.md section 6 on minimum data; brief S12.01-S12.03).
purpose.who_uses_it: Every signed-in person starting a chat on any of the six apps; signed-out Chrome users see the mark only.
problems_solved: The person knows the app is ready and where to type.
A name appears only when it is known and allowed; clearing the preferred name removes it.
Organisation members see which workspace a new chat will belong to (Web).
use_cases: Open the web chat page and read 'Good morning, <first name>' above a composer whose placeholder reads 'How can I help you today?'.
Clear the preferred name in settings and see the neutral greeting on the next new chat.
Open the CLI and read the model, access mode, folder and recent sessions before typing.
Open the mobile Chat tab in Local mode and see a greeting built only from local personalization settings.

where_to_find_it: Web: /chat new chat page, empty state of the chat (apps/web/app/chat/page.tsx:12; apps/web/features/chat/pages/WebChatPage.tsx:7646).
Desktop (public Electron app): same web page, because the window loads the hosted app origin plus the new-chat route (apps/desktop/electron/main.ts:1065).
Mobile: Chat tab empty state (apps/mobile/src/features/chat/components/ChatEmptyState.tsx:59).
CLI: start panel shown while there are no messages: 'Welcome to AGI' (apps/cli/src/tui/tui_app.rs:2773).
VS Code: sidebar chat empty state 'Start a conversation' / 'Ask about your code or describe a change.' (apps/extension-vscode/src/features/sidebar-webview/webviewContent.ts:172).

features.summary: Offers things to try on the new-chat screen. Web has a one-off starter prompt from onboarding and a 'Connect your apps (optional)' link. Mobile shows connector chips. VS Code lists up to three projects, skills and connected apps. Web and Desktop have no standing prompt list. CLI and Chrome have none.

purpose.what_it_does: Gives a person a quick way to begin: a prefilled starter prompt (Web, from onboarding), connector suggestions (Web link, Mobile chips), and in VS Code recent projects, enabled skills and connected apps that prefill the composer.
purpose.why_it_exists: Empty screens leave people unsure what to ask. Suggestions teach what the product can do and push useful connections (brief S12.04, S12.08, S12.09). The owner prefers a bare mobile screen, so suggestions there are limited to connectors (doc: docs/decisions/2026-11-10-founder-decisions.md D-2026-11-10-01).
purpose.who_uses_it: New and returning signed-in people; VS Code developers; mobile Cloud users with connectors allowed.

Re-finding a recent project from the VS Code start panel.

features.summary: One-step ways to set up the next message and explanations of the modes. Web and Desktop have the Chat | Work switch with hover explanations and a slash menu with descriptions and examples. CLI explains each permission mode. Chrome has page action chips. Mobile has no task chips file; modes sit in the Add to chat sheet.

purpose.why_it_exists: People do not know what the modes mean until told (brief S12.05, S12.21).
purpose.who_uses_it: New and returning users on every app.

features.summary: Switches the next message to image or video generation so the send creates media. Web and Desktop have 'Create image' and 'Create video' rows in the plus menu, with badges and reasons when blocked, and /image. Mobile has the same names in 'Add to chat'. CLI has /image on managed access. VS Code and Chrome have none.

purpose.what_it_does: Puts the composer in image or video mode; the send starts generation instead of a chat reply, with settings such as aspect ratio.
purpose.why_it_exists: Media generation is costly and needs explicit intent and model choice (brief S12.12, S12.13).
purpose.who_uses_it: People creating pictures or clips; plan holders with the media capabilities.
problems_solved: Choosing generation instead of chat.
Seeing why generation is blocked.
Knowing what input a video accepts.
use_cases: Click Create image, type a prompt and send.
Attach a picture to edit it in image mode.
Click Create video and see that attached files are not sent unless they are PNG, JPEG or WebP.
In CLI run /image a red bicycle.

where_to_find_it: Web and Desktop (Electron): plus menu rows 'Create image' and 'Create video' (ComposerPlusMenu.tsx:160-161,1299-1301); '/image' slash command (slashCommands.ts:46-52).
Mobile: 'Add to chat' sheet rows 'Create image' and 'Create video' (AddToChatSheet.tsx:927,943), cloud only.
CLI: '/image <prompt>' on managed access only (tui_app.rs:1094-1100,5576).
VS Code and Chrome: none found (brief says missing).
prerequisites: Capability canUseImages or canUseVideoGeneration and plan capability image_generation or video_generation (AddToChatSheet.tsx:331-342; ChatComposerNew.tsx:1057-1071).
A media model available in the deployment.
Not a free-trial session on web (ChatComposerNew.tsx:1070-1071).
screens_and_controls: Row badges: checking, retry, unavailable or an upgrade badge (ComposerPlusMenu.tsx:334-360).
Hover title: 'Free video availability could not be checked. Click to retry.', 'This deployment is not ready for video generation.', or the entitlement hint (ComposerPlusMenu.tsx:317-332).
Mobile: model list for the active kind, aspect ratio, resolution, duration, 'Transparent background', cost estimate; indicator 'Create an image'/'Create a video' on the composer (chat.tsx:493-495).
Persistent paywall or free-limit card with a dismiss control (WebChatPage.tsx:5337-5352).
journey: Open a new chat.
Choose Create image or Create video (or /image).
Optionally attach a picture and choose model and options.
Type the prompt and send.
The app starts generation, shows progress, then the media appears in the chat.
Leave the mode or send another prompt.
feedback_and_outputs: Notices: 'Video generation works from your prompt only. Attached files are not sent to the video model. Leave video mode first if you want to send this file to the chat model.' (ChatComposerNew.tsx:2229).
'Video takes PNG, JPEG or WebP images only...' (line 2240).
'Image mode takes images only...'.

settings: Mobile aspect ratio, resolution, duration and transparent background in the chat view store.

features.summary: A button next to the empty composer that starts a spoken, hands-free conversation. Web and desktop show it only for cloud-managed chats when the account may use voice. Mobile opens a voice intro, then a live voice chat. The CLI uses a push-to-talk /voice command. VS Code has no voice mode.

purpose.what_it_does: Lets a person leave the typed box and talk to the assistant. On web and desktop the button 'Start voice mode' enters a voice session surface. On mobile it creates a 'Voice chat' conversation and opens it in live voice, or falls back to turn-based voice on the device. In the CLI /voice records with push-to-talk and sends the transcript as a message. (apps/web/features/chat/components/Composer/VoiceEntryButton.tsx:9) (apps/mobile/app/(app)/(tabs)/chat.tsx:1071) (apps/cli/src/voice.rs:1)
purpose.why_it_exists: The area brief says the new-chat screen must let the user start a spoken (voice-mode) conversation (doc: knowledge-base/data/area-briefs/012-new-chat-experience.md, S12.14). The mobile requirements say live voice is separate from dictation and must be labelled unavailable when it is (doc: docs/product/requirements.md, M-VOICE-004).
purpose.who_uses_it: People on web, desktop, mobile and the CLI who want hands-free or spoken chat, including people who cannot type easily.
problems_solved: Typing is slow or impossible while walking, driving or when hands are busy.
Dictation only fills the box; voice mode is a back-and-forth spoken chat.
People need a clear reason when voice cannot be used (Local mode, signed out, switched off).
use_cases: On web, click the round voice button in an empty composer and talk with a cloud model.
On mobile, tap the voice button in the chat input, accept the first-use intro, pick a voice, and talk.
In the CLI, type /voice, hold SPACE to record, release to send the transcript.
On desktop, use the hosted web composer's voice button, or the desktop voice hotkey to toggle dictation.

where_to_find_it: Web: round button labelled 'Start voice mode' at the end of the composer, shown instead of the send button while the field is empty and no turn is running (apps/web/features/chat/components/Composer/ChatComposerNew.tsx:6955).
Desktop: the public Electron window shows the hosted web app, so it is the same button (doc: AGENTS.md section 5, 'The public Desktop shows the hosted web app').

Mobile: round button with accessibility label 'Start voice mode' and hint 'Opens hands-free voice conversation' in the chat input when it is idle and empty (apps/mobile/src/features/chat/components/ChatInput.tsx:2293); also the '/voice' slash command (apps/mobile/src/features/chat/components/ChatInput.tsx:1563).
CLI: '/voice' or '/v' slash command in the line REPL and the TUI (apps/cli/src/repl/slash_commands.rs:530) (apps/cli/src/tui/tui_app.rs:6352).

VS Code: none. Chrome: a microphone button labelled 'Voice input' exists in the side panel (apps/extension/src/side_panel.ts:14099); whether it is dictation or voice mode was not opened beyond its label (unknown).
prerequisites: Web: the canUseVoice capability is granted, the host passes a voice handler, and the chat is cloud-managed (no on-device model, no local turns, provider mode ManagedGateway or ManagedNative) (apps/web/features/chat/pages/WebChatPage.tsx:5907).
Server: the plan must allow voice and the capability flag must be on, or the session request is refused (apps/web/app/api/voice/live/sessions/route.ts:308).

Mobile: the canUseVoice capability; live voice also needs Cloud mode, a signed-in account, a native build with WebRTC and an https server; otherwise it stays turn based (apps/mobile/src/features/voice/services/liveVoiceAvailability.ts:21).
CLI: a microphone and one transcription route (account, a provider key, or a local whisper program) (apps/cli/src/voice.rs:1).
screens_and_controls: Web: VoiceEntryButton (title and aria-label 'Start voice mode'); a separate dictation microphone button sits beside it (apps/web/features/chat/components/Composer/ChatComposerNew.tsx:6941).
Web voice session: VoiceModeSurface, VoiceOrb, VoiceComposer, VoiceSettingsModal, AudioRoutePicker in apps/web/features/chat/components/Voice.
Mobile: VoiceIntroHint, VoiceOnboardingSheet ('Meet Voice', Continue), VoicePickerSheet, VoiceInlineBar (apps/mobile/app/(app)/(tabs)/chat.tsx:1454).
CLI: prompt text of push-to-talk; SPACE records, ESC exits (apps/cli/src/voice.rs:49).
journey: Web: open a new chat with a cloud model; the composer is empty so the voice button replaces Send.
Click 'Start voice mode'; the page calls enterVoiceSession which stops any dictation and dispatches the enter event (apps/web/features/chat/stores/voice-session-store.ts:220).
The voice surface asks the server for a live session; the server checks capability, plan, allowance or budget, and reserves usage (apps/web/app/api/voice/live/sessions/route.ts:731).
Talk; captions and the orb show state; use settings for voice, language, pace.

Mobile: tap the voice button; first time a 'Meet Voice' sheet shows, then a voice picker, then startVoiceMode creates a 'Voice chat' conversation and opens it with voice=live (apps/mobile/app/(app)/(tabs)/chat.tsx:1114).
If live voice is unavailable but the on-device recognizer is guaranteed, mobile shows the inline turn-based voice bar with the reason (apps/mobile/app/(app)/(tabs)/chat.tsx:1076).
feedback_and_outputs: Web: voice orb, captions and announcements during the session; a usage-limit error is flagged so Retry is not offered (apps/web/features/chat/stores/voice-session-store.ts:63).

Mobile: Alert 'Voice is unavailable' with 'The chat could not be started.' or the switched-off text; inline reason strings such as 'Live voice runs in AGI Cloud, so Local Mode stays turn based.' (apps/mobile/src/features/voice/services/liveVoiceAvailability.ts:17).

Mobile intro disclosure: 'Your voice is transcribed on this device and never recorded.' (on-device) or that audio streams to the voice provider and the transcript is saved (live) (apps/mobile/src/features/voice/components/VoiceOnboardingSheet.tsx:67).
CLI: transcript is appended to the session labelled '(spoken)' in the TUI (apps/cli/src/tui/tui_app.rs:4469).
settings: Web: dictationEnabled setting and a billing 'disabledFeatures' switch affect dictation, not voice mode (apps/ web/features/chat/components/Composer/ChatComposerNew.tsx:1790).
Web voice session store keeps voice, language, pace, reasoning (store name agi-web-voice-session) (apps/web/features/chat/stores/voice-session-store.ts:23).
Mobile: voiceEnabled, voiceOnboardingSeen, start-with-voice-on-launch (apps/mobile/app/(app)/(tabs)/chat.tsx:1124) (apps/mobile/stores/settingsStore.ts:55).
CLI: language argument to /voice, validated against supported languages (apps/cli/src/repl/slash_commands.rs:536).

working: Web voice entry button renders only when a voice handler exists, canUseVoice is granted, no turn is streaming and the field is empty (apps/web/features/chat/components/Composer/ChatComposerNew.tsx:6955).
Web hands a handler to the composer only for managed models without local turns (apps/web/features/chat/pages/WebChatPage.tsx:5907) (apps/web/features/chat/pages/WebChatPage.tsx:7672).
Server session route checks plan, flag, training opt-out, free allowance or paid budget and reserves usage (apps/web/app/api/voice/live/sessions/route.ts:308).
Web dictation is refused for Local and own-key (DirectByok) selections and for conversations that hold local or own-key turns (apps/web/features/chat/components/Composer/ChatComposerNew.tsx:2048).
Mobile voice entry, intro sheet, picker, live route push and on-device fallback are wired (apps/mobile/app/(app)/(tabs)/chat.tsx:1071).
CLI /voice with push-to-talk and three transcription backends, with a cloud-egress gate for Local privacy sessions (apps/cli/src/voice.rs:980).
incomplete: CLI cannot be used as a spoken reply loop: the module records and transcribes; whether it speaks answers was not checked (unknown) (apps/cli/src/voice.rs:1).
Desktop: no desktop-only code for the voice-mode button was found; it relies on the hosted web app (apps/web/features/chat/pages/WebChatPage.tsx:7672).
disconnected_or_disabled: Web voice button is hidden for Local and own-key chats because voiceManaged is false for them (apps/web/features/chat/pages/WebChatPage.tsx:5907).
Chrome side-panel mic button is hidden unless canUseVoice is granted (apps/extension/src/side_panel.ts:15242).
not_available: VS Code: no voice mode. A dictation client exists (apps/extension-vscode/src/features/sidebar-webview/dictationClient.ts) but no live voice entry was found (brief: missing).
Mobile Local mode: live voice is not offered ('Live voice runs in AGI Cloud') (apps/mobile/src/features/voice/services/liveVoiceAvailability.ts:17).

established.statement: From the new-chat screen the user can start a spoken (voice-mode) conversation.
Live voice mode is separate from dictation; if unavailable the UI labels it unavailable.
Voice privacy is documented so the user knows whether audio is local or provider/cloud.
No interim dictation text, as in ChatGPT and Claude (founder decision).

acceptance_criteria: On web with a cloud model and an empty composer, 'Start voice mode' shows; typing a character replaces it with Send.
With a Local or own-key model selected, the button does not show and dictation is refused.
With canUseVoice off for the account, the button is absent on web and mobile shows 'Voice is unavailable'.
A plan without voice gets a 403 from the live session route and the UI shows the plan message.
Mobile in Local mode or signed out never opens live voice and shows the reason text.
First mobile use shows the 'Meet Voice' sheet once; later uses skip it.
CLI /voice with an unsupported language prints the supported list and does not record.
inferred: The button hides while a turn runs so a spoken session cannot start over a stream [inferred from sendButtonMode !== 'stop'].
Voice minutes are metered against plan allowance and usage budgets, since the route reserves usage before a session [inferred from reserveManagedUsageRequest call].
proposed: [proposed] Show a visible reason on web when the button is hidden because the model is Local or own-key, instead of hiding it silently.
[proposed] Record in this knowledge base whether the Chrome mic button is dictation or voice mode.

steps.what_happens: Person clicks 'Start voice mode'; the composer calls the host handler.
enterVoiceSession cancels any dictation listening and dispatches the enter event to the session reducer.
The page asks the server for a live session. The server checks the canUseVoice flag, plan voice permission, free allowance or paid budget, and reserves usage.
Audio and replies run between the device and the live voice provider chosen by the server; the model comes from the live voice catalog.
Mobile checks Local mode, sign-in and native module, then creates a 'Voice chat' conversation and opens it with voice=live.
Mobile fallback: turn-based voice uses the on-device speech recognizer, with the disclosure that the voice is transcribed on the device.
CLI records with the default microphone, writes a temporary WAV, transcribes through the account, a provider key, or a local whisper program, then deletes the recording.

execution_and_data_flow.models_and_providers: Web live voice uses a catalog-resolved live model and a plan-dependent backend model chosen on the server, not by the user (apps/web/app/api/voice/live/sessions/route.ts:290). Voice is only offered for managed (Cloud) models; own-key and Local selections are excluded (apps/web/features/chat/pages/WebChatPage.tsx:5907). CLI transcription can use the AGI account, an OpenAI key, or a local whisper program (apps/cli/src/voice.rs:1). Provider names for live voice were not read: unknown.

access_and_usage.account: Web and desktop: signed-in account needed for the live session route (user id read at session creation). Mobile: signed-in for live voice, none for turn-based on-device voice. CLI: account only for the managed backend.
access_and_usage.permissions: Microphone permission on mobile and browser (mobile has permission alerts: apps/mobile/src/features/voice/components/voicePermissionAlert.ts). On the server the canUseVoice capability must be available for the subject (apps/web/app/api/voice/live/sessions/route.ts:308).
access_and_usage.subscription: A plan whose tier policy has allowVoice is required; otherwise 403 (apps/web/app/api/voice/live/sessions/route.ts:318). Free plans get a seconds allowance (freeVoiceAllowanceSeconds) and paid plans are checked against a budget and a voice_minutes allowance (apps/web/app/api/voice/live/sessions/route.ts:340). Exact plan names: unknown here.
access_and_usage.limits_and_metering: Sessions are reserved in blocks (LIVE_VOICE_BLOCK_SECONDS) with a lease; usage is settled, abandoned sessions are settled before the allowance is read (apps/web/app/api/voice/live/sessions/route.ts:380). Numbers are config in code, not restated here.
access_and_usage.flags: canUseVoice capability flag evaluated per user, workspace, plan and surface (apps/web/app/api/voice/live/sessions/route.ts:299). Dictation can also be switched off by a billing 'disabledFeatures' entry (apps/web/features/chat/hooks/use-dictation.ts:44).
access_and_usage.model_compatibility: Only managed gateway or managed native models (apps/web/features/chat/pages/WebChatPage.tsx:5907).
access_and_usage.provider_restrictions: The session refuses when the live voice model or the backend model may train on inputs and the user opted out, or the chat carries Google user data (apps/web/app/api/voice/live/sessions/route.ts:330).
access_and_usage.local_mode: Web: no voice-mode button and dictation is off for Local selections. Mobile: live voice is off in Local mode ('Live voice runs in AGI Cloud, so Local Mode stays turn based.') but on-device turn-based voice can run where the recognizer is guaranteed (apps/mobile/app/(app)/(tabs)/chat.tsx:1069). CLI Local privacy sessions gate cloud transcription (apps/cli/src/voice.rs:980).

features.summary: Lets a person make a chat that is not kept in history, search or memory. Web shows a plus-menu row ('Use incognito'), mobile shows an eye-off header toggle, Chrome a menu item, desktop a 'New Temporary Chat' menu entry, the CLI a no-persistence flag. Projects cannot hold temporary chats. Cloud copies are purged after 30 days.

purpose.what_it_does: Marks the next or current chat as temporary. A temporary chat is created with isTemporary true, its messages are not written to history, it is excluded from search and memory, and its attachments stay out of the Library. (apps/web/lib/temporary-chat-policy.ts:21-33)
purpose.why_it_exists: The brief requires that before or during a new chat the user can switch it to a temporary chat not kept in history (doc: knowledge-base/data/area-briefs/012-new-chat-experience.md, S12.17). The requirements say temporary chats must not read or update memory (doc: docs/product/requirements.md:765). A founder decision says temporary chats keep no 30-day safety copy (doc: docs/decisions/2026-09-27-founder-decisions.md, D-2026-09-28-05).
purpose.who_uses_it: Anyone asking something private or one-off on web, desktop, mobile, Chrome or the CLI.
problems_solved: Private questions should not clutter history or feed memory.
People need a clear promise of what is and is not kept.
People can change their mind: save a temporary chat, or end it with a warning.
use_cases: Turn on 'Use incognito' from the web plus menu before the first message.
Turn on 'Start new chats as temporary' in Privacy settings so every new chat starts temporary.
On mobile tap the eye-off icon, confirm 'Turn on temporary chat?', then chat.
Midway through, turn it off on web and choose 'Save chat' to keep the messages.

Temporary chats keep no 30-day copy for safety review.

'End temporary chat' asks for confirmation naming that the messages are lost.

steps.what_happens: Person picks 'Use incognito'; with no conversation yet the composer stores pendingTemporaryChat true.
On send the page resolves temporaryIntent (project must be empty) and creates the conversation with isTemporary.
The server writes the conversation row with is_temporary true, refuses message persistence for it, filters it from search and retrieval, and leaves memory out of the turn.
Turning it off mid-chat: the host performs an update (PUT /api/chat/conversations/:id) and writes the server value back; with kept messages it first saves them after a confirm.
A nightly cron deletes temporary chats and files older than 30 days unless on legal hold.
Mobile Local mode: the chat stays on the device; Cloud mode creates the conversation remotely with isTemporary.

features.summary: Short first-run flows on each app. Web has a two-step wizard at /welcome with starter prompts. Mobile has hero, about-you and device-setup screens. The CLI has a terminal setup wizard. VS Code has a walkthrough and a first-run panel. Chrome opens a Welcome page on install. Each can be skipped.

purpose.what_it_does: Greets a first-time person, asks for light personalization or setup, and then lands them in the first chat. Web asks for a preferred name and work description, then offers starter prompts. Mobile asks to accept terms, collects name and work, then offers a local model download or sign in to Cloud. (apps/web/features/onboarding/components/OnboardingWizard.tsx:36) (apps/mobile/app/(public)/onboarding.tsx:280)

purpose.who_uses_it: New users on every app.
problems_solved: Empty new-chat screens do not tell a new person what to do.

features.summary: A typed but unsent message comes back after navigating away or reloading. Web saves it in browser local storage per conversation, mobile saves it on the device with its attachments, VS Code keeps it in webview state, Chrome keeps it for the browser session. The CLI does not restore drafts. Temporary chats never save drafts.

purpose.what_it_does: Writes the text in the composer to storage while the person types and fills it back in when the same chat is opened again. (apps/web/features/chat/components/Composer/composer-draft-storage.ts:131) (apps/mobile/src/features/chat/draftStore.ts:148)
purpose.why_it_exists: The brief requires that an unsent draft typed in a new chat is restored after navigation or reload (doc: knowledge-base/data/area-briefs/012-new-chat-experience.md, S12.23). The experience contract lists conversation draft state and says failed uploads preserve the draft (doc: docs/product/experience-contract.md:113, 777).
purpose.who_uses_it: Anyone who writes long messages, switches chats, or whose tab reloads.
problems_solved: Lost text after an accidental reload or navigation.
A private draft following the person into another chat.
Stale drafts from old documents coming back.
use_cases: Type a long question, open another page, come back and find it.
Reload the browser tab and keep the text.
On mobile, leave the chat screen and return.
In VS Code, switch sidebar views and return to the draft.

screens_and_controls: The normal composer; no separate control. Web shows a notice if the draft cannot be saved (apps/web/features/chat/components/Composer/ChatComposerNew.tsx:693).

The text is written to storage on each change.
Leave the page, reload or switch chat.
Return to the same chat: the text is filled back in.
Send or clear the box: the stored draft is emptied.
feedback_and_outputs: Chrome shows a restored notice or a failure notice (spDraftRestored, spDraftRestoreFailed) (apps/extension/src/side_panel.ts:10148-10154).
Web shows the draft-not-saved notice when storage refuses a write (apps/web/features/chat/components/Composer/ChatComposerNew.tsx:4124).

working: Web storage: key prefix agi-composer-draft, record version 2, one key per owner id and conversation (or 'new-chat') in localStorage (apps/web/features/chat/components/Composer/composer-draft-storage.ts:1-24).

Each document load gets a random owner id kept in sessionStorage; drafts of previous owners are copied to the new owner, and removed only when the load is a reload (apps/web/features/chat/components/Composer/composer-draft-storage.ts:60-110, 184).
Empty text is stored as an empty record so an old or legacy draft cannot return (apps/web/features/chat/components/Composer/composer-draft-storage.ts:131).
Composer parks outgoing draft in the chat store and reads the persisted draft on arrival (apps/web/features/chat/components/Composer/ChatComposerNew.tsx:4140-4155).
Draft is cleared when the chat is temporary (apps/web/features/chat/components/Composer/ChatComposerNew.tsx:4118).
Mobile stores draft text and attachments with provenance (local or cloud owner) in MMKV under 'composer-draft:' (apps/mobile/src/features/chat/draftStore.ts:5-13).
VS Code keeps drafts per thread in webview state (apps/extension-vscode/src/features/sidebar-webview/webviewContent.ts:4247).

features.summary: On the web, a signed-out visitor can chat in a limited text-only mode, with a daily message count, spend caps and age confirmation, and prominent 'Log in' and 'Sign up for free' links. It is off unless bot protection is ready and the guest.chat flag is on. Mobile and CLI let people start Local without an account and prompt sign-in for Cloud.

steps.what_happens: The /chat layout finds no signed-in user and no session cookie and asks if guest chat is open.
The access check requires bot protection and evaluates the guest.chat flag for a web visitor.
The browser posts a turn; the server checks flag, CSRF, human caller, schema, age, then per-network and per-device rate limits.
The server moderates the prompt, prices the turn and reserves spend at device, network and global scope.
The reply streams from the Free-plan default chat model through its provider route with a turn timeout; the spend hold is settled with real usage.
Mobile and CLI Local paths run on the device with no account.

features.summary: Keeps the text a person has typed but not sent. Web and Desktop write it to browser storage per chat and, for saved Cloud chats, to our server so another device sees it. Mobile stores it on the device. A failed send or a stranded queued message puts text back. Temporary chats keep nothing.

purpose.what_it_does: Saves unsent composer text per conversation (and one for the new-chat screen), restores it after reload, crash, chat switch or failed send, and on the web syncs it to the account so a second device or tab can pick it up, with a compare dialog when two versions collide.
purpose.why_it_exists: Losing a half-written prompt is a top annoyance; the leaders keep drafts per chat. It also guards against text leaking from one chat into another and keeps private chats private (brief S13.16 to S13.18).
purpose.who_uses_it: Every person who types in the composer on Web, Desktop (which shows the hosted web app, doc: AGENTS.md section 5), Mobile, Chrome side panel, and in a limited way VS Code and the CLI.
problems_solved: Text lost on reload, crash or navigation
Text from one chat appearing in another
A failed send that looks like the message vanished
A queued follow-up lost when the person changes chat
use_cases: Type a long prompt, reload the tab, see it still there with the same chat open.
Start a draft on a laptop, open the same Cloud chat on another browser, find the draft.
A send fails; the text returns to the box with a notice.
Switch to another chat mid-sentence and come back; the sentence is waiting.

working: Web and Desktop browser storage: per conversation key, versioned record, per-tab owner id so one tab cannot clear another tab's text, copy forward on reload, empty draft kept as a tombstone (apps/web/features/chat/components/Composer/composer-draft-storage.ts:21,60,146).
