features.summary: CLI recalls earlier prompts with Up and Down and keeps them in history.txt. Suggestions are three follow-up questions shown after a reply: Web and Desktop show them after searched or research turns when the setting is on, Mobile shows them in Cloud chats, VS Code offers three fixed prompts in its native chat panel.

purpose.what_it_does: Lets a terminal user step back through sent prompts and forward again, restoring the unfinished draft at the end, and offers clickable follow-up questions after an answer.
purpose.why_it_exists: Retyping long prompts is slow; the leaders show related questions after answers. Suggestions are a fast way to continue (brief S13.19, S13.20).
purpose.who_uses_it: CLI users for history; chat users on Web, Desktop, Mobile and the VS Code chat panel for suggestions.
problems_solved: Retyping a prompt
Not knowing what to ask next
use_cases: In the CLI press Up twice to rerun an older prompt with a change.
Press Down past the newest prompt to get back the half-typed text.
After a web-searched answer click a suggested question to ask it.
On Mobile in a Cloud chat tap a suggestion chip.

features.summary: The + button lists ways to add files and context and switch tools on. Output makes the reply a Document, Presentation or Spreadsheet file. The microphone dictates into the box for review. The round voice button starts a hands-free conversation when the box is empty. Cloud features need our servers; Mobile dictation runs on the device.

purpose.why_it_exists: Matches ChatGPT and Claude composers: one place for everything attachable, and speech as an input (brief S13.34 to S13.37).
purpose.who_uses_it: All chat users; Mobile users who dictate on the go; CLI users with /dictate and /voice.

steps.what_happens: Output choice is stored as office format in composer toggles.
Send includes office_creation and office_format; the server adds an instruction and the Office file tool.
Web dictation records audio in the browser and posts it to the server route.
Server checks the kill switch, plan allowance and privacy setting, and sends audio to the transcription provider; audio is not stored.
Transcript returns and is inserted in the box.
Mobile dictation recognises speech on the device.
Chrome hands audio to the browser's own speech service; AGI receives only text.

features.summary: While a reply runs, a person can keep typing. The message is held in a queue (with Edit and Cancel) and sent when the reply ends, or it is steered into a running cloud task that reads it at its next step. On the CLI, /btw asks a side question that leaves the main task alone.

purpose.what_it_does: Lets a person send another message while an AI reply or agent task is still running. The message either waits in order (queue) or is handed to the running task as guidance (steer). The CLI also offers a side question (/btw) answered from the chat so far without changing it.
purpose.why_it_exists: Waiting for a long reply to finish before typing is slow. Leading chat and coding assistants let people queue, redirect or ask aside while work runs; the brief (S13.38 to S13.41) requires the same in every app.
purpose.who_uses_it: Anyone using chat or agent tasks in AGI Workforce: web and desktop (Electron shows the web app) users, phone users, VS Code and Chrome users, and CLI users.
problems_solved: No dead time while a long reply or task runs.
A running task can be corrected without stopping it and losing progress.
A quick question can be asked without disturbing the main task (CLI).
A queued message can be fixed or dropped before it goes out.
use_cases: On web, type the next question during a streaming reply; it appears as 'Queued' and sends when the reply ends.
During a long AGI Work cloud task on web, press Steer on a queued row so the agent reads it at its next step.
On mobile, open 'Message the agent' on a running task and send a change of course.
On the CLI, type '/btw what did we decide about X?' during a turn and get a short answer in the transcript.

where_to_find_it: Web (and desktop through the hosted web app): the composer. A 'Queued messages' list appears above the input with buttons Steer, Edit, Cancel (apps/web/features/chat/components/Composer/ChatComposerNew.tsx:5011-5063). The input placeholder during a reply is 'Follow up' (ChatComposerNew.tsx:353).

Task detail also has a steer section (apps/mobile/src/features/tasks/components/CloudRunSteerSection.tsx:1-60).

Setting agiWorkforce.composer.followUpBehavior (apps/extension-vscode/package.json:1238).

screens_and_controls: Web: Steer, Edit and Cancel buttons on each queued row; the label reads 'Queued: ...', 'Queued 2 of 3: ...' or 'Sent to the running reply: ...' (ChatComposerNew.tsx:5017-5062).

journey: 1. Start a reply or agent task.
2. While it runs, type the next message in the composer and send it (Enter).

3. Web/desktop: the message appears as a 'Queued' row (ChatComposerNew.tsx:3952-3972). If Follow-up behavior is Steer and the run is a cloud run, it is steered automatically (ChatComposerNew.tsx:4494-4507); otherwise press Steer on the row.
4. Optional: press Edit (text and attachments return to the box) or Cancel (row removed).
5. When the reply ends the first queued message for that chat is sent (ChatComposerNew.tsx:4340-4382); one message is released per finished turn.
6. A steered row shows 'Sent to the running reply' and disappears once the agent has read it (ChatComposerNew.tsx:4445-4454).
7. CLI: during a turn type '/btw question' and press Enter; the answer appears as a system message starting 'btw:' (tui_app.rs:4714-4731).
feedback_and_outputs: Web notices: 'This reply cannot take a message now, so yours sends when it finishes.' (ChatComposerNew.tsx:4470); 'Your message did not reach the running reply. It is still queued.' (ChatComposerNew.tsx:4465).
Web notice when chat is switched: 'Your queued message was not sent: you switched chats before the reply finished.' plus whether it was saved as a draft (ChatComposerNew.tsx:4401-4418).
Web research: 'Your guidance is applied when the current step finishes, and the plan updates to follow it.' (ResearchActivity.tsx:604-612).
Mobile: 'Sent. The agent reads your message at its next step.' or errors in an alert text (RunSteerInput.tsx:84-100).
Server: 202 on accepted steer; 409 messages such as 'This task already has 10 messages waiting...' (apps/web/app/api/llm/v1/chat/completions/runs/[runId]/steer/route.ts:62-85).
CLI: status text 'answering the side question' (tui_app.rs:7636).

acceptance_criteria: Type a message during a streaming reply on web: a 'Queued' row appears with Steer (only for a cloud run), Edit and Cancel; the message is sent once when the reply ends.
Queue two messages: rows read 'Queued 1 of 2' and '2 of 2'; only one is sent per finished reply.
Click Edit: the text and its attachments return to the box and the row is removed or replaced on re-send; Cancel removes the row and nothing is sent.
Queue a message, then switch to another chat before the reply ends: nothing is sent into the other chat, a notice explains, and the text is saved as a draft in the original chat.

On a running cloud task with Follow-up behavior set to Steer, an Enter-sent message without attachments shows 'Sent to the running reply' and the agent acts on it at its next step; with an attachment it stays queued.
Press Cmd/Ctrl+Shift+Enter with the setting at Queue: that one message is steered instead.
On mobile, 'Message the agent' on a running task sends text and shows 'Sent. The agent reads your message at its next step.'; on a finished task the control is not shown.
On the CLI, '/btw <question>' during or between turns returns a 'btw:' answer and the main conversation history is unchanged.

steps.what_happens: Person sends while a turn is active; the web composer stores the send arguments with the current conversation id as a queued row and clears the box.
If steering applies (setting Steer, or inverted, and a streaming cloud run exists, no attachments), the composer calls steerActiveTurn, which posts the text to the run's steer endpoint.

Server checks rate limit, CSRF, run id, message length, secret handling, then appends {id,text,queued_at} to pending_steer if the run is in a held state, not pausing or cancelling, under 10 waiting, and not a Code run; returns 202.

The executor takes and clears pending_steer at its next step boundary and gives the messages to the model; the web composer drops the 'Sent to the running reply' row when the run's activity shows the steer was read.

When the turn ends, the composer sends the first queued message for the same conversation through the normal send path; messages queued for another conversation are returned to that chat's draft with a notice.
Mobile 'Message the agent' posts to the same steer endpoint via the cloud run client.
VS Code steer calls the local developer runtime's steerTurn for the active turn; on a turn-ended error it queues instead.

CLI /btw copies the conversation text, adds a short 'Side question' prompt with no tools, and streams a completion from the session's provider and model; the answer is shown as a system message. Which provider answers depends on CLI configuration (unknown).

execution_and_data_flow.models_and_providers: Queue and Edit/Cancel use no model. A steer is read by whichever model runs the cloud task; the model choice is the task's own and the steer adds no routing rule (found no model code in the steer route). VS Code steers the local developer runtime on the same model as the active turn; a different requested model forces queueing instead (ChatStateManager.ts:4837-4841). CLI /btw uses the session's provider and model and obeys the Local-to-cloud privacy guard (agent/chat.rs:1725-1727).

access_and_usage.account: Web steer needs a signed-in user because the endpoint resolves a user-scoped database (steer/route.ts:35-37). Queueing on web, mobile, VS Code, CLI needs no extra account step beyond whatever sending a message needs. Chrome queueing needs a ready managed cloud chat with an owner (side_panel.ts:8704-8711).
access_and_usage.permissions: Run ownership is enforced by user_id and organization_id in the SQL (cloud-agent-run-service.ts:2807-2810). Steer text passes the secret-handling gate: secrets block the request or are redacted (steer/route.ts:46-50). CSRF token required (route.ts:37-38).
access_and_usage.subscription: none found in the code for the steer route or the queue; subscription limits apply to the underlying chat or task run, not to steering itself [inferred].
access_and_usage.limits_and_metering: Rate limit bucket 'llm-completion' on the steer route (route.ts:32). Max 10 waiting steers per run and 4,000 characters per message (packages/contracts/cloud-contracts/src/cloud-agent-runs.ts:80-81). VS Code queue cap 20 (ChatStateManager.ts:276); Chrome queue has a lane cap (side_panel.ts:8727-8730). No usage metering of the steer itself found.
access_and_usage.flags: Settings, not flags: web followUpBehavior (default queue), codeFollowUpQueueMode (desktop host only), VS Code agiWorkforce.composer.followUpBehavior (default queue). No feature flag found.
access_and_usage.model_compatibility: Steering applies to any model run inside a managed cloud agent run. VS Code steer needs the same model as the active turn and no extra effort setting, edit-automatically off and shell approval off (ChatStateManager.ts:4696-4704). Web steer: no model check found.
access_and_usage.provider_restrictions: none found in the code for queue or steer. CLI /btw is blocked if the privacy boundary check fails (agent/chat.rs:1725).
access_and_usage.local_mode: Web and mobile queue works the same in any mode because it is on the device; web Steer needs a cloud agent run id, so it is not offered for a Local reply (canSteerQueued needs streamingRunId, ChatComposerNew.tsx:4486). VS Code steers its local developer runtime without cloud. CLI queue and /btw work locally; /btw on a Local session refuses cloud egress (agent/chat.rs:1725). Whether mobile steer works for a Local task: unknown (RunSteerInput posts to the cloud run API, steerCloudRun).

features.summary: Lets a person pick one or more files on their device and stage them on the next message: web and desktop composer, phone attach sheet, CLI commands, VS Code sidebar and Chrome side panel. Each app checks type, size and count first and tells the person which files were refused and why.

purpose.what_it_does: Opens the system file chooser (CLI: takes a path) and turns the chosen files into staged attachments that go with the next message. The web admission step checks duplicates, file count, empty files, size, type, image size and total message size, then reports 'Attached N of M files. Not attached: ...' (apps/web/features/chat/hooks/use-attachments.ts:222-246).
purpose.why_it_exists: An assistant can only work on documents and pictures the person can hand over. The brief marks the device picker and multi-select (S14.01, S14.15) done on all six apps (doc: knowledge-base/data/area-briefs/014-attachment-intake-components.md). The requirements say a chip shows name, type and size and a removed file is not sent (doc: docs/product/requirements.md:990-993).
purpose.who_uses_it: Anyone sending a document, spreadsheet, slide deck, image or source file to the assistant on any of the six apps.
problems_solved: Getting a local file into the conversation without copying its text by hand.
Attaching several files in one action.

Knowing which files were refused, so the model is not asked about a file it never received (the web draft keeps a refusal list that is turned into notes on the turn: use-attachments.ts:304-317, apps/web/features/chat/lib/attachment-metadata.ts:28-34).
use_cases: Web or desktop: attach a PDF and two images to ask for a comparison.
Phone in Cloud mode: tap File and pick a Word document to summarise.
CLI: /attach report.pdf to ask questions about a PDF in the workspace.
VS Code: attach three source files from the workspace before asking for a refactor.

steps.what_happens: Person opens the attach control and picks files in the browser chooser; handleFileDrop passes them to addChatAttachments, which refuses them in video, image or restricted-free modes where the model cannot read them.
admitFiles applies the rules and builds chips with object URLs; pictures are rewritten without location and camera details.
Limits used in those rules were fetched earlier from the account endpoint.
On send the web page uploads the files to the managed cloud upload endpoints (presign path and complete path) and sends their asset ids with the message.
Phone: picker returns files, validation runs, chips show; in Cloud mode upload happens with retry; in Local mode documents are read on the phone.
CLI: file read on the computer, wrapped as a document or image block or as <attached_file> text, then sent with the next turn to whichever provider the session uses.
VS Code: file read with the editor API into pending attachments held in the extension; sent with the next message.
Chrome: file read in the panel, then uploaded to the managed cloud upload client on admission.

execution_and_data_flow.models_and_providers: Whether the model can read a file depends on the selected model: a restricted free model takes images only (ChatComposerNew.tsx:2267-2285); a local on-device model on web cannot read attachments (packages/contracts/local-runtime/src/inference.ts:131); phone and Chrome compare the image count to the model's image limit (attachmentValidation.ts:187-203; side_panel.ts:10150-10160). The picker itself uses no provider.

access_and_usage.account: Web upload goes through authenticated upload routes; whether an anonymous web visitor can attach is unknown. Chrome needs a signed-in Cloud chat in ready state (side_panel.ts:10006-10017). Phone File card needs Cloud mode. CLI and VS Code need no account for local reads.
access_and_usage.permissions: Browser file chooser needs none. Phone Photos uses the system picker (no broad library permission requested first: apps/mobile/__tests__/photo-picker.test.ts:32). VS Code requires workspace trust. CLI is limited to workspace roots.
access_and_usage.subscription: Per-message file count and byte limits come from the plan limits table; every plan entry I read uses the same count constant of 20 (billing-catalog.ts:544,575,596). The server may lower or raise limits per account and offers large files to some accounts (chat-attachments.ts:43-55).
access_and_usage.limits_and_metering: Policy ceilings: 25 MiB per file and per message, 20 MiB per image, 20 files; without a handshake 12 MiB and 10 files (chat-attachment-policy.json:2-11). Chrome: 5 files. VS Code: 8 files per batch, 10 MB each. CLI: 12 MiB documents (cloud/attachments.rs:43-45), 40,000 characters per /files file. Whether picking a file is metered as usage: not found in the picker code.

access_and_usage.provider_restrictions: none found in the code for the picker itself.

features.summary: Lets a person drop files on the chat or paste a copied image or file into the message. Web and desktop show a full-window 'Drop files here' overlay; VS Code and Chrome take drops on the composer; the CLI pastes a clipboard image with Ctrl+V; the phone has a 'Paste image' card but no drop.

purpose.what_it_does: Routes dropped and pasted files into the same intake as a picked file (web: handleFileDrop and the shared paste decision), so checks, chips and notices match. Large pasted text becomes a text file attachment and pasted code is fenced, so ordinary text still pastes as text (packages/platform/utils/src/composerPaste.ts:12,131-142; ChatComposerNew.tsx:2372-2400).
purpose.why_it_exists: Dragging a file or pasting a screenshot is the fastest way to attach. The brief lists S14.02 and S14.03 (doc: knowledge-base/data/area-briefs/014-attachment-intake-components.md).
purpose.who_uses_it: Desktop and browser users, developers in VS Code and Chrome, CLI users sending screenshots to a vision model, phone users with an image on the clipboard.
problems_solved: No file dialog needed for a screenshot or a file already open in a folder window.
A huge text paste no longer floods the message box; it becomes 'Pasted text.txt' with an undo (ChatComposerNew.tsx:2358-2370).
The same clipboard gives the same result in web, the shared editor and Chrome (composerPaste.ts header comment).
use_cases: Drag three PDFs from Finder onto the web chat.
Paste a screenshot with the paste shortcut into the Chrome side panel.
Press Ctrl+V in the CLI to attach the clipboard image.
On the phone copy a picture and tap 'Paste image' in the attach sheet.

working: Web overlay listens on the window for dragenter, dragleave, dragover and drop, only reacts to drags carrying Files, and hands every dropped file to the attachment hook (DragDropOverlay.tsx:22-70).
Web editor drop and paste: ComposerEditor reads files from the transfer and calls onDropFiles / onPasteDecision (packages/ui/unified-chat/src/composer-editor/ComposerEditor.tsx:120-139).

Paste decision: any pasted file becomes a file attachment; text of 10,000 characters or more becomes 'Pasted text.txt' (numbered if taken); multi-line code is fenced (composerPaste.ts:12,131-142,231-244).
Desktop: folder drops show an 'Approve this folder?' prompt and leave file drops to the page (apps/desktop/electron/workspaceDrop.ts:36-60).

Chrome: drop and paste read through filesFromDataTransfer and admitted with upload (side_panel.ts:14584-14589,15818-15823).

CLI: Ctrl+V and /attach clipboard stage the clipboard bitmap (tui_app.rs:916-941,4098-4108); long text pastes collapse to '[Pasted text #N +L lines]' and the full text is sent (composer_edits.rs:137; tui_app.rs:5488).

incomplete: Phone has no drag-and-drop; the brief says 'missing' for S14.03 on the phone but the Paste image card exists in code (AddToChatSheet.tsx:713).

not_available: Phone: drag-and-drop (no code found).

steps.what_happens: Browser delivers drag or paste events; web filters to drags that carry Files, reads files, and calls handleFileDrop.

features.summary: Lets a person give a web address; the page is read once and its text added to the conversation. CLI uses /attach with a link, VS Code uses the plus menu item 'Web page', and the Chrome side panel uses 'Add a web page by link'. Each app has its own reader, size cap and rules.

purpose.what_it_does: Fetches a page, turns HTML into plain text and adds it as context. CLI: runs the web fetch tool and pushes the text as a user message (apps/cli/src/repl/mod.rs:937-968). VS Code: fetches from the extension with a 15 second timeout and 2 MiB cap (apps/extension-vscode/src/data/composerContext.ts:250-310). Chrome: asks our server to read the page (apps/extension/src/features/cloud-bridge/pageContextClient.ts:18-58; apps/web/app/api/page-context/read/route.ts:19-40).
purpose.why_it_exists: Brief item S14.08: attach a web page by URL so its content is context (doc: knowledge-base/data/area-briefs/014-attachment-intake-components.md).
purpose.who_uses_it: CLI, VS Code and Chrome users who want the assistant to read a documentation page or article.
problems_solved: Copying page text by hand.
Reading the page without giving it your browser sign-in (Chrome note spLinkAccountRead).
Treating fetched text as untrusted: CLI marks it as page content, not instructions (repl/mod.rs:963).
use_cases: CLI: /attach https://example.com/docs to ask about a doc page.
VS Code: Web page item to paste an API reference link.
Chrome: paste a link to a public article and ask for a summary.

Chrome user-blocked sites (side_panel.ts:6606).

working: CLI: /attach accepts http and https; fetch blocks other schemes, loopback, private and metadata addresses, pins DNS per hop, follows up to 5 redirects, 30 s per hop, 2 MiB body cap; HTML tags stripped; output marked untrusted (features/exec/tools/web/mod.rs:39-70,118-126,536-600).

CLI: Local privacy mode refuses the tool: 'web_fetch is unavailable in Local privacy mode' (features/exec/tools/mod.rs:724-735) [inferred to apply because attach_url_context calls the tool executor, repl/mod.rs:955].
VS Code: input validation, fetch with redirect follow and 15 s timeout, body cap 2 MiB, HTML to text, truncated text (composerContext.ts:250-310).
Chrome: validated link, user-blocked check, POST to the page read route with sign-in token, response parsed against a schema (side_panel.ts:6601-6640,14892-14930; pageContextClient.ts:18-58).

Server route: CSRF check, two rate limits (30 per minute, 500 per day, fail closed), URL fetch guard with 1.5 MiB response, 20,000 content characters, 5 redirects, content types html, plain text, xhtml (route.ts:19-40; rate-limit.ts:272-282; url-fetch-tool.ts:42-46; page-context.ts:5-9).
incomplete: CLI page text is added as a conversation message, with no chip and no way to remove it (repl/mod.rs:960-966); /attach list and remove deal only with staged images and documents (tui_app.rs:6226-6245).
VS Code reads non-HTML bodies raw without a content-type check (composerContext.ts:296-298).
VS Code fetch has no private-address guard in this function (composerContext.ts:272-310).
disconnected_or_disabled: CLI refuses in Local privacy mode by design.
not_available: Web, desktop and phone: no URL attach (brief: n/a).

Local means no hidden API or cloud call; network context must not leave the device in Local privacy mode.

proposed: [proposed] Add a private-address guard and content-type check to the VS Code reader.
[proposed] Show the CLI attachment as a removable chip.

steps.what_happens: CLI: link checked for http or https, then the fetch tool runs on the person's computer and contacts the website directly.
CLI: page text is added to the session; it goes to the model provider with the next turn.
VS Code: the extension host fetches the page directly from the website.
VS Code: text becomes a pending context attachment sent with the next message.
Chrome: panel posts the link and account token to our page read route.
Server checks CSRF and rate limits, fetches the page with the guarded fetcher and returns text.
The website serves the page to our server.
Panel sanitises and bounds the text and attaches a page chip.

features.summary: Lets a person reuse a file already kept in their Library (web, desktop, phone), choose a GitHub repository for a code task (web code surface), or point the CLI at a repository or folder. Library items become ordinary attachments. Folder attach is a listing of names in the CLI only. VS Code folder or repository attach was not found in code.

purpose.what_it_does: Gives three ways to bring existing material into a task without picking a new file from the device: a Library picker in the chat composer, a repository picker in the web code composer, and folder or repository scoping in the CLI.
purpose.why_it_exists: People keep files in the Library and in repositories already. Re-uploading them wastes time and storage. The brief (S14.10, S14.11, S14.12) lists these as required intake paths. A founder decision says web and desktop chat have no attach-a-folder control (doc: docs/decisions/2026-09-27-founder-decisions.md, D-2026-09-27-02), which fits the code: the desktop folder dialog attaches single files, not folders (apps/web/features/desktop-host/components/LocalFolderAttachDialog.tsx:240).
purpose.who_uses_it: Signed-in web, desktop and phone users with files in their Library; developers using the web code surface or the CLI.
problems_solved: Re-picking and re-uploading a file that is already saved
Giving a coding task its repository without pasting code
Showing the model what a folder holds without sending every file
use_cases: On web, open the plus menu, tap Add from library, tap a recent file; it appears as a chip on the draft.
On the phone in Cloud mode, open the attach sheet and tap a Library picture under Attach from Library.
On the web code surface, choose a repository from the Select repository list before starting a task.
In the CLI, type @src/ in a message so the model sees the names of the entries in that folder.

where_to_find_it: Web and desktop (desktop shows the hosted web app, doc: AGENTS.md section 5): composer plus menu, row 'Add from library' (apps/web/features/chat/components/Composer/ComposerPlusMenu.tsx:159, :1011). The submenu lists up to 6 recent files and a 'Browse all' link to /library (apps/web/features/chat/components/Composer/ComposerFilesMenu.tsx:41).

Web and desktop, AGI Work bar: a 'Files' button opens a popover with a search field 'Search library files', 'Browse all' and 'Upload from device' (apps/web/features/chat/components/Composer/ChatComposerNew.tsx:369, :7094; apps/web/features/chat/components/Composer/ComposerFilesMenu.tsx:231). It is shown only when the AGI Work bar is visible (ChatComposerNew.tsx:2768, :7090).

Desktop only: plus menu row 'Attach from local folder' (shown when a desktop host is present) opens a dialog titled 'Attach from a local folder' where one file is picked (apps/web/features/chat/components/Composer/ComposerPlusMenu.tsx:163, :1105; apps/web/features/desktop-host/components/LocalFolderAttachDialog.tsx:25, :240).

Web code surface: repository chip 'Select repository' with a 'Search repositories' field (apps/web/features/code/code-surface.ts:143, :280; apps/web/features/code/components/CodeComposer.tsx:802).
CLI: '@' then a folder path, '--repo' / '-C', '--add-dir', '/add-dir', '/files' (apps/cli/src/mentions.rs:315; apps/cli/src/lib.rs:411, :422; apps/cli/src/claude_parity.rs:221, :223).
VS Code, Chrome: no Library, repository or folder attach found in the code.
prerequisites: Library and repository lists need a signed-in cloud account [inferred from the /api/library and /api/github/repositories routes, which are account scoped].

Repository list needs a connected GitHub installation; states are unconfigured, linking-unavailable, no-installation, authorization-pending, reauthorization-required, ready, error (apps/web/features/code/hooks/use-code-repositories.ts:11-26).

Desktop folder dialog needs an approved folder; the dialog says 'No folders are approved yet. Choose one, and Desktop asks your permission before it reads anything inside.' (LocalFolderAttachDialog.tsx:26).
CLI folder mention sends the listing only in a trusted workspace; otherwise only the path (apps/cli/src/mentions.rs:336-342).
screens_and_controls: Web plus menu submenu: loading row 'Loading files', empty row 'No files in your library yet.', error row 'The library could not be loaded.', attach failure row 'That file could not be added. Try again.' (ComposerFilesMenu.tsx:34-37; ComposerPlusMenu.tsx:1059-1066).

Phone sheet: horizontal row of Library picks; image picks show a picture, others show a file card; 'Loading your Library'; 'Your Library could not load.' with a 'Try again' button (AddToChatSheet.tsx:760-830).
Web code: repository list rows show the full name and a private marker, with 'Manage repository access on GitHub' (code-surface.ts:295; CodeComposer.tsx:672-740).
CLI: listing block '<directory path=...>' sent to the model, capped at 200 entries (mentions.rs:30, :347).
journey: Web: open the plus menu, tap 'Add from library'.
The list loads from the Library (GET /api/library, 6 items).

Tap a file. The app downloads its bytes, wraps them in a File with the saved name and type, and sends it through the same intake as a device file (ComposerFilesMenu.tsx:164-176; ChatComposerNew.tsx:6011).
The chip appears; the menu closes. If the file is refused, a notice names it and the reason.

Phone Cloud mode: open the sheet, tap a pick, the sheet closes and the item is added through the composer's normal add path with the same duplicate and limit checks (AddToChatSheet.tsx:520-528; apps/mobile/app/(app)/(tabs)/chat.tsx:1052).
CLI: type @folder/ and send; the model receives the entry names.
feedback_and_outputs: A chip for the attached file; a refusal notice naming the file and reason.
Web 429 on a Library download: 'You are going a little fast. Try again in N seconds.' or the plan cap and reset time (ComposerFilesMenu.tsx:123-141).
CLI: skipped mentions list a reason such as 'larger than 256 KB', 'holds credentials, only the path was sent', 'workspace is not trusted, only the path was sent' (mentions.rs:340, :388-392).
settings: Desktop approved folders (workspace roots) are managed in the desktop host, not in this feature [inferred from listWorkspaceRoots/pickWorkspaceRoot imports, LocalFolderAttachDialog.tsx:16-25].
CLI workspace trust decides whether folder listings are included (mentions.rs:309-313).

working: Web/desktop plus-menu Library picker: fetch recent files, download the chosen file, add it through addChatAttachments so size, type and duplicate checks apply (apps/web/features/chat/components/Composer/ComposerFilesMenu.tsx:91-176; apps/web/features/chat/components/Composer/ChatComposerNew.tsx:6011, :2223).
Web AGI Work bar 'Files' popover with search, Browse all and Upload from device (ComposerFilesMenu.tsx:231-354; ChatComposerNew.tsx:7094).
Phone Cloud Library section: loads 12 image and file assets, skips videos, shows loading and error-with-retry states, and adds the pick through the composer (AddToChatSheet.tsx:395-436, :760-830).
Phone Library items carry an asset id, so a send does not upload them again: only attachments without an asset id are uploaded (apps/mobile/stores/chat/chatExecutionStore.ts:2478-2483).
Phone Local mode lists recent non-image files from local conversations (AddToChatSheet.tsx:368-385).
Web code repository picker with search and every connection state (apps/web/features/code/hooks/use-code-repositories.ts:60; apps/web/features/code/components/CodeComposer.tsx:672-802).
CLI folder mention produces a name-only listing, skips build and dot directories, and honours workspace trust (apps/cli/src/mentions.rs:336-352, :468-488).
CLI '--repo/-C' moves the session to another repository; '--add-dir' and '/add-dir' add extra readable roots (apps/cli/src/lib.rs:411, :422; apps/cli/src/claude_parity.rs:332).
incomplete: Folder attach gives names only, never contents, in the CLI (apps/cli/src/mentions.rs:468-488); '/files' refuses a directory with 'not a file' (apps/cli/src/agent/mod.rs:3013-3020).
Desktop 'Attach from local folder' attaches one file at a time, not a folder (LocalFolderAttachDialog.tsx:240).
The plus-menu Library list is capped at 6 recent files and has no search; only the AGI Work bar popover has search (ComposerFilesMenu.tsx:41; ComposerPlusMenu.tsx:1016).
Whether the selected repository is passed to the code task as context was not traced end to end; the draft holds repository and repositoryUrl (CodeComposer.tsx:175-177) [inferred].
disconnected_or_disabled: The Files popover exists only inside the AGI Work bar (ChatComposerNew.tsx:7090 inside the workScopeBarVisible branch), so it is not reachable when that bar is hidden.
not_available: Library picker: CLI, VS Code and Chrome (no Library code found in apps/cli, apps/extension-vscode, apps/extension).

Repository attach: phone and Chrome (no code found); VS Code: no repository or folder attach control found; the file picker sets canSelectFolders false and the context kinds are selection, open-files, problems, git-diff, terminal, url (apps/extension-vscode/src/features/sidebar-webview/ChatStateManager.ts:3985; apps/extension-vscode/src/protocol/webviewMessages.ts:145-152). The brief marks VS Code done but its cited lines show unrelated code.
Folder attach on web, desktop, phone, VS Code and Chrome (doc: docs/decisions/2026-09-27-founder-decisions.md, D-2026-09-27-02).

established.statement: A Library item becomes a normal attachment and goes through the same checks as a new file.
The user can pick a file already in their Library and attach it (web, desktop, phone).
The user can attach a code repository as the context for a task (web, desktop, CLI per brief).
The user can attach a folder so the assistant can use the files in it (CLI per brief).
Web and desktop chat have no attach-a-link or attach-a-folder control, because the leaders have none.
Every attachment path respects Local, own key and Cloud boundaries; nothing may silently route a Local file to another mode.

acceptance_criteria: On web, Add from library lists at most 6 recent Library files and a chosen file appears as a chip.
A Library file that breaks a limit is refused with a notice naming it, exactly as a device file would be.
When /api/library cannot be reached the submenu shows 'The library could not be loaded.' and nothing is attached.
On the phone in Cloud mode, a Library pick that is already on the draft raises the 'Already attached' alert and is not added twice.
On the phone, a Library item that has an asset id is not uploaded again on send.
In the CLI, '@dir/' in a trusted workspace sends entry names only and never file contents; in an untrusted workspace only the path is sent.
On the web code surface, each repository connection state shows its own message, not a blank list.
inferred: A Library attach on web re-uploads the bytes at send because the draft holds a File, not an asset id [inferred from libraryItemToFile building a File and the upload happening at send in apps/web/features/chat/pages/WebChatPage.tsx:2684].

Library downloads may count against a plan download allowance, since the file route calls assertDownloadAllowance for large files and the menu has code for a 429 with a cap and reset time (apps/web/app/api/files/[id]/route.ts:173; ComposerFilesMenu.tsx:106-141).
proposed: [proposed] Let the plus-menu Library submenu search, as the AGI Work popover does.
[proposed] Reuse the Library asset id on web so a Library file is not downloaded and uploaded again.
[proposed] Decide whether VS Code should show repository or folder context at all; the brief says done but the code shows none.

The chosen file's bytes are fetched from the file route and wrapped in a File on the device.
The File goes through the same on-device intake checks as a device file.
On send the file is uploaded again like any other attachment (see F014-10).
Phone Cloud: the sheet lists assets from the Library; a pick keeps its asset id and skips upload on send.
Phone Local mode lists files from local conversations; nothing is fetched from servers.
CLI expands @dir/ into a name listing read from the local disk.

Desktop asks permission before reading an approved folder (LocalFolderAttachDialog.tsx:26). CLI paths are validated to stay in the workspace (apps/cli/src/mentions.rs:325).

access_and_usage.limits_and_metering: Menu shows 6 files (ComposerFilesMenu.tsx:41); phone shows 12 (AddToChatSheet.tsx:127). A Library file download may be refused with a 429 and a cap and reset time (ComposerFilesMenu.tsx:106-141). CLI listing capped at 200 entries (mentions.rs:30).
access_and_usage.flags: The web project Google Drive entry is gated by connectorsReleased (not part of this feature). No flag found for the Library picker.
access_and_usage.model_compatibility: Attached Library images and PDFs need a model that can read them; the same conflict banner applies (apps/web/features/chat/components/Composer/ChatComposerNew.tsx:1554).

Switch to a cloud model or remove the attachment.' (packages/contracts/local-runtime/src/inference.ts:131; ChatComposerNew.tsx:1589). Phone Local mode: no cloud Library; recent local non-image files are listed; the 'File' card is hidden (AddToChatSheet.tsx:368-385, :722). CLI works from the local disk.

A Google Drive picker exists only for project knowledge on the web, not for chat attachments.

problems_solved: Documents the refusal behaviour so testers expect it
Separates the project-knowledge Drive picker from chat attachments

A user wants a Drive spreadsheet in chat and must download it first.
A project owner adds Drive files to project knowledge from the Sources panel (not chat).

features.summary: Shows each attachment before sending as a chip: a thumbnail for images, an icon with kind and size for documents, and a remove control. Web and desktop, phone, VS Code and Chrome have chips; the CLI lists staged items in text. Only the phone opens an image full screen. No app replaces a file in place.

purpose.what_it_does: Lets the person see what is attached, tell files apart, and take one out before the message goes.
purpose.why_it_exists: A person must be sure the right files go to the model and must be able to undo a mistake. Brief items S14.16 to S14.18, S14.22, S14.28 to S14.30.
purpose.who_uses_it: Everyone who attaches files on any app.
problems_solved: Sending the wrong file
Not knowing whether a file is still uploading or ready
Telling several files with similar names apart
use_cases: Drop two pictures on web, see two thumbnails numbered in image-edit mode, remove one.
Phone: tap a picture chip to look at it full screen, then remove it.
CLI: run /attach list to see what is staged, /attach remove 2 to drop one.
VS Code: drag a file in, see its icon and size, press the X.

features.summary: Shows an attachment's upload stage (Preparing, Uploading, Verifying), offers Retry on a failed file and cancels a running upload. On web the upload starts at send, on the phone at send too, on Chrome as soon as the file is added. Reading the content after upload has no visible stage anywhere.

purpose.what_it_does: Tells the person where each file is in the upload, lets them try again after a failure, and lets them stop an upload still running.
purpose.why_it_exists: Large files and weak networks fail or stall. People need to see that, fix it, or give up without losing the message. Brief S14.19, S14.20, S14.26, S14.27; test row W04 says failed uploads preserve the draft and do not send a partial set without a decision (doc: docs/product/requirements.md).

established.statement: While a file uploads, its chip shows that the upload is in progress.
After upload, the attachment shows that its content is being read until it is ready.
A failed upload offers Retry on that file.
While uploading, the user can cancel that upload.
Failed uploads preserve the draft and do not send a partial attachment set without an explicit decision.
Switching conversations during upload never attaches a result to the wrong conversation.

acceptance_criteria: On web, a file in flight shows Preparing, Uploading or Verifying under its name; a retryable failure shows 'Upload failed' and Retry.
Pressing Retry on web re-runs the attempt with the same text and files.
A refusal that cannot succeed (for example an unsupported type) shows the reason and no Retry on web.
On phone, cancelling during upload leaves the chip with a Retry control and nothing is sent.
On phone, a failed upload blocks send and names the files that did not upload.
On Chrome, a failed upload shows Retry and Send stays unavailable until the file is ready or removed.
No stage after upload says the content is being read (known gap).

steps.what_happens: The device checks each file against limits and types before any upload.
Refusals are stored as a draft record and appended to the outgoing turn as notes.
The upload client repeats the type and size checks.
At send the server reads each file, cuts long text, and refuses an unreadable or locked PDF.

features.summary: Auto lets the product pick a model for each message. The default setting chooses which model a new chat starts with. Web has an Auto row, extra routing profile rows and a Default model setting. Mobile and VS Code have Auto; the CLI has an --auto flag and a config default. Chrome starts on Auto.

purpose.what_it_does: Offers Auto as a choice at the top of the picker and stores a lasting default model or profile for new chats.
purpose.why_it_exists: Many people do not want to pick a model each time. Auto routes by task, plan and cost; a default removes repeated setup. Inference cost is a design constraint, so routing is centralised (doc: AGENTS.md section 7).
purpose.who_uses_it: Anyone who wants the product to choose, and anyone who always starts with the same model.
problems_solved: Choosing a model for every message.
Starting each new chat on the wrong model.
Paying for a stronger model than a message needs.

CLI user starts with --auto so the managed router picks per turn.
VS Code user leaves agiWorkforce.model on auto.

features.summary: Choosing a model row makes the next message use it. The choice is remembered for later sessions, and each saved conversation keeps its own model when reopened. Switching to a model that cannot handle the chat warns first on Web and VS Code. Locked rows cannot be chosen.

purpose.what_it_does: Applies the chosen model to the next message, stores it as the remembered choice, and on a saved conversation stores it on that conversation.
purpose.why_it_exists: People expect the app to use the model they picked, to remember it, and to reopen an old chat on the model that chat used. Switching mid-chat can lose images, tools or cache, so people must be warned.
purpose.who_uses_it: Everyone who chooses a model.
problems_solved: The model resetting to a default on every reload.
A reopened chat continuing on an unrelated model.
Silent loss of attached images or tools after a switch.
Crossing from a local model to a cloud model without consent.
use_cases: Web user opens an old chat and the composer shows that chat's model.
Web user picks a model unable to read images in a chat with images and sees a warning with 'Switch anyway'.
Desktop user leaves a local model after a local answer and is asked to start a new chat.
VS Code user picks a model with no chat open and sets the default for new chats.

established.statement: The user can pick a specific model and the next message uses it.
The chosen model is remembered for the next session.
A conversation can keep its own model, separate from the default used elsewhere.

steps.what_happens: Person clicks a row; the footer checks the lock and the compatibility findings.
With no saved chat the global selection is set at once and stored in the browser.
With a saved chat, the page sends PUT /api/chat/conversations/{id} with model; the server validates the route and updates web_conversations.
After the save succeeds the page sets the global selection and clears any substitution note.
On open of a saved chat, the page reads the chat's model and sets the selection.
Desktop: a local model is chosen in memory and the turn runs on the local server on the computer.
CLI Enter calls session.switch_model or enter_managed_model; managed models can start a new managed session.
Mobile saves the choice in MMKV; a cloud chat's model is patched and synced remotely.

execution_and_data_flow.models_and_providers: The selected model id is passed to the chat completion request; the server may add a provider route. A model picked from a managed route must match a configured route (route.ts:205-206). Local models never go through the catalogue and run on the local server.

access_and_usage.account: Choosing a model needs no account on Web for a global change; saving it on a saved chat needs sign-in. Cloud models need a signed-in plan.
access_and_usage.permissions: The conversation PUT needs authentication and a CSRF token (apps/web/lib/hooks/useConversations.ts:909-910).
access_and_usage.subscription: modelLock decides whether a row is locked by plan, environment or availability (ComposerFooter.tsx:1190-1200, 1289-1296); on Free the model resets to a free one when the lock applies (ComposerFooter.tsx:1349-1351).
access_and_usage.limits_and_metering: Switching never blocks; a note says the prompt cache restarts and prior context is billed again at input price (comment at ComposerFooter.tsx:1058-1062; test ComposerFooter.model-switch-note.test.tsx). Mobile provider switch mid-chat can need a higher plan (ModelPickerSheet.tsx:490-499).
access_and_usage.model_compatibility: Findings for images, attachments, tools and context size, with 'unknown_model' ignored (ComposerFooter.tsx:1180-1184). VS Code describes capability losses (modelConstants.ts:347; commandSetup.ts:1359-1370).
access_and_usage.provider_restrictions: VS Code refuses a switch across a trust boundary inside a chat (commandSetup.ts:1334-1339). Web refuses Regenerate across Local to BYOK (WebChatPage.tsx:5748-5760).
access_and_usage.local_mode: Web and Desktop: a local selection is kept in memory only; leaving it after local answers needs a new chat (useLeaveLocalModel.tsx). Mobile: local models need the download and runtime state to be ready before selection (ModelPickerSheet.tsx:510-529). CLI: Local rows are never locked (model_picker.rs:196-214).

aliases: Try again with (regenerate with another model, Web)
features.summary: On Web and Desktop a person can regenerate an answer on another model from the answer's refresh menu, 'Try again with', without changing the chat's saved model. No way to send a new message on a one-off model was found. Mobile and Chrome retry with a model but keep that model afterwards.

purpose.what_it_does: Re-runs one assistant answer on a model chosen in the answer's regenerate menu, so the person can compare or recover without switching the conversation's model.
purpose.why_it_exists: People want to see how another model answers the same question, or get past a failed or limited answer, without changing the chat's model for later messages.
purpose.who_uses_it: Web and Desktop users who see a weak or failed answer.
problems_solved: A bad answer from one model.
A model that hit its limit.
Wanting a second opinion on one answer.
use_cases: User opens 'Try again with' on an answer and picks another model.
A Free user retries on a free model from the allowed list.
A user who hit a usage limit card retries on another model.

features.summary: Shows what each model can do and how heavy it is. Web and Desktop list capabilities as filter chips and in a model detail card, with context and output limits and credit estimates there. Short-list rows show a price band and a high-usage hint. Mobile offers four filters; CLI, VS Code and Chrome show text details.

purpose.what_it_does: Lets a person compare models before choosing one: which inputs and outputs a model handles, whether it can use tools, how much text it can hold, and how fast it uses up the plan allowance. The data comes from the shared model catalogue, never from a per-app list.
purpose.why_it_exists: A person should not pick a model that cannot read their image, cannot use tools, or burns their allowance quickly, and then find out after a failed or costly turn. The product contract says the selector shows 'Context/tool/multimodal support where useful' (doc: docs/product/experience-contract.md, section 7.3) and that unsupported capabilities are visible (doc: docs/product/requirements.md, M-MODEL-005).
purpose.who_uses_it: Anyone choosing a model in Web, Desktop, Mobile, CLI, VS Code or Chrome; developers reading the public models list.
problems_solved: Picking a model that cannot read images, audio or tools.
Not knowing a model's context size before pasting a long document.
Not knowing a model eats the usage allowance faster than others.
Guessing which models are fast or heavy.
use_cases: On Web, open the model menu, choose 'All models', press the 'Vision' filter chip, and see only models that read images.
On Web, press the question-mark button beside a row to open the About card and read 'Context ceiling', 'Output ceiling' and 'Credits per 1M tokens'.
On the CLI, run /models to list models with T/V/R/P/A flags, context and output size.
A developer calls the public models endpoint to read context_window, max_output and capabilities.

steps.what_happens: Person opens the model menu; Web fetches the plan-aware catalogue and, separately, provider availability.
Server builds catalogue entries for the caller's plan: capabilities, context, output, price band, admission. Kill switches and training opt-out filter the list.
Browser filters the entries by the chips and renders rows; opening the About card computes credit figures in the browser.
Mobile filters its own model list with shared catalogue metadata on the device.
CLI reads the bundled shared catalogue and prints flags; it makes no network call for /models.

features.summary: Tells a person what state a model row is in. Rows say which plan unlocks a locked model, mark preview models, warn 30 days before a model leaves, and show when a provider is down. Web and Desktop carry all of these. Mobile has lock, outage, retirement and an Instant filter. CLI, VS Code and Chrome cover parts.

purpose.what_it_does: Turns catalogue and health facts into short labels on picker rows: the plan needed, 'Coming soon', 'Beta' for a missing environment, a preview stage, a leaving date, an outage notice, and a speed hint.
purpose.why_it_exists: A person must not pick a model that will fail, and should know why a model is locked and what unlocks it. The product contract lists 'Runtime availability', 'Plan/credit lock', 'Rollout status' and 'Disabled reason' as selector content (doc: docs/product/experience-contract.md section 7.3). Mobile requires locked cloud models to be labelled so the user 'cannot accidentally start Cloud' (doc: docs/product/requirements.md, M-MODEL-003).
purpose.who_uses_it: Anyone choosing a model, especially Free and lower-plan users deciding whether to upgrade.
problems_solved: Tapping a model that the plan cannot run and getting a failed turn.
Not knowing which plan unlocks a model.
Being surprised when a model is retired.
Choosing a model whose provider is down.
use_cases: A Free user opens the Web menu and sees a locked row marked with the plan name and 'and above', and clicks it to reach the upgrade page.
A model retires in 12 days; its Web row says 'Leaving <date>' and Mobile says 'Retires <date>'.
A provider degrades; the Mobile row greys out with 'Unavailable' and the reason.
A CLI user on Free sees 'needs <plan>' beside a cloud model.

steps.what_happens: Server computes per-model admission, health and retirement date for the caller's plan.
Web fetches /api/models when the menu opens to learn which providers are degraded.
Browser computes locks for the short list from the known plan and the catalogue, then renders labels.
Mobile reads outages from /api/models (60 s cache) and plan locks from its tier store.
CLI reads the cached tier from disk and decides locks without a network call.
Tap on a plan lock opens the upgrade or billing page.

features.summary: Lets a person choose how hard a reasoning model thinks, switch on a faster serving tier where a model offers one, and choose shorter or longer answers. Web and Desktop have effort, thinking, Fast mode and a style selector with length. Mobile has effort and Fast mode and a style list. CLI, VS Code and Chrome are partial.

purpose.what_it_does: Gives per-turn control over reasoning depth, serving speed and answer length without changing the model.
purpose.why_it_exists: Harder questions need more thinking, simple ones do not; some models offer a faster, pricier tier; people differ on how long answers should be. Effort above a model's default is a compute escalation gated by plan (packages/contracts/types/src/model-catalog.ts:2610-2635 comment).
purpose.who_uses_it: Chat users on every surface; paid users for Fast mode and higher effort.
problems_solved: Paying for deep reasoning on easy questions.
Waiting for slow answers when speed matters.
Getting answers that are too long or too short.
use_cases: On Web, drag the effort slider from 'Medium' to 'High' for a hard maths question.
On Mobile, tap the gauge button in the composer, pick a level, tap 'Done'.
On Web with a paid plan and usage credits on, turn on 'Fast' for a quick answer.
Pick 'Brief' in the Web style menu to get one-line answers.

aliases: Use Auto / Remove attachments / Choose a compatible model
features.summary: Protects a person from silent surprises when the model changes. Web and Desktop warn before a switch that would lose images, tools or context, offer Use Auto, Remove attachments or Choose a compatible model for unreadable files, note the prompt-cache reset, and say when another model answered. VS Code has a switch dialog. Mobile and CLI disclose fallbacks.

purpose.what_it_does: Checks whether the next model can handle the current chat, asks before a lossy switch, blocks sending attachments the model cannot read until the person chooses, and tells the person which model actually answered and why.
purpose.why_it_exists: Switching models can drop images, disable tools or trim history; fallbacks can put a different model behind an answer. The shared rule is that a substitution is disclosed, never silent (packages/contracts/types/src/chat-fallback-reason.ts:23-28), and the selector must show provider and routing provenance (doc: docs/product/experience-contract.md sections 7.3 and 8.1).
purpose.who_uses_it: Anyone switching models in a long chat or sending files; anyone whose preferred model failed.
problems_solved: Losing images or tools after a switch without knowing.
Sending a file to a model that cannot read it.
Not knowing which model produced an answer after a failure or limit.
Unexpected extra cost when the prompt cache resets.
use_cases: Switch a chat with pasted images to a text-only model: Web shows 'Switch to <model>?' with reasons and 'Switch anyway'.
Attach a PDF to a model that cannot read it: Web shows 'Use Auto', 'Remove attachments', 'Choose a compatible model'.
The chosen model is down: the reply says it came from a backup model and why.
In VS Code, switching to a model with a smaller window shows a modal listing what is lost.

features.summary: Shows which turns in a chat transcript are the person's and which are the assistant's. Each app marks the author a different way: a right-aligned bubble with a hidden heading on web and in the shared desktop bubble, a '>' marker in the CLI, a hidden 'You said:' label in VS Code and Chrome, and a 'You' role label on mobile.

purpose.what_it_does: Marks every transcript turn with its author so the eye and a screen reader can tell the user's turns from the assistant's. The web app uses layout (user turns in a right-aligned bubble, assistant turns as a flat column) plus a hidden heading; it deliberately has no avatars (apps/web/features/chat/components/messages/MessageBubble.tsx:2593-2594).
purpose.why_it_exists: The brief requires that the author of each turn is visually distinguishable and announced to assistive technology (doc: knowledge-base/data/area-briefs/016-user-message-components.md, S16.01). Without it a long transcript is hard to read and unusable with a screen reader.
purpose.who_uses_it: Every person who reads a chat transcript; screen-reader users rely on the hidden headings and labels most.
problems_solved: Telling your own turns from the assistant's at a glance in a long chat.
Letting a screen reader announce who spoke before each turn.
Keeping the same idea (bubble, marker or label) readable in a terminal, a side panel and a phone.
use_cases: Scrolling back through a long web chat to find what you asked.
Navigating the transcript by headings with a screen reader.
Reading a CLI session where the '>' marker separates your prompt from the reply.
Checking in the VS Code panel which message was yours before pressing a message action.

where_to_find_it: Web: every chat transcript. User rows carry data-role=user, assistant rows data-role=assistant (apps/web/features/chat/components/messages/MessageBubble.tsx:2572).
Desktop (public Electron app): shows the hosted web app, so it is the same as web (ARCHITECTURE.md:51-54).

Desktop (internal Tauri build): the shared chat bubble, user turns in a bubble capped at 85% width with a hidden 'You said:' heading (packages/ui/unified-chat/src/components/MessageBubble.tsx:726-736).

Mobile: user turns right-aligned, labelled 'Your message: ...' for accessibility; assistant turns left-aligned with the model name or 'AGI' as role label (apps/mobile/src/features/chat/components/MessageBubble.tsx:1129, 2217-2222, 2237).
CLI: the terminal transcript prefixes user turns with '>' and assistant turns with a star marker (apps/cli/src/tui/tui_app.rs:2881-2896).
VS Code: user messages are right-aligned boxes (85% max width) with a hidden 'You said:' label (apps/extension-vscode/src/features/sidebar-webview/webviewContent.ts:617-623, 5771).

Chrome: each message has a hidden heading reading 'You said:' or 'AGI said:' (apps/extension/src/features/side-panel/bubbles.ts:383-389; apps/extension/_locales/en/messages.json keys spAuthorUser, spAuthorAssistant).

For the hidden labels: a screen reader or the browser's accessibility tree.

established.statement: The author of each turn is distinguishable visually (avatar, name, alignment/bubble style or terminal marker) and announced to assistive technology.
On web every user row carries data-role=user and a hidden heading 'You said:'; assistant rows carry 'Assistant said:'.
Every chat surface should show message labels and keep one set of chat concepts across surfaces.

acceptance_criteria: Web: a user row has data-role=user and contains a visually hidden 'You said:' heading; an assistant row has 'Assistant said:'.
Web: the user bubble is never wider than 75% of the column and sits at the end side.
Mobile: the user turn is announced as 'Your message: ...' by a screen reader.
CLI: a user turn starts with '>' and a reply with the star marker.
VS Code and Chrome: each user message has a hidden 'You said:' label in the accessibility tree.
In a right-to-left language the user bubble sits on the end (left) side [inferred from items-end / flex-row-reverse].
inferred: The labels should be translated; web uses plain English strings in MessageBubble.tsx while Chrome and the shared bubble use translation keys [inferred].
Heading levels should be consistent so heading navigation works [inferred].
proposed: [proposed] Give the CLI a screen-reader-friendly author word (for example 'you') beside the glyph.
[proposed] Use one assistant label text across web and Chrome.

features.summary: Shows what a sent message carried: its text, then any files and images, then chips for non-file context such as a skill, a connector prompt or connector resources. Web shows image thumbnails that open a lightbox. Each app shows a different subset; mobile, CLI, VS Code and Chrome have their own versions.

purpose.what_it_does: Displays the sent text, the files and images that went with it (image thumbnails, file chips with name and size) and chips for context that is not a file. On web those chips list a skill as '/name', a connector prompt as 'Prompt: name' and connector resources as 'Resource: name' (apps/web/features/chat/components/messages/MessageContextChips.tsx:17-57).
purpose.why_it_exists: So a person can check, after sending, exactly what the assistant received: briefs S16.02 to S16.04 require text, attachments and non-file context to be visible on the sent message.
purpose.who_uses_it: Anyone who attaches files, uses skills or connectors, or reviews a past chat.
problems_solved: Not knowing which files or context the answer was based on.
A broken-image icon when an attachment URL no longer loads.
Silent loss when a long file was only partly read.
use_cases: Attach a photo, send, then click the thumbnail to see it full size.
Send a message using a skill and see the '/skill' chip.
Send with a connector prompt and see 'Prompt: name' with the connector named for screen readers.
Attach a very long document and read the note that only part of it was read.

steps.what_happens: On send, the web hook adds the user message (text, attachments, metadata) to the local store right away, before the network answers.
The request is posted to the chat completions endpoint; for a Local model the turn stays on the device and never reaches that route.
The server reports files it only partly read in a response header; the page writes the names onto the user message.
The bubble draws thumbnails or chips from message.attachments and chips from metadata.mcpContext and metadata.sendReplay.skillName.
A click on a thumbnail opens the lightbox; an image error marks that attachment broken and swaps in a named chip.

data.what: Attachments (name, type, size, URL, thumbnail URL) and metadata (mcpContext, sendReplay.skillName, truncatedAttachments) on the user message
data.where_stored: Chat store on the device; saved with the conversation message rows on our servers for cloud chats
data.synced: Yes for cloud conversations; Local-model turns stay on the device [inferred from useChatStream.ts:4160-4163]
data.retained_or_deleted: Follows the message; deleting a message removes it. Retention rules for attachment files: unknown

execution_and_data_flow.models_and_providers: The bubble is model independent. But which model a free-plan turn runs on can depend on attachments, skills and connector context, because they are passed to the free-model router (apps/web/lib/hooks/useChatStream.ts:4166-4177).

access_and_usage.account: Sending needs an auth token on web (useChatStream.ts shows 'Not authenticated' when the token is missing). Showing already-sent attachments needs no extra rule found.
access_and_usage.permissions: Attachment URLs are fetched by the browser; access control for the file URLs: unknown.
access_and_usage.subscription: No entitlement check on the display. Whether a plan allows attaching or connectors is decided in the composer and server (not read here).
access_and_usage.limits_and_metering: File read-length limits exist server-side and are reported as truncation (chat-attachment-truncation.ts:50-56). Numeric limits: unknown.
access_and_usage.flags: none found in the code for the display.
access_and_usage.model_compatibility: A model that cannot read images is a composer and server concern; not decided in the bubble.
access_and_usage.local_mode: Local-model turns run on the device and do not reach the completions route, so the server truncation header does not apply (useChatStream.ts:4160-4163). How a Local turn reports a partly read file: unknown.

aliases: Edited message, version n of m
features.summary: Shows when a message was sent and that it was edited. On web the time is inside the 'More message actions' menu as 'Sent at HH:MM' with the full date on hover. The edited mark is the 'n/m' version pager on a user message that has several versions. Chrome shows the time inline. Mobile, CLI and VS Code show no time.

purpose.what_it_does: Gives each sent message a time, and marks a user message that has more than one version through the version pager read out as 'Edited message, version n of m'.
purpose.why_it_exists: The brief asks that each user message exposes when it was sent, and that an edited message is visibly marked (S16.05, S16.06).
purpose.who_uses_it: People who revisit old chats and people who edit questions and want to know which version they are reading.
problems_solved: Not knowing when something was asked.
Not noticing that you are looking at an earlier version of an edited question.
use_cases: Hover a message, open the menu and read the exact send time.
After editing a question, see '2/3' beside it and page back to the first version.
Chrome user glances at the time under each bubble.

where_to_find_it: Web and public Electron desktop: hover or focus the message, open 'More message actions', read 'Sent at <time>' at the top of the menu (apps/web/features/chat/components/messages/MessageBubble.tsx:3957-3972).
Web edited mark: version pager left of the action row on a user message with more than one version (MessageBubble.tsx:3706 region, VariantPager.tsx:44-100).
Mobile: version pager under the user bubble with label 'Edited message, version n of m' (apps/mobile/src/features/chat/components/MessageBubble.tsx:548-590, 3198-3202). No time shown.

Chrome: a time label in each bubble's action row (apps/extension/src/features/side-panel/bubbles.ts:614; apps/extension/src/features/side-panel/dom.ts:15-17). No edit marker because Chrome cannot edit.
CLI and VS Code: no time and no edited marker found.
prerequisites: A sent message. For the edited mark: the message has at least one more version (web needs message variants on; see settings).
screens_and_controls: Web: menu label 'Sent at' with a <time> element; the title attribute holds the full local date and time (MessageBubble.tsx:3960-3971).
Pager buttons labelled 'Previous version' and 'Next version'; text '2/3'; a polite live region reads 'Edited message, version 2 of 3' (VariantPager.tsx:19-23, 69-100).
journey: Send a message.
Hover or focus it; open 'More message actions'; read 'Sent at HH:MM'; hover the time for the full date.
Edit the message and save (see F016-05).
The edited message now shows '2/2'; the screen reader announces 'Edited message, version 2 of 2'.
feedback_and_outputs: Time text in the person's locale, hour and minute only.
Pager position text and a live region announcement.
settings: Message variants switch: NEXT_PUBLIC_MESSAGE_VARIANTS (build), a 'variants' query parameter, or local storage key agi.message-variants; default on (apps/web/features/chat/lib/message-variants-gate.ts:1-60).

working: Web: timestamp in the menu of both user and assistant messages, hidden while the message streams (MessageBubble.tsx:3957-3972; test apps/web/features/chat/components/messages/MessageBubble.timestamp.test.tsx:144-149).
Web: pager shown only when a message has siblings and the surface can page; disabled while the conversation streams (VariantPager.tsx:44-60; MessageBubble.tsx:992-1002).
Mobile: pager for user messages with the 'Edited message, version n of m' label (apps/mobile/src/features/chat/components/MessageBubble.tsx:3198-3202).
Chrome: time shown for every message in the action row (bubbles.ts:614).
incomplete: Web has no separate 'edited' badge; a single-version message shows no mark even if it was edited under the variants-off setting, where the old text is replaced (MessageBubble.tsx:992-1002; WebChatPage.tsx:5634-5656) [inferred].
Web time is behind a menu, not inline; hour and minute only, no date unless hovered.
Brief lists the pager UI as unfinished on web and desktop (S16.11 'Unfinished: ui'); the code has a working pager with tests, so which part is unfinished is unknown.
disconnected_or_disabled: Pager is hidden when variants are switched off, because no sibling versions are kept then (message-variants-gate.ts:50-60; WebChatPage.tsx:2048-2077).
not_available: Timestamp on mobile, CLI, VS Code (brief: missing; I found none in apps/mobile/src/features/chat/components/MessageBubble.tsx where createdAt is used only for the activity start time at line 2524, and none in the CLI or VS Code user message code).
Edited marker on CLI, VS Code and Chrome: those apps cannot edit a message.

A user message that was edited after sending is visibly marked as edited.

Web: hovering the time shows the full local date and time.
Web: while the message streams there is no timestamp.

features.summary: Puts the text of a sent message on the clipboard. On web a Copy icon in the message's action row turns into a check for two seconds and shows a 'Copied to clipboard' toast. Mobile has 'Copy Message' in the long-press menu, Chrome has a Copy message button, and the shared desktop bubble has a Copy button. CLI and VS Code have none.

purpose.why_it_exists: Every chat surface should offer Copy (docs/product/requirements.md section 6.2) and the brief requires it on sent messages (S16.07).
purpose.who_uses_it: Anyone who wants to reuse or share a prompt.
problems_solved: Retyping a long prompt.
Moving a prompt to another tool.
use_cases: Copy a long prompt to tweak it elsewhere.
Copy a question to paste into a ticket.
Copy a prompt on phone through the long-press menu.

features.summary: Lets you change a sent message and resubmit it for a new reply. On web the bubble turns into an editor; saving adds the new version beside the old one and you page between them with previous and next arrows. With versions switched off the old reply is deleted after a confirm. Mobile edits in a modal. CLI, VS Code and Chrome cannot edit.

purpose.what_it_does: Opens an editor on a user message, resubmits the changed text as a new turn, and keeps the old message and its reply reachable through a pager ('2/3').
purpose.why_it_exists: Edit and resubmit is a universal chat concept (docs/product/requirements.md section 6.2) and the brief requires edit in place (S16.08) and paging between versions (S16.11). The migration comment says earlier behaviour destroyed the old answer, so versions were added (apps/web/db/neon/0156_message_thread_variants.sql:5-9).
purpose.who_uses_it: People who want to fix or refine a question without losing the first answer.
problems_solved: Typo or wrong wording in a prompt.
Losing a good earlier answer when you try a new wording.
Accidentally deleting later replies.
use_cases: Fix a typo in a prompt and compare both answers.
Rework a question three times and page between versions.
On phone, edit a prompt and its attachments through a modal.

where_to_find_it: Web and public Electron desktop: pencil button 'Edit message' in the user message's action row (apps/web/features/chat/components/messages/MessageBubble.tsx:3726-3739).
Mobile: long-press, 'Edit Message', opens MessageEditModal (apps/mobile/src/features/chat/components/MessageBubble.tsx:1642-1644, 3310).

Internal Tauri desktop: edit icon under the bubble opens an inline textarea with Cancel and Save (packages/ui/unified-chat/src/components/MessageBubble.tsx:737-780), shown only if the host passes onEdit.
CLI, VS Code and Chrome: no edit control found.
prerequisites: The conversation is not streaming; for the free website trial, the trial must not be used up (WebChatPage.tsx:5478-5495).
Message is a user message.
screens_and_controls: Web editor (EditableMessage) with save and cancel; pager buttons 'Previous version' and 'Next version' beside the message (VariantPager.tsx).
Confirm dialog 'Replace this message?' with button 'Replace' when versions are off and replies would be deleted (WebChatPage.tsx:5636-5646).
Mobile modal edits text and attachments; save asks confirmations before rewriting.
journey: Click Edit message on your message.
The bubble becomes an editor with the text.
Change the text, then save (or cancel).
A new turn is sent. With versions on, the old version stays; with versions off a confirm names how many replies will be deleted.
Use the arrows to page between versions.

steps.what_happens: Click Edit: the bubble asks the page's beginEdit; the page runs planMessageEdit and answers whether the editor may open.
Save: text is trimmed, empty is ignored; with versions off and replies below, a confirm opens first.
runSubmitEdit checks the Local-to-own-key boundary, the replay of recorded send options and connector context; any refusal sets a chat error and stops.
With versions on, sendMessage posts the new text with the edited row's parent id, so the new row is a sibling; the stream replies on the server (cloud) or on the device (Local model).
With versions off, sendReplacingMessages deletes the replaced server rows only after the new turn is saved.
Paging moves the active leaf, the visible thread switches.

features.summary: Sends the same message again for a fresh reply and recovers from a failed send. On web the user message has a 'Retry this message' button; after a failure the error notice offers Retry. Mobile shows 'failed to send' with Retry, VS Code marks a message 'Not sent' and offers Retry, Chrome offers Send again and a Retry on errors. CLI has none.

purpose.what_it_does: Re-sends a user message (and its attachments and recorded send options) to get a new reply, and lets a person retry after a turn failed.
purpose.why_it_exists: Retry and regenerate are universal chat concepts (docs/product/requirements.md section 6.2). The briefs require resend from the message (S16.09), a clear failed state (S16.15) and a Retry that replaces the failure (S16.16).
purpose.who_uses_it: Anyone whose reply failed, was poor, or never arrived.
problems_solved: Retyping a prompt after a network or provider error.
Duplicate user messages after a retry.
Not knowing a message did not go through.
use_cases: The connection dropped mid-reply: click Retry in the error notice.
Ask again for a different answer with 'Retry this message'.
Phone message queued offline fails: tap Retry next to 'failed to send'.
VS Code message shows 'Not sent': press Retry in the error block.

established.statement: A sent user message can be re-sent unchanged from the message itself to get a fresh reply.
When a user message fails to deliver, the transcript shows a clear failed state for that turn.
A failed send offers Retry that re-sends the same turn (text and attachments) and replaces the failure with the new outcome.
The failure banner shows the error and Retry only when the last user message has no good reply; Retry rolls back from that user message inclusive so the resend replaces it.
Nothing silently routes a Local chat to BYOK or managed cloud.
An irreversible action asks first and names what is lost.

acceptance_criteria: Web: 'Retry this message' sends the same text and attachments again and is disabled while streaming.
Web: after a failed turn, the Retry control appears only while the last user message has no successful reply.
Web: with versions off and later replies, a confirm 'Retry this message?' names how many replies are deleted.
Web: when the free trial is used up, Retry opens the upgrade dialog and sends nothing.
Web: retrying a Local conversation under an own-key model shows a refusal and sends nothing.
Mobile: a message that failed to send shows 'failed to send' and Retry; after three failures an alert says the limit is reached.
VS Code: a failed message shows 'Not sent'; the error Retry resends and clears the error block.
Chrome: Send again appears only on the latest user message.
inferred: The resend should keep attachments; web passes userMsg.attachments [inferred from WebChatPage.tsx:5810].
CLI should offer some way to re-run the last prompt; today only prompt history exists [inferred from apps/cli/src/tui/prompt_history.rs].
proposed: [proposed] Show a 'Not sent' mark on the web user bubble itself, as VS Code and mobile do.
[proposed] Add a CLI retry command or key for the last failed turn.

features.summary: Branch from here copies a conversation up to a chosen message into a new conversation, so the person can try another direction while the original stays unchanged. Web and the hosted desktop do it in the cloud, the internal Tauri desktop does it on the device in Local mode, the CLI forks the whole session, and VS Code forks before a user message.

purpose.what_it_does: Creates a second conversation that holds the messages of the first up to the chosen message. The original chat is not changed. Web also lists sibling branches so the person can page between them (apps/web/lib/services/conversation-branch-service.ts:88-192).
purpose.why_it_exists: People want to explore a different follow-up without losing the first line of conversation. The competitor guidance records Branch as a context-preserving divergence point, distinct from edit, regenerate or continue (doc: docs/product/competitive-guidance.md:214).
purpose.who_uses_it: Anyone who wants to try a different question from an earlier point: general chat users on web and desktop, and developers using the CLI or VS Code.
problems_solved: A different question normally needs a new chat and a re-pasted context.
Editing a message replaces the later thread, so the first path is lost (MessageBubble.tsx edit is a separate action).
Experiments in a long working session risk the good result already reached.

steps.what_happens: Web: person chooses the menu item; the hook checks sign-in, gets a token, adds CSRF headers.
Web: POST sends messageId and a new request id to the branches route.

Server checks the Free daily allowance (one conversation create and one message write), then opens a transaction, returns an existing branch for the same request id, locks the source, verifies the message, enforces the branch caps.
Server inserts the new conversation, the branch link and the copied messages with new ids, and the id map; after commit it schedules artifact indexing for copied assistant messages.
Page adds the conversation to the local store, shows the toast and navigates.
Tauri desktop, Local: invoke chat_branch_conversation; SQLite copy runs in the app.
CLI: /fork persists the session file and forks it into a new managed session file on disk; no server call is in this path.
VS Code: the webview posts a messageAction, the extension asks the local CLI runtime to fork through a message index, then resumes the new thread.
