features.summary: While a reply is running, a message you type waits in a queue (shown as a Queued row with Edit and Cancel) and is sent when the reply ends. Unsent text is also kept as a draft per conversation. Web syncs drafts across devices. VS Code marks each message Sending, Queued, Running, Steered, Not sent or Cancelled.

purpose.what_it_does: Holds follow-up messages written during a running reply, shows them as waiting, and sends them when the turn ends. Keeps unsent composer text for each conversation so leaving and returning does not lose it (apps/web/features/chat/components/Composer/ChatComposerNew.tsx:3951-3972,4342-4420).
purpose.why_it_exists: People think of the next question while the model is still answering. They also leave chats half-written. Without a queue and a draft the text is lost or the send is blocked. [inferred]
purpose.who_uses_it: Everyone who chats; developers on VS Code, CLI and Chrome use the same ideas in their own forms.
problems_solved: A second message typed during a reply is not lost.
Unsent text survives switching chats, reloads and, on web, other devices.
A failed or cancelled send is visible as its own state (VS Code).
use_cases: Type a follow-up while a long answer streams; it appears as 'Queued: <text>' and goes out when the answer ends.
Click Edit on a queued row to change it, or Cancel to drop it.
Half-write a message, open another chat, come back and find the text there.
Edit the same draft on two web tabs and choose which version to keep.

where_to_find_it: Web composer: a list labelled 'Queued messages' above the input with rows 'Queued: <text>' (or 'Queued 1 of 2: <text>'), and buttons Edit and Cancel, and Steer when the running reply can take it (ChatComposerNew.tsx:5009-5063).

Hosted desktop: same as web (doc: AGENTS.md section 5). Tauri desktop: a section labelled 'Follow-up messages' with rows 'Queued', 'Steering' or 'Not sent' and buttons Edit, Send now, Remove (packages/ui/unified-chat/src/components/FollowUpQueue.tsx).
Mobile: rows with accessibility labels 'Queued message n of m: <text>', 'Edit queued message', 'Cancel queued message' (apps/mobile/src/features/chat/components/ChatInput.tsx:1857-1902).

VS Code: your message bubble has a dashed border and a caption Sending, Queued, Running, Steered, Not sent or Cancelled; queued ones have Edit and Cancel icons (apps/extension-vscode/src/features/sidebar-webview/webviewContent.ts:624-690,5554-5591).
Chrome side panel: list 'Queued messages' with 'Queued: <text>', Edit, Cancel (apps/extension/src/side_panel.ts:15312-15364; apps/extension/_locales/en/messages.json).
CLI: the hint line shows '· 1 message queued' or 'N messages queued' while a turn runs (apps/cli/src/tui/tui_app.rs:2064-2075).

Drafts: web 'Choose which draft to keep' dialog with 'Here' and 'Elsewhere' and buttons 'Use the other version' and 'Keep this version' (apps/web/features/chat/components/DraftConflictDialog.tsx:67-93).
prerequisites: Queue: a reply must be running (isTurnActive).
Web draft sync: signed in, a stored (non-temporary) conversation, and no on-device model selected or used in that chat (use-conversation-draft-sync.ts:75-84).

established.statement: A message sent while a reply is still running is shown as queued (not yet sent) until it goes out.
While a user message is not yet accepted by the service, it shows a pending, sending or queued state.
Unsent composer text is kept as a draft per conversation, separate from sent messages, and a failed send returns to the composer as an unsent draft.
The composer holds a list of queued follow-ups and sends them when the stream ends.
The draft is saved as its own field, never as part of the message list, with a revision to detect conflicts; temporary chats store no draft.
Saves are debounced and retried up to 3 times; a conflict can be resolved by keeping mine or theirs.
Drafts are not synced for conversations that hold Local-model turns.
Local, own key and Cloud are separate trust boundaries; nothing may silently route a Local chat to another boundary.

acceptance_criteria: Sending while a reply runs shows a 'Queued' row and the box clears.
Edit on a queued row puts its text back; sending again replaces that slot, not adds one.
Cancel removes the row and sends nothing.
When the reply ends the first queued message is sent exactly once.
Typing in a stored chat, waiting about 2 seconds, and opening the same chat on another device shows the same draft (web).
Editing the same draft on two devices produces the 'Choose which draft to keep' dialog with both versions.
A temporary chat never stores a draft on the server.
After 3 failed saves a persistent toast with Retry appears.

[inferred] Drafts must be removed or cleared on sign-out; the mobile store clears account-scoped drafts (draftStore.ts:205).

steps.what_happens: Person presses send while a turn is active; the composer stores the send arguments with the conversation id and clears the box.
When the turn ends, the composer sends the first queued item in the same conversation; items for another conversation become a draft and a notice.
Draft text is parked in the web chat store and in browser storage as the person types.
After the debounce the sync hook PUTs the draft with its revision to the conversation route; the server writes draft and draft_updated_at or answers 409 with the current draft.
A conflict opens a toast and dialog; the person keeps this version or the other.
Mobile saves drafts in on-device storage; Chrome in session storage; VS Code in webview state; CLI in memory.

features.summary: In the CLI, your messages from a /voice session start with '(spoken)' in the transcript. When you resume a session that was pulled from your AGI account or a cloud code session, the CLI puts a system line first: 'The messages below came from <origin>.' Other apps have neither.

purpose.what_it_does: Marks the source of messages in the CLI terminal screen: spoken text and imported history (apps/cli/src/tui/tui_app.rs:4469,7566-7571,691-698).
purpose.why_it_exists: Speech-to-text can make mistakes, and an imported conversation did not start on this computer. A marker tells the reader how much to trust the wording and where the text came from. [inferred]
purpose.who_uses_it: CLI users who dictate or who continue conversations from their AGI account or cloud Code sessions.
problems_solved: Reader cannot tell typed text from a spoken transcript.
A resumed session looks like it began here, though it came from the account or the cloud.
use_cases: Run /voice, speak a request, and read '(spoken) <transcript>' in the transcript.
Run the resume command for an account conversation and see 'The messages below came from your AGI account.'
Teleport a cloud Code session and see 'The messages below came from the cloud Code session.'

where_to_find_it: CLI terminal UI only: slash command /voice (alias /v) with an optional language code (tui_app.rs:6352-6368).

Web, desktop, mobile, VS Code, Chrome: none (brief S16.19, S16.20).

Imported note: a session created by the account or cloud-code import commands (lib.rs:2519-2530,2642-2650; sessions.rs:662,771).

steps.what_happens: Person types /voice; the TUI leaves the alternate screen and calls run_voice_mode.
Voice mode picks a transcription backend: managed (our servers, needs sign-in), OpenAI API (outside service, needs a key), or a local whisper program (device).
In Local mode without opt-in the cloud backends are replaced by the local program or voice is refused.
New session messages are appended to the screen and user rows get the '(spoken)' prefix.
On resume, the TUI reads imported_from from the session metadata file and inserts the system line.

execution_and_data_flow.models_and_providers: Voice may call a transcription provider (AGI managed service, OpenAI Whisper API) or a local whisper program; then the transcript goes to the chat model as a normal user message. features.summary: Marks each reply as an assistant reply, shows the model that actually answered with its usage and time, shows a working indicator before text arrives, and renders the text as it streams in. Present on web, desktop (hosted web app), mobile, CLI, VS Code and Chrome in different forms.

purpose.what_it_does: Tells the person who wrote each answer (assistant, and which model), shows that the assistant is still working, and fills the answer in as it arrives. After the answer is done it offers the model name, token counts and run time. On web the label comes from stored message data, so it survives a reload (apps/web/features/chat/components/messages/MessageBubble.tsx:2398).
purpose.why_it_exists: The product is model agnostic and can route a turn through Auto, so the person needs to see which model really answered, not only which one they picked. A visible and announced working state stops a slow first token from looking like a hang (apps/cli/src/tui/tui_app.rs:3005-3020).
purpose.who_uses_it: Every person who chats on any of the six apps; testers checking routing; support staff reading a screenshot.
problems_solved: Cannot tell which model answered after Auto routing
Blank screen while waiting for the first token
Screen reader users not told when a reply finished or failed
No way to see how much a turn used
use_cases: Open the more-actions menu on a web answer to read the time sent, the model and the token counts.
Watch a mobile answer stream in with a spinner and status label, then read the provider and model line under it.
Run a CLI turn and read the answer details line (model, tokens in and out, cost if any, time).
Use a screen reader on web and hear one short phrase per generation change, such as Response complete.

where_to_find_it: Web and Desktop (Desktop shows the hosted web app): answer text, then the action row under it. The model name is a small answered-by text at the end of the row, shown on hover or focus and always on touch (MessageBubble.tsx:4119-4127). The More message actions menu shows Sent at, the model and token counts (MessageBubble.tsx:3957-3976, 4075-4092).

Mobile: a line under the answer gives the provider and model (ProvenanceFooter, apps/mobile/src/features/chat/components/MessageBubble.tsx:2995); a usage line sits beside it (MessageBubble.tsx:2998). Action-row button label is More message actions for <model> (MessageBubble.tsx:3188).

VS Code: a small label in the answer action row; hover for the token detail (apps/extension-vscode/src/features/sidebar-webview/webviewContent.ts:4879-4885, 4941-4953).
Chrome side panel: a meta label in the bubble action row with model name and elapsed time (apps/extension/src/features/side-panel/bubbles.ts:463-469, 608-620).
prerequisites: A conversation with at least one sent message.
Model label depends on stored message fields (model, requested model, route lane); older messages without them show no label (MessageBubble.tsx:2398-2415).
screens_and_controls: Web: TypingIndicator reads Preparing with a spinning mark (apps/web/features/chat/components/messages/TypingIndicator.tsx:9-21). Streaming text uses StreamingMarkdownContent (MessageBubble.tsx:3217-3226).
Web screen reader: one hidden status line with a phrase per state (ChatMessageList.tsx:2089-2091).

established.statement: Assistant turns are distinguishable from the user's visually and to assistive tech, ideally naming the assistant or model.
The answer body renders incrementally as tokens arrive, with markdown formatting.
While the assistant works, a visible and announced working indicator is shown.
For each answer the user can see which model actually answered and its usage (tokens, cost, time).
A turn that returns nothing shows an explicit no-response error with retry, not an empty bubble.
When an answer fails after some output, the partial text is kept and marked incomplete with the reason.
Message actions work after app reload (M-CHAT-005).

acceptance_criteria: On web, after an Auto turn finishes, the answered-by text names the model that answered and begins Auto chose.
On web, the More message actions menu shows Sent at plus token counts when the message has stored usage.
On mobile, a finished cloud answer shows the provider and model line; a local answer shows Local Mode and the model name.
With a screen reader on web, a finished turn produces the phrase Response complete, a stopped one Response cancelled. Partial response saved.
Before the first token, the working indicator is visible on web, mobile and CLI.
After a page reload, the model label is still shown (it comes from stored fields).
inferred: Model label should come from the resolved model, not the picked one [inferred from MessageBubble.tsx:2398 using message.model first and mobile preferring metadata.resolvedModel at MessageBubble.tsx:786-790].
proposed: [proposed] Give the web TypingIndicator its own status role so it is announced even if the list-level line is removed.
[proposed] Show cost in the web usage detail so web matches the CLI line.

steps.what_happens: Client checks gates, then POSTs to the follow-ups route.
Route checks sign-in, CSRF, rate limit, ownership; temporary chats return an empty list.
If suggestions are already on the message, they are returned.
Else the managed-cloud route is admitted, a usage lease is reserved, one non-streaming model call runs and output is sanitised to at most three lines.
The model provider answers.
Result is saved into message metadata if none exists and returned.

aliases: Regenerate, retry, continue, branch and answer versions
features.summary: Lets the person re-run an answer, retry a failed or stopped one, continue a cut-off answer, switch the model for a retry, branch a new chat from an answer, and page through attempts. Built on web and mobile; the CLI, VS Code and Chrome cover only some of it.

purpose.what_it_does: Gives the person controls to get another attempt, finish a truncated answer, fork the chat at an answer and compare attempts.
purpose.why_it_exists: Models fail, stop at output limits or give weak answers; people need recovery without retyping.
purpose.who_uses_it: Anyone who gets a failed, partial, stopped or unsatisfying answer.
problems_solved: Failed or interrupted turns
Answers cut at the output limit
Trying a different model on the same prompt
Exploring a different path without losing the original

Press Continue generating after a length cutoff.

established.statement: A completed answer can be regenerated in place, producing a new attempt.
A failed answer shows Retry that re-runs the turn and replaces the failure.
An answer cut off by the output limit offers Continue that resumes the same answer; a user Stop is not a cut-off.
The user can regenerate with a different model in one step.
Branching keeps history to that point and leaves the original unchanged.
When an answer has several attempts the user can page between them.
Retry and regenerate are chat requirements.
Regenerate must not silently cross from Local to BYOK; it fails closed with a visible reason.

steps.what_happens: Person presses Regenerate; the page rolls back to the preceding user turn and re-sends it, as a new sibling variant.
A boundary check refuses a regenerate that would move a Local chat to a BYOK model.
Trial exhausted opens the upgrade dialog instead of running.
The server streams a new answer from the chosen model and provider.
Continue sends the history through the truncated answer plus a continue instruction and appends the reply.
Branch posts the message id and a request id to the branches endpoint and opens the new conversation.
Mobile branch calls forkConversation with the fork point message id.

execution_and_data_flow.models_and_providers: Regenerate re-uses the chat route with the same or a chosen model from regenerateModelOptions. Continue uses the model of the message (useChatStream.ts: message.model || selectedModel). Any catalog model; Local and BYOK keep their own boundary rules.

access_and_usage.limits_and_metering: Each regenerate and continue is a new metered turn [inferred]; amounts unknown.
access_and_usage.model_compatibility: Continue only for models and finish reasons that count as cut off (isContinuableFinishReason).
access_and_usage.provider_restrictions: Local to BYOK crossing is refused.
access_and_usage.local_mode: Web regenerate in a Local chat stays local and is refused for BYOK targets. Mobile Continue is not offered for local conversations (continuableAnswer.ts requires the cloud execution mode). Mobile retry works in local chats [inferred from retry action not gated by mode, mobile MessageBubble.tsx:1654].

features.summary: Lets a person reshape an answer in one step (shorter, longer, other tone) or pick one span of it to ask about. Today only the mobile app can pick a span, and it quotes the span into the next reply. No app has a one-step shorten, expand or tone action for chat answers.

purpose.what_it_does: The intended feature has two parts: three one-step rewrites of a whole answer (shorter, longer, different tone) and selecting part of an answer to revise it or ask about it. In the code, only a mobile 'Select Text' sheet exists. It lets the person highlight text in an answer and press 'Quote in reply', which puts the quote above the next message they send (apps/mobile/src/features/chat/components/SelectTextSheet.tsx:123; apps/mobile/app/(app)/chat/[id].tsx:1663-1671, 2638). The three one-step rewrite actions are not present for chat answers in any app I searched.
purpose.why_it_exists: The brief lists these as expected answer actions so a person does not have to retype 'make this shorter' or 'sound friendlier' (doc: knowledge-base/data/area-briefs/017-assistant-message-components.md, S17.23 to S17.26). The reason beyond the brief is [inferred] from the leaders-parity policy in AGENTS.md section 10.
purpose.who_uses_it: People reading an assistant answer who want a different length or tone, or want to question one sentence of a long answer. Today only mobile users reach the span-selection half.
problems_solved: Avoids retyping a long instruction to shorten, expand or restyle an answer (intended, not built for chat answers).
Lets a person point at exactly which sentence they mean when replying (mobile only, as a quote).
Avoids copying text out of the app to refer to one part of an answer.
use_cases: On mobile, open an answer's action menu, choose Select Text, highlight one sentence, press Quote in reply, then type 'explain this' (apps/mobile/src/features/chat/components/MessageBubble.tsx:1688-1693).
On mobile, quote a code line from an answer and ask for a fix (apps/mobile/__tests__/SelectTextQuote.test.tsx, code-line test).
Intended on any app: press Shorten on a long answer and get a shorter version in one action (not built).

where_to_find_it: Mobile: open the action menu on an assistant message and choose 'Select Text' (the accessibility action reads 'Select text') (apps/mobile/src/features/chat/components/MessageBubble.tsx:1688-1693, 1807). The sheet is titled 'Select Text' (SelectTextSheet.tsx).
Web, Desktop (Electron shows the hosted web app), CLI, VS Code, Chrome: no shorten, expand, tone or selected-span action on chat answers found. Not available.

Related but a different feature: the web artifact viewer has a selection toolbar with 'Improve', 'Edit with AI' and an action list including 'Make shorter', 'Make longer' and tone choices. It edits an artifact, not a chat answer (apps/web/features/chat/components/artifacts/ArtifactSelectionToolbar.tsx:21-26; packages/ui/unified-chat/src/lib/artifact-selection-request.ts:44-70).
prerequisites: Mobile: an assistant message with visible text. The Select Text action is shown only when the message has text (MessageBubble.tsx:1688).

Quote in reply is offered only when the host passes onQuoteSelection (MessageList.tsx:404); without it the sheet is a plain selectable read-only view (SelectTextSheet.tsx, ScrollView branch; test: apps/mobile/__tests__/SelectTextQuote.test.tsx 'keeps the plain selectable view').
screens_and_controls: Select Text sheet: header 'Select Text', a Close button, a multiline text box labelled 'Message text' holding the answer as plain text, a footer line showing the selection in quotes or 'Select part of the message to quote it in your reply.', and a 'Quote in reply' button that stays disabled until text is selected (SelectTextSheet.tsx).
Quoted reply bar above the composer, with a dismiss control (apps/mobile/app/(app)/chat/[id].tsx:2638).
journey: 1. Open the actions for an assistant message.
2. Choose 'Select Text'. The sheet slides up with the answer as plain text.
3. Drag the selection handles over the span. The footer shows the span in quotes.
4. Press 'Quote in reply'. The sheet closes and a quote bar appears above the composer (SelectTextSheet.tsx quoteSelection; MessageList.tsx:349-352).
5. Type a message and send. The sent text becomes '> <author>: <quote>' then a blank line then the typed text ((app)/chat/[id].tsx:631-646).
6. The assistant answers the whole message, with the quote as context. It is not a targeted rewrite of the span [inferred from the send format].
feedback_and_outputs: Footer text echoes the chosen span.
In the thread the sent message shows the quote as a chip (MessageBubble.tsx:532-538, 2290).
No toast or rewrite result: the quote does not itself produce a new answer.

acceptance_criteria: On each app that offers it, the answer actions include Shorten, Expand and a tone choice, each starting one rewrite with one press.
The rewrite result is a new version of the answer linked to the original, and the original stays reachable (same expectation as regenerate variants, S17.28) [inferred].
Selecting a span and choosing the revise action sends a request that names the selected span and leaves the rest of the answer unchanged.

features.summary: Lets a person rate an assistant answer with thumbs up or down (press again to remove) and report a harmful or wrong answer. Ratings go to the feedback table; reports go to the content-reports table for trust and safety. Built on web, desktop and mobile; rating only in VS Code; absent in CLI and Chrome.

purpose.what_it_does: Each finished assistant answer carries a Good response and a Bad response control. A rating is tied to that message id and sent to the server; pressing the same control again removes it. A thumbs-down can open a short form with a reason and comment. A separate Report action files a trust-and-safety report about the answer.
purpose.why_it_exists: Ratings tell the team which answers worked. Reports give people a way to flag harmful content; the mobile code names the Google Play generative-AI policy as the reason a report control must exist on every assistant turn (apps/mobile/src/features/chat/components/ReportFlagButton.tsx, header comment). Brief items S17.29-S17.31.
purpose.who_uses_it: Signed-in people on web, desktop (hosted web app) and mobile; VS Code users for ratings; the trust-and-safety team and operators who read the stored rows.
problems_solved: No signal on whether answers are good (web comment at MessageBubble.tsx:1196-1203 says this was collected nowhere before).
No in-app way to flag harmful or inaccurate answers.
Duplicate or double-click reports (client report id is an idempotency key: apps/web/app/api/mobile/content-report/route.ts insert 'on conflict (client_report_id) do nothing').
use_cases: Web: press 'Bad response', choose 'Did not follow instructions' and add a comment, then Submit.
Web: open the more-actions menu on an answer and choose 'Report this response'.
Mobile: choose 'Report…' from the message menu, pick a category such as 'Harmful or dangerous', press 'Save report'.
VS Code: press the helpful or unhelpful button on an answer in the chat panel.

where_to_find_it: Web and Desktop (Electron shows the hosted web app, doc: AGENTS.md section 5): under each assistant answer, thumb-up button labelled 'Good response' and thumb-down labelled 'Bad response'; the tooltip becomes 'Remove rating' once pressed (apps/web/features/chat/components/messages/MessageBubble.tsx:3777-3819). Report is a menu item 'Report this response' in the answer's more-actions menu (MessageBubble.tsx:4062-4073).

Mobile: message menu items 'Good Response' / 'Remove Good Response', 'Bad Response' / 'Remove Bad Response' and 'Report…' (apps/mobile/src/features/chat/components/MessageBubble.tsx:1708-1718); double-tap on an answer gives a thumbs-up (lines 1630-1637). The accessibility action names are 'Good response', 'Bad response', 'Report' (lines 1817-1824).

VS Code: native chat panel helpful/unhelpful feedback (apps/extension-vscode/src/features/chat-participant/chatParticipant.ts:680-682) and thumb buttons in the sidebar webview with labels from L10N goodResponse, badResponse, removeRating (webviewContent.ts:4698-4724). No report.
CLI and Chrome: no rating or report control found. CLI has a separate /feedback command for general product feedback (apps/cli/src/claude_parity.rs:195-206) which is not per-answer.
prerequisites: Web, mobile (Cloud conversation) and VS Code ratings need a signed-in account: the server answers 'Sign in to rate a response' (apps/web/app/api/feedback/route.ts:298); mobile throws 'Sign in to rate this Cloud message.' (apps/mobile/stores/chat/chatMessageStore.ts:141); VS Code shows 'sign in to AGI Cloud to rate answers' (answerRating.ts:62-66).
The answer must be finished (not streaming) and have readable content (web: hasReadableTurn at MessageBubble.tsx:3764; mobile: canRate at MessageBubble.tsx:1625).
Report on the web server does not require sign-in (user id optional) but needs a CSRF token and passes a rate limit (content-report route).
screens_and_controls: Web: two icon buttons with pressed state (aria-pressed) and a details form (heading from ResponseRatingDetails.tsx) with a 'Reason' group, a text area 'What was wrong with this response?', a 'Close feedback form' button and 'Submit' (apps/web/features/chat/components/messages/ResponseRatingDetails.tsx:124-208).

Web report: a menu item that reads 'Report this response', then 'Reporting…', then 'Reported' (MessageBubble.tsx:4062-4073). There is no confirmation step and no category choice: category is fixed to 'harmful' and the note is empty (MessageBubble.tsx:1170-1185).

Mobile report sheet: title 'Report this response'; six categories (Harmful or dangerous, Inaccurate or misleading, Offensive or hateful, Misinformation, Privacy concern, Other); 'Additional details (optional)' up to 500 characters; checkbox 'Email this report to support'; buttons 'Save report' and 'Cancel' (apps/mobile/src/features/chat/components/ReportFlagButton.tsx).

Mobile result screen titles: 'Report submitted for review', 'Send this report to AGI?', 'Report queued', 'Report saved on this device' with Send, 'Email support instead' and Done or Cancel (ReportFlagButton.tsx DELIVERY_TITLE and DELIVERY_BODY).
journey: Rate: 1. Wait for the answer to finish. 2. Press Good response or Bad response. 3. The button lights up at once (optimistic). 4. On thumbs-down on web or Cloud mobile, a details form opens; pick a reason and/or write a comment and press Submit, or close it. 5. Press the lit button again to remove the rating.

Report on web: 1. Open the answer's more-actions menu. 2. Choose 'Report this response'. 3. The item reads 'Reporting…' then 'Reported' and a toast says 'Reported. Thank you: our trust and safety team will review it.'

Report on mobile: 1. Message menu, 'Report…'. 2. Pick a category (Save report stays disabled until one is chosen). 3. Optionally add details or tick the email option. 4. Press 'Save report'. 5. Read the result sheet. If it says 'Send this report to AGI?', press Send to consent, or 'Email support instead'.
feedback_and_outputs: Web rating: pressed state; on failure a toast 'Could not send that. Please try again.' or 'Could not remove your rating. Please try again.'; a rate-limit sentence 'You've sent a lot of feedback in the last hour. Try again later.' (packages/contracts/cloud-contracts/src/response-rating.ts).
Web report: success toast above; failure toast 'Could not send the report. Please try again.' and the menu item returns to normal (MessageBubble.tsx:1190-1193).
Mobile rating toast: 'Thanks for your feedback' or 'Rating removed' (MessageBubble.tsx:244-249).

Mobile report body texts: 'Your report was sent to the AGI safety team for review.', 'Saved on this device. Nothing was sent.', 'Saved on this device. It sends as soon as it can.' (ReportFlagButton.tsx).

Details form note that tells what is stored: 'Your rating, reason and comment are saved with your account, this chat and response IDs, and your browser and device details. The response text is not attached.' (response-rating.ts RESPONSE_RATING_SHARING_NOTE).
settings: none found in the code (no setting to hide the controls).

working: Web rating: optimistic UI, queued requests so a removal waits for the vote before it, rollback and toast on failure (MessageBubble.tsx:1213-1360).

Server stores one rating per user and message by deleting any previous row and inserting the new one in a transaction under an advisory lock (apps/web/app/api/feedback/route.ts:37-46, 285-300); DELETE with message_id removes it (route.ts:401-422).

Web report posts to /api/content-report with a client-generated reportId; the route re-exports the mobile intake handler (apps/web/app/api/content-report/route.ts; apps/web/app/api/mobile/content-report/route.ts).

Mobile rating: stores the reaction on the message; for Cloud conversations also posts a rating to the feedback endpoint and patches the cloud message reaction, rolling back on failure (apps/mobile/stores/chat/chatMessageStore.ts:127-243; apps/mobile/src/features/chat/services/cloudMessageMutations.ts:38-89).
Mobile report: saves to device storage first, then tries the server, with consent-gated queueing and connectivity-triggered flush (apps/mobile/services/contentReport.ts:228-300, 318-357).
VS Code rating: posts to /api/feedback with Bearer token, remembers rating in extension state (apps/extension-vscode/src/features/feedback/answerRating.ts; submitFeedback.ts).
Desktop (Electron) inherits web behaviour because it shows the hosted web app (doc: AGENTS.md section 5); I did not run it.
incomplete: VS Code: rating works (native panel and sidebar) but there is no report (no content-report reference in apps/extension-vscode/src).
Web report has no category, note or confirmation, unlike mobile (MessageBubble.tsx:1170-1185); the draft's 'confirm' step does not exist on web.
Mobile details form for thumbs-down is Cloud-only: submitResponseRatingDetails throws RATING_DETAILS_CLOUD_ONLY for non-Cloud conversations (chatMessageStore.ts:1119-1126).
disconnected_or_disabled: Cloud contracts name 'chrome' as a rating surface with a ready message (response-rating.ts CHROME_RESPONSE_RATING_MESSAGE), but no Chrome source uses it (search of apps/extension/src for response_rating found nothing). The contract exists; the Chrome control does not.
not_available: CLI: no per-answer rating or report found (apps/cli/src/cloud/feedback.rs is general feedback only).
Chrome: no rating or report found in apps/extension/src.
VS Code: report not available.

established.statement: A thumbs-up on an answer records positive feedback tied to that message.
A thumbs-down records negative feedback tied to that message.
An answer can be reported (harmful or incorrect) to the trust-and-safety intake from the answer itself.
Every async flow has complete states: loading, error, retry, cancellation, offline and permission denial.
Reports must tell the truth about what happened: a report that never left the phone must never read as submitted.
A mutation fired straight from onClick for an action a user cannot undo must ask first; ratings are undoable, reports are not removable by the user in the code seen.

acceptance_criteria: Pressing Good response on a finished answer lights the button and sends one POST to /api/feedback with feedback_context 'response_rating', rating 'up' and the message id.
Pressing the lit button again sends DELETE /api/feedback?message_id=<id> and clears the state.
A failed rating request restores the previous state and shows an error message.
Choosing 'Report this response' on web sends one POST to /api/content-report and shows the thank-you toast; a failure returns the item to its normal state.
On mobile, 'Save report' is disabled until a category is chosen, and the result sheet states truthfully whether the report was sent, queued or only saved on the device.
Rating and report controls do not appear while an answer is streaming or on the person's own messages.
A signed-out person who presses a rating control is told to sign in rather than seeing a silent failure (VS Code, mobile Cloud; web server returns 401).
inferred: Reporting from Local mode must stay possible without an account (route comment says user_id is optional so Local-only users can report).
Once reported, the web item should not allow a second report for the same answer until reload; it does this only in component state ([inferred] from reportState).
proposed: [proposed] Add a category and note step on the web report to match mobile and the server schema.
[proposed] Add a report and rating control to VS Code, CLI and Chrome, using the shared feedback contract.
[proposed] Use the existing Chrome rating surface name in response-rating.ts when building the Chrome control.
[proposed] Show a different toast for a Local-mode rating that stays on the device.

features.summary: Shows what happened when an answer did not end normally: it failed after some text (kept, marked incomplete with a reason), the model refused, the person stopped it, or nothing came back. Each case has its own notice and a next step such as Retry, Try again or Switch model. Chrome lacks a refusal state; VS Code does not mark a stopped answer.

purpose.what_it_does: When an assistant turn ends abnormally the app keeps whatever text arrived and adds a notice that says which case it is and what to do next. The four cases are partial failure, refusal by the model's safety layer, stop by the person, and an empty reply.
purpose.why_it_exists: A cut-off answer that looks like a normal one misleads people, and a blank bubble says nothing. The server and clients already share wording so a person who meets the same failure on web, mobile, CLI or an editor reads the same thing (apps/cli/src/errors.rs:70-76 comment; apps/web/app/api/llm/v1/chat/completions/lib/turn-completeness.ts header). Brief items S17.37-S17.40.
purpose.who_uses_it: Anyone using chat on any of the six apps when a model, connection, safety layer or their own Stop button ends a turn early.
problems_solved: Partial answers passing as complete.
Refusals read as generic errors or as normal answers.
Blank assistant bubbles after an empty model reply.
No clear route to try again, switch model or appeal a refusal.
use_cases: A connection drops half way through a long answer: the text stays, a notice gives the reason and Retry.
The model declines for safety reasons: the notice says so; on web an appeal dialog and Retry, on mobile Switch model and Report.
The person presses Stop: the answer keeps what arrived and reads 'Response stopped.' with Try again.
The provider returns nothing: web shows 'The model finished without returning a response.'; the CLI retries once automatically.

journey: 1. Send a message and watch the answer stream.
2. Something ends the turn early: connection loss, provider failure, refusal, Stop pressed, or an empty reply.
3. The app keeps any text that arrived and adds the matching notice.
4. Read the reason sentence (and the reference id if shown).
5. Press Retry or Try again (or Switch model, Continue generating, or the appeal/Report control).
6. A new attempt replaces or follows the failed one.

established.statement: When an answer fails after some output, the partial output is kept and visibly marked incomplete, with the reason.
When the model or safety layer refuses, the answer shows a distinct refusal state, not a generic error or normal answer, with a next step. Refusal state is missing in Chrome.
An answer the user stopped is marked as stopped, keeps what arrived, and offers to try again.
A turn that returns nothing shows an explicit 'no response' error with retry, not an empty bubble.
Every async flow has complete states: error, retry, cancellation, offline, permission denial.
The chat transcript includes an error/retry card and retry/regenerate.
Never silent failures or dead controls.

acceptance_criteria: Interrupting a stream after some text leaves the text visible and adds a notice naming a reason (not a raw provider payload).
A refusal finish shows a notice that is visually and verbally distinct from a failure and offers at least one next step.
Pressing Stop keeps the partial text, marks the answer as stopped and offers Try again (when no text arrived) or a way to continue.
A turn with no text, tool call or file shows a 'no response' message with Retry rather than an empty bubble.
Retry replaces the failure notice with the new attempt's outcome.
On Free plan, 'Switch model' is not offered when no compatible Free model exists (web).
The same cause reads the same on web, mobile, CLI and VS Code (shared wording).
inferred: Stopped answers on VS Code should be marked like other apps [inferred from S17.39 'done' status versus the unread payload].
Stop, failure and refusal should not be metered as a successful answer: unknown, not checked.
proposed: [proposed] Read payload.stopped in the VS Code done handler and show a stopped notice with a retry.
[proposed] Add a refusal state to Chrome using the finish reason from the managed stream.
[proposed] Add a Retry on mobile refusal notices and on mobile stopped answers that kept text.
[proposed] Give web refusal the same 'rephrase or pick another model' wording as mobile.

steps.what_happens: The client sends the turn and streams the answer; the server judges the ending: empty output, cancelled, error, refusal or output limit, and marks the turn truncated or blocked.
A stream failure arrives as a stream-error frame or code with a message, retryable flag and request id; the client stores it on the message metadata.
The client chooses a notice from message metadata: finishReason stopped, refusal or content_filter, a stream error, or no visible output, then renders the reason and actions.
Person presses Stop: the client aborts the request and stamps finishReason 'stopped' on the kept message.
Person presses Retry or Try again: the client reruns the turn; on web it uses the regenerate path, creating a new attempt.

CLI: a finished generation is judged on the device; an empty reply is sent once more, other failures raise a typed error with a hint. The provider call itself is made by the CLI to the chosen provider.

data.retained_or_deleted: Kept with the conversation. Web deletes the placeholder assistant message when a turn is abandoned before it starts (useChatStream.ts:4365-4378).

execution_and_data_flow.models_and_providers: The failure comes from whichever model route served the turn. Reasons are mapped from provider-neutral codes (provider_rate_limited, provider_overloaded, content_filter and so on) in turn-error-notice.ts:83-105 and the web gateway's turn-completeness classifier, so wording does not name vendors. Which providers emit refusals is not established.

access_and_usage.account: No separate account rule: the notices are display of a turn the person already ran. Failure causes can themselves be account issues (session expired, plan restriction, usage limit) shown with their own reasons (ChatMessageList.tsx reason table).

Plan and usage-limit causes get their own sentences ('the selected model is not part of your plan', 'you have reached a usage limit on your account'). Mobile has Free-quota wording in streamFailureNotice (test: streamFailureNotice.test.ts 'says when a Free account can continue').
access_and_usage.limits_and_metering: Whether stopped, failed or empty turns are billed or counted: unknown (not traced). CLI records usage for the superseded empty attempt (chat.rs:2279 superseded_usage).
access_and_usage.model_compatibility: Output-limit and refusal behaviour depends on the finish reason the model route reports. Continue and Switch model depend on route and plan.
access_and_usage.local_mode: Mobile Local turns use the same message bubble, so notices render from the same metadata; which Local-inference code writes streamError or finishReason was not found in the files read: unknown. CLI works the same for any provider. Local inference needs no paid plan (product rule), and these notices have no plan check.

Mobile uses the gateway sentence alone, without the 'may be incomplete' prefix.
Web refuses to show text containing braces and falls back to a cause sentence.

Web Retry calls regenerate; VS Code disables the button after one press and resends the last turn; Chrome disables the button and calls onRetry.

purpose.what_it_does: The record's own text ('Test', 'Click', 'Works') is placeholder text and describes no real behaviour (doc: knowledge-base/data/area-briefs/018-conversation-level-controls.md is the only source of S18.01). The one brief item, S18.01, says a new conversation gets a meaningful title without the user naming it (doc: knowledge-base/data/area-briefs/018-conversation-level-controls.md:5-6). On the web the server first saves a short plain-text cut of the first question, then may schedule a short model-written title (apps/web/app/api/chat/conversations/[id]/messages/lib/persist-message.ts:165-198).

purpose.who_uses_it: Every signed-in person who starts a chat on any app. No special role is needed [inferred from the absence of a role check in persist-message.ts:165-198].

features.summary: The remaining 27 items of the conversation controls area: rename, pin, archive, delete, duplicate, move to project, mode, privacy, search, jump, branches, export, share, details, tools, tasks and continuation. The code exists on Web and Mobile for most; CLI and VS Code have a few; Chrome very few. The brief is partly out of date.

purpose.what_it_does: Groups the per-conversation actions a person can take after a chat exists. The brief lists 27 items S18.02 to S18.28 (doc: knowledge-base/data/area-briefs/018-conversation-level-controls.md:10-140). Examples verified in code: Web header menu with Rename, Move to project, Share, Export, Duplicate as branch (apps/web/features/chat/components/ConversationTitleMenu.tsx:153-209); Mobile menu with Share, Rename, Pin, Move to project, Duplicate, Mark as unread, Archive, Delete (apps/mobile/src/features/conversation-actions/useConversationActions.ts:263-293).
purpose.why_it_exists: People need to organise, protect, search and share long-lived chats, and the leaders (ChatGPT and Claude) offer these actions; the shared sidebar item comments say its menu order matches both leaders (packages/ui/ui/src/sidebar/SessionItem.tsx:326-329).
purpose.who_uses_it: Signed-in people with existing conversations, on every app; the set differs by app.
problems_solved: Finding old chats (pin, archive, search, projects)
Mistaken deletion (confirmation, restore route)
Sharing or exporting a chat
Keeping settings per chat (instructions, privacy)
use_cases: Web: pin a chat so it stays on top, then archive it later.
Mobile: long-press a chat, choose Move to project, pick a project.
CLI: type /rename or /fork inside a session.
Web: set a conversation's own instructions through the conversation update API.

where_to_find_it: Web: header title button labelled 'Conversation options' opens a menu with 'Rename', 'Move to project' or 'Change project', 'Share…', 'Print', 'Export…', 'Duplicate as branch', Archive toggle and Delete (apps/web/features/chat/components/ConversationTitleMenu.tsx:142-209).

Web and Desktop sidebar row: a more-options button; menu order Share, Rename, Pin or Unpin, Mark as unread, Archive, Delete, then Move to project flyout (packages/ui/ui/src/sidebar/SessionItem.tsx:326-386).
Mobile: conversation menu with 'Share', 'Rename', 'Pin'/'Unpin', 'Move to project', 'Duplicate', 'Mark as unread', 'Archive', 'Delete' (useConversationActions.ts:263-293).
CLI: slash commands '/resume', '/fork' (alias '/branch'), '/rename', '/export', '/title' (apps/cli/src/tui/tui_app.rs:6002-6033,6571).
Web share dialog headings 'Share conversation', 'Public link ready', 'Shared with your workspace', 'Conversation links' (ShareConversationDialog.tsx:262-270).
Mobile shared links list at settings/shared-links (apps/mobile/app/(app)/settings/shared-links.tsx).
VS Code, Chrome: exact labels not opened; unknown.

Archive on mobile shows only for cloud conversations (line 290).

established.statement: The user can rename a conversation and the new title persists.
A conversation can be pinned and unpinned.
A conversation can be archived (hidden, kept) and restored.
A conversation can be deleted, with confirmation, and disappears everywhere.
A conversation can be duplicated into a new independent one.
Move to Project and Copy into Project (original stays).
Mode switch, privacy switch through an explicit flow that explains the consequence.
Search in conversation, jump between matches, outline, jump to a turn, jump to latest, scroll restoration, branch navigation.
Export, share, shared-link management, details, context inspector, usage summary.
Conversation-level instructions, enabled tools, connected accounts, active tasks, continuation on another device.
Nothing may silently route a Local chat to BYOK or managed cloud; a Local-to-BYOK move is an explicit fork with consent.
An action a user cannot undo asks first and names the consequence; a removed chat is archived or moved to Recently deleted.

acceptance_criteria: Rename persists after reload on Web, Mobile and CLI.
Pinned chats stay at the top and unpin returns them.
Archive hides a chat and restore brings it back.
Delete asks first and the chat leaves every list.
Turning a chat temporary while it is in a project is refused.
Edited resend of a local-history chat does not cross Local to BYOK without refusal (WebChatPage.tsx:5535-5545).
Share dialog lists links and revoke works.
Each 'missing' item is either built or shown as unavailable, not as a dead control.
inferred: The brief's per-app status needs a refresh because at least two items (mobile Duplicate, web instructions) exist in code [inferred from route.ts:276 and useConversationActions.ts:282].
proposed: [proposed] Re-audit all 27 items against code and update the brief.
[proposed] Add a visible web control for conversation instructions.
[proposed] Build outline, scroll restoration and Copy into Project, or drop them from the area.

features.summary: When a person sends a message, the app shows it at once with a working row, shows any follow-up that waits behind a running answer as Queued, and shows a Preparing or Thinking label until the first output. Web, mobile, VS Code, Chrome and CLI each implement this separately.

purpose.what_it_does: Shows the person that a sent message was taken, that work has started, and that later messages are waiting their turn. Each app shows a label before the first output arrives and lets the person edit or cancel a waiting follow-up.
purpose.why_it_exists: A silent gap after pressing send looks like a hang. The product contract says every async flow needs designed loading and state views (doc: docs/product/experience-contract.md:82).
purpose.who_uses_it: Anyone chatting on Web, Desktop (which shows the hosted web app), Mobile, CLI, VS Code or Chrome.
problems_solved: No dead time after sending: the user bubble and an assistant placeholder paint before any network wait on web (apps/web/lib/hooks/useChatStream.ts:4288-4309).
A second message typed while an answer streams is not lost or sent in the middle: it waits in a visible queue (apps/web/features/chat/components/Composer/ChatComposerNew.tsx:3948-3972).

A slow first token does not look like a freeze: web names the model being connected to and counts seconds (apps/web/lib/hooks/agentActivityLabel.ts:90-101); the CLI adds a still-working hint after 10 seconds (apps/cli/src/tui/tui_app.rs:3000-3010).
use_cases: Send a question on web and see Preparing, then Connecting to the model with a second counter, then the answer.
Type a follow-up while a long answer streams; it shows as Queued with Edit and Cancel, and sends when the answer ends.
On a phone with no network, write a message and see it marked queued offline until the connection returns.
In the CLI, type while a turn runs and see '1 message queued' in the composer hint.

where_to_find_it: Web (and Desktop, which loads the hosted web app: apps/desktop/electron/main.ts:1065-1066, doc: AGENTS.md section 5): the composer send button, the Queued chip beside it, the queued row above the composer, and the Preparing row in the transcript.
Mobile: the composer queued rows (labelled 'Queued message N of M'), the 'queued' badge on an offline message bubble, and the Preparing line in the assistant bubble.
CLI: the composer hint line during a turn and the spinner line with 'Thinking' or 'Preparing context'.
VS Code: the sidebar chat; the user message shows 'Sending' or 'Queued' under it; the send button reads 'Queue follow-up' or 'Steer follow-up' while a turn runs.
Chrome side panel: the 'Queued messages' list above the composer and the Preparing thinking row.
prerequisites: A chat open with a model route that can answer (Local, own key or Cloud).
To queue: a turn must already be running; the composer must have text or an attachment.
screens_and_controls: Web: send button (modes send, stop, queue; title 'Queue message · will send after current response finishes'), chip 'Queued' or 'Queued N', row text 'Queued 1 of 2: <preview>' with buttons Steer, Edit queued message, Cancel queued message (ChatComposerNew.tsx:5022-5053; SendButton.tsx:57-76,113-115).

Mobile: queued row buttons 'Edit queued message' and 'Cancel queued message' (ChatInput.tsx:1856-1902); offline placeholder 'Offline, message will send on reconnect (N queued)' (ChatInput.tsx:1645-1650).
CLI: hint '  … working, Esc or Ctrl-C to cancel · type to queue a message' and '(Enter to queue, /btw to ask aside)' (tui_app.rs:2064-2075).
VS Code: icon buttons with aria labels 'Edit this queued message' and 'Cancel this queued message' (webviewContent.ts:5554-5590).
Chrome: list items 'Queued: text' or 'Queued 1 of 3: text' with Edit and Cancel (side_panel.ts:15312-15345; _locales/en/messages.json spQueuedLead, spQueuedLeadNumbered).
journey: 1. Type a message and press Enter or the send button.
2. The message appears as your bubble at once; on web an assistant placeholder appears in the same frame (useChatStream.ts:4288-4290).

3. A waiting row shows: web 'Preparing' with a spinning mark (TypingIndicator.tsx:15-18); mobile 'Preparing' (MessageBubble.tsx:2504-2510); Chrome 'Preparing' (side_panel.ts:6339); CLI 'Preparing context' until the model request starts, then 'Thinking' (tui_app.rs:8226,8429,8544).
4. On web the timeline then reads 'Connecting to <model> · Ns' and later 'Waiting for the first token from <model> · Ns' (agentActivityLabel.ts:90-101).
5. If you send another message while the turn runs it joins the queue; you can Edit it (text returns to the composer) or Cancel it.
6. When the turn ends, the first queued message is sent automatically (web ChatComposerNew.tsx:4346-4383; mobile ChatInput.tsx:1170-1195; Chrome side_panel.ts:8736-8756; CLI tui_app.rs:7274-7283).
7. If the turn was stopped, the CLI returns queued text to the composer instead of sending it (tui_app.rs:8754-8760).
feedback_and_outputs: Web: chip 'Queued' (one) or 'Queued 2' (several); row 'Sent to the running reply' for a message steered into a running Cloud run (ChatComposerNew.tsx:360).

Web notice if you switch chats with a queued message: 'Your queued message was not sent: you switched chats before the reply finished.' plus whether it was saved as a draft (ChatComposerNew.tsx:4403-4415).
Mobile offline: bubble badge 'queued' (accessibility label 'Message queued offline'), or 'failed to send' with a Retry button when the offline send failed (MessageBubble.tsx:2228-2290).

Chrome: 'You can queue up to N messages. Wait for the answer, or cancel one.' when the lane is full; 'Your queued message was not sent because the chat changed. It is back in the composer.' (messages.json spQueuedFull, spQueuedReturned).
settings: Web: followUpBehavior setting decides whether Enter queues or steers a follow-up; Cmd/Ctrl+Shift+Enter inverts it for one message (ChatComposerNew.tsx:1791,4494-4507; test ChatComposerNew.followUpSteer.test.tsx).
VS Code: followUpBehavior (steer or queue) and enterBehavior (webviewContent.ts:5081-5092).
Mobile, CLI, Chrome: no queue setting found.

CLI: queued_prompts list, '1 message queued' or 'N messages queued' in the hint, joined with a blank line and sent as one message after the turn (tui_app.rs:2064-2075,7274-7283,8482). The brief marks CLI queue as missing; the code contradicts that (doc: knowledge-base/data/area-briefs/019-streaming-and-response-presentation-states.md S19.02).
CLI: Preparing context then Thinking, with a 'still working' hint after 10 s with no text (tui_app.rs:2155,3000-3010,8544).
VS Code: delivery-state labels 'Sending' and 'Queued', queued Edit and Cancel controls, Steer or Queue send button, 'Stopping…' status (webviewContent.ts:634-635,5554-5590,5776-5777,5081-5092).

Chrome: queued list capped by LANE_CAP (100), Edit and Cancel, next follow-up sent after a finish or a failure, queue returned to composer when the chat changes (side_panel.ts:8719-8765,9855; packages/client/client-runtime/src/queue/types.ts:9).
incomplete: Mobile: the visible waiting text is only Preparing; the text does not say which context is being read (MessageBubble.tsx:2504-2510).

Web and mobile queues are held in component memory; a queued message is not stored across an app restart [inferred from useState and useRef use at ChatComposerNew.tsx:910-911 and ChatInput.tsx:490-513].
VS Code: no visible 'Preparing' word was found; the typing indicator only has the accessibility label 'AGI is responding' (webviewContent.ts:5019-5033). Searched the file for Preparing: no match.
disconnected_or_disabled: Web SendButton 'queue' mode is a presentational mode; which screen passes it was not traced (SendButton.tsx:8).
not_available: No plan-based limit on queueing was found on any app.
CLI: the live frame shows 'Preparing context' but nothing says which files, memory or attachments are being read (tui_app.rs:8544).

established.statement: After sending, the surface shows the request was accepted and work has started, before any output.
A request that cannot start yet is shown as waiting or queued.
Before the model answers, the surface shows it is preparing (context, attachments, memory).
Every async flow has complete states: loading, empty, disabled, error, offline, retry, cancellation.
A hidden or disabled control is better than an enabled no-op.

acceptance_criteria: Press send on web: the user bubble and a waiting row appear in the same frame, with the network blocked.
While a turn streams on web, send a second message: the Queued chip shows; send a third: it reads Queued 2; Cancel one: the count drops.
Edit a queued message on web: the text returns to the composer and the queued row is replaced when re-sent, not duplicated.
End the running turn: the first queued message is sent without a click.
On mobile, send while streaming: a 'Queued message 1 of 1' row shows with Edit and Cancel.
On mobile in airplane mode: the sent bubble shows 'queued'; if the later send fails it shows 'failed to send' and a Retry button.
In the CLI, type during a turn and press Enter: the hint shows '1 message queued'; press Esc: the text returns to the composer.
In VS Code, send during a turn: the user message shows 'Queued' with Edit and Cancel icons.
inferred: A queue should survive an accidental app restart or say it will not [inferred from the brief's 'is not dropped silently' wording and the in-memory queue code].
The waiting text on every app should say what is being prepared, as the brief says only CLI says 'Preparing context' [inferred from S19.03].
proposed: [proposed] Show the same 'Queued N' count on mobile and VS Code as on web.
[proposed] Say what is being read (attachments, memory, project files) in the Preparing label when that is known.

steps.what_happens: The person presses send; the app adds the message and a waiting row to the on-screen list.
If a turn is already active, the message goes into an in-memory queue instead of being sent.
A timer updates the Connecting to or Waiting for the first token label every second until the response starts (web only).
The app posts the chat request to the managed chat endpoint for Cloud turns; the label stays until the first event arrives.

steps.what_happens: For a Local model on web the turn runs through runLocalTurn on the device and the ticker is stopped at once.
When the running turn ends, the first queued message is sent (web, mobile, Chrome) or all queued text is joined and sent once (CLI).

features.summary: While the assistant works in steps, each step shows its own label: searching the web, running code, calling a connector, writing a file or artifact, generating an image or video. Web has the fullest set; mobile, VS Code, Chrome and CLI show most of them in their own style.

purpose.what_it_does: Turns the assistant's tool calls into readable live labels and a final summary, with detail on expand.
purpose.why_it_exists: Progress is data: tool calls, files and failures are meant to be typed events the person can read (doc: docs/product/experience-contract.md:80).
purpose.who_uses_it: Anyone watching an answer that uses search, code, connectors or file creation.
problems_solved: The person can tell the assistant is working and on what.
A failed or stopped step stays visible instead of vanishing.
A connector call names the service in plain words, not a raw tool id (packages/ui/unified-chat/src/components/connector-step-sentence.ts:60-94).
use_cases: Ask a question needing the web: see 'Searching the web for <query>', then 'Searched the web · 4 sources'.
Ask for a spreadsheet script: see 'Running code'.
Ask for a document in an artifact: see 'Creating <file name>' with a line count and seconds, click to open the panel.
Generate an image: see a Generating image card; generate a video: see a still-being-generated card with percent.

where_to_find_it: Web and Desktop: the 'Agent activity' timeline above the answer (AgentActivityTimeline.tsx:869), the Creating row (ArtifactCreatingRow.tsx), the image card 'Generating image' and the video card.
Mobile: the activity timeline in the assistant bubble (AgentActivityTimeline.tsx), the web search card, the Writing card for artifacts, Generating image and Generating video cards.
CLI: tool cells in the transcript (glyph, icon, tool name, summary) and the '/image' line 'Generating the image. Esc stops it.'
VS Code: the activity group above the answer with running, completed and error counts.
Chrome: the agent activity block with step rows, and the Preparing/thinking row.
prerequisites: A route and model that can call tools; tools such as web search depend on the provider route or AGI harness, not on the model itself (doc: AGENTS.md section 4).
Connectors need to be connected for connector steps.
screens_and_controls: Web timeline summary line, collapsed by default, expandable; step rows with status; web search rows show sources.
Web Creating row is a button with aria-label '<label>. Show the code being written' (ArtifactCreatingRow.tsx:71).
Mobile image card has Stop and Retry (MessageBubble.tsx:2512-2530).
CLI Esc stops an image generation (tui_app.rs:7586).
Video: 'Resume checking' button on web when status checking paused (MessageBubble.tsx:3318-3330).
journey: 1. Send a request that needs a tool.
2. For the first second the web summary says 'Working' (AgentActivityTimeline.tsx:51,357-367).
3. A step starts: the live label shows that step (for example 'Searching the web for <query>', 'Running code', 'Reading <file>', 'Reading from <Service>').
4. Web search with sources shows 'Reading N sources' while running (AgentActivityTimeline.tsx:203-206).
5. The step finishes: label becomes done form ('Searched the web · N sources', 'Read from <Service>').
6. A file or artifact being written shows 'Creating <name>' with lines and seconds; the raw code is kept out of the chat body (MessageBubble.tsx:2057-2060, 2980-2987).
7. When all is done the summary becomes 'Worked for Ns' or the search summary.
feedback_and_outputs: Web: 'Searching the web for <arg>' / 'Searching the web', 'Running code', 'Reading <path>', 'Creating image', 'Editing image' (agentActivityLabel.ts:24-34,53-82).
Web: 'Searched the web' with '· N source(s)'; 'Search stopped' when cancelled (AgentActivityTimeline.tsx:141-165).

Web image: 'Generating image' and 'Generating with <model label>' (ImageGenerationCard.tsx:222-231). Video: 'Your video is still being generated' and 'N% complete.'

features.summary: When a step needs the person's approval, an answer, or an offline device, the turn pauses and says so. Web, mobile and Chrome show Needs approval or input labels and cards; CLI and VS Code have approval modals and cards; device waits show on web, mobile and Chrome.

purpose.what_it_does: Pauses a running turn at a step that needs a human decision or a missing device, and shows exactly what is being asked with the controls to answer.
purpose.why_it_exists: Risky tools must not run unseen; the assistant also sometimes needs facts only the person has, and some steps run on the person's own desktop.
purpose.who_uses_it: Anyone running agent steps: file writes, shell commands, connector actions, desktop steps.
problems_solved: No tool with side effects runs without a visible decision.
A paused turn does not look frozen: the summary and the screen reader both say it is waiting.
An offline desktop shows a clear wait with a cancel option instead of a silent hang.
use_cases: Approve a file write the assistant proposes.
Answer a clarifying question asked mid-task through a card or form.
See 'Waiting for your desktop' when a desktop step has no online device.
Deny a tool with guidance (VS Code, Chrome).

where_to_find_it: Web and Desktop: the tool step card in the activity timeline (ToolCallCard) and interactive cards in the message.

CLI: a modal over the transcript for approvals and questions.
VS Code: an inline card titled 'Approval needed' or 'AGI asks'.
Chrome: step rows with Approve and Decline, and a connector input form.
prerequisites: A turn with a tool that requires approval, an input request, or a device step.
For a device step: a registered desktop that is currently offline (to see the wait).
screens_and_controls: Web buttons: 'Allow', 'Allow for this chat' (hidden for high-risk), 'Deny' (packages/contracts/types/src/tool-approval-policy.ts:22-32; ToolCallCard.tsx:411-440). The brief and the draft say 'Approve'; the web card says Allow.

Web device wait text: 'Waiting for <device or your desktop>. Open the desktop app to continue.' with a Cancel button, or 'Running on this device. Approve it if your desktop asks.' (ToolCallCard.tsx:340-346).
Web expired text: 'This approval request expired or is no longer active.' (ToolCallCard.tsx:371).
Chrome: Approve, Decline, optional 'Allow for this chat' and guidance field (bubbles.ts:959-1042; messages.json spApprovalApprove, spApprovalDecline).
VS Code: card title 'Approval needed' with risk label and 'Deny and tell AGI what to do instead'; question card 'AGI asks' (webviewContent.ts:7117-7140,7241,7262-7290).
CLI: approval and question modals (tui_app.rs:1651,1729); request kinds include Question, AskUser and McpElicitation (approval_broker.rs:23-60).
journey: 1. A step reaches a gate; the run status becomes awaiting approval, paused with an input request, or awaiting device.

2. The turn summary changes: web 'Needs approval · <step>' or 'Waiting for your input · <step>' (AgentActivityTimeline.tsx:337-343); mobile 'Needs approval' and 'Waiting for <device>' (AgentActivityTimeline.tsx:249-255); Chrome 'Needs your approval · t', 'Needs your input · t', 'Waiting for your desktop · t' (messages.json).
3. The screen reader hears 'Response paused, waiting for your approval' (web, ChatMessageList.tsx:1753-1757) or 'Approval needed: <step>' (AgentActivityTimeline.tsx:375-377).
4. The person chooses; the card shows the recorded outcome (VS Code: 'Approved once.', 'Turn aborted.'; Chrome: recorded Approved or Declined).
5. The run resumes through the server (resume endpoints) or ends if denied.

established.statement: A step needing approval pauses the turn visibly in a waiting-for-approval state with approve and deny controls.
When the assistant needs information it shows a waiting-for-input state with a way to answer.
A step needing an offline device shows it is waiting for or cannot reach that device.
Capability honesty: a hidden or disabled control is better than an enabled no-op.
Do not use one generic approval setting; approval domains are separate.

acceptance_criteria: Trigger a tool that needs approval on web: the card shows Allow and Deny and the summary reads Needs approval; a screen reader announces the pause.
Click Deny: the step is declined and the turn continues or ends as designed; the card shows Denied.
Trigger a question card: the summary reads Waiting for your input; answering resumes the turn.
Take the only desktop offline and trigger a desktop step: the step card says Waiting for your desktop with Cancel.
On mobile, leave an approval unanswered and reopen after it expires: the expired notice shows.
In the CLI, a file write shows a modal; Esc or No denies and the turn continues.
In VS Code, an approval card takes keyboard focus on its first action when the transcript is followed.
inferred: VS Code should say when a device step cannot run [inferred from S19.24 status 'done' in the brief, contradicted by code search].
The web summary line should name the device wait like the screen reader line does [inferred].
proposed: [proposed] Add an awaiting-device branch to the web and shared summary.
[proposed] Show the offered options as buttons on every app for single-choice questions.

features.summary: The answer appears while the model writes it. The waiting row gives way when text arrives, text is added in small batches so the screen does not flicker, and lists, tables and code blocks take shape while partial. Each app has its own renderer.

purpose.what_it_does: Streams model text to the screen in batches, swaps the waiting indicator for the answer, and renders markdown while it is incomplete.
purpose.why_it_exists: Long answers would otherwise show nothing until the end; batching keeps the page smooth.
purpose.who_uses_it: Everyone reading answers.
problems_solved: Visible progress during long answers.
No flicker or tap lag from one render per token (mobile services/streaming.ts:244-250).
An unfinished code fence still looks like code.
use_cases: Read a long answer as it appears.
Scroll up while it streams without being pulled to the bottom.
Watch a table or list form.
Expand a thinking block.

where_to_find_it: Web and Desktop: the assistant message body in the transcript.
Mobile: the assistant bubble.
CLI: the live transcript area during a turn.
VS Code: sidebar chat message.
Chrome: side panel message.
prerequisites: A model route that streams.
screens_and_controls: Web scroll anchoring: follow the bottom unless the reader scrolled up (ChatMessageList.tsx:1558-1589,1632-1638).
Thinking block expand and collapse on web, mobile (ThinkingUi tests exist), others unknown.
CLI: scroll the transcript during a turn; Ctrl+O toggles expanded tool output (tui_app.rs:8455-8460).
journey: 1. After send the waiting row shows (F019-01).
2. The first text arrives: on web the typing indicator condition becomes false because the last message is streaming (ChatMessageList.tsx:1350).
3. Text appends once per frame on web (frame-coalesced-appender.ts:20-70, fallback 32 ms), every 16 ms on mobile (streaming.ts:250), every 80 ms redraw tick in the CLI (tui_app.rs:8438).

4. Markdown is rendered on the partial text; an open code fence is closed for display on web (MessageBubble.tsx:446-449) and a fence is re-opened for the visible tail in the CLI (tui_app.rs:5495-5512).
5. The turn ends and the streaming flag clears.
feedback_and_outputs: Answer text growing in place.

features.summary: After a turn ends, the screen says whether it completed, finished with errors, or was stopped, and while a stop is in progress it says so. A Cloud stop on web waits up to about 30 seconds for the server to confirm. Text that already arrived is kept.

purpose.what_it_does: Shows the end state of a turn and the stopping state, and records a user stop as stopped, not failed.
purpose.why_it_exists: People need to know whether to trust the answer and whether the assistant is still working.
purpose.who_uses_it: Everyone who sends turns and anyone who presses Stop.
problems_solved: A stop is not mistaken for an error.
A Cloud task that did not stop is not hidden: the person is told to check its activity.
Partial success is distinct from success and failure.
use_cases: Press Stop mid-answer and keep the part already written.
See 'Worked for 42s' after an agent run.
See 'Finished with errors' when one step failed.
Stop a Cloud agent task and wait for the confirmation.

where_to_find_it: Web and Desktop: the Stop button (aria 'Stop the current response', title 'Stop generation') replacing send; the status line 'Stopping the Cloud task…' under the message; the activity summary.
Mobile: stop control in the composer; the 'Response stopped.' notice under the bubble.
CLI: Esc or Ctrl-C; transcript line '⊘ Stopped'; status 'stopping the turn…'.
VS Code: Stop button; 'Stopping…' status and 'Stop response' label.
Chrome: send button in stopping mode; 'Stopping…' status in the bubble; 'Cancelled after <time>' summary.
prerequisites: A running turn.

journey: 1. Press Stop.

2. Web: the request is aborted at once; if the turn belongs to a Cloud run, 'Stopping the Cloud task…' shows and a cancel request is sent, then the run is polled once a second up to 30 times for a terminal state (cancel-cloud-run.ts:4-20; useChatStream.ts:5408-5453).

3. If confirmed, the loading state clears; if not, an error toast says 'The Cloud task has not confirmed it stopped. Check its activity before retrying.' and the stop stays unconfirmed (useChatStream.ts:5427-5438).
4. The message is marked finishReason stopped and the activity cancelled; the text that arrived is kept and saved (useChatStream.ts:6136-6170).
5. The summary reads Stopped (or the last real step), the screen reader says 'Response cancelled. Partial response saved.' (ChatMessageList.tsx:1155-1159).

established.statement: A finished turn is clearly shown as completed and the indicator stops.
A run that finished with some steps failed is shown as partially completed, distinct from success and failure.
After Stop, the surface shows the stop in progress until it takes effect.
A stopped turn ends in a clear stopped state that keeps what arrived.
Stop/cancel works: interrupted state is recorded and the UI recovers.
Cancellation is one of the states every async flow must design.

acceptance_criteria: Press Stop on a plain answer on web: streaming ends, the text stays, the summary reads Stopped or similar, and a screen reader hears 'Response cancelled. Partial response saved.'
Press Stop on a Cloud agent run on web: 'Stopping the Cloud task…' shows until the run is terminal; the notice disappears.
Block the cancel confirmation: after about 30 seconds an error toast says to check the task's activity.
Run a task where one step fails but the last succeeds: web summary reads completed; where the last step fails it reads Finished with errors.
Stop on mobile: bubble shows 'Response stopped.'; reopening the chat shows the same state.
Stop in the CLI: '⊘ Stopped' shows and queued text returns to the composer.
Stop twice quickly: the second press does nothing while cancellation is pending.

The stop confirmation time should be the same on web and Chrome [inferred].

features.summary: When a turn fails, the app says why in plain words and offers the next move: retry, switch model, sign in again, shorten the message, or check usage. Text that arrived stays and is marked. Web maps about 30 server codes to 18 causes.

purpose.what_it_does: Turns failure codes into one clear sentence plus actions, shows a reference id for support, and never invents a wait time.
purpose.why_it_exists: A raw provider error is useless and sometimes unsafe to show; the person needs the next step.
purpose.who_uses_it: Anyone whose turn fails: rate limit, plan limit, expired session, provider down, too-long input.
problems_solved: Wrong fixes: shortening a message when the provider is down.
Lost partial answers.
Unactionable errors.
use_cases: Provider overloaded: see Retry and Switch model.
Rate limit with a stated wait: 'Try again in about 30 seconds'.
Context too long: told to start a new chat or remove attachments.
Report a problem quoting 'Reference: <id>'.

Mobile: a red notice under the bubble with Retry and Switch model; a paywall sheet for plan limits.
CLI: an error line with a hint line.
VS Code: an error card with headline, optional detail and an action button.
Chrome: an error bubble with Retry and a Switch model action and optional recovery button.

2. The server sends an error frame with message, code, retryable, optional retryAfterSeconds and requestId (apps/web/app/api/llm/v1/chat/completions/lib/upstream-error-copy.ts:44-70).

Wait a moment and retry, or switch to another model if your plan has one.'; with a stated wait 'Try again in <wait>' (245-254); provider outage; timeout; contextLength 'Start a new chat, remove some attachments, or choose a model with a larger context window.'; messageLength 'Shorten it or send it in parts'; attachment; sessionExpired 'Your session ended before this turn finished. established.statement: A rate-limited turn says so, with when to retry if known.
A turn blocked by an exhausted budget or plan limit names it and points to the fix.
An expired sign-in says so and offers to sign in again.
A provider outage says so and offers retry or another model.
A turn failing on user input explains what to change.
A turn failing after useful output keeps it and marks the failure.
Never invent a wait time; only the provider's stated figure up to 24 hours.

acceptance_criteria: Force a rate-limit with a stated wait: the notice includes 'about N seconds/minutes' and no invented time when none was stated.
Force provider_overloaded: the notice offers Retry and Switch model.
Force an expired session: the sentence says sign in again; no retry loop.
Send an over-long message: the notice names shortening or a bigger context model.
Fail mid-stream: previous text remains and the notice says it may be incomplete or kept above.
Force a failure with a request id: 'Reference: <id>' appears and matches the server log.
Leave a user message unanswered 10 seconds on web: no failure notice yet; after 45 seconds the default notice appears.
Hit a plan limit on mobile: the paywall sheet opens.

Usage limit sentences should name the limit [inferred from S19.22].

steps.what_happens: The upstream provider returns an error or ends the stream badly.
The AGI gateway classifies the error, builds a sentence with code, retryable, wait and request id, and sends it as an error frame or HTTP error.
The client stores the error on the message metadata (streamError) and maps the code to a cause and sentence.
The notice renders with Retry or Switch model; retry re-sends the previous user message.
For plan or usage limits the server may return a paywall payload and the client opens a paywall card or sheet.
The CLI classifies provider HTTP statuses locally (401/403 auth, 429 rate limit, 5xx unavailable) and prints a hint.

features.summary: When the link drops during a Cloud turn, the app shows 'Reconnecting…' and re-reads the server's saved event journal from the last event it saw. Cloud runs continue on our servers after the window closes, so reopening shows the latest or final state. The CLI runs local background processes.

purpose.what_it_does: Keeps a turn alive across a dropped connection, a closed window or a restart. For Managed Cloud turns the server writes every event to a journal; the app asks for events after its last sequence number and shows the 'Reconnecting…' label until events flow again (apps/web/lib/hooks/useChatStream.ts:3093-3200; packages/contracts/cloud-contracts/src/managed-cloud-agent-runs-client.ts:528-582). On the CLI, 'agi background' starts a detached local process that keeps working after the terminal closes (apps/cli/src/background.rs:246-300).
purpose.why_it_exists: Long agent turns outlive a flaky network, a laptop lid or a phone going to the background. Without resume the person would lose the answer or pay for a second run. Brief items S19.19, S19.20, S19.29 require a visible reconnect state, resume rather than restart, and work that continues after the UI closes (doc: knowledge-base/data/area-briefs/019-streaming-and-response-presentation-states.md).
purpose.who_uses_it: Anyone running a long Cloud turn on Web, Desktop, Mobile or the Chrome extension; CLI users who start background runs; VS Code users who reopen a session.
problems_solved: A dropped connection no longer leaves the answer spinning or lost.
Closing the window or app does not cancel Cloud work.

A duplicate paid run is avoided because a recent unanswered question with no run is waited on, not called stopped (apps/mobile/src/features/chat/inFlightTurnRecovery.ts, comment above questionMayStillBeAnswered).
A run that died on the server is reported as stopped instead of spinning forever (apps/web/lib/hooks/useChatStream.ts:4128-4135).
use_cases: Start a long research turn on the web, lose Wi-Fi, see 'Reconnecting…', and watch it continue when the network returns.
Close the Desktop window mid-run, reopen later and find the finished answer.
Start a Cloud turn on the phone, switch apps, return and see the answer that finished meanwhile.
Run 'agi background start <prompt>' in the terminal, close it, then 'agi background attach <id>' later.

journey: 1. The person sends a Cloud turn; the server starts a run and journals every event.
2. The connection drops (network loss, server time budget, app suspended).
3. The app shows 'Reconnecting…' on the answer.
4. The app asks the server for events after the last sequence it saw and appends only what is missing.
5. When the first event or snapshot arrives the label clears and text continues.
6. If the run already finished, the final state is read and shown without replaying what was already on screen.
7. If the run cannot be followed, the turn is marked failed with an error rather than left spinning.
8. After closing and reopening the window or app, the app asks whether a run is still going for the conversation and follows it or loads the finished answer.

CLI: background runs start a detached supervisor process, are listed, logged, stopped, removed and attached (apps/cli/src/background.rs; apps/cli/src/lib.rs:1718-1819); 'agi resume' continues a saved session.
VS Code: session resume through the runtime (apps/extension-vscode/src/features/sidebar-webview/ChatStateManager.ts:2913).
