Brief says 'poll every 2.5 seconds on web'; Mobile, Desktop (Tauri) and Chrome call followRun without a poll interval, so they use the client default of 1 s (packages/contracts/cloud-contracts/src/managed-cloud-agent-runs-client.ts:153-157; apps/mobile/services/streaming.ts:983; apps/desktop/src/runtime/CloudRuntime.ts:700).
CLI background runs are local processes: they stop if the machine sleeps or reboots and end as 'ended without a result' (apps/cli/src/background.rs:46-60, 215-244). They are not Cloud runs.
disconnected_or_disabled: Web cursor replay is switched off for temporary conversations and turn continuations (apps/web/lib/hooks/useChatStream.ts:3041-3042).
not_available: CLI: no 'Reconnecting' state for a chat turn (brief S19.19 missing; none found in apps/cli/src/tui/tui_app.rs besides Remote Control).
VS Code: no 'Reconnecting' state for a chat turn (brief S19.19 missing); background continuation unverified (brief S19.29).

Local mode (mode:local): no durable run or journal exists; recovery and reconnect apply to Managed Cloud only (apps/mobile/src/features/chat/inFlightTurnRecovery.ts:turnToAsk returns null when not cloud).

established.statement: On a drop, the answer shows Reconnecting and the app re-follows the run from the last sequence number it saw (poll every 2.5 seconds on web).
Work that was already running is picked up again after reconnect or reopen and shown as resuming rather than restarting.
Work keeps running after the UI is closed and its result is there, or resumes, when the user returns.
If the run cannot be followed the answer is marked failed rather than left spinning.

acceptance_criteria: Drop the network mid Cloud turn on Web: 'Reconnecting…' appears, then clears on the first new event; no text is duplicated.
Reopen a conversation whose run finished while the app was closed: the final answer and its finished state show without re-running.
Reopen while the run is still working: the app follows it and shows live progress, not a restart.
Kill the run on the server side (stall past the deadline): the app shows the 'stopped running on the server' error, not a spinner.
Mobile: put the app in the background during a Cloud turn, return: the answer is complete or follows on.
CLI: 'agi background start', close the terminal, 'agi background list' shows the run; 'stop' ends it and the state reads 'stopped'.
Chrome: close and reopen the side panel mid-run: the turn re-attaches with 'Reconnecting…' then continues.
inferred: A Local turn needs no reconnect state because no remote run exists [inferred].
Reconnect copy should be the same wording on every app that has the state [inferred from the shared label on Web, Mobile, Chrome].
proposed: [proposed] Add a 'Reconnecting…' state to the CLI and VS Code chat turns.
[proposed] Give Mobile, Desktop and Chrome the same 2.5 s poll interval as Web to reduce request load, or record why 1 s is needed.
[proposed] Record a device test of background continuation on iOS and Android and update the brief.

steps.what_happens: Person sends a Cloud turn; the server starts a run and writes each event to the journal with a sequence number.
The app streams events and records the highest sequence seen on the message (cloudAgentRun.lastSequence).
Connection drops, or the server sends x_run_detached when its function time budget ends.
App sets the reconnecting phase and calls followRun after the last sequence; it polls every 2.5 s on Web.
Server returns run state plus events after the sequence; the run snapshot route is rate limited under 'agent-run-follow'.
First event or snapshot clears the phase; new text is reconciled against text already shown so nothing repeats.
At a terminal run state the follow ends, tools are finished, the turn is saved and loading stops; on failure the error is surfaced.
After reopen the app lists runs for the conversation, follows a live one or loads the finished answer; a run silent beyond the deadline is called stalled.
CLI: 'agi background start' spawns a detached supervisor that runs 'agi --print' in the same folder and writes run.json and output.log under the config directory.

execution_and_data_flow.models_and_providers: Reconnect is independent of the model. The run records the provider and model it used (columns provider and model in cloud_agent_runs). The follow client never chooses a model; mobile deliberately cannot override the model on an approval resume (apps/mobile/services/streaming.ts comment in streamCheckpointResume).

access_and_usage.account: Cloud follow needs a signed-in account; the runs endpoints use the user-scoped database and CSRF for state changes (apps/web/app/api/llm/v1/chat/completions/runs/[runId]/route.ts:41-44, 70-72). A changed account stops the follow on Web and Mobile (apps/web/lib/hooks/useChatStream.ts assertTokenOwner; apps/mobile/services/streaming.ts isCloudAccountEpochCurrent).
access_and_usage.permissions: Run rows are isolated per user (row level security enabled, apps/web/db/neon/0061_cloud_agent_runs.sql:61-62). CLI background runs only signal processes they own (apps/cli/src/background.rs:203-214).
access_and_usage.subscription: No reconnect-specific entitlement was found in the code. Starting the Cloud turn is governed by the normal chat entitlement and quota checks; following an existing run was not seen to be metered.
access_and_usage.limits_and_metering: Poll 2.5 s on Web (apps/web/lib/hooks/useChatStream.ts:1365); 1 s default elsewhere; up to 5 transient errors retried by followRun; rate limit bucket 'agent-run-follow' on the snapshot route; mobile 3 reconnect attempts; stall deadline = tool-call limit 120 s + 30 s margin (apps/web/lib/deadline-policy.ts:8, 28). The numeric limiter values: unknown.
access_and_usage.flags: none found in the code for the reconnect label itself.
access_and_usage.model_compatibility: Not model dependent in the code read.
access_and_usage.provider_restrictions: Provider-funded Free models use a separate Free chat route on mobile (apps/mobile/services/streaming.ts, streamChat refuses them on the managed route); whether that route is followable after a drop: unknown.
access_and_usage.local_mode: Local mode has no run journal and no reconnect label. Mobile asks the server about in-flight turns only for Cloud conversations (apps/mobile/src/features/chat/inFlightTurnRecovery.ts, turnToAsk). The CLI background command runs on the device and needs no subscription of its own; the model route it uses follows CLI settings [inferred].

features.summary: Each finished turn is stored with its final state (done, failed or stopped) and returns after a restart. Web, Desktop, Mobile and the CLI restore the conversation. Only the Chrome extension shows a saved label; the CLI has a /save command. No app shows a save time or a visible save-failed notice.

purpose.what_it_does: Saves the assistant turn and its metadata, including the finish reason, stream error, activity and run reference, then loads them again when the conversation is reopened. Web writes the turn to the server (apps/web/lib/hooks/useChatStream.ts:2779-2840); Mobile keeps Local chats in device storage and loads Cloud chats from the server (apps/mobile/stores/chat/chatMessageStore.ts:1729-1735, 772-830); the CLI writes a session file (apps/cli/src/agent/mod.rs:2627-2670); the Chrome extension keeps history in browser storage and mirrors it to the account with a visible label (apps/extension/src/side_panel.ts:587-690).
purpose.why_it_exists: A person must find the conversation and each turn's outcome after closing the app, and must know whether the work is kept. Brief items S19.14 (saving results) and S19.28 (session restored after restart) require this (doc: knowledge-base/data/area-briefs/019-streaming-and-response-presentation-states.md).
purpose.who_uses_it: Anyone who closes and reopens a conversation on any of the six apps.
problems_solved: Lost answers after a restart.
A stopped or failed turn reappearing as if it were complete (stopped turns keep finishReason 'stopped', apps/web/lib/hooks/useChatStream.ts:693, 2809-2815).
Not knowing whether a Chrome chat is on the account or only in the browser.
A cancelled CLI turn leaving a lone prompt in the session file (apps/cli/src/lib.rs:8613-8626).
use_cases: Reopen a Web conversation after a restart and see the last turn marked stopped.
Open the Chrome side panel and read 'Saved to your account' under the title.
Run 'agi resume latest' in the CLI to continue an earlier session.
Open an earlier VS Code session from the session list.

journey: 1. A turn finishes, is stopped or fails.

3. The person closes the app.

5. The app loads the stored messages with their metadata.
6. Each turn renders its final state: done, failed or stopped.
7. Chrome shows the persistence label; the CLI shows 'Managed session saved' only after /save.

steps.what_happens: A turn settles; the app builds metadata including finishReason and streamError.
Web posts the assistant message to the messages endpoint.
The server inserts the message under a lock, sets the active leaf, and stamps 'stopped' if the referenced run was cancelled and no reason was sent.
On reopen the app loads stored messages and renders each turn's state from its metadata.
Mobile Local chats are saved by the persist middleware to MMKV on the phone and never sent to a server.
Chrome stores the chat in chrome.storage.local and mirrors it to the account when allowed; the label reflects the sync state.
CLI writes the session file after turns and on exit; sync_to_account runs after exit.

features.summary: Turns the plain Markdown text a model writes into readable structure in every AGI Workforce app: paragraphs, headings, bold, italic, strikethrough, bulleted, numbered and nested lists, task checkboxes, quotes, dividers, inline code, and backslash-escaped symbols. It is client-side display code with no plan check.

purpose.what_it_does: Parses the model's reply as Markdown and draws it with the matching text styles. Web and Tauri desktop share the React component MarkdownContent (packages/ui/unified-chat/src/components/markdown/MarkdownContent.tsx:874-960). Mobile has its own parser and renderer (apps/mobile/src/features/chat/components/MessageContentRenderer.tsx). The CLI draws styled terminal lines (apps/cli/src/tui/markdown_renderer.rs:142-439). VS Code and the Chrome side panel use markdown-it (apps/extension-vscode/src/webview/render.ts:16-24; apps/extension/src/features/side-panel/markdown.ts:141-146).
purpose.why_it_exists: Models answer in Markdown. Showing raw hash marks and asterisks makes answers hard to read, so each app turns them into structure. The brief lists this as items S20.01 to S20.10 and S20.21 (doc: knowledge-base/data/area-briefs/020-markdown-and-text-rendering.md).
purpose.who_uses_it: Every person who reads an answer in Web, Desktop, Mobile, CLI, VS Code or Chrome. Nobody has to turn it on.
problems_solved: Answers read as structured text instead of raw Markdown symbols.
A symbol the model escaped with a backslash shows as the plain character.
Lists, quotes and task items keep their shape on small screens and in a terminal.
use_cases: A reader sees a step-by-step answer as a numbered list with nested bullets.
A reader sees a checklist answer with open and ticked boxes.
A CLI user reads a headed, bulleted answer in the terminal.
A reader sees a quoted passage set apart from the explanation.

where_to_find_it: Web: assistant and user messages in the chat page (apps/web/features/chat/components/messages/MessageBubble.tsx:2884-2906).

Desktop (Tauri build): chat messages through the shared unified-chat MessageBubble (packages/ui/unified-chat/src/components/MessageBubble.tsx:827-835). The public Electron Desktop shows the hosted web app, so it gets the web rendering (AGENTS.md section 5; apps/desktop/electron/main.ts:345).
Mobile: the message list rendered by renderMarkdownContent (apps/mobile/src/features/chat/components/MessageContentRenderer.tsx:1625-1679).
CLI: the terminal chat view (apps/cli/src/tui/tui_app.rs:2923, 2970) and the one-shot print path (apps/cli/src/lib.rs:7324).
VS Code: the sidebar chat webview (apps/extension-vscode/src/features/sidebar-webview/webviewContent.ts:5368-5380).
Chrome: the side panel assistant bubble (apps/extension/src/features/side-panel/bubbles.ts:401).
prerequisites: A reply that contains Markdown. Nothing else; there is no setting or plan gate in the rendering code I read.
screens_and_controls: No control for plain formatting. Reading only.
Task checkboxes in a chat message are read-only on web and desktop (MarkdownContent.tsx:443-449 renders a disabled input when no toggle is supplied).

Task checkboxes are tickable only where the host passes onTaskToggle: the web artifact preview (apps/web/features/chat/components/artifacts/ArtifactPreview.tsx:354, 1934) and the mobile artifact full screen (apps/mobile/src/features/chat/components/ArtifactFullScreen.tsx:1101). No chat message bubble passes it (searched apps/web, apps/desktop/src, packages/ui/unified-chat).
journey: The model streams or finishes a reply.
The app prepares the text (math delimiters, hyphenated labels, citations) and parses it.
The app draws paragraphs, headings, lists, quotes, dividers and inline styles.

If the reply is empty, the web bubble shows a notice that the model finished without returning a response (apps/web/features/chat/components/messages/MessageBubble.tsx:2870-2880); mobile returns nothing (MessageContentRenderer.tsx:1626).
feedback_and_outputs: Styled text on screen. On web, h1 to h3 have named heading styles and paragraphs have bottom spacing (MarkdownContent.tsx:775-790, 392-399).
A tick glyph inside a bordered square for a done task (MarkdownContent.tsx:419-454).
In the CLI, headings keep their # prefix in an accent colour (markdown_renderer.rs:222-228), bullets show a dot, tasks show a ballot-box glyph (markdown_renderer.rs:325-331).
settings: None specific to formatting. Text size and theme come from each app's general settings (not read in detail).

working: Web and Tauri desktop: remark-gfm, remark-math and remark-breaks feed react-markdown with custom components for paragraph, h1-h3, lists, quote, task checkbox (MarkdownContent.tsx:771-805; remarkPlugins.ts:71-77).

Ordered lists keep their start number (MarkdownContent.tsx:473-483). Nested lists render through the same list components [inferred]. Task items drop the bullet (MarkdownContent.tsx:456-471, 485-512).

Raw HTML in an assistant answer is parsed, then sanitised (MarkdownContent.tsx:819-823). For user messages the host sets literalHtml so HTML shows as text (MarkdownContent.tsx:944; MessageBubble.tsx 2895-2900).
Mobile: own block parser with headings, lists (nested, ordered, task), quotes, rules, indented and fenced code (MessageContentRenderer.tsx:254-300, 787-796, 1073).

CLI: pulldown-cmark with tables, strikethrough and task lists on (markdown_renderer.rs:147-150); headings, bold, italic, strike, bullets, ordered numbering, quotes, rules, inline code are handled (markdown_renderer.rs:206-400). Terminal control characters are stripped first (markdown_renderer.rs:146; apps/cli/src/terminal_text.rs:3-19).

VS Code and Chrome: markdown-it with html disabled; tasks via the shared markdownItTaskLists plugin, which writes a role=checkbox span with a tick or box glyph (packages/ui/unified-chat/src/components/markdown/markdownItTaskLists.ts:24-27).

Backslash escapes: web normalises math delimiters but leaves a backslash-dollar alone (packages/platform/utils/src/markdownSource.ts:208); the Markdown parser drops the backslash for other symbols [inferred]. Mobile has protectEscapes and restoreEscapes (MarkdownInline.tsx:36-41).
incomplete: CLI headings are drawn with their literal # marks, e.g. '    ## text' (markdown_renderer.rs:222-228). The brief's S20.02 says hash marks must not show. The brief's status for CLI is done.
Chat task checkboxes cannot be ticked on any app; only artifact views pass a toggle handler (see screens_and_controls).

Line-break handling differs: web uses remark-breaks (remarkPlugins.ts:3, 74) and Chrome sets breaks true (markdown.ts:144), but VS Code sets breaks false (render.ts:19). A single newline inside a paragraph is therefore a line break on web and Chrome and a space in VS Code [inferred from markdown-it behaviour].
Web styles only h1, h2 and h3 explicitly (MarkdownContent.tsx:775-789). h4 to h6 fall back to the library default elements [inferred].
disconnected_or_disabled: onTaskToggle is implemented in MarkdownContent (MarkdownContent.tsx:920-924) and in the mobile renderer (MessageContentRenderer.tsx:1660-1668) but is not wired into chat bubbles.
not_available: CLI: no raw-HTML pass-through; HTML events fall into the catch-all arm and are ignored (markdown_renderer.rs:433).
Chrome: no CSS classes survive the sanitiser (markdown.ts:130 forbids class), so styling is applied by stylesheet selectors on elements.

established.statement: Assistant text separated by blank lines renders as distinct paragraphs with spacing.
ATX headings (# to ######) render as styled headings, not literal hash marks.
Bold, italic and strikethrough render with matching text styles.
Ordered lists show their numbers, respecting the start value, with indentation. Unordered lists show bullets. Nested lists indent deeper under the parent.
GFM task items render as checkboxes reflecting their state.
Lines starting with > render as an indented, distinct quotation block; a thematic break renders as a divider; inline code is monospace.
Backslash-escaped delimiters (star, dollar, underscore) display as the literal character without the backslash.
No requirement for Markdown rendering was found in docs/product or docs/decisions (searched for markdown, table, footnote, katex).

acceptance_criteria: A reply with two paragraphs separated by a blank line shows two spaced paragraphs on all six apps.
A reply with '## Title' shows a styled heading with no visible hash marks on web, desktop, mobile, VS Code and Chrome. On CLI this currently fails (gap).
'**a** *b* ~~c~~' shows bold, italic and struck text on every app.
'3. x' then '4. y' shows numbering that starts at 3 on web (test RenderingMatrix 'starts an ordered list at the number the author wrote').
A nested bullet under a bullet shows deeper indentation on every app.
'- [x] done' and '- [ ] open' show a ticked and an empty box; in a chat message the box cannot be toggled.
'\*not bold\*' shows asterisks with no backslash.
inferred: Empty or whitespace-only replies should show nothing extra in the renderer itself; the web bubble adds a separate notice for a finished reply with no output [inferred from MessageBubble.tsx:2870-2880].
Formatting must be identical in meaning across apps, differing only in presentation [inferred from AGENTS.md section 5 shared contract layer].
proposed: [proposed] Make the CLI draw headings without the literal # marks, keeping the level by colour and weight.
[proposed] Decide one line-break rule for all apps and test it.
[proposed] Decide whether chat checkboxes should be tickable, since the toggle code exists.

features.summary: Shows text between triple backticks as a monospace block that keeps spaces and line breaks. Web and desktop add a language label and Copy, Download, Expand and Edit buttons, and colour the code with Shiki after the block finishes streaming. Other apps draw their own blocks. If colouring fails, plain code still shows.

purpose.what_it_does: Draws fenced and indented code as a distinct, scrollable monospace block so whitespace is preserved and code can be copied.
purpose.why_it_exists: Models answer programming and command-line questions with code. Readers need exact characters, a quick copy, and a visual break from prose (doc: knowledge-base/data/area-briefs/020-markdown-and-text-rendering.md S20.11).
purpose.who_uses_it: Developers and anyone following commands or snippets in an answer, on all six apps.
problems_solved: Spaces and line breaks in code are kept.
One click copies the whole block (web, VS Code, Chrome, mobile).
Unknown languages and highlight failures still show readable code.
Shell commands are labelled as examples that have not run (web).
use_cases: Copy a Python snippet from a web answer.
Download a block as a file named for its language on web or mobile.
Read a diff with green and red lines.
Read a bash block in the CLI with a framed header.

where_to_find_it: Web and Desktop (Tauri): inside any assistant message with a fenced block; header shows the language and buttons 'Copy', 'Edit' (when an editor is attached), 'Download <file name>', 'Expand code' (packages/ui/unified-chat/src/components/markdown/CodeBlock.tsx:176-207).

Mobile: a code card with accessibility labels '<language> code block', 'Preview HTML', 'Edit code', 'Expand code', 'Show more code', 'Show less code' (apps/mobile/src/features/chat/components/CodeCard.tsx:431, 505, 524, 542, 555).

features.summary: Turns [text](address) and bare web addresses into links, blocks raw scripts and unsafe link types, and holds images from other sites until the reader clicks Load image. Web, mobile and Chrome keep that image rule. VS Code removes images. The CLI shows link addresses in brackets and does not link bare addresses.

purpose.what_it_does: Draws links the reader can follow, removes anything that could run code, and stops a reply from silently fetching images from other hosts.
purpose.why_it_exists: A model reply can contain hostile links, HTML or images that call an attacker's server. The brief requires sanitised markup and safe link handling (doc: knowledge-base/data/area-briefs/020-markdown-and-text-rendering.md S20.12, S20.13, S20.24, S20.25). AGENTS.md section 6 requires security to fail closed.
purpose.who_uses_it: Every reader of answers with links or images; security reviewers.
problems_solved: Script or javascript links in a reply cannot run.
A remote image cannot track the reader before they agree.
Bare URLs become tappable (not CLI).
Failed images show a readable notice with Retry.

features.summary: Shows pipe tables as a grid with a header row. Wide tables scroll sideways inside their box. purpose.who_uses_it: Readers of comparisons, lists of numbers and schedules.

features.summary: Draws formulas written as $...$ or \( \) inline and $$...$$ or \[ \] as blocks. Web and desktop use remark-math with KaTeX; mobile draws KaTeX in a locked web view; VS Code and Chrome use a shared markdown-it math plugin. The CLI has no math support and shows the source text. Money amounts are not read as maths.

purpose.what_it_does: Turns LaTeX in an answer into typeset formulas, and keeps dollar prices as plain text.
purpose.why_it_exists: Science, finance and maths answers are written in LaTeX. Raw TeX is unreadable (doc: knowledge-base/data/area-briefs/020-markdown-and-text-rendering.md S20.19, S20.20).
purpose.who_uses_it: Students, engineers and analysts reading maths answers.
problems_solved: Formulas read as maths, not code.
Models use several delimiter styles; all are accepted.
A price like $5 and $10 is not turned into a formula.
A formula that cannot be drawn still shows its source.
use_cases: Read a quadratic formula as a centred block.
Read an inline variable in a sentence.
See 'costs $5 or $10' stay as text.
Read a formula in the VS Code sidebar.

working: Web and desktop: preprocessMath converts \( \) to $...$ and \[ \] to a $$ fenced block, escapes currency dollars, skips code ranges, and lifts one-line $$x$$ onto its own lines (preprocessMath.ts:6-22; markdownSource.ts:153-228). remark-math parses; rehypeKatex draws (remarkPlugins.ts:71-77; MarkdownContent.tsx:819-823).
Currency rule on web: a dollar followed by a digit is escaped when its pair is missing, followed by a digit, or the span reads as prose (markdownSource.ts:24-31, 216-220).
Streaming: a KaTeX error span is hidden on the live tail (MarkdownContent.tsx:748).

Mobile: display math blocks are collected (MessageContentRenderer.tsx:1395-1412) and drawn by MathBlock in a web view with a locked content policy (MathBlock.tsx:22-23); renderMathMarkup uses throwOnError true so failure falls back to the source text in a tinted box (MathBlock.tsx:283-291; packages/ui/unified-chat/src/lib/math-markup.ts:26).
VS Code: markdownItMath makes data-math nodes; renderMath turns them into sanitised MathML, and on failure writes the source back with its delimiters (render.ts:199-214; markdownItMath.ts:85-98).
Chrome: KaTeX loads lazily; throwOnError false; if loading fails the source shows with a title spMathUnavailable (markdown.ts:258-312).

In markdownItMath an inline dollar must not sit next to a word or digit before it or after the closing dollar, and must not have spaces inside (markdownItMath.ts:21-27); this rule applies to VS Code and Chrome only.
incomplete: Web non-streaming failure appearance is the library default error span; its look was not read.
not_available: CLI: no math option in the parser (markdown_renderer.rs:147-150); formulas appear as raw text [inferred]. Brief status missing is correct.

aliases: Live rendering while the answer streams in
features.summary: While an AI answer is still arriving, the reader sees formatted text grow on every app. On web and desktop finished blocks are kept and only the unfinished tail is redrawn, a half-typed table or link is hidden, an open code fence shows as code, and screen readers hear new words every two seconds.

purpose.what_it_does: Draws the answer as formatted Markdown (headings, lists, code, tables, links) while the model is still writing, instead of showing raw symbols until the end. Web and desktop split the text into finished blocks and an unfinished tail (packages/ui/unified-chat/src/components/markdown/StreamingMarkdownContent.tsx:73-135). Mobile, CLI, VS Code and Chrome each re-draw the answer so far with their own renderer.
purpose.why_it_exists: Answers arrive a few words at a time. Without repair the reader would see stars, backticks and pipes flicker, a table jump around, or a code block appear as prose. Re-drawing a long answer on every word is also slow, so web keeps finished blocks. [inferred from the code comments and tests]
purpose.who_uses_it: Everyone who watches a reply being written, on Web, Desktop (hosted web app), Mobile, CLI, VS Code and Chrome. Screen-reader users are served by the announcer on web and desktop.
problems_solved: Raw Markdown symbols visible mid-answer.
A table that is half typed flashing as plain text.
A link whose address is still arriving showing as a broken link.
An open code fence showing as prose.
A screen reader re-reading the whole growing answer on every word.
use_cases: Ask for a comparison table and watch it appear once its header and divider are complete (web).
Ask for code; the code block shows as code from the opening fence, before the closing fence arrives.
Ask a long question with a screen reader and hear the answer in word-sized pieces every two seconds (web).
Watch a reply grow in the terminal UI (CLI).

where_to_find_it: Web: any chat turn while the reply is streaming; message body is built in apps/web/features/chat/components/messages/MessageBubble.tsx:2884-2893 and :2914.
Desktop: the public Electron app shows the hosted web app, so it is the same screen (doc: AGENTS.md section 5; apps/desktop/electron/main.ts:345 loads a URL).
Mobile: the chat screen while a reply streams (apps/mobile/src/features/chat/components/MessageBubble.tsx:2089-2125).
CLI: the terminal chat UI, an answer block prefixed with a sparkle glyph (apps/cli/src/tui/tui_app.rs:2952-2970).
VS Code: the AGI sidebar chat transcript (webviewContent.ts:3167).
Chrome: the side panel chat (apps/extension/src/side_panel.ts:6373).
prerequisites: A chat turn in progress; no setting is needed.

Web guest chat, the model compare page and the thinking block also use the same component (apps/web/features/chat/guest/GuestChat.tsx:345, apps/web/features/models/components/CompareAnswersPage.tsx:422, apps/web/features/chat/components/ThinkingBlock.tsx:181).
screens_and_controls: No control. The reader just watches.
Web shows a small spinning mark above the text while prose streams (MessageBubble.tsx:2830-2833).

Mobile shows a blank placeholder labelled 'Block in progress' for a block that cannot be drawn yet, and 'Equation in progress' for an open display equation (MessageContentRenderer.tsx:1400-1411, :1476-1486).
After a stopped or cut-off block, mobile shows the code plus the line 'This block was not finished.' (MessageContentRenderer.tsx:1487-1507).
journey: 1. The person sends a message.
2. Text starts arriving; the app draws it as formatted Markdown straight away.
3. Web/desktop: blocks that are finished stay drawn; only the last unfinished part changes.
4. An unclosed code fence is drawn as a code block; an unfinished table row or header is held back; a link with a half-typed address shows only its label.
5. A screen reader on web hears the new words about every two seconds.

6. When the answer ends, the full renderer takes over: numeric citation markers become links, task boxes become clickable, and code is syntax highlighted (MarkdownContent.tsx:915-923; mobile highlightCode is off while streaming, MessageBubble.tsx:2113).
feedback_and_outputs: Formatted text growing in place.
Web: a polite hidden live region carries the spoken text (StreamAnnouncer.tsx:97-105).
VS Code: the transcript is a polite live log (webviewContent.ts:3167).
Mobile: placeholder boxes for blocks not yet drawable.
settings: None found in the code for this feature.

working: Web/desktop: StreamingMarkdownContent splits the text with a Markdown parser, keeps the last two blocks unsettled (TAIL_NODE_RESERVE = 2) and draws each settled block once with a stable key (packages/ui/unified-chat/src/components/markdown/splitMarkdownBlocks.ts:6, :183-200, :205-243; StreamingMarkdownContent.tsx:110-123). MarkdownContent is wrapped in React.memo (MarkdownContent.tsx:962).

Web/desktop: a reference link or footnote whose definition arrives later folds the whole answer back into one unit so it resolves (StreamingMarkdownContent.tsx:76-104; test StreamingMarkdownContent.test.tsx:198-250).

Web/desktop: completeInlineTokens closes an open code span, drops a link whose address is unfinished and closes a dangling bold marker (completeInlineTokens.ts:148-162, :140-144). It skips code fences while looking for these (completeInlineTokens.ts:37-56).
Web/desktop: holdIncompleteGfmTable cuts the row being typed and cuts a header until its divider row is valid (streamingTableHold.ts:47-74). It does not hold a whole finished table.

Web: an unterminated fence is closed for display by closeUnterminatedFence, only when extractTrailingUnclosedBlock finds one (apps/web/features/chat/components/messages/MessageBubble.tsx:446-449, :2083). The Markdown parser also draws an unclosed fence as code to the end of the text [inferred from CommonMark; test side-panel-markdown-fence.test.ts:5 shows the same for Chrome's parser].
Web: a half-written math error and a streaming rich block are hidden while streaming (MarkdownContent.tsx:748, :638-640).

Web/desktop: StreamAnnouncer announces only the new words, cut at the last space, every 2000 ms, then the rest when the stream ends (StreamAnnouncer.tsx:3-13, :33-74). The web bubble passes announce={false} to StreamingMarkdownContent and wraps the announcer itself (MessageBubble.tsx:2889, :2914). The shared bubble in unified-chat does the same (packages/ui/unified-chat/src/components/MessageBubble.tsx:825-841).

Mobile: prepareMarkdownSource holds an unfinished table, an open image tail and open inline tokens while streaming (apps/mobile/src/features/chat/components/markdownBlockSyntax.ts:530-542). classifyStreamingFence lets a fence with an unfinished structured body wait or show the last good lines (packages/ui/unified-chat/src/components/markdown/assistantFence.ts:440-458; MessageContentRenderer.tsx:1414-1426). Code is not highlighted while streaming (MessageBubble.tsx:2113).

CLI: streaming_markdown_tail renders only the last 200 source lines, re-opens a fence if an earlier line opened one, and shows the last 40 rendered lines (apps/cli/src/tui/tui_app.rs:5492-5508, called at :2968).
VS Code: every token re-renders the whole answer with markdown-it, then sanitizes it (webviewContent.ts:7852-7856; webview/render.ts:216-226).
Chrome: every update re-renders the whole answer into the bubble (apps/extension/src/side_panel.ts:6373-6384; features/side-panel/markdown.ts:607-614).
incomplete: Mobile has no settled-block cache: renderMarkdownContent re-draws the full text inside a memo keyed on content (MessageBubble.tsx:2089-2125, :2114; MessageContentRenderer.tsx:1628-1665). Whether mobile avoids re-parsing finished blocks is unknown beyond that.

VS Code and Chrome do not call completeInlineTokens or holdIncompleteGfmTable (no import found outside unified-chat and mobile). A half-typed table or open bold marker is drawn as the parser sees it. [inferred from search]
CLI has no table hold or inline-token repair; it only windows the text (tui_app.rs:5495-5508).
VS Code has no per-answer streaming announcer; the transcript container is a polite live log (webviewContent.ts:3167). Chrome has none found for answer text (not handled in the code).
disconnected_or_disabled: The brief points at StreamingMarkdownContent.tsx:171 and side_panel.ts:4463; the first file ends at line 147 and the second line is CSS. These brief citations are stale. (doc: knowledge-base/data/area-briefs/020-markdown-and-text-rendering.md)
not_available: Settled-block caching on mobile, CLI, VS Code and Chrome (not implemented there).
Table hold on CLI, VS Code and Chrome.

established.statement: While a reply streams, partial text renders as formatted Markdown progressively rather than raw syntax; required on all six apps.
An unclosed ``` fence mid-stream renders as a code block, not prose, until the closing fence arrives; required on all six apps.
packages/ui/unified-chat is shared by desktop, web, Chrome and VS Code, so nothing in it may assume one surface's routing, billing or account model.
Production code has no silent failures or dead controls; accessible behaviour must be real.

acceptance_criteria: Web: stream a reply containing a table; the header and divider are never drawn as pipe text, and the table appears once the divider row is valid.
Web: stream a reply with an opening code fence and no closing fence; the text after the fence is shown inside a code block.
Web: a link whose address is half typed shows only its label until the closing parenthesis arrives.
Web: while streaming, earlier paragraphs are not re-rendered when a new word arrives (render-count check).
Web with a screen reader: new words are announced about every 2 seconds, never half a word, and the remainder is read once when the stream ends.
Mobile, CLI, VS Code, Chrome: an open code fence draws as code during streaming and no raw symbols for headings, bold or lists remain visible.
After the stream ends, the final text equals one full parse of the whole answer.
inferred: Parity on VS Code and Chrome (table hold, inline repair) is wanted, because the brief marks every app done for S20.22 and S20.23 while the code shows different depth. [inferred]
proposed: [proposed] Move completeInlineTokens and holdIncompleteGfmTable into the VS Code webview renderer and the Chrome side panel renderer.
[proposed] Add a streaming announcer to the Chrome side panel and VS Code webview, or document why the live log is enough.
[proposed] Refresh the stale line references in the brief.

features.summary: Web and desktop let the reader press Ctrl or Cmd+F to search the open chat, step through messages that match, see every match highlighted, and print or export the chat as Markdown, PDF, Word, HTML or JSON. Mobile has text selection, PDF, print, text and Markdown export but no find. CLI exports source text only.

purpose.what_it_does: Lets the reader copy part of an answer by selecting it, find a word inside the current conversation with highlighted matches, and take the conversation out of the app as a file or a paper print with formatting kept.
purpose.why_it_exists: Long answers need quoting, searching and archiving. Print and export must keep headings, tables, code and maths or the file is hard to use. [inferred]
purpose.who_uses_it: Anyone reading long chats: people quoting an answer, people checking what was said, people sending a chat to a colleague or keeping a record.
problems_solved: Finding a phrase in a long conversation.
Keeping tables, code and maths in a PDF or Word copy.
Printing a virtualized chat that normally only has some rows in the page.
Quoting part of an answer on a phone.
use_cases: Press Ctrl+F in a web chat, type 'invoice' and press Enter to jump between messages that mention it.
Open the chat title menu, choose Print, and get the whole chat on paper (web).
Export a chat as a Word document with tables and maths intact (web).
On the phone, choose Export as PDF and share it through the system share sheet.

journey: Find (web): 1. Press Ctrl/Cmd+F; the bar opens and focuses. 2. Type a word. 3. The label shows how many messages match and the matches are painted in the text. 4. Press Enter or the next arrow to scroll the list to the next matching message. 5. Escape or the close button clears the query.

Print (web): 1. Open the title menu, choose Print. 2. The app marks the page for print, expands the list and opens the browser print dialog. 3. After printing, the mark is removed (print-conversation.ts:1-31).

Export (web): 1. Choose 'Export…'. 2. Pick a format and options. 3. Press the export button. 4. A file downloads and a toast says 'Exported as <format>' (EnhancedExportDialog.tsx:161); on error 'Export failed. Please try again.'.

Export (mobile): 1. Open the conversation export sheet. 2. Pick PDF, Print, Text or Markdown. 3. The app writes a file in its exports folder and opens the share sheet; Print opens the system print dialog (fileCreation.ts:804-830; ConversationExportSheet.tsx:104-140).
Select (mobile): 1. Long-press or use the message action 'Select Text'. 2. Select words in the sheet.

established.statement: A reader can drag-select text continuously across paragraphs, lists and code in one answer (web, desktop, mobile, VS Code, Chrome done; CLI unverified).
Searching finds text inside an answer and highlights matching words in the rendered answer (web and desktop done; mobile, CLI, VS Code, Chrome missing).
Printing or exporting an answer or conversation keeps rendered formatting: headings, lists, tables, code, maths (web, desktop, mobile, CLI done; VS Code, Chrome missing).
An action a user cannot undo asks first; an agent never destroys user data. Export must not overwrite existing files silently.
Desktop is a real app but its chat shows the hosted web app, so web find and export reach Desktop.

acceptance_criteria: Web: Ctrl/Cmd+F opens the bar, focuses it, and Escape closes it and clears highlights.
Web: typing a word that appears 3 times in one answer paints 3 highlights and does not change the text of the message.
Web: with more than 500 matches only the first 500 are painted and the page stays responsive.
Web: Print produces every message of a long chat, not only the mounted rows; page background is white.
Web: export a chat with a table, a code block and a formula as PDF and Word; each keeps its structure.
Mobile: Export as PDF writes a file in the exports folder and opens the share sheet; a cancel leaves no error alert.
Mobile: Select Text lets the person select across the whole answer text.
CLI: /export notes.md refuses to overwrite an existing file and says so.

features.summary: Arabic and Hebrew text should read right to left, and a block the app cannot draw (a failed diagram, an unknown card or an unknown fence) should turn into readable text. Web sets one direction per message body, mobile sets it per block, and the CLI, VS Code and Chrome have no direction code. Fallbacks exist on every app.

purpose.what_it_does: Shows right-to-left languages with the right direction and alignment, and keeps unreadable or unsupported blocks visible as plain text with a way to copy the source.
purpose.why_it_exists: A reply in Arabic shown left to right is hard to read. A broken diagram or unknown card must not make the message disappear. [inferred]
purpose.who_uses_it: Readers of Arabic, Hebrew and other right-to-left languages; anyone whose answer contains a diagram or card the app cannot draw.
problems_solved: Arabic answers aligned left and reordered wrongly.
A Mermaid diagram with a syntax error leaving a blank hole.
An unknown 'x-surface' card or the literal language 'unknown' vanishing from the answer.
An unknown programming language failing to highlight.
use_cases: Ask a question in Arabic on web and read the answer right-aligned.
Mixed list on mobile where Arabic items are right-aligned and English items stay left.
A model writes a broken Mermaid diagram; the reader sees the error line, the source and a 'Copy diagram source' button.
A model writes a card of a kind the app does not know; a headline and text are shown instead.

where_to_find_it: Web and Desktop: any assistant message; the message body carries dir='auto' (apps/web/features/chat/components/messages/MessageBubble.tsx:2839, :3212).
Mobile: assistant answers, headings, paragraphs and list items (apps/mobile/src/features/chat/components/MessageContentRenderer.tsx:632-639, :1097, :1211-1253, :1338).
Diagram failure on web and desktop: inside the answer where the diagram fence was (packages/ui/unified-chat/src/components/markdown/MermaidDiagram.tsx:363-375).
Unknown card on web: a bordered section with the card headline (apps/web/features/chat/components/messages/InteractiveCardBlock.tsx:227-238).
VS Code and Chrome: unknown surfaces as a plain paragraph (assistantFence.ts:488-494).
prerequisites: No setting. Mobile app is built with native right-to-left support but does not force it (apps/mobile/__tests__/rtl-native-config.test.ts:3-18).
screens_and_controls: 'Copy diagram source' button on a failed or ready diagram; label changes to 'Source copied' or 'Copy failed' (MermaidDiagram.tsx:265-282).
'Show source' / 'Hide source' toggle on a drawn diagram (MermaidDiagram.tsx:342-344).
Failed diagram message: 'This diagram could not be drawn: <reason>. Its source is kept below.' (MermaidDiagram.tsx:366-368).
Mobile: 'This block was not finished.' under a block that never completed (MessageContentRenderer.tsx:1487-1507).
journey: 1. The answer arrives (or finishes).
2. Web: the browser picks the direction from the first strong letter of the message body; the text aligns to the start edge.
3. Mobile: each heading, paragraph and list item checks its own first strong letter and, if right-to-left, gets right alignment and reversed list rows.
4. If a diagram fails, the failed state shows the reason, a copy button and the source code.
5. If a card kind is unknown, the fallback headline and text are shown.
6. If a fence language is unknown, the code is shown plain.
feedback_and_outputs: Right-aligned text and mirrored list markers (mobile).
Status line 'This diagram could not be drawn: ...' (read as a polite status).
A plain paragraph or section instead of the missing block.
Failed diagram is reported as a client failure 'mermaid_render' (MermaidDiagram.tsx:233, :248).
settings: None found in the code. The code theme setting affects highlighting but not fallback.

working: Web/Desktop direction: the prose container has dir='auto', so the browser decides the direction of the whole message body from its first strong letter; alignment uses text-start (MessageBubble.tsx:2839, :3212). A source-string test checks this (apps/web/features/chat/components/messages/__tests__/MessageDirection.test.tsx).

Mobile direction: textDirection() returns rtl if the first strong letter is Hebrew or Arabic range (packages/ui/unified-chat/src/components/markdown/textDirection.ts:5-14); mobile applies writingDirection rtl and right alignment to headings, paragraphs and list items and reverses list rows (MessageContentRenderer.tsx:632-639, :1097, :1211-1253, :1338). Test: apps/mobile/src/features/chat/components/__tests__/MessageContentRenderer.blocks.test.tsx:558-569.

Export direction (web): PDF and Word exports use one direction for the document from the first block with strong text (textDirection.ts:59-64; export-pdf.ts:295, :383; export-docx.ts:82). Tests: textDirection.test.ts.

Diagram fallback: render errors, external-resource blocks and empty output set a failed state with reason, copy button and source (MermaidDiagram.tsx:228, :240, :249, :363-375). Streaming holds the diagram pending instead of failing (test StreamingMarkdownContent.test.tsx:252-340).

Unknown or invalid structured fence: classifyAssistantFence returns a fallback with reason 'unknown' for the language 'unknown' and for names starting with 'x-surface-', and 'invalid' for fences that fail to parse (assistantFence.ts:84, :180-182, :211-218). Web draws a paragraph with data-answer-fallback (MarkdownContent.tsx:677-678, :720-721). VS Code and Chrome do the same in HTML (assistantFence.ts:488-494; used at webview/render.ts:59-67 and markdown.ts:188-197).
Unknown card on web: SingleCard shows a section with the card's fallback headline and text when no renderer matches or the card is not recognised (InteractiveCardBlock.tsx:227-238).

Unknown programming language: code is drawn as plain text until or unless the highlighter resolves it (HighlightedCode.tsx:55 returns plain code when no lines; resolveHighlightLanguage returns null for unknown names, highlightLanguages.ts:115).

Mobile fences: an invalid closed fence shows as code, an unfinished one shows code plus 'This block was not finished.' (MessageContentRenderer.tsx:1414-1426, :1487-1507). Mobile has canRenderAssistantSurface to choose between a surface and fallback (AssistantSurface.tsx:37; MessageContentRenderer.tsx:1510).
CLI: unknown code language falls back to plain text highlighting (apps/cli/src/tui/markdown_renderer.rs:592-601).
incomplete: Web direction is one choice per message body, not per paragraph: MarkdownParagraph and list components set no direction (MarkdownContent.tsx:392-399, :790-792). A reply that starts in English and continues in Arabic is laid out left to right throughout. [inferred from the code; not run]
Web has no direction on code blocks and tables; tables use text-start/text-end classes by alignment only (MarkdownContent.tsx:540-548).
Mobile table cells default to text-align 'left' regardless of direction (MessageContentRenderer.tsx:~470-480 cellStyle, textAlign alignments[colIdx] ?? 'left').
The shared unified-chat MessageBubble has no dir attribute (rg for dir='auto' finds only the web bubble and the composer).
disconnected_or_disabled: The brief points at MessageBubble.tsx:2026 and MarkdownContent.tsx:540 for right-to-left; line 540 is table alignment, not direction; the real web hook is dir='auto' at 2839 and 3212. (doc: knowledge-base/data/area-briefs/020-markdown-and-text-rendering.md)
not_available: Right-to-left handling on CLI (markdown_renderer.rs has no direction code), VS Code (webview/render.ts has none), Chrome (side-panel markdown.ts has none found), and mobile export HTML.
Per-paragraph direction on web.

steps.what_happens: The answer text is rendered on the device. Web wraps it in an element with dir='auto'; the browser picks the direction.
Mobile calls textDirection on each heading, paragraph and list item text and adds the right-to-left style.
For each fence the app classifies the language and body; unknown or invalid gives a fallback object holding the text.
A diagram is drawn by a browser-side renderer inside a hidden host; any error sets the failed state.
Copy source writes the diagram text to the clipboard and shows 'Source copied' or 'Copy failed'.

features.summary: Each fenced code block in a reply shows its language name in a header bar and, once the reply has finished streaming, coloured code. Web and the hosted Desktop use the shared Shiki highlighter. Mobile and CLI have their own colourers. Chrome side panel has label and colours. VS Code shows neither.

purpose.what_it_does: Shows the language of a fenced code block as a small label in the block header, and colours keywords, strings and comments so code is easier to read. On web the colour theme can be chosen from six named themes.
purpose.why_it_exists: Brief items S21.01 and S21.02 require every block to name its language and be highlighted by language. It makes code in an AI answer readable and tells the reader what kind of code it is.
purpose.who_uses_it: Anyone reading a model reply that contains code: end users on Web, Desktop, Mobile, CLI and the Chrome side panel; engineers and testers who check rendering.
problems_solved: Plain monochrome code is hard to scan.
The reader cannot tell which language a snippet is without reading it.
Highlighting very large or half-streamed code can freeze the page, so limits and streaming rules protect the main thread.
use_cases: Read a Python snippet in a web chat reply with coloured keywords and a 'python' label.
Switch the code theme in web Appearance settings and see all blocks recolour.
Read a bash block in the CLI with a '┌─ bash ─' header line.
Watch a long reply stream: the last block is plain text, then turns coloured when the block ends.

where_to_find_it: Web (and Desktop, which shows the hosted web chat per AGENTS.md section 5): the header bar of every fenced code block in an assistant message. Label text comes from the fence (packages/ui/unified-chat/src/components/markdown/CodeBlock.tsx:178).

Web theme choice: Settings, Appearance section, a code theme select listing GitHub, GitHub dimmed, GitHub high contrast, Catppuccin, Dracula soft, Everforest (apps/web/features/settings/sections/AppearanceSection.tsx:246-264; labels at packages/ui/unified-chat/src/components/markdown/shikiHighlighter.ts:58-73).

steps.what_happens: The reply text is parsed as Markdown; fences become code elements with a language class.
CodeBlock lower-cases the language, draws the header, and renders HighlightedCode with enabled=false for the stream tail.
HighlightedCode checks the 32-entry cache, else loads the highlighter, the chosen theme and the language grammar through dynamic imports, tokenises, stores the result.
The loaded grammar and theme modules are fetched as bundle chunks from wherever the app is served (hosted web origin for web and Electron).

purpose.who_uses_it: Developers and other users who reuse code from replies.

A saved file needs a sensible name, such as Dockerfile for docker code.
CSV or TSV downloads could carry spreadsheet formulas that execute when opened.

features.summary: A diff block shows added lines in green and removed lines in red. Web, mobile, the CLI diff review and VS Code do this; web and mobile also have an artifact change view between versions. Marking the line an error points at is not in any app. Chrome has no diff colouring.

purpose.what_it_does: Colours lines of a suggested change: added, removed, and context. The artifact change view compares two versions of an artifact by line or word. The CLI review shows git changes per file and hunk.
purpose.why_it_exists: Brief items S21.09 to S21.11: a reader must see what a suggestion changes. The error-line item wants the line named by an error to stand out, but nothing implements it.
purpose.who_uses_it: Developers reviewing suggested changes.
problems_solved: A plain diff is hard to scan.
Versions of an artifact need a readable comparison.
use_cases: Read a diff block in web chat.
Open the changes view of an artifact on web or mobile.
Review changed files with /diff-review in the CLI.
Read a patch block in the VS Code sidebar with hunk headers.

where_to_find_it: Web and hosted Desktop: any fence labelled diff (CodeBlock.tsx:225). Artifact changes view in the artifact panel (apps/web/features/chat/components/artifacts/ArtifactPreview.tsx:3209-3217).
Mobile: diff, patch or udiff fence in the code card (CodeCard.tsx DIFF_FENCE_LANGUAGES), and the artifact changes view (apps/mobile/src/features/chat/components/ArtifactChangesView.tsx).
CLI: /diff-review overlay and /diff summary (apps/cli/src/tui/tui_app.rs:6582-6667,5902-5914).
VS Code: diff or patch fence in the webview (apps/extension-vscode/src/webview/render.ts:30-42).
Chrome: none.
prerequisites: A reply with a diff fence, or two artifact versions, or git changes for the CLI.
screens_and_controls: Web diff body: each line a row with data-diff-kind add, remove or context.
Artifact changes view: summary line such as 'No changes since version N' or counts of added and removed lines.
CLI diff review keys: Up/Down file, Left/Right hunk, y approve, n reject, s skip, d twice discard, Enter done, Esc close.
journey: Receive a reply with a diff block.
Read green added and red removed lines.
For artifacts, open the changes view to compare versions.
For the CLI, run /diff-review and decide per file or hunk.

settings: Mobile can hide plus and minus signs in diffs (useShowDiffSigns; apps/mobile/__tests__/CodeCardAppearance.test.tsx:87).

features.summary: VS Code has an Apply button on each code block that opens a proposed change in the active editor, with Accept and Reject controls and a stale-file check. The CLI has /diff-review, which stages, unstages or discards changes already on disk. Web, Desktop, Mobile and Chrome cannot apply code to files.

purpose.what_it_does: Lets the user turn a suggestion into a real file change only after reviewing it. In VS Code the block is shown as a diff against the editor and applied on Accept. In the CLI the user reviews git changes per file and hunk.
purpose.why_it_exists: Brief item S21.27: suggested code should reach the user's files, but never without review.
purpose.who_uses_it: Developers using VS Code or the CLI on their own repository.
problems_solved: Copy and paste into the right place is error prone.
Silent overwrite of edited files must be avoided.
use_cases: Click Apply on a TypeScript block while a .ts file is open; review; Accept.
Run /diff-review in the CLI, approve one file, reject another.
Press d twice in the CLI review to discard an unstaged hunk.

where_to_find_it: VS Code: 'Apply' button (label 'Apply code changes') in the code block hover actions (render.ts:36-41; webviewContent.ts:1454-1460); then CodeLens 'Accept', 'Reject', 'Accept All in File' in the editor (apps/extension-vscode/src/providers/diffDecorationProvider.ts:165-190).
CLI: /diff-review (apps/cli/src/tui/tui_app.rs:6582-6667) and /diff panel (tui_app.rs:5899-5909).
Web, Desktop, Mobile, Chrome: none.
prerequisites: VS Code: an open text editor, a diff provider available, the block's language fits the file's language, and the file is inside the folder the conversation works in (ChatStateManager.ts:2250-2272; platform/codeBlockTarget.ts:38-58).
CLI: a git repository with changes; repository config is checked first (tui_app.rs:6584-6591).
screens_and_controls: VS Code Apply button text changes to 'Opening…', then 'Review opened' or the failed label (webviewContent.ts:5490-5495,8413-8420).
A side-by-side tab titled '<file>: proposed change' opens beside the editor (diffDecorationProvider.ts:325-331).
Accept and Reject with keyboard hints Ctrl+Shift+A and Ctrl+Shift+R (diffDecorationProvider.ts:176,182).
CLI overlay keys y, n, s, arrows, d d, Enter, Esc.

feedback_and_outputs: VS Code warnings: open a file first (chatNotice.openFileForDiff), diff unavailable, language mismatch message, outside-folder message (codeBlockTarget.ts:43-52), stale-edit message on Accept (diffDecorationProvider.ts:381-385), 'Could not apply diff, document may have changed.'

settings: none found for Apply. VS Code keybindings exist for accept and reject (core/commandSetup.ts:1034-1046).

working: VS Code: Apply posts proposeDiff with code and language (webviewContent.ts:5486-5496); the extension validates, builds a session over the selection or the cursor point, shows the diff and posts diffProposed or diffProposalFailed (ChatStateManager.ts:2250-2292). When the selection is empty, the block is proposed as an insertion at the cursor, not a whole-file replacement (ChatStateManager.ts:2275-2277).

VS Code: acceptDiff refuses if the text changed since the proposal and otherwise applies a WorkspaceEdit replace (diffDecorationProvider.ts:375-398). Reject stashes the session and removes it (diffDecorationProvider.ts:400-405).
VS Code: a second Apply while one is pending marks the earlier one failed with 'newerDiffReplaced' (webviewContent.ts:5486-5489).

CLI: the review overlay stages approved files and hunks, unstages rejected ones, and discards an unstaged hunk only after a second d press (diff_review.rs:1-9,878-905; tui_app.rs:1298-1381). Skipped files are untouched (tui_app.rs:1381 comment).
incomplete: The CLI /diff-review reviews changes already written to disk by tools or the user; it does not take a code block from the reply and write it. So the brief's CLI 'apply suggested code' is met only as review of existing changes. [inferred from tui_app.rs:6582-6667]
VS Code Accept applies the edit to the editor document; saving the file is a separate step not performed by this code [inferred].

features.summary: Lets a person ask the assistant to run code instead of only writing it. Web has a Run code toggle and a /code command. Mobile has a Run code row in Add to chat. The cloud runs the code in a sandbox, subject to the plan and a settings switch. CLI and VS Code run code through the agent's shell tool with approvals.

purpose.what_it_does: Web composer: the Run code toggle and the /code command switch on code execution for the next message (apps/web/features/chat/components/Composer/ChatComposerNew.tsx:2565, :3247-3263). Mobile: a Run code row in the Add to chat sheet (apps/mobile/src/features/chat/components/AddToChatSheet.tsx:1242-1252). The server then gives the model an execute_code tool that runs in a managed sandbox, or the provider's own code tool (apps/web/lib/e2b/execution-tools.ts:258-269). The tool takes only language and code (apps/web/lib/e2b/execution-tools.ts:80-83). CLI and VS Code run commands through the agent's shell tool and ask for approval first (apps/cli/src/tui/approval_broker.rs:23-26; apps/extension-vscode/src/features/sidebar-webview/webviewContent.ts:8867-8872).
purpose.why_it_exists: Claude and ChatGPT can run the code they write. A person gets a checked answer, a chart or a file instead of code they must run themselves. [inferred]
purpose.who_uses_it: Signed-in web and mobile users on a plan with sandbox allowance; developers using CLI or VS Code with their own machine.
problems_solved: The assistant can compute and test instead of guessing.
The person does not need a local runtime to try code.
The person can say no: a settings switch turns cloud running off (apps/web/lib/server/code-execution-policy.ts:24-37).
use_cases: Ask for a data summary and have the assistant run the analysis.
Type /code and a question to force a run.
On the AGI Code page, start a cloud coding session and pick the Coding harness.
In the CLI, approve a shell command the agent wants to run.

established.statement: The user can have code run (sandbox or local) from the chat and see it execute.
Where multiple runtimes exist, the user can choose the runtime or language.
Before running, the user can supply input parameters or stdin.
Before or when code runs, the user is told what permission it needs and what it can touch and why.
If the requested runtime or execution is unavailable, the UI says so clearly instead of failing silently.
Capabilities settings must include code execution, file creation, network egress and a domain allow list.
Sandboxed code execution is treated as read-only in the permissive approval mode; the leaders accept that risk.

acceptance_criteria: With Run code on and a capable model, the sent request carries code_execution true.
With a model that cannot run code, the web toggle is disabled and its title explains why; /code shows the notice.
With the account switch off, a run is refused and the assistant tells the user it can be turned on in Settings, Capabilities.
With no sandbox configured, the assistant states that code execution is not configured and does not retry.
A free-plan run states its lifetime in minutes.
Mobile shows the Run code row only in cloud mode with the capability granted.
No app shows an input or stdin field today (documents the gap).
inferred: Local and own-key chats must not silently route code to the managed sandbox (doc: AGENTS.md section 6) [inferred]; the code agrees: BYOK and local-only plans have zero sandboxes.
proposed: [proposed] Show a visible reason on mobile and on the web toggle auto-off (a short notice when a model change switches Run code off).
[proposed] Add an optional input/stdin field to the execute_code tool and the composer.
[proposed] Show a one-line permission summary (network reach, file area, lifetime) the first time code runs in a chat.

steps.what_happens: Person switches on Run code and sends. The send includes code_execution.
Server decides: managed sandbox tools if provisioned, else the provider's own code tool for the routed provider, else nothing (turn is told to disclose).
Server checks the account switch, plan sandbox count and lifetime, and managed compute access; a failed plan lookup refuses.
The sandbox service starts a sandbox and runs the code. Outbound network is limited to GitHub, npm and PyPI hosts for chat runs.
Output returns to the model and the client; the page shows it (F021-08).
CLI and VS Code: the agent proposes a shell command, the person approves, and it runs on the person's own machine.

access_and_usage.account: Web, mobile: sign-in needed; the server resolves the user's entitlement (code-runs/route.ts:86-93). CLI and VS Code local shell: no account needed for local commands [inferred].
access_and_usage.permissions: Account switch Cloud code execution and file creation (default on) (code-execution-policy.ts:24-37). Tool approval policy ask_every_time forces approval for reruns (route.ts:116-128). CLI and VS Code per-command approval.
access_and_usage.subscription: Capability canUseCloudExecution gates the web composer (ChatComposerNew.tsx:1630-1631) and mobile (AddToChatSheet.tsx:255). Sandbox slots per plan: local-only 0, byok 0, free 2 with a 60-minute lifetime, basic 5, pro 10, team 10 (billing-catalog.ts:583-699); the max plan and enterprise use the 20-per-user ceiling (billing-catalog.ts:473, :569, :720).
access_and_usage.limits_and_metering: Sandbox compute is reserved and metered per second against credits for paid plans; Free uses a platform-funded daily allowance (runtime.ts:117-127; apps/web/lib/e2b/compute-metering.ts). Rerun route function limit 300 seconds (code-runs/route.ts:46; chat-code-runs.ts:6).
access_and_usage.flags: AGI_E2B_EXECUTION=1 and E2B_API_KEY (gate.ts:6-28); AGI_MANAGED_COMPUTE_PRIVATE_BETA (gate.ts:30-37; brief S21.21); capability canUseCloudExecution checked by assertCapabilityAvailable (route.ts:94-104); mobile flag FEATURES.codeExecution (apps/mobile/lib/v1FeatureFlags.ts:34); desktop managed flag code_execution (DesktopCloudSettingsModal.tsx:566).
access_and_usage.model_compatibility: Needs registry capability codeExecution, or tools plus the deployment capability, or Auto (ChatComposerNew.tsx:1638-1642). Mobile needs capabilities.codeExecution true (ChatInput.tsx:582).
access_and_usage.provider_restrictions: Native provider code tools exist only for provider:anthropic, provider:google, provider:openai (execution-tools.ts:211-232). The managed sandbox accepts any non-empty provider name (execution-tools.ts:207-209).
access_and_usage.local_mode: Mobile Local mode: Run code is not offered (cloud mode required) (AddToChatSheet.tsx:249-255; ChatInput.tsx:577). Own key: plans byok and local-only have maxSandboxes 0 (billing-catalog.ts:583-608); runtime.ts:122-124 states Local and BYOK stay outside managed sandbox provisioning. Whether a provider's own hosted code tool works with an own key: unknown. CLI and VS Code run on the device.

CLI and VS Code stop the response in progress (apps/cli/src/tui/tui_app.rs:8441-8449; apps/extension-vscode/src/features/sidebar-webview/webviewContent.ts:5865-5871).
purpose.why_it_exists: Re-running a script after a fix or a hiccup should not need a new chat message; a runaway run needs an exit. [inferred]
purpose.who_uses_it: Mobile users who want to rerun code; CLI and VS Code users who want to interrupt an agent.
problems_solved: Re-run without retyping.
Stop long waits.
Ask before running again when approvals are strict.
use_cases: Tap Run again after the first output looked wrong.
Stop a rerun that takes too long.
Press Esc in the CLI to cancel an agent turn.
Click Stop response in VS Code.

where_to_find_it: Mobile: a Run again button under a finished code step in the agent activity timeline and tool call rows, only in cloud mode with the capability granted (apps/mobile/src/features/chat/components/AgentActivityTimeline.tsx:389-394, :554-562; ToolCallTimeline.tsx tool row; CodeRunAgain.tsx:95).
CLI: Esc or Ctrl-C while a turn runs (apps/cli/src/tui/tui_app.rs:8441-8449).
VS Code: the Stop response button in the composer; Escape also stops when the setting allows (webviewContent.ts:3365, :5865-5871, :5939-5941).
Web: no rerun or stop control in the Code Execution panel (apps/web/features/chat/components/messages/CodeExecutionBlock.tsx). The chat composer's general stop for a turn was not read.
Chrome: shows a Stopping status line for a response stop (apps/extension/src/features/side-panel/bubbles.ts:651-657); no run-level control.
prerequisites: Mobile: cloud mode, canUseCloudExecution granted, a conversation id, a finished step whose tool is execute_code with code text (AgentActivityTimeline.tsx:389-394; apps/mobile/src/features/chat/utils/executedToolCode.ts:42-44).
screens_and_controls: Run again button, accessibility label Run this code again (CodeRunAgain.tsx:132-142).
Stop button, accessibility label Stop the run, plus a Running indicator (CodeRunAgain.tsx:118-130).
Confirmation alert titled Run this code again? with buttons Cancel and Run again (packages/contracts/cloud-contracts/src/chat-code-runs.ts:11-16; CodeRunAgain.tsx:82-87).
journey: 1. Mobile: tap Run again.
2. If approvals are set to ask every time, or the setting is not loaded, an alert asks first (CodeRunAgain.tsx:40, :90-93).
3. The app posts the code to the server (apps/mobile/src/features/chat/services/codeRun.ts:35-48).
4. A Stop button replaces Run again while running.
5. Output, Error and plots appear under the step (CodeRunAgain.tsx:153-201).
6. A timeout shows the took-too-long text; other failures show the did-not-run text.
feedback_and_outputs: Took too long: This run took too long to answer, so the app stopped waiting. It may still finish on the server. (CodeRunAgain.tsx:20-21).
Failure: The code did not run. Try again. (codeRun.ts:10).
Server messages such as Running code is turned off for this account. Turn it on in Settings, Capabilities. (apps/web/app/api/chat/conversations/[id]/code-runs/route.ts:109-112).
Approval prompt message: Your approvals are set to ask before every action. The code runs again in this chat's cloud sandbox and can change the files there. (chat-code-runs.ts:13-15).
settings: Tool approvals policy (ask every time) (route.ts:116-128; mobile hook useToolApprovalPolicySync).

working: Mobile Run again with approval prompt, stop, timeout text, failure text, output, error and plots (CodeRunAgain.tsx).
Server route checks ownership, capability, account switch, approval, managed compute, then runs and records audit events (route.ts:76-199).

Server run honours the request's abort signal and answers with CODE_RUN_STOPPED_MESSAGE; the message warns that stopping restarts the code session and earlier variables are gone (apps/web/lib/e2b/types.ts:118-119; runtime.ts:1179, :1214-1222, :1256).
CLI cancel: Esc or Ctrl-C breaks the wait, cancels the in-flight stream and records the turn as cancelled (tui_app.rs:8441-8449, :8714-8722).
VS Code Stop response sends a cancel message and shows Stopping (webviewContent.ts:5865-5871).
incomplete: CLI and VS Code stops cancel the whole turn; no per-run stop was found (tui_app.rs:8441; webviewContent.ts:5870).

Mobile Stop aborts the app's wait; the copy admits the server may still finish (CodeRunAgain.tsx:20-21). The server passes the request signal to runCode (route.ts:184), so an abort should reach it [inferred].
The web server has a rerun endpoint but no web client caller was found.
Rerun is limited to the execute_code tool name (executedToolCode.ts:42-44).
disconnected_or_disabled: Web: POST code-runs exists with a test but nothing in apps/web calls it (search of apps and packages).
not_available: Reset runtime: no control in any app found. The nearest behaviour is that stopping a run restarts the code session (types.ts:118-119) and a deleted conversation releases its sandbox (runtime.ts:15-18).
VS Code retry and reset claimed by the brief: the cited lines (webviewContent.ts:3722, :2510) are not about code runs; not confirmed.
Chrome: none.

established.statement: A failed or finished execution can be re-run in place.
A running execution can be stopped by the user.
The user can reset the execution runtime or state.
When approvals ask before every action, the rerun must ask first and name the consequence.
An action a user cannot undo asks first and names the consequence.

acceptance_criteria: Mobile Run again shows only in cloud mode with the capability granted and a finished code step.
With approvals set to ask, tapping Run again shows the alert before any request; Cancel sends nothing.
While running, Stop replaces Run again; tapping it stops the wait without an error message.
A request that exceeds the wait shows the took-too-long text.
The server returns 409 approval_required when approval is needed and not given.
The server refuses a rerun for a conversation the caller does not own (404).
CLI: Esc during a turn returns control with the partial reply kept.
inferred: Stopping a run should say it restarts the session (the server message does) [inferred requirement from types.ts:118].
proposed: [proposed] Add Run again to the web Code Execution panel using the existing endpoint.
[proposed] Add a Reset code session control with a confirmation naming lost variables.
[proposed] Stop one run without cancelling the whole CLI or VS Code turn.

steps.what_happens: Person taps Run again; the app may show an approval alert first.
The app posts language and code (and approved true when approved) to the code-runs endpoint, waiting up to 300 seconds.
The server checks ownership, the capability, the account switch, the approval policy and managed compute access, then gets the conversation sandbox.
The code runs in the sandbox; output and PNG results return; audit events record only names, never code or output.

features.summary: Reading aids for long code. Web chat code blocks have no line numbers, wrap switch or collapse; they scroll in a capped box, with an Expand code dialog. Mobile has more than the brief says: a Wrap long lines setting, Show more and Show less on blocks over 20 lines, and line numbers in the full-screen source viewer.

features.summary: Shows where an answer's facts came from. A small chip in the text names the source site and opens it. On Web, Desktop and Chrome a preview card shows title, site and dates before opening; on Mobile a tap shows an alert first. A Sources control lists every result. CLI has no chips; VS Code has a plain list.

purpose.what_it_does: Turns source references in an answer (marker numbers such as [1], or links to cited pages) into chips with the site name, groups adjacent markers into one chip with a count, shows a preview of each source, and lists all sources of the turn under the answer.
purpose.why_it_exists: A person must be able to check a claim. Chat answers built on web search are only trustworthy if each fact points to a page the person can open. The brief requires chips, previews and result lists on every app (S22.01, S22.02, S22.03).
purpose.who_uses_it: Anyone who asks a question that triggers web search or provider-native grounding, on Web, Desktop (Electron shows the hosted web app), Mobile and the Chrome side panel; VS Code users get a basic sources list.
problems_solved: Claims without a way to verify them.
Several sources at one sentence cluttering the text (grouped into one chip).
Grounded results whose link host is a routing vendor, so every source looked the same (publisher domain is read from the title instead).
Losing the full result set when only a few sources are cited (Citations and More sections).
use_cases: Ask a current-events question, read the answer and hover a chip to see the page title and snippet before opening it.
On a phone, tap a [n] marker, read the alert with site, date and snippet, then choose Open page.
Open the Sources control to see every page the search returned, cited ones first.
In the Chrome side panel, tap a chip on a touch screen to open the card first, then follow the link.

where_to_find_it: Web and Desktop (Electron hosted web app): inline chips in the answer text and a pill labelled 'Sources' (with a count above 3) under the answer, which opens the right-hand 'Research panel' with headings 'Citations' and 'More' (apps/web/features/chat/components/research/ResearchPanel.tsx:505, :517, :604; apps/web/features/chat/components/messages/MessageBubble.tsx:3595).

Mobile: inline [n] citations in assistant text, and a pill 'Sources' (or 'Sources so far' while the turn is unfinished) that opens a page sheet with headings 'Citations' and 'More' (apps/mobile/src/features/chat/components/CollapsibleSources.tsx:160).
Chrome side panel: chip inside the answer plus a collapsible sources footer (details element) (apps/extension/src/features/side-panel/sources.ts:136).
VS Code: a collapsible list under the answer, summary from the localised 'sources' string (apps/extension-vscode/src/features/sidebar-webview/webviewContent.ts:4755). No chips.
CLI: none. Links print as 'text (url)' (apps/cli/src/tui/markdown_renderer.rs:265-281).
prerequisites: The turn used a search or grounding route that produced sources. Web search is a Cloud (managed) tool; see access_and_usage.
Signed in for Cloud chat on the app [inferred from web search being a server tool-loop tool].
screens_and_controls: Chip: pill with favicon (or globe icon), site name and '+N' for extra sources; it is a link that opens in a new tab with rel noopener noreferrer (packages/ui/unified-chat/src/components/markdown/CitationChip.tsx:145-150).
Hover or keyboard-focus card (Web/Desktop): per source title, host, published date, retrieved date, snippet (CitationChip.tsx:80-122).
Mobile chip: tap shows an alert with title, site, 'Published ...', retrieved label and snippet, buttons 'Cancel' and 'Open page' (apps/mobile/src/features/chat/components/CitationChip.tsx:42-50).
Sources pill and panel or sheet: favicon stack or first-letter marks, query line, 'Citations' and 'More' sections, Close button.
Chrome chip: hover/focus card, Escape closes, a touch pointerdown opens the card and suppresses the first click (apps/extension/src/features/side-panel/sources.ts:64-69).
journey: Person sends a question that needs current facts.
The server runs web search (up to 3 calls per turn, up to 5 results each) and streams the sources with the answer.
The answer text carries citation markers; the app turns them into chips.
Person hovers, focuses or taps a chip and reads the preview.
Person opens the page (new tab on Web, Desktop and Chrome; in-app browser on Mobile) or opens the Sources control to see every result.

steps.what_happens: Person asks a question; the client asks for streaming chat and Web search may be on.
Server offers the web_search tool to a tool-capable model and runs the tool loop; at most 3 searches of 5 results per turn.
Search request goes to the registered search provider over HTTPS with one retry on 429 or 5xx.
Search budget is checked first: Free plan gets a rolling count cap, paid plans and automated surfaces are charged to managed credits.
Sources and answer stream back; the client builds chips and the Sources list from them.
Web and Desktop chips draw favicons from a third-party favicon address unless the source carries one.
Opening a chip opens the page in a new tab (web, Chrome) or the in-app browser (mobile).

data.synced: Mobile has a sync helper (messageSources.ts:224); web is server stored. Exact sync path unknown

execution_and_data_flow.models_and_providers: Search is a server tool, so any tool-capable model can call it. Provider-native grounding from some model providers also yields sources (packages/ai/providers/google/src/__tests__/grounding-sources.test.ts exists; openai citation markup tests exist). The search vendor is registered in web-search-providers.json, not tied to the chat model.

access_and_usage.account: Web search runs in Cloud chat, which needs a signed-in account [inferred]. Chips themselves need no account once the sources are in the message.
access_and_usage.permissions: No extra person permission found. Mobile opens links only if they are valid external http(s) URLs (sourceDisplay.ts:20).
access_and_usage.subscription: Free plan: 20 search calls per rolling 30 days (apps/web/lib/web-search/search-budget.ts:32-33). Paid plans: calls charged to managed credits (search-budget.ts:107-115). Result count is 5 for both (web-search-tool.ts:54-55).
access_and_usage.limits_and_metering: 3 calls per turn, 10 for AGI Work turns, query length 400 (web-search-tool.ts:56-58). Calls are metered under rate card features web_search_perplexity and web_search_grounding (search-budget.ts:36-39).
access_and_usage.flags: The search backend needs its provider key to be configured; without it the tool reports not_configured and the model is told not to retry (web-search-tool.ts:185-210).
access_and_usage.model_compatibility: Needs a tool-capable model for the search tool [inferred from the toolsCapable gating pattern in request-processor.ts:1357-1425]; provider-native grounding is a separate route.
access_and_usage.provider_restrictions: Single search provider entry in the repo (web-search-providers.json:4-8).
access_and_usage.local_mode: Not established. Mobile Local Mode and CLI web search paths for chips were not found; the cloud tool loop is where search is wired. Local chat sources exist in retained Tauri desktop code (TauriRuntime.ts:1115) but that is internal. Chips on already-stored sources need no network except favicons on Web.
