features.summary: Charts in answers draw as bar, line, pie, donut or scatter charts that show values on hover or tap. A data table sits under the chart, and Web offers a PNG download. Built on Web, Desktop and Mobile; CLI, VS Code and Chrome have no chart drawing.

purpose.what_it_does: Draws a chart from structured data in an answer, lets the person read exact values and inspect the underlying numbers in a table, and exports the picture.
purpose.why_it_exists: Numbers are easier to understand as charts, and a person must be able to check the data behind a picture. The brief requires interactive charts (S22.08) and inspectable data (S22.09). The requirements list 'Charts and inline visualizations' among outputs.
purpose.who_uses_it: Web, Desktop (Electron hosted web) and Mobile users who ask for analysis, comparisons or reports.
problems_solved: Reading values off a static picture.
A chart that cannot be checked against data.
A chart failing silently (error fallback and data table remain).
use_cases: Ask for a bar chart of monthly sales and hover a bar for its value.
Open 'View chart data' to copy numbers.
Download the chart as a PNG for a slide.
Read a chart in a report on Mobile and scrub across points.

features.summary: Location answers show a map with numbered pins and a list; place answers show cards with rating, address, hours and links. Web and Mobile (Cloud only) and Chrome (map only) draw maps. Real place data needs a places key, and the map tile provider is still a public development default.

purpose.what_it_does: Draws a tile map with markers for places in an answer, lists each stop with a link to open it in a maps service, and shows rich place cards (name, rating, address, hours, phone, website, photos) from a places search.
purpose.why_it_exists: Location questions are answered best by a map and real data. The brief requires interactive maps (S22.10) and place cards (S22.11). The places tool is built so the model does not answer from memory.
purpose.who_uses_it: Web and Desktop (Electron hosted web), Mobile Cloud users and Chrome side panel users.
problems_solved: Model inventing ratings or opening hours (the tool is required for place questions and says so when unavailable).
Opening unsafe links (only allowed map provider URLs open).
Maps that swallow page scrolling (wheel zoom is off).
use_cases: Ask 'coffee near Union Square', see rated places and a map.
Ask for a map of a few landmarks and open one in Maps.
Open a place popup for address, hours and website.

Server offers search_places only if the key exists and the question needs places; offers search_maps on map intent for web, mobile and chrome.
Places search runs against the places vendor; the call is billed and refused when credits are short.

Tile route fetches from the configured tile vendor.

execution_and_data_flow.models_and_providers: Tools need a tool-capable model on a streaming turn (request-processor.ts:1391-1401). The places vendor is Google Places; the tile vendor is configurable. Neither is a chat model provider.

access_and_usage.account: Tile route calls getClerkAuthUser; Mobile needs a signed-in bearer to load tiles (mapTiles.ts:36-60). Whether the web tile route rejects anonymous requests was not traced.
access_and_usage.permissions: search_places is a read tool, auto-allowed in read-only mode (apps/web/app/api/llm/v1/chat/completions/lib/tool-metadata.ts:138-144).
access_and_usage.subscription: Places search is charged per call at a rate card price and refused with 'no credits left' text when unaffordable (places-tool.ts:110-113,147-157). Plan-specific allowance: unknown.
access_and_usage.limits_and_metering: Places limit 1-10, default 5 (packages/contracts/types/src/places-search.ts:16-18); map pins up to 10 in answer-ui (answer-ui.ts:19); tile zoom floor 2, ceiling 22 (map-tile-provider.ts:30-31).
access_and_usage.flags: GOOGLE_PLACES_API_KEY set or not; AGI_MAP_TILE_URL_TEMPLATE set or not.
access_and_usage.provider_restrictions: One places vendor; the tile vendor must support {z}/{x}/{y} and https.
access_and_usage.local_mode: Map and place cards come from the Cloud tool loop, so they do not appear in Local chat [inferred]. Mobile explicitly blocks tiles outside Managed Cloud (MessageBubble.tsx:2462; mapTiles.ts:24).

features.summary: Product comparison and itinerary cards are built and connected, with more reach than the brief says. Web, Desktop, Mobile and Chrome show both; prices appear only when sourced, and availability is not shown. A text-based 'View as comparison' toggle also exists on Web. Reservation choices and calendar grids are not built.

purpose.what_it_does: Product comparison puts two to four products side by side with price, store, buy link and spec rows. The itinerary card shows trip stops with times, notes, a map and direction links. A separate Web toggle turns a prose comparison into a card.
purpose.why_it_exists: Choosing what to buy or planning a day is easier in structured form. The brief lists comparison (S22.17), price and availability (S22.18), itinerary (S22.19), reservation choices (S22.22) and calendar grids (S22.23).

features.summary: When the assistant writes an email, a card shows To, Subject and body with Edit, Copy and Open-in-mail actions. Other drafts (chat message, post, document, snippet) show as a plain draft card with copy. Contact cards and task or issue cards do not exist. No action sends a message directly.

purpose.what_it_does: Turns an assistant reply that contains an email fence (a code block labelled email) into an editable email card with To, Cc, Bcc, Subject and body. Other writing fences (message, post, document, snippet, writing) become a labelled draft card. An email-type artifact opens in the artifact panel as a read-only email preview with a Copy button. (packages/ui/unified-chat/src/components/markdown/assistantFence.ts:219-241; packages/ui/unified-chat/src/components/artifact-components/EmailArtifact.tsx:81-167)
purpose.why_it_exists: The brief says an email draft should read as an email, not as a code block, and should offer copy, send and open actions (S22.25). Message drafts (S22.26) and contact and task cards (S22.24, S22.27) are listed as the same kind of widget. (doc: knowledge-base/data/area-briefs/022-rich-answers-and-structured-result-widgets.md)
purpose.who_uses_it: Any signed-in person who asks the assistant to write an email or a message on web, desktop (which shows the hosted web app), mobile, VS Code and Chrome. [inferred from shared fence pipeline]
problems_solved: A draft email no longer has to be copied out of a code block and reformatted.
A long email can be handed to the mail app even when it is too long for a mail link (the body is copied instead).
A person can fix a word in the draft before using it, and can save the edit back into the chat message when the chat allows it.
use_cases: Ask 'write an email to my landlord about the leak', read the card, press Copy email, paste into a mail client.
Press Open in mail app to start a new mail with To and Subject filled in.
Ask for a chat message reply, get a 'Chat message' card, copy it.
Open an email artifact in the artifact panel and copy it as text.

where_to_find_it: Web and Desktop (hosted web app): inside an assistant reply in chat; card header reads 'Email'; actions 'Edit', 'Copy email', 'Open in mail app' (packages/ui/unified-chat/src/components/markdown/EmailBlock.tsx:113-116). Email-type artifacts open in the artifact panel (apps/web/features/chat/components/artifacts/ArtifactPreview.tsx:1812,1981).

Mobile: inside an assistant reply; card titled 'Email' with actions 'Copy email', 'Edit', 'Open in Mail' (apps/mobile/src/features/chat/components/DraftSurfaces.tsx:413-459). Other drafts show their label with Copy and Share (DraftSurfaces.tsx:154,611-700).

VS Code and Chrome: the reply renders an 'Email' section with a 'Copy email' button only; writing drafts have an editable text area and 'Copy draft' in VS Code (packages/ui/unified-chat/src/components/markdown/assistantFence.ts:515-535; apps/extension-vscode/src/webview/render.ts:60-70; apps/extension/src/features/side-panel/markdown.ts:191).
CLI: none found; no email fence handling in the CLI markdown renderer (apps/cli/src/tui/markdown_renderer.rs searched for email).
prerequisites: A reply where the model wrote an email fence. A finished email block needs a recipient or a subject, and a body; otherwise it falls back to ordinary text (packages/ui/unified-chat/src/components/markdown/richBlocks.ts:122-152).
Edits can be saved only where the chat provides an edit handler; otherwise the card says 'Edits are temporary in this view.' (EmailBlock.tsx:267).
screens_and_controls: Email card: To, Cc, Bcc (only if present or after Edit), Subject, body text area; buttons Edit, Copy email, Open in mail app; when edited: 'Save changes', 'Cancel' (EmailBlock.tsx:96-118,255-290).
Cancel with unsaved changes asks 'Discard unsaved changes?' with 'Discard changes' and 'Keep editing' (EmailBlock.tsx:276-286).
Email artifact preview: subject heading, recipient rows, Copy button, body rendered as markdown (EmailArtifact.tsx:100-167).
journey: Ask the assistant to draft an email.
While the reply streams, the card shows the fields read-only and hides the action buttons (EmailBlock.tsx:120,205).
When the reply ends, Edit, Copy email and Open in mail app appear.
Optionally press Edit, change the fields, press Save changes (or Cancel and confirm discard).
Press Copy email to put 'To:/Cc:/Bcc:/Subject:' lines and the body on the clipboard, or Open in mail app to open a mailto link.
feedback_and_outputs: Copy button label changes to 'Email copied' or 'Copy failed, clipboard unavailable' (EmailBlock.tsx:109-114).

If the mail link would exceed 2000 characters, the body is copied and the mail app opens without it; the card says 'This message is too long for a mail link, so it was copied. Paste it into the new email.' (richBlocks.ts:176-200; EmailBlock.tsx:90-103,160-180).
If saving fails: 'Changes could not be saved. Your draft is kept here; try again.' (EmailBlock.tsx:155-160).
Mobile shows an alert 'Could not open Mail' when the link cannot be opened (DraftSurfaces.tsx:385-391).
settings: None found in the code for the draft widgets themselves.
Text strings go through the shared UI translation keys such as richBlock.copyEmail (EmailBlock.tsx:113).

working: Email fence parsing and card on web/desktop: parseEmailBlock accepts To, Cc, Bcc, Subject headers, then a blank line and body (richBlocks.ts:122-152); MarkdownContent renders EmailBlock (MarkdownContent.tsx:640-642).
Copy, Edit, Open in mail app with a 2000-character mailto cap (richBlocks.ts:176-200; EmailBlock.tsx:92-103).

Mobile email draft surface with Copy email, Edit, Open in Mail and save-back (apps/mobile/src/features/chat/components/DraftSurfaces.tsx:340-460; AssistantSurface.tsx:589-650). The brief lists no mobile status for S22.25 but the code exists.

Writing drafts (message, document, post, snippet, writing) on web as WritingBlock, on mobile as WritingDraftSurface (assistantFence.ts:233-241; MarkdownContent.tsx:665-689; DraftSurfaces.tsx:611). The brief says message drafts are missing on every app (S22.26); the code contradicts it for the card with copy.

VS Code and Chrome render an email section with Copy email and writing sections through the shared classifier (assistantFence.ts:515-535; render.ts:60-70; markdown.ts:191). The brief says missing for these apps; the code contradicts it for a copy-only card.
Email artifact type in the artifact panel with Copy (ArtifactPreview.tsx:1812,1981; EmailArtifact.tsx:81-167).
incomplete: No Send action on any app: the widget offers copy and open-in-mail only (EmailBlock.tsx:123-158; DraftSurfaces.tsx:448-459). The brief asks for 'copy/send/open'.
Message draft has copy (and share on mobile) but no send to chat, SMS or Slack (WritingBlock.tsx:30-60; DraftSurfaces.tsx:154).
VS Code and Chrome email cards cannot open a mail app or edit the fields (assistantFence.ts:515-516).
disconnected_or_disabled: EmailArtifact (artifact panel) is separate from EmailBlock (chat fence); it has no Edit or Open-in-mail action (EmailArtifact.tsx:100-167). Whether the model produces email-type artifacts in practice is unknown.
not_available: Contact cards (S22.24): no contact card kind in the fence classifier or the interactive card registry (assistantFence.ts:82-141; InteractiveCardBlock.tsx:38-51). Missing on all six apps.
Task and issue cards (S22.27): no such card kind found. Missing on all six apps.
Email draft widget on CLI: none found.

established.statement: An email draft renders as an email widget (to, subject, body) with copy/send/open actions.
A chat/SMS/Slack message draft renders as a message widget with copy/send.
Person/contact answers render a contact card (name, role, email/phone actions).
Tasks/issues (e.g. Linear, GitHub, Jira) render as task/issue cards with status and link.
An action a user cannot undo asks first and names the consequence; a mutation fired straight from onClick is a defect.

acceptance_criteria: An assistant reply with an email fence containing To, Subject and body shows an Email card on web, mobile, VS Code and Chrome.
On web and mobile, Copy email puts To/Subject lines and the body on the clipboard.
On web and mobile, Open in mail app builds a mailto link; for a body that makes the link longer than 2000 characters the body is copied and the notice is shown.
While the reply is still streaming the fields are read-only and the action buttons are hidden on web.
Edit then Cancel with changes asks to confirm discard.
An email fence without recipient/subject or without body renders as ordinary text.
Contact, message-send and task cards: absent today; a tester records them as not built.
inferred: Direct send needs an account connection (mail or chat connector) and an approval step, so it must go through the tool approval system. [inferred from AGENTS.md section 9 and the connector system]
VS Code and Chrome cards should offer the same copy behaviour; open-in-mail is not required there. [inferred]
proposed: [proposed] Add a Send action that calls a connected mail connector after an approval card; keep Copy and Open as fallbacks.
[proposed] Add contact and task card kinds to the interactive card registry (packages/contracts/types/src/interactive-cards.ts) so every app renders them or falls back to text.

features.summary: When the assistant needs permission for an action, an approval card shows what it will do, a risk label and the parameters, with Allow and Deny choices. When it needs facts from you, a question card lets you pick options or type an answer and send. Each app has its own version.

purpose.what_it_does: Approval cards stop a tool call until the person allows or denies it (once, for this chat, or always where the scope is offered). Question cards (clarify.v1) show up to four questions with up to four options each and an optional 'something else' box; the answers go back to the assistant as the next turn input. (apps/web/features/chat/components/approvals/ToolApprovalCard.tsx:57-140; apps/web/lib/services/clarify-tool-service.ts:12-16; apps/web/features/chat/components/messages/cards/ClarifyCard.tsx:86-229)
purpose.why_it_exists: Consent must be explicit before an action that changes things, and a vague request is better answered with a few structured questions than with a guess. (doc: AGENTS.md section 9; area brief S22.28, S22.29)
purpose.who_uses_it: Anyone using an agent that calls tools (all six apps) and anyone whose request is vague (web, desktop, mobile, Chrome, VS Code; CLI shows tool-server questions).
problems_solved: The person sees the tool name, risk tier, destructive notice and parameters before saying yes.
The assistant does not guess missing details; it asks.
A tool server can ask for typed input (CLI elicitation) without leaving the terminal.
use_cases: A cloud tool wants to send data to a connector; the card shows the parameters and the person presses Allow once.
A vague request 'plan my trip' triggers a card with questions about dates and budget; the person picks options and presses Send answers.
In the CLI, a command run asks 'Apply this patch?' with y/n keys.
An MCP server asks for a token; the CLI overlay shows a masked field with Accept, Decline, Cancel.

where_to_find_it: Web and Desktop (hosted web app): approval card is a section labelled 'Approve <tool>' with buttons from the scope labels (Allow once, Allow for this chat, Always allow) and 'Deny' (apps/web/features/chat/components/approvals/ToolApprovalCard.tsx:79-140; packages/contracts/types/src/tool-approval-policy.ts:23-36). Question card is a card in the reply with buttons 'Send answers' and 'I'll just type it' (ClarifyCard.tsx:195-216).

Mobile: approval controls with 'Raw JSON' toggle, guidance field and decision buttons (apps/mobile/src/features/chat/components/CloudToolApprovalControls.tsx:260-410). Question card with 'Send answers' and 'I'll just type it' (apps/mobile/src/features/chat/components/ClarifyCard.tsx).

CLI: full-screen approval overlay titled 'Tool Approval' with keys y, n, s, a, d, t and Tab to add a note; MCP request overlay with Accept, Decline, Cancel (apps/cli/src/tui/widgets/approval_overlay.rs:1-30; elicitation_overlay.rs:1-25,375).

screens_and_controls: Web approval: label, risk badge (Low/Medium/High/Critical risk), destructive notice, parameter list, 'Raw JSON' details, decision group (ToolApprovalCard.tsx:79-140; packages/contracts/cloud-contracts/src/tool-approval-presentation.ts:16-23).

steps.what_happens: The model calls the clarify tool or a tool needing approval; the server builds a card and streams it with the reply.
The app validates the card, shows it, and blocks sending while streaming or in a temporary chat.
The person's answer is posted to the respond route, which checks the card and updates the stored message.
The paused turn resumes with the answer.
CLI approval and elicitation are answered on the device and returned to the local agent loop or MCP server.

features.summary: A study answer can include flip-style flashcards and an interactive quiz. Web shows them in the artifact panel with answer checking, hints, retake and print. Mobile shows them inline in chat and in the artifact viewer. The brief says missing everywhere, but the code builds both on web and mobile.

purpose.what_it_does: Reads quiz and flashcards blocks (JSON inside a quiz or flashcards fence) from a markdown document and shows them as an interactive quiz and flip cards. The quiz checks multiple-choice and short answers, shows hints and explanations, scores, and can ask the assistant to explain missed questions. (packages/ui/unified-chat/src/lib/study-set.ts:1-60,238-360; apps/web/features/chat/components/artifacts/study/QuizView.tsx; FlashcardsView.tsx)

problems_solved: Answers are hidden until the person answers (mobile: the set's source is never shown, StudyDocumentView.tsx:15-19).

features.summary: HTML, React and SVG artifacts run live in a sandboxed frame in the artifact panel on web and desktop, and in a sandboxed web view on mobile, with full screen on both. Third-party MCP app panels render as interactive frames in the web chat; mobile shows only their text result. CLI, VS Code, Chrome have neither.

purpose.what_it_does: Runs small HTML, React or SVG artifacts live in an isolated frame so a demo, page or app can be used, refreshed, opened in a new tab and expanded. An MCP app card loads a third-party app's interface into a sandboxed frame inside the chat and lets it call the connector's tools after approval. (apps/web/features/chat/components/SandboxedIframe.tsx:380-440; apps/web/features/chat/components/artifacts/artifact-render.ts:11-19; apps/web/features/chat/components/messages/cards/McpAppCard.tsx:200-420)
purpose.why_it_exists: People expect to try a generated page or app without leaving the chat, and connectors can ship their own interface. (doc: area brief S22.36-S22.38)
purpose.who_uses_it: Anyone asking for a demo, mini-app, page or SVG; anyone using a connector that ships an MCP app.
problems_solved: Generated code can be tried at once, safely isolated from the account.
Connector apps show their own interface instead of plain text.
Preview failures show a message rather than a blank frame.
use_cases: Ask for a calculator in HTML and use it in the panel.
Expand a generated landing page to full screen.
Use a connector's chart app inside the chat.
On mobile, open a React demo in a full-screen preview.

where_to_find_it: Web and Desktop (hosted web app): artifact panel Preview tab for html, react and svg artifacts; controls 'Enter fullscreen'/'Exit fullscreen' (title 'Expand'), More menu items 'Refresh preview' and 'Open in new tab' (apps/web/features/chat/components/artifacts/ArtifactPreview.tsx:2352-2366,2937-2940,3565-3567).
Web chat: MCP app card appears in the reply, text 'Loading MCP App…', 'Allow once' and 'Deny' for tool-call approval (McpAppCard.tsx:430-495).

Mobile: artifact full-screen viewer with SafeArtifactPreview; inline preview for html/react (apps/mobile/src/features/chat/components/ArtifactFullScreen.tsx:1722; SafeArtifactPreview.tsx:98-99). MCP app card shows the tool's text result only (apps/mobile/src/features/chat/components/cards/McpAppCard.tsx:48-54).
CLI, VS Code, Chrome: none found for live previews; Chrome has no mcp-app entry in its card registry (apps/extension/src/features/side-panel/bubbles.ts:243-249).
prerequisites: An artifact of type html, react or svg (ArtifactPreview.tsx:1806; artifact-render.ts:11-14).
MCP apps need a connected connector whose tool returns an app resource, and the cloud service (the card loads data from /api/mcp-apps/payload).
Mobile MCP card loads only where managed cloud tiles may load (canLoad = canLoadManagedCloudTiles, mobile InteractiveCardBlock.tsx:1103-1112).
screens_and_controls: Web artifact toolbar: Preview and source tabs, fullscreen toggle, More menu with Refresh preview and Open in new tab.
Web preview frame states: 'Loading preview…' then the frame; a banner when scripts cannot run (SandboxedIframe.tsx:380-415).
MCP card: loading spinner, error line, fallback text, device-permission ask, 'Allow once' / 'Deny' for app-initiated tool calls (McpAppCard.tsx:430-495).
Mobile preview: 'Nothing to preview yet.', 'This preview stopped with an error.', 'Open link?' prompt for links (SafeArtifactPreview.tsx:217-240; navigation prompt at 160-170).
journey: Ask for a demo or app; the reply creates an html/react/svg artifact.
Open the artifact; the Preview tab loads the sandboxed frame.
Use the app; press Refresh preview if needed; Enter fullscreen to expand; Open in new tab for a separate page.
For an MCP app: the card loads, the app starts, and any tool call it makes asks Allow once or Deny.
feedback_and_outputs: Banner 'This artifact's scripts cannot run here...' when scripts are blocked (SandboxedIframe.tsx:392-402).
MCP fallback to the plain tool result with a notice when the app cannot load or is too large (McpAppCard.tsx:343-348; MCP_APP_TOO_LARGE_MESSAGE).
Mobile load timeout headline and error text (SafeArtifactPreview.tsx:226-238).
settings: Environment names NEXT_PUBLIC_SANDBOX_ORIGIN (dedicated sandbox origin for artifacts, apps/web/lib/artifact-sandbox.ts:159) and NEXT_PUBLIC_MCP_APP_SANDBOX_ORIGIN (McpAppCard.tsx:112). Values not recorded.

working: Web/desktop live preview of html, react, svg in a sandboxed iframe; either a dedicated cross-origin sandbox or a srcdoc fallback with sandbox 'allow-scripts allow-modals' (SandboxedIframe.tsx:396-430; artifact-render.ts:25-40).
Fullscreen with the native Fullscreen API as an enhancement over an in-page expanded layout (ArtifactPreview.tsx:1787-1800).

Web MCP app card with an app bridge, sandbox route, payload route, CSP from the resource, device-permission ask, tool-call approval, https-only link opening (McpAppCard.tsx:200-420; apps/web/app/api/mcp-apps/sandbox/route.ts; apps/web/app/api/mcp-apps/payload/[payloadId]/route.ts).

features.summary: A person creates a project: a named workspace that groups chats, files and instructions. Web, mobile, CLI and VS Code can create one. Chrome only lists existing projects. In Cloud the project is saved to the account and checked against the plan project limit. Mobile Local mode keeps it on the phone.

purpose.what_it_does: Creates a project with a name and optional description, instructions, colour, icon emoji, accent colour and defaults, then opens it as its own workspace. On the server it is a row in user_projects owned by the signed-in user (apps/web/app/api/projects/route.ts:138-252).
purpose.why_it_exists: Chats, files and standing instructions need one home so each chat starts with the same context. Brief items S23.01 to S23.03 require a signed-in user to create a named project saved to the account (doc: knowledge-base/data/area-briefs/023-project-workspace.md).
purpose.who_uses_it: Signed-in people on Web, Desktop (hosted web app in Electron), Mobile, CLI and VS Code. On the phone in Local mode no account is needed (apps/mobile/src/features/projects/store.ts:420-433).
problems_solved: Repeating the same background in every chat
Keeping related chats and files together
Having the same project on every app that uses the account
use_cases: A designer makes 'Brand refresh' on the web and later picks it on the phone.
A developer runs agi projects create in a terminal, then links a folder to it.
A VS Code user creates a project with starting instructions from the command palette.
A phone user in Local mode makes a project that never leaves the device.

working: POST /api/projects validates the body, requires CSRF and rate limit, applies the 'projects' feature gate, refuses when the plan limit is 0, trims name, description and instructions, defaults colour, stores iconEmoji and accentColor when sent, and returns 201 (apps/web/app/api/projects/route.ts:138-252).
A positive plan limit is enforced inside the insert transaction by the database function assert_user_resource_limit, and a limit hit returns the plan message (route.ts:213-241).
POST /api/projects/sync also refuses a project limit of 0 (apps/web/app/api/projects/sync/route.ts:104-107); the CLI and mobile create through this sync push (apps/cli/src/cloud/mod.rs:442-455).

VS Code creates through the shared cloud-contracts projects client (apps/extension-vscode/src/features/projects/projectsClient.ts:66-75).

established.statement: A signed-in user can create a named project saved to the account that opens as its own workspace.
A project has a name and an optional description set at creation and editable later.
The user can choose a project icon and colour and the choice shows wherever the project appears.
Cover image or identity badge is not applicable.
Projects are present on all seven technical surfaces of the product.
Signed-in projects belong to the Cloud continuity domain and must converge across Web, Mobile, Desktop and Chrome.

acceptance_criteria: Creating with an empty or blank name is refused on every app.
A created project shows after reload on web and in agi projects list.
A project created with no colour gets the default colour; one created with iconEmoji and accentColor returns both.

On the free plan the sixth project is refused with the plan message.
A mobile Local project is absent from the account and a Cloud project is absent from device-only storage.
Description and instructions are saved trimmed.

features.summary: Lets a project owner share a project with people in the same workspace (organisation), choose who can open it, give each person Can view, Can edit or No access, copy a link, and stop sharing. Members see instructions and files; each person's chats and memories stay private. Access requests do not exist. Built on Web, Desktop (hosted web) and Mobile.

purpose.what_it_does: Shares one project inside an organisation. The share has an audience (everyone in the workspace can view, or only people the owner invites) and optional per-person grants (read, write, none). Members open the project and see its instructions and files. Editors may change name, description, instructions and appearance. Chats and memories stay with each person. (apps/web/db/neon/0315_private_shared_projects.sql:3)

steps.what_happens: Owner presses Share; the app sends PUT with the audience to the share route.
Server checks rate limit and CSRF, resolves the caller's organisation and checks the sharing right (sharing.manage, or content.share on a project they own).
Server reads the organisation's shared-project limit; zero blocks sharing.
One SQL statement inserts or updates organization_shared_projects for a project the caller owns and calls the limit guard; Health space violates a constraint and is refused.
Server writes an audit event and returns the shared project.
Owner adds people; each person gets one PATCH that upserts organization_project_access after checking a write grant can only go to a role that may edit.
A member opens the project; the server returns the project when it is theirs or in their readable shared set, marking write or read access.
An editor saves; the owner-only update misses, the server resolves editor access, refuses owner-only fields, then updates as non-owner.
Copy link writes the project page address to the clipboard; no server call.

steps.what_happens: Web archive: optimistic local update, then PUT with isArchived; reverted with a toast on failure.
Server tries the owner update (user must equal owner); a miss for a non-owner leads to editor resolution and the owner-only refusal.
Duplicate: server loads the owned source, refuses Health, checks the plan project limit, inserts the copy and its files in one transaction.
Export: server reads the owned project and its files and returns the JSON attachment; browser saves it.
Delete: server opens a transaction, serialises with legal holds, sets deleted_at, marks files deleted, unfiles chats; a hold aborts with forbidden.
CLI archive and delete call the same project routes and update the local project cache file.
Mobile Cloud delete or archive edits the local cloud project store and marks it for sync; the sync route applies it with a version check.
Mobile Local project delete removes the project from the device store only.

access_and_usage.subscription: Duplicate is limited by the plan's project limit; zero blocks it. Archive, export and delete have no plan rule found. (apps/web/app/api/projects/[id]/duplicate/route.ts:74)

features.summary: The Library lists a signed-in person's saved files in one place and splits them into All, Uploads, Generated files and Artifacts. Web and Electron desktop use the shared tab row. Mobile uses filter chips. The CLI and VS Code only list artifacts, from a different index. Chrome is unverified.

purpose.what_it_does: Lets a person see every saved file the account owns in one list, then narrow it to files they uploaded, files the assistant generated, or saved artifacts that open in a viewer. The list comes from the server table of stored media (media_assets) through GET /api/library. (apps/web/app/api/library/route.ts:148-212; apps/web/lib/server/media-assets.ts:402-440)
purpose.why_it_exists: Uploads, generated files and artifacts all end up as stored files, and people need one place to find them again instead of hunting through chats. The brief asks for All-files, Uploaded, Generated and Artifact views (doc: knowledge-base/data/area-briefs/024-library-and-file-management-experience.md S24.01-S24.04). The public support page describes the same tabs (doc: apps/web/content/support/library.md).
purpose.who_uses_it: Any signed-in person on web, Electron desktop or mobile. Developers on the CLI and VS Code use only the artifact list.
problems_solved: Finding a file made or uploaded in an old chat.
Telling apart what I uploaded from what the assistant made.
Reopening a saved artifact (page, diagram, document) without going back to the chat.
use_cases: On web, open /chat/library?surface=artifact to land on the Artifacts tab (apps/web/features/library/components/LibraryView.tsx:76-78,137-139).
On mobile, tap the Uploads chip to see only what I attached (apps/mobile/src/features/library/index.tsx:136-142).
In a terminal, run 'agi artifacts list' to print the account's artifacts (apps/cli/src/lib.rs:1359-1368).
In VS Code, browse the artifacts tree and open one (apps/extension-vscode/src/features/artifacts/artifactsTree.ts:32-60).

where_to_find_it: Web: page /chat/library, heading 'Library' (apps/web/app/chat/library/page.tsx; packages/ui/unified-chat/src/components/library/LibraryView.tsx:1002-1011).

Desktop (Electron, the public desktop): shows the hosted web app, so the same /chat/library page (doc: AGENTS.md section 5; apps/desktop/electron/__tests__/windowRegistry.test.ts:33-41 lists /chat/library and /chat/library?surface=artifact as chat routes).
Desktop (Tauri, retained internal build): DesktopLibrary inside DesktopShellV3 (apps/desktop/src/features/v3/DesktopShellV3.tsx:784; apps/desktop/src/features/library/DesktopLibrary.tsx).
Mobile: route apps/mobile/app/(app)/library/index.tsx; screen title 'Library' (apps/mobile/src/features/library/index.tsx:842-860 area).
CLI: command group 'agi artifacts' with subcommand list (apps/cli/src/lib.rs:1359-1368).
VS Code: an artifacts tree view (apps/extension-vscode/src/features/artifacts/artifactsTree.ts).
Chrome: the side panel shows artifacts for the open conversation (doc: docs/product/surface-feature-matrix.md:199); I did not open Chrome code.
prerequisites: A signed-in account. Web shows 'Sign in to see your library' when signed out (apps/web/features/library/components/LibraryView.tsx:115-129). Desktop shows 'Sign in to see your Library' (apps/desktop/src/features/library/DesktopLibrary.tsx, DesktopLibrary function). Mobile shows 'Signed out' with 'Sign in to see the images, videos, and files saved to your account.' (apps/mobile/src/features/library/index.tsx:1262-1270 area).
Files only appear if they were saved to the account. Files attached to a temporary chat are never listed (apps/web/lib/server/media-assets.ts:428-431 comment and clause).
screens_and_controls: Web/desktop: search box 'Search files and projects', tab row labelled 'Filter the library' with tabs All, Images, Videos, Documents, Artifacts, Uploads, Generated files; 'Show more' button; sort menu; 'Recently deleted' toggle; 'Grid view'/'List view' (packages/ui/unified-chat/src/components/library/LibraryView.tsx:91-99,1002-1058,1100-1115).

Mobile: horizontal chip row All, Images, Videos, Documents, Uploads, Generated files, Artifacts, Code, Charts, Research; each chip has accessibility label '<name> filter' (apps/mobile/src/features/library/index.tsx:897-938,1204).
CLI: 'agi artifacts list [--project <id>] [--limit N] [--json]' (apps/cli/src/lib.rs:1359-1368).
journey: Open the Library (web: /chat/library; mobile: Library from the drawer).
The list loads the first page of 24 items, newest-modified first.
Click or tap a tab or chip: All, Uploads, Generated files or Artifacts.
Web asks the server again with the tab's filter and shows 'Loading your library' while waiting (LibraryView.tsx:1085-1092 area).
Pick an item to open it. An artifact opens in an in-page artifact view; an image or file opens in the viewer.
Use 'Show more' to load the next 24.
feedback_and_outputs: Loading: 'Loading your library' with a spinner on web; spinner on mobile until first load finishes (apps/mobile/__tests__/LibraryFreshness.test.tsx).

Empty: web 'Your library is empty' with 'Upload a file' button (LibraryView.tsx:2226-2255). Mobile: 'Nothing here yet' plus one line per chip, such as 'Files you upload will appear here' and 'Files AGI creates for you will appear here' (index.tsx:1262-1287).

Error: web red box with the message and a 'Retry' button; default text 'Something went wrong.' (LibraryView.tsx:504,1068-1082). Mobile 'Library could not be loaded' with 'Check your connection and try again.' and Retry (index.tsx:1233-1260).
Storage line 'X of Y file storage used' and downloads line under the heading (LibraryView.tsx:1114-1134 area).
settings: Web layout choice is remembered in browser localStorage key 'agi-library-view-mode' (LibraryView.tsx:131-147) - see F024-04.
No other setting found.

working: Web and Electron desktop: the seven-tab row maps to server filters; Uploads sends origin=uploaded, Generated files sends kind=file and origin=generated, Artifacts sends surface=artifact (packages/ui/unified-chat/src/components/library/LibraryView.tsx:91-116; apps/web/lib/server/media-assets.ts:415-421).

Server: GET /api/library parses kind, sort, surface, origin, q, limit, offset, requires a user-scoped database, returns 24 items by default and a has_more flag (apps/web/app/api/library/route.ts:148-212; packages/contracts/cloud-contracts/src/library.ts:84,101-115).
Deep links: ?surface=artifact opens Artifacts; ?tab=<id> opens that tab, ?item= opens an item, ?q= prefills search (apps/web/features/library/components/LibraryView.tsx:76-78,137-141).

Mobile: Uploads and Generated files chips ask the server with origin (and kind=file for Generated) (index.tsx:136-142). Artifacts chip shows artifacts merged from the device store and the cloud list, filtered to the current app mode, with no image artifacts (index.tsx:320-326).

Mobile keeps an offline copy of the default first page in a persisted store 'library-store-cloud' (apps/mobile/src/features/library/libraryCacheStore.ts) and shows it with safe retry guidance when a load fails (apps/mobile/__tests__/LibraryAssetsError.test.tsx).
Saving an artifact to the Library: POST /api/library stores the text as a media_assets row with origin 'saved_artifact' (route.ts:214-273).

CLI: 'agi artifacts list' reads the hosted artifact index /api/artifacts/index (apps/cli/src/cloud/artifacts.rs:23-24). VS Code lists the same index in a tree (apps/extension-vscode/src/features/artifacts/artifactActions.ts imports ManagedCloudArtifactIndexEntry).
incomplete: Generated files tab on web and mobile is limited to kind 'file', so a generated image or video is not in it; it is in Images or Videos (LibraryView.tsx:115 area; apps/mobile/src/features/library/index.tsx:136-142). [inferred from the mapping]

Tauri DesktopLibrary passes only a read, delete, restore, preview and media-job transport; it has no upload, folder, add-to-chat or download actions (apps/desktop/src/features/library/DesktopLibrary.tsx, transport memo).
Chrome artifact view: not verified (brief S24.04 says unverified).
disconnected_or_disabled: Contract field resource_type and function libraryResourceTypeFor exist, but GET /api/library does not read resource_type and no UI uses it (packages/contracts/cloud-contracts/src/library.ts:47-60,96-99; apps/web/app/api/library/route.ts:155-163; search of apps and packages found only library.ts and its test).
not_available: CLI, VS Code and Chrome have no Uploads or Generated files views (doc: docs/product/surface-feature-matrix.md:197-199).
Artifacts are not in the CLI/VS Code Library list; they list a different index built from chat messages (apps/cli/src/cloud/artifacts.rs:1-12).

established.statement: One Library view lists every file the user owns across chats, generation, uploads and projects.
A view shows only uploaded files.
A view shows only files the assistant generated.
A view lists the user's artifacts and opens each one.
Each tab asks the server for a fresh first page of 24 items.
Uploaded and generated files appear once with accurate type, size, origin and pagination; delete/restore shows in listing.

acceptance_criteria: On web, each of All, Uploads, Generated files and Artifacts triggers a GET /api/library with the matching origin/kind/surface params and limit=24.
An uploaded file appears under Uploads and All, and not under Generated files.
A generated PDF or office file appears under Generated files; a generated image does not.
A saved artifact appears under Artifacts on web and under the Artifacts chip on mobile, and opens.
Signed out: no library request is made and a sign-in message shows, not an empty-library message.
A failed load shows an error with a Retry button, not an empty list.
inferred: The Tauri DesktopLibrary should reach the same tab behaviour as web, since both render the shared LibraryView. [inferred]
CLI and VS Code should state that they list artifacts only. [inferred]
proposed: [proposed] Add an Artifacts tab-equivalent to Chrome and confirm it against the hosted index.
[proposed] Show the same tab names on mobile and web (mobile adds Code, Charts, Research chips).

steps.what_happens: Person opens the Library or clicks a tab; the shared view builds query params (limit 24, sort, kind/surface/origin, q, deleted) and calls the host transport.
Web transport sends GET /api/library with the session cookie.

Server applies the chat-conversation rate limit, resolves the user-scoped database, validates the query and runs the SQL over media_assets for that user and active organization, excluding temporary-chat files and deleted rows.
Server returns the page plus has_more, next_offset and (first page only, not Recently deleted) storage and download meters.
Client validates the response with LibraryListResponseSchema; a bad shape becomes an error with Retry.
On mobile, Artifacts chip rows come from the device artifact store and cloud artifacts, filtered by app mode, without any /api/library call for them.
CLI and VS Code call the hosted artifact index, not /api/library.

execution_and_data_flow.models_and_providers: Listing and filtering use no model. Each row only records which provider and model made a generated file (provider, model columns); mobile shows the model's short name as the source label (apps/mobile/src/features/library/libraryClient.ts:65-73). No provider is called to list files.

access_and_usage.account: Signed-in account required for the server list on web, desktop and mobile (apps/web/features/library/components/LibraryView.tsx:278; apps/desktop/src/features/library/DesktopLibrary.tsx; apps/mobile/src/features/library/useLibraryAssets.ts loadFirstPage returns empty when no owner). CLI and VS Code need a signed-in account for the hosted artifact index (apps/cli/src/cloud/artifacts.rs).
access_and_usage.permissions: Rows are scoped to the user and the active organization (apps/web/lib/server/media-assets.ts:402-440). Reads go through a user-scoped database (apps/web/app/api/library/route.ts:152).
access_and_usage.subscription: No tab is gated by plan (none found in the code). Plan only sets the storage allowance and monthly download allowance shown in the header (apps/web/lib/server/file-storage.ts:77-91; apps/web/lib/services/tier-unit-quota-service.ts:446-463).
access_and_usage.limits_and_metering: Page size 24 default, 100 max (library.ts:84-85). Rate limit group 'chat-conversation' (route.ts:149). Storage and download meters are returned only on the first page of the non-deleted view.
access_and_usage.flags: none found in the code for the tabs. Mobile hides image edit when the imageGen flag is off, which is unrelated to listing (index.tsx:1122).
access_and_usage.model_compatibility: Not affected. Any model's output is listed once stored.
access_and_usage.provider_restrictions: none found in the code; provider is only a label on the row.
access_and_usage.local_mode: The server Library lists only files stored in AGI Cloud. The Tauri desktop screen states that local-only sessions keep files on the device and are not cataloged there (apps/desktop/src/features/library/DesktopLibrary.tsx, signed-out text). On mobile, artifacts are filtered to the current app mode, so local artifacts show in local mode (index.tsx:320-326); whether the server list is requested in local mode is not gated in the code I read (index.tsx uses clerkUserId only), so this is unknown.

working: Web: Images sends kind=image, Videos kind=video, Documents kind=file with surface=file (packages/ui/unified-chat/src/components/library/LibraryView.tsx:108-116).
Server filters 'kind = any(...)' and accepts several kinds in one request (apps/web/lib/server/media-assets.ts:407-410; apps/web/app/api/library/__tests__/route.test.ts).
Contract rejects a kind that is not image, video or file (packages/contracts/cloud-contracts/src/library.ts:91-94,101-103).
Mobile classifies each row as image, video or document from kind or mime type (apps/mobile/src/features/library/libraryClient.ts:57-62) and filters rows by that class (index.tsx:328-345).
Mobile opens images full screen, videos in a player, documents in FileViewerScreen (index.tsx:1118-1153).
incomplete: Mobile Images, Videos, Documents chips use scope {} on the server and filter only the loaded pages, so a rare kind may need 'Show more' paging to appear (apps/mobile/src/features/library/index.tsx:136-142,328-345). [inferred]
There is no finer file-type filter (by extension or by pdf, spreadsheet, slides) in any UI, although the contract defines resource types (library.ts:16-28).
disconnected_or_disabled: LIBRARY_RESOURCE_TYPES includes 'audio' and the classifier can return it, but GET /api/library does not read resource_type and no tab uses it (library.ts:16-28,47-60; route.ts:155-163).
not_available: Audio view, kind and viewer: none on any app (library.ts:8 lists only image, video, file; no Audio tab in TABS).
CLI, VS Code and Chrome media-type views (doc: docs/product/surface-feature-matrix.md:197-199).

steps.what_happens: The person picks Add to chat, Add to Work or Add to project on a row.
The web page fetches the stored bytes from /api/files/<id> and builds a File.
For chat or Work, the File is parked in memory with the chosen mode and draft, and the browser goes to a new chat.
For a project, the File is uploaded to the project knowledge endpoint; the server checks the file count and storage allowance and stores a project copy.
For Open chat, the browser routes to /chat/<conversation id>.
On mobile, Add to chat stages the asset (uri, mime, name, size, asset id) for the new chat and switches to the Chat tab.

features.summary: Deleting a Library file hides it and keeps it for 30 days in Recently deleted. During that time it can be restored. A person can also erase it for good, unless a legal hold blocks it. A daily job removes files older than 30 days. Built on web and mobile, and in the internal Tauri desktop.

purpose.what_it_does: Gives soft delete, a trash view, restore within 30 days, permanent delete on request and automatic purge after 30 days.
purpose.why_it_exists: Accidental deletion must be recoverable, and agents or people must not destroy data in one step. (AGENTS.md section 9; S24.34 in the area brief)
purpose.who_uses_it: Any signed-in person managing Library files.
problems_solved: Accidental deletes.
Needing to free space on purpose.
Keeping evidence under legal hold.
use_cases: Restore a deleted report the next day.
Permanently erase a sensitive upload.
Check what will be erased soon ('Kept until <date>').
Erase fails because the file is on legal hold.

Internal Tauri desktop: same shared view with delete, restore and permanent-delete transports (apps/desktop/src/features/library/DesktopLibrary.tsx:163-181).
Mobile: Library header options menu, item 'Recently deleted', then 'Back to Library' to leave (apps/mobile/src/features/library/index.tsx:275-293).
prerequisites: Signed in. Library rows only (temporary-chat files are never listed).

Web confirm for Delete: title 'Delete <name>?', text 'It moves to Recently deleted, where it stays restorable for 30 days before it is removed for good.' (LibraryView.tsx:731-742).
Web confirm for permanent: 'Permanently delete <name>?' 'The stored bytes are erased now. Nothing restores this file, and anything linking to it stops resolving.' (744-755).

Mobile: alert 'Delete from Library?' with text 'moves to deleted items'; header 'Recently deleted. Erased after 30 days. Long press to restore.'; action menu Restore and Delete permanently; alert 'Delete permanently?' '...erased now instead of after 30 days. This cannot be undone.' (index.tsx:556-605, 879).

steps.what_happens: The person confirms Delete; the app sends DELETE /api/media?id=<uuid> with a CSRF token (web) or the authenticated API client (mobile).
The server validates the id, sets deleted_at now() for the user and active workspace, returns {success}.
Opening Recently deleted calls /api/library?deleted=true, which lists rows deleted in the last 30 days, newest deletion first, with erase_after.
Restore sends POST /api/media?id=; SQL clears deleted_at only when deleted_at is newer than 30 days.

Delete permanently sends DELETE with permanent=true; in a transaction the server locks the row, checks the legal hold (refuses and audits if held), deletes the stored object, deletes the row, then purges derived records.
A daily cron selects assets deleted over 30 days ago, up to 500 per run, and erases bytes and rows while respecting holds.

features.summary: Opens a PDF inside AGI Workforce so a person can read it without leaving the app. Web (and the public Electron Desktop, which shows the web app) frame the PDF in the browser. Mobile draws it with the system viewer on iOS and a bundled viewer on Android. Page thumbnails, page jump, fit and rotate are not built.

purpose.what_it_does: Shows a stored PDF in an in-product reader. On web it is an iframe pointing at the file route with a PDF-only flag (packages/ui/unified-chat/src/components/library/LibraryView.tsx:1171, 1306). In a project, the knowledge-file preview modal frames the file and can open at a given page (apps/web/features/projects/components/FilePreviewModal.tsx:410-416). On mobile the file is copied to the device and drawn by a viewer (apps/mobile/src/features/chat/components/artifact-viewers/DocumentFileView.tsx:173-206).
purpose.why_it_exists: A person who generated or uploaded a PDF should read it where they work, and a citation should be able to open the PDF at the cited page. The brief asks for an in-product PDF reader (S25.01) with thumbnails, page navigation, fit and rotate (S25.12, S25.13, S25.15-S25.17) (doc: knowledge-base/data/area-briefs/025-file-previews-and-readers.md).
purpose.who_uses_it: Signed-in people on web, Electron Desktop and mobile who keep PDFs in the Library or in a project's knowledge list.
problems_solved: Reading a PDF without downloading it and opening another app.

Jumping to the page a citation points at (web project modal and mobile pass a page number; apps/web/features/projects/components/FilePreviewModal.tsx:412, apps/mobile/src/features/chat/components/artifact-viewers/FileViewerScreen.tsx:104).
Refusing to frame anything that is not a PDF, so a hostile file cannot be framed as a document (apps/web/app/api/files/[id]/route.ts:219-221).
use_cases: Open a generated report PDF from the Library on web.
Open a PDF source from a project's knowledge list and land on the cited page.
Read a PDF on a phone from the Library or a project's Sources tab.
See 'This PDF is too large to preview. Download it to open it.' for a very large chat upload.

where_to_find_it: Web and Electron Desktop: the Library page (apps/web/app/chat/library/page.tsx:1-20) opens the file viewer when a tile is clicked, tile label 'Open <file name>' (packages/ui/unified-chat/src/components/library/LibraryView.tsx:1496-1498). Viewer dialog label '<file name> viewer'.

Web project: a knowledge file row in the Sources/knowledge list opens a modal labelled 'Preview: <file name>' (apps/web/features/projects/components/FilePreviewModal.tsx:282, KnowledgeFilesPanel.tsx:447).

Mobile: Library file card (apps/mobile/src/features/library/index.tsx:786-800) and the project Sources tab (apps/mobile/src/features/projects/components/ProjectSourcesTab.tsx:890) open a sheet via FileViewerScreen.

Tauri desktop tree (retained, not the public Desktop): DesktopLibrary (apps/desktop/src/features/library/DesktopLibrary.tsx:181) has its own 'Library file preview' dialog, but the shared Library never calls it (see gaps).
prerequisites: Signed in to a Cloud account on web, Desktop and mobile (apps/web/app/api/files/[id]/route.ts:198; apps/mobile/src/features/library/index.tsx:461-463).
The item must be marked previewable: a PDF always is (apps/web/app/api/library/route.ts:51-56).
screens_and_controls: Web Library viewer: header breadcrumb 'Library > <name>', buttons 'Download <name>' and 'Close file viewer', and an 'Ask about this file' box (LibraryView.tsx:1210-1275, 1349). No zoom group for a PDF (zoom shows only for an image, line 1221).
Web project modal: header with file name, type and size, 'Download' and 'Close' buttons; the PDF fills a 70vh frame (FilePreviewModal.tsx:351-415).
Mobile sheet: title, size and 'Page n' detail, 'Open chat' (when the file has a chat), 'Share <file>', Close; on Android a caption 'Page n of N' under the PDF (PdfFileView.tsx:197-233).

Tap or click the PDF.
Wait for the spinner or 'Opening <file>' indicator.
Read; scroll inside the frame (the browser or system draws the pages).
Close with Escape or the close button (web), or the Close control or swipe down (mobile).
feedback_and_outputs: Spinner while loading; the web Library frame has no spinner of its own, the browser shows its PDF frame [inferred].
A too-large chat upload answers 'This PDF is too large to preview. Download it to open it.' (route.ts:51, 118-123).

Mobile failures: 'Could not open this file' with Retry, or 'This file could not be shown here' with Retry and Share; a password PDF says 'It is protected by a password. Share it to open it in another app.' (DocumentFileView.tsx:114-171).
settings: None found in the code for PDF preview.

working: Web Library: PDF opens in an iframe at the file URL plus preview=pdf, title = file name (LibraryView.tsx:331-337, 1171-1173, 1306-1310). Server serves only PDF bytes for that flag and adds a CSP and X-Frame-Options SAMEORIGIN (apps/web/app/api/files/[id]/route.ts:219-221, 346-352).
Web project modal frames the stored file and adds #page=N when a citation page is given (FilePreviewModal.tsx:410-416); SourcesPanel passes the page (SourcesPanel.tsx:844-846).
Electron Desktop loads the hosted web app, so it gets the web viewer (apps/desktop/electron/main.ts:1065-1066; doc: docs/product/definition.md:452-454).

Mobile iOS: PDF copied into cache and drawn by the system document view in a WebView with scripts off (DocumentFileView.tsx:185-206). Mobile Android: bundled pdf.js page in an isolated WebView, bytes sent in 256 KB chunks, 'Page n of N' caption, opens at a requested page, fails after 15 s of silence (PdfFileView.tsx:29-236; pdfViewerBridge.ts:1-2; apps/mobile/assets/pdfjs/pdf-viewer.json exists).
incomplete: No thumbnails, page-jump box, fit-to-width, fit-to-page or rotate control in any app; only open-at-page from a citation exists. The browser or system PDF frame may add its own controls; not verified.
Mobile 'page' is passed on open only; the iOS WebView receives #page=N (DocumentFileView.tsx:19-21).
disconnected_or_disabled: DesktopLibrary (Tauri tree) passes no inlinePreviewUri or textPreviewUri to the shared Library and its own preview dialog hangs off openPreview, which LibraryView never calls (grep of packages/ui/unified-chat/src finds openPreview only in the transport interface, LibraryView.tsx:267). The desktop test asserts inlinePreviewUri is undefined (apps/desktop/src/features/library/__tests__/DesktopLibrary.test.tsx:162-180). So a PDF clicked there frames the relative file URL with no bearer header [inferred].
not_available: VS Code: no PDF reader found in apps/extension-vscode/src/features/artifacts (reads artifact text only).
Chrome: side panel offers Open and Download buttons for answer files and an image viewer, no PDF reader found (apps/extension/src/features/side-panel/generatedFiles.ts:281-300).
CLI: no PDF preview; 'agi library show' reads the text route, which has no PDF kind (apps/web/lib/server/file-text-preview.ts:28-38).

established.statement: A PDF opens in an in-product reader.
A document shows page thumbnails; users can navigate pages; viewers can fit to width, fit to page, and rotate.
The viewer contract needs loading, error, unsupported and expired states, and a full-screen or native route on mobile.

On mobile Android the caption reads 'Page n of N' once loaded; a password PDF shows the password message and a Share button.
Escape closes the web Library viewer.
[proposed] Thumbnails, a page box, fit and rotate exist on every app that shows PDFs.
inferred: Thumbnails, page controls, fit and rotate are required by the brief but have no code today [inferred from the brief and code search].
The PDF frame should work on desktop without exposing the account token in a URL [inferred from the egress rules in AGENTS.md section 6].
proposed: Use one shared page-control strip (thumbnail rail, page box, fit width, fit page, rotate) in the shared Library viewer so web, Electron and any desktop host get it once.
Give the web Library PDF frame a visible spinner like the project modal's and mobile's.

steps.what_happens: Web/Electron: person clicks the tile; the shared Library sets the viewer item when previewable is true.
The viewer builds the frame address (file URL plus preview=pdf) and the browser requests it with the session cookie.

The server checks rate limit, user scope and workspace, rejects non-PDF for the flag, applies the 30 MB cap, checks the download allowance, reads the object from storage and returns bytes with a frame-restricting CSP.
Object bytes come from private media storage.
The browser's own PDF frame draws the pages.
Mobile: the app downloads the bytes with the account token to a cache copy, then draws them (iOS system frame, Android bundled pdf.js).

access_and_usage.limits_and_metering: 30 MB inline serve cap (route.ts:45) and rate limit 'files-serve' (route.ts:195). Egress bytes recorded (route.ts:330-336). The project modal's own knowledge-file route: whether it spends the allowance is unknown.

Mobile opens a file under a Cloud scope; an on-device file:// source is read in place without fetching (useLocalFileCopy.ts:44, FileViewerScreen.test.tsx:191), but which screens pass one is unknown. features.summary: Shows text, Markdown and code files as readable text. In a web project the preview modal renders Markdown and code blocks; the shared Library viewer, mobile and Tauri show plain monospace text. The CLI prints files with terminal colour when run in a terminal. VS Code opens chat artifacts in an editor tab.

purpose.what_it_does: Reads a text-like file and shows it. Web project modal fetches the raw file and renders Markdown through the chat Markdown component or code through a fenced block with a language (apps/web/features/projects/components/FilePreviewModal.tsx:81-164). The shared Library viewer fetches a text preview from the server and prints it in a pre block (packages/ui/unified-chat/src/components/library/FileTextPreview.tsx:86-89). The CLI prints the same text (apps/cli/src/lib.rs:7318-7334).
purpose.why_it_exists: People keep notes, logs, Markdown and code in projects and the Library and should read them without downloading. The brief wants text, Markdown rendering and syntax-aware code (S25.02-S25.04).
purpose.who_uses_it: Web, Electron Desktop, mobile and CLI users; VS Code users reading assistant artifacts.
problems_solved: Reading a file inline instead of downloading.
Reading Markdown formatted.

use_cases: Open a README.md in a project's knowledge list and see headings and lists.

Run 'agi library show <id>' to read a Library note in the terminal.

features.summary: Shows spreadsheets as a table, Word files as text and presentations as slide text or slides. The web project modal also draws a presentation as slides in the browser (apps/web/features/projects/components/FilePreviewModal.tsx:419-425).
purpose.why_it_exists: People attach spreadsheets, documents and decks and want to check them without another app. The brief asks for spreadsheet, presentation, document and archive previews (S25.08-S25.11).
purpose.who_uses_it: Web, Electron Desktop, mobile and CLI users with Office files.

features.summary: Opens an image in a viewer. Web and Electron Desktop show it in the Library overlay with zoom buttons. Mobile opens a full-screen view with pinch, double-tap and pan. The Chrome side panel has a small image viewer for answer files. VS Code has none, and the retained Tauri Library cannot show images.

Mobile: ImageFullScreen with a pinch, pan and double-tap hook (apps/mobile/src/features/chat/components/ImageFullScreen.tsx:50; ZoomableImage.tsx:112-213). Chrome: a dialog from generated answer files (apps/extension/src/features/side-panel/mediaViewer.ts:11-30).

problems_solved: Seeing detail in a generated image.
Opening an image without leaving the Library.
use_cases: Click a generated image tile and zoom to 200%.
Tap an image on mobile and pinch in.
Open an image in a project knowledge modal.
Open an answer image from the Chrome side panel.

features.summary: Plays video in the product with the player's own controls on web, Electron Desktop, mobile and the Chrome side panel. Audio files have no player, and transcript panels and timestamp navigation do not exist. The retained Tauri Library cannot play video correctly.

purpose.what_it_does: Plays a stored video. Web: a video element with controls pointed at the file URL, served with byte ranges (packages/ui/unified-chat/src/components/library/LibraryView.tsx:1292-1301; apps/web/app/api/files/[id]/route.ts:258-310). Mobile: downloads the video to a cache folder and plays it from a local page in a WebView (apps/mobile/services/fileCreation.ts:553-621; Library index.tsx:486-511, 1144).
purpose.why_it_exists: Generated videos should be watched where they are saved. The brief asks for audio and video players with transcripts and timestamps (S25.06, S25.07, S25.23, S25.24).
purpose.who_uses_it: People who generate videos with the media features, on web, Electron, mobile and Chrome.
problems_solved: Watching a generated video without downloading.
Seeking in large videos through range requests.
use_cases: Play a generated clip in the Library.
Seek in a long video on web.
Watch a clip on a phone.
Watch a video in an answer in the Chrome side panel.

Mobile: mp4, webm and quicktime only, cached per account, plays with autoplay in a local HTML page (fileCreation.ts:566-621).
Chrome: video blob URL with a lease released on unmount (generatedFiles.ts:340-410).

not_available: Audio player in the Library or file viewers on web, mobile, Desktop, VS Code, Chrome: web does not mark audio previewable so a click does nothing (library/route.ts:51-58; LibraryView.tsx:810); mobile classes audio as a document and shows 'Preview isn’t available for this file type.' with Share (libraryClient.ts:55-60; FileViewerScreen.tsx:190-212). Audio elements exist only for voice samples and speech (apps/web/features/chat/components/Voice/VoiceSampleButton.tsx, apps/mobile/src/features/voice/services/voiceSamples.ts).
Transcript panel and timestamp navigation: no code found in any app.
VS Code and CLI: no player.

features.summary: Lets a person enlarge an image and view content full screen. Web and Electron show a full-window overlay with zoom buttons for images (25 to 400 percent). Mobile uses a full-screen sheet and pinch zoom up to 5 times. Web artifact preview also has a real full-screen mode. PDFs, text and video have no zoom control.

purpose.what_it_does: Provides zoom buttons in the Library viewer for images (packages/ui/unified-chat/src/components/library/LibraryView.tsx:1142-1145, 1221-1250), a full-window overlay (lines 1197-1208), mobile pinch zoom (apps/mobile/src/features/chat/components/ZoomableImage.tsx:112-213) and a web artifact full-screen toggle that uses the browser's full-screen request (apps/web/features/chat/components/artifacts/ArtifactPreview.tsx:1796-1797).
purpose.why_it_exists: Detail and focus: people need to enlarge content and remove distractions. Brief S25.14 and S25.25.
purpose.who_uses_it: Web, Electron, mobile users viewing images, files and artifacts.
problems_solved: Reading fine detail in an image.
Focusing on one file.
use_cases: Zoom a chart image to 300% on web.
Pinch into a photo on mobile.
Expand an artifact preview to full screen on web.
Open a project file as a full-screen sheet on mobile.

Header 'Close file viewer'; Escape closes (line 1183-1188).
Mobile close control 'Close file' and swipe down (FileViewerScreen.tsx:24, 94-98).
journey: Open an image.

Close.
feedback_and_outputs: Percent text updates (100 default).
Buttons disable at 25 and 400.
settings: None found in the code.

working: Web zoom 25 to 400, step 25, default 100, applied as a CSS scale; shown only when the item is an image with an inline preview address (LibraryView.tsx:1142-1145, 1169, 1221, 1288).
The viewer is a fixed full-window dialog with a scrim, not browser full-screen (LibraryView.tsx:1197-1208). A host can place it inside a container via containerId (lines 1178-1181, 1381).
Mobile pinch 1x to 5x, double-tap 2.5x, pan clamp (ZoomableImage.tsx:13-14, 112-183).
Web ArtifactPreview calls the browser full-screen request and handles leaving through Escape (ArtifactPreview.tsx:767-790, 1796-1797).

Mobile text and PDF views offer no app zoom control; the iOS system view and Android WebView may allow pinch (setBuiltInZoomControls in PdfFileView.tsx:182), not verified.
disconnected_or_disabled: Tauri Library: viewer shows no image to zoom because inlinePreviewUri is not provided [inferred] (DesktopLibrary.test.tsx:178).
not_available: VS Code: no viewer zoom (editor has its own).
Chrome: image viewer found (mediaViewer.ts) but no zoom control found.

features.summary: Gets a file or its text out of AGI Workforce. Web and the public Desktop (which shows the web app) can download the original and a text copy from the Library viewer. The CLI saves the original. Mobile opens the phone share sheet. VS Code copies or saves an artifact. No app has a copy button or opens the file in its native app on web, Desktop or Chrome.

purpose.what_it_does: Lets a person take a stored file out of the product: save the original bytes, save a plain-text copy of what the reader extracted, copy artifact content, or hand the file to another app. It covers the Library viewer and project preview modal on web, the Library on mobile, the library commands in the CLI and the artifact commands in VS Code.
purpose.why_it_exists: A preview is not the file. People need the real file to edit it in the right program, send it on, or keep it. The experience contract says downloaded bytes must open in the expected application and match the stored artifact (doc: docs/product/experience-contract.md:784).
purpose.who_uses_it: Anyone with files in their Library or project sources: office workers with documents and spreadsheets, developers with generated code artifacts, mobile users who want to send a file elsewhere.
problems_solved: A file the viewer cannot show can still be saved and opened elsewhere.
A long document can be kept as plain text without the original format.
A phone user can send a generated file into any app that accepts it.
A developer can put a generated artifact into the workspace or the clipboard.
use_cases: Open a PDF in the web Library and click the download icon to save it.
Open a Word file, wait for its text, click 'Download as text' to save a .txt copy.
On the phone, long-press a Library file and choose Share to send it to another app.
In a terminal, run agi library download <id> to save a generated file into the current folder.

steps.what_happens: Person clicks Download in the web viewer. If the file is a large upload and the host offers downloadInBrowser, the meter is checked and the browser downloads from the server directly.
Otherwise the viewer fetches the asset with the session cookie, turns it into a blob and saves it under the original name.
The file route checks the plan's download allowance (when the file spends it), then streams bytes or redirects to private storage, and records egress bytes.
'Download as text' reuses the already loaded text preview and saves it locally; no new request is made.
Mobile downloads the file with the account token only when the URL is the API's own origin, writes it into the device export folder, and opens the share sheet.
CLI calls GET /api/files/{id} with the account token and writes the response to disk.
VS Code re-derives artifact content from the source chat message fetched from the cloud, then copies or saves it locally.

features.summary: Ask a question about a file. purpose.what_it_does: Gives the person an honest message when a file has no inline preview, failed to load, or was cut short, and points to the way out: download, share, or the CLI download command.
purpose.why_it_exists: A blank panel or a half-shown file misleads people. The product rule is no silent failures and no fake responses (doc: AGENTS.md section 9).
purpose.who_uses_it: Anyone opening a file type the product cannot render, or a large document, spreadsheet or text.

steps.what_happens: Library list marks each item previewable if it is an image, video, PDF, has a text-preview kind or metadata says so.
Viewer opens only previewable items; for non-image, non-video, non-PDF items it requests {uri}/text.
Server loads the asset, picks the kind, refuses unknown types (404) and oversize (validation), reads the stored bytes, extracts text, cuts at the character limit and returns truncated.
Viewer validates the response with the shared schema; a bad shape or any HTTP error becomes 'failed' and the fallback card shows.
Viewer renders text or the first 500 rows of a table and the note if truncated or rows were dropped.
CLI fetches the same text route and prints it, then the stop note if truncated.

features.summary: Each artifact a reply makes appears as a card under the reply with its title and kind. On web, desktop (the web app in Electron) and Chrome the card opens or hides the viewer beside the chat. On mobile it opens a full-screen sheet. CLI and VS Code have list commands, not cards. Closing never deletes the artifact.

purpose.what_it_does: Shows each artifact as a small card in the conversation, opens it in the viewer, closes the viewer without deleting anything, and lets the person reopen it from the card, the artifacts toggle or the list. Web caps the message at three cards, adds a '+N more' button and a 'Download all' button (InlineArtifactCards.tsx:14,39-85).
purpose.why_it_exists: Long code or documents would flood the chat. A card keeps the answer readable and the artifact one tap away, as in the leading assistants. [inferred] The repository guidance asks for real file cards that stay valid after refresh (doc: docs/product/competitive-guidance.md:285).
purpose.who_uses_it: Anyone who asks the assistant to build a page, document, diagram or file, on web, the Desktop window, the phone app and the Chrome side panel. CLI and VS Code users reach artifacts by list and open commands.
problems_solved: Keeps big generated content out of the message body
Gives a stable way to find and reopen what was made
Lets many artifacts from one reply be reached or saved together
use_cases: Ask for a landing page, click Open on the card and read it beside the chat
Close the viewer, then reopen it later from the artifacts toggle
Save every artifact of a reply with Download all
On a phone tap the card to read the document full screen

features.summary: Shows whether an artifact is being written, finished, stopped early or failed to render. Web and Chrome show a live view that grows as text arrives. Web adds a banner for a stopped artifact, an error panel with View source and Retry, and a loading state. Mobile shows 'Writing…', 'Failed' or 'Stopped' on its card. CLI has none.

purpose.what_it_does: Marks each artifact as writing, finished, stopped or failed, updates the view live while text arrives, and replaces a broken preview with a message and a way forward (ArtifactPreview.tsx:3228-3253).
purpose.why_it_exists: Models take time to write a page, replies can be cut off, and previews can fail. A silent blank would look like a bug. The product contract asks for a repairable error on invalid generated content (doc: docs/product/experience-contract.md:782).
purpose.who_uses_it: Anyone watching an artifact being generated or opening one that was stopped or cannot run.
problems_solved: No blank frame while a library loads
A stopped reply is not mistaken for a complete file
A failed render offers source and retry
use_cases: Watch a page's code appear in the panel while the reply streams
Open an artifact from a stopped reply and read the banner
See 'This artifact couldn't be rendered.' and press Retry
Wait while the sandbox loads the React runtime

features.summary: Lets a person switch a renderable artifact between its preview and its source. On web, Desktop and mobile a person can edit the text and save it as a new version. Only the newest version of a stored artifact can be edited; older versions and file formats like PDF or images cannot. CLI, VS Code and Chrome are read-only.

features.summary: Shows which version of an artifact is on screen, lets a person step to the previous or next version, open any version from a history list, restore an older version as a new latest copy, and see what changed since the version before. Web, Desktop and mobile have it. CLI, VS Code and Chrome do not.

purpose.what_it_does: Keeps every saved version of an artifact, shows 'v2/3' with previous and next buttons, a history list with when and what changed, and a Restore action that adds the old text as the newest version without deleting the ones between (ArtifactVersionHistory.tsx:61-182; artifacts-store.ts:976-989).
purpose.why_it_exists: Edits, regenerations and conflicts create several versions. People need to look back and undo without losing work (doc: docs/decisions/wire-or-cut.md:325).
purpose.who_uses_it: Anyone editing or regenerating an artifact.
problems_solved: Undo a bad edit
See what changed
Recover a version after a sync conflict

features.summary: Lets a signed-in Cloud user publish an artifact to a share link, choose who can open it (anyone, the workspace, or invited people), see that state, and withdraw the link. Web and mobile have the full set. The CLI has publish, audience and unpublish for public or workspace. VS Code only shows state and opens the link. Chrome has none.

purpose.what_it_does: Sends a copy of an artifact (a page, diagram, document or code file the assistant made) to the AGI Cloud publish service, which returns a link. The owner can change who may open the link, see that state, and unpublish so the link stops working. [apps/web/app/api/artifacts/publish/route.ts:78] [apps/web/app/api/artifacts/publish/[token]/route.ts:72]
purpose.why_it_exists: Claude and ChatGPT let people share an artifact by link. The project's own wording for S26.31 is: publish to a link, copy it, choose who can open it, take it down (doc: knowledge-base/data/area-briefs/026-artifact-container-and-panel.md). Without it a made page can only be copied or downloaded.
purpose.who_uses_it: A person on Cloud (managed) with an artifact in a chat who wants someone else to view it. Team members who want a workspace-only link. A developer using the CLI to publish from a terminal.
problems_solved: Gives a stable link to an artifact so others can open it without a copy-paste.
Lets the owner narrow the audience after publishing and see at a glance whether it is open to everyone.
Lets the owner withdraw a link.
use_cases: Publish an HTML page the assistant built and send the link to a colleague.
Switch a published link to workspace-only before sharing internal content.
Invite named people by email so only they can open the page.
From the terminal, run the CLI publish command for an artifact id and print the link.

where_to_find_it: Web viewer (artifact panel): toolbar button labelled 'Publish' (accessible name 'Publish artifact to a public link'); on a narrow panel the same action is a menu item 'Publish' (apps/web/features/chat/components/artifacts/ArtifactPreview.tsx:2305, apps/web/features/chat/components/artifacts/ArtifactPreview.tsx:2924).

Web after publishing: a bar under the toolbar with the link, a 'Copy link' button, a selector labelled 'Who can open this' with 'Anyone with the link', 'Everyone in this workspace (N)' (only when the publisher belongs to a workspace) and 'Only people you invite', and an invited-people editor when 'Only people you invite' is chosen (ArtifactPreview.tsx:3010, ArtifactPreview.tsx:3037, ArtifactPreview.tsx:3054-3069).

Web unpublish and list: Settings, Shared links, section 'Published artifacts' with row buttons 'Open', 'Copy', 'History', 'Unpublish' (apps/web/features/settings/sections/PublishedArtifactsSection.tsx:524, :600, :608, :634-644; mounted from apps/web/features/settings/sections/SharedLinksSection.tsx:502 and apps/web/features/settings/components/WebSettingsModal.tsx:289).
Web Library: item action 'Share link' for artifact items, with a confirm 'Create a public link to <name>?' (packages/ui/unified-chat/src/components/library/LibraryView.tsx:1864, :713-720).

Desktop (public Electron app): shows the hosted web app, so the web controls apply [inferred from AGENTS.md section 5: 'The public Desktop shows the hosted web app'] (doc: AGENTS.md). The internal Tauri desktop only writes a local file and has no cloud publisher (apps/desktop/src/features/artifacts/publishAdapter.ts:1-17).

Mobile (AGI Mobile) full-screen artifact: a header icon (accessible name 'Publish artifact to a public link', or 'Republish artifact link' once published), then under the content a link row with copy, 'Share publication link' and open-in-browser icons, and a 'Who can open this' radio group plus 'Unpublish artifact' (apps/mobile/src/features/chat/components/ArtifactFullScreen.tsx:1319-1331, :1578-1625, :1633; apps/mobile/src/features/chat/components/PublishedArtifactControls.tsx:153-216).

steps.what_happens: Person presses Publish. The viewer checks the artifact kind and sends artifact id, title, kind, language, content and conversation id.
The shared publish function refuses unless the artifact was created in managed (Cloud) mode and the requested mode matches.
The publish service checks CSRF and the 'share-create' rate limit (5 per minute), applies the external-sharing policy gate, moderation and outbound content inspection.
The service checks the per-user publication cap, upserts the published row (token kept on republish) and appends a version if content changed.
The receipt (link, visibility, workspace member count) is validated on the client, shown, and the link is copied.
Audience change sends PATCH {visibility}; the server checks workspace plan and permission, connector-use and sharing policy, then moves the grant row in one transaction.
A visitor opens /shared-artifact/<token>; the server reads public rows first, then workspace and invited rows for a signed-in user, else shows the unavailable or invite-only page.
Unpublish sends DELETE; the row is deleted and the link no longer resolves.
CLI path: connects only for managed privacy, re-derives the artifact content from the conversation message, and posts the same publish request.
