execution_and_data_flow.models_and_providers: No model runs for sharing. The content published is whatever a model produced earlier. Moderation and outbound-content inspection are server checks, not a chosen provider. Provider choice is not read by this feature.

access_and_usage.account: Signed-in account required. Web routes use a user-scoped database; mobile asserts a signed-in Cloud account before sending (apps/mobile/src/features/chat/services/artifactPublishing.ts:60-70); the CLI needs a stored sign-in (apps/cli/src/cloud/client.rs:375-379). Viewing a public link needs no account (page.tsx:29-34).
access_and_usage.permissions: Only the owner can publish, change audience or unpublish (queries filter by user id: published-artifact-service.ts:573). Workspace audience also needs the 'content.share' permission in that workspace (org-shared-artifact-service.ts:214-219). External sharing is subject to workspace policy (publish route via buildExternalSharingGateResponse, [token]/route.ts:180). A publication that reads connected apps cannot be made public ([token]/route.ts:176-178).
access_and_usage.subscription: No plan check on a public or invited publish was found in the publish route or service (read apps/web/app/api/artifacts/publish/route.ts and published-artifact-service.ts). Workspace audience needs the 'team_admin' capability on the workspace plan: team, team_premium, enterprise (apps/web/lib/services/org-entitlements.ts:22,133-138; packages/contracts/types/src/billing-catalog.ts:362).
access_and_usage.limits_and_metering: Content up to 1,000,000 characters and title up to 300 (published-artifact-service.ts:50-51; publish/route.ts:36-42). Per-user cap of 200 publications (artifact-index.ts:132; published-artifact-service.ts:59,413-415), then a conflict error. Rate limit 'share-create' 5 per minute (rate-limit.ts:424-428). Up to 100 invited viewers per page (published-site-viewer-service.ts:13). No usage credits are charged for publishing; none found.
access_and_usage.flags: No feature flag found for publishing itself. Mobile and web both gate on the artifact kind. The 'connectors released' flag affects only connected-app artifacts.
access_and_usage.model_compatibility: Not model dependent; any artifact kind in the allowed list can be published regardless of the model that wrote it.
access_and_usage.provider_restrictions: None by provider. The restriction is by mode: only artifacts created in managed Cloud mode can be published (artifacts.ts:256-276).
access_and_usage.local_mode: In Local (on-device) mode nothing is uploaded. Web returns the message 'This artifact was created in <mode> mode. Publishing uploads it to AGI managed cloud, so it is unavailable in this privacy mode. Download the artifact instead.' (artifacts.ts:261-266). Mobile Local mode shows 'Switch to AGI Cloud to publish' (ArtifactFullScreen.tsx:299-301; artifactPublishing.ts:357-358). CLI refuses non-managed sessions (client.rs:361-373). Signing in is required for Cloud publish; Local use itself needs no payment. [inferred for payment: no plan check found]

features.summary: Lets a person copy an artifact, rename it, save it to the Library, add a copy to a project's knowledge, start Work from it, and jump back to the chat that made it. Web has most of it. Mobile has Save to Library and Library Open chat. CLI and Chrome only open the source chat. VS Code has none.

purpose.what_it_does: Keeps and reuses an artifact beyond the one chat: an independent copy, a new name, a file in the Library, a file in a project's knowledge, a Work request seeded from it, and a link back to the conversation that produced it.
purpose.why_it_exists: The brief requires duplicate, rename, save to Library, attach to a project, continue in another chat and jump to the source chat (S26.24-S26.28, S26.38) so artifacts are not trapped in one conversation.
purpose.who_uses_it: Anyone who iterates on an artifact, files finished work, or returns to the chat that produced a gallery or Library item.
problems_solved: Editing a variant without damaging the original.
Finding a made file again outside the chat.
Giving a project the artifact as reference material.
Getting from a gallery or Library tile back to its conversation.
use_cases: Duplicate a landing page, then change the copy.
Rename 'Untitled' to a meaningful name.
Save a report to the Library and later add it to a new chat.
Open the originating chat from the gallery tile.

steps.what_happens: Duplicate: the store creates a new artifact object in the browser store and selects it.
The browser store persists to local storage and later pushes artifacts to the account's chat-sync endpoint for managed conversations; conversations that answered on the device are skipped.
Rename updates title in store and current version; the rename is marked so it pushes.
Save to Library posts the file name and content with CSRF; the server rate-limits, stores the bytes as a saved_artifact and returns the new file id.
Save to project uploads the file through the project knowledge client, which registers it for extraction.
Library 'Add to chat' downloads the item, stages it as an attachment and routes to a new chat.
'Open chat' navigates to /chat/<conversationId> (web), opens the browser to that URL (CLI, Chrome) or pushes the chat route (mobile).

access_and_usage.account: Duplicate and rename work on the stored panel artifact without a server call. Library, project and sync need a signed-in account. Mobile Library save needs a Cloud account.

access_and_usage.subscription: No plan check found in the Library save route or project save wiring I read. File storage and download meters are applied to the Library list (library/route.ts:178-180); how a full quota is enforced on save is unknown.
access_and_usage.limits_and_metering: Library save content up to 1,000,000 characters (library/route.ts:214); over it the error 'This artifact is too large to save to your Library.' Rate limit key 'chat-conversation'. Title length capped by ARTIFACT_TITLE_MAX_CHARS (ArtifactTitleField.tsx:78).
access_and_usage.flags: Cloud-document saves (Google Docs, Drive, OneDrive) are hidden while connectors are unreleased (ArtifactPreview.tsx:2448,2459). No flag on duplicate, rename, Library or project items.
access_and_usage.local_mode: Duplicate and rename work on the device. Mobile Library save is refused for non-Cloud artifacts (libraryService.ts:10-12). Chrome open-on-web hides for temporary chats and unsynced chats. Whether web Library save blocks Local-origin artifacts is not handled in the code I read (the save menu item has no privacy check, ArtifactPreview.tsx:2537-2548). features.summary: Lets a person pick part of an artifact and ask the assistant to change only that part, leave comments on passages, slides or elements, and send open comments to the assistant together. purpose.what_it_does: Turns a selection or a comment into a precise edit request sent as a chat message, so the assistant revises just that part. Comments are saved on the artifact, can be resolved, and open ones can be sent in one message.
purpose.why_it_exists: The brief requires selection edits, inline comments and collected requests (S26.17-S26.19). The code comment in ArtifactEditRequestLayer says it follows ChatGPT's 'Request edits' layer (apps/web/features/chat/components/artifacts/ArtifactEditRequestLayer.tsx:28-34).
purpose.who_uses_it: People iterating on documents, decks and pages who want targeted changes without retyping context.
problems_solved: Vague whole-artifact prompts that rewrite too much.
Losing notes about what to fix.
Sending many fixes one by one.
use_cases: Select a paragraph, choose Improve then Make shorter.
In a page preview, press Request edits, click a heading, type a change.
Comment on slide 3, resolve later.
Press 'Ask AI to apply all 4 open comments'.

steps.what_happens: Person selects text. The toolbar reads the browser selection and the surrounding rendered text.
The request text is built from title, selected text, nearby context, optional slide scope and the current content if the artifact was hand-edited.
The text is sent as a normal user message in the active chat.
The chat turn pipeline runs with the conversation's current model and mode; the reply creates a new artifact version.
steps.evidence: Turn goes through handleSend (WebChatPage.tsx:6098); which provider runs depends on the chat mode, not read here.

steps.what_happens: Comment create sends body and anchor to the comments route; the server checks CSRF and rate limit and stores the row under the user's id.
'Ask AI to apply all' builds one message from open threads and sends it the same way.
Mobile only fills the composer and closes the viewer; the person sends.

data.what: Comment rows (body up to 4000 characters, anchor with quoted text and nearby text, author user or assistant, resolved time)
data.synced: Server only; shown on any device where the same account opens the artifact
data.retained_or_deleted: Deleted with the comment or its parent thread (cascade on parent id); no foreign key to the artifact, so deletion with the artifact is not enforced by the table (0369_artifact_comments.sql:8-12). Retention beyond that unknown.

data.where_stored: Becomes a chat message in the conversation

execution_and_data_flow.models_and_providers: The request is an ordinary chat turn, so the model and provider are whatever the conversation uses (Cloud, own key or Local). The artifact edit feature itself does not choose or call a model. Comments do not call a model.

access_and_usage.account: Selection edits need only the chat. Comments need a signed-in account.
access_and_usage.permissions: Comments are scoped to the author's user id by row-level security; no sharing with others.
access_and_usage.subscription: No entitlement check found on comments routes. Edit requests are chat turns, so the usual plan allowance and limits for the chat turn apply [inferred]; not read here.
access_and_usage.limits_and_metering: Comment body 1 to 4000 characters; 500 comments per artifact; rate limit key 'chat-conversation' on comment routes; selection text capped at 4000 characters with 400 characters of context each side. The edit request consumes whatever the chat turn costs.
access_and_usage.model_compatibility: The request text asks for a reply in the artifact's format; it works with any model that answers in that format [inferred].
access_and_usage.local_mode: Selection and element edit requests are chat messages, so in Local mode they run on the device model. Comments are sent to our servers even for Local conversations: the comment gate checks only that the artifact id is a UUID (artifact-comments.ts:70-72; ArtifactPreview.tsx:2213) and I found no privacy-mode check. This is a possible trust-boundary gap and is unverified.

aliases: Connected-data status, refresh, and artifact usage
features.summary: A web-only 'live artifact' lets an HTML or React artifact read the owner's connected apps, shows 'Updated <time>' or 'Connect <app> to refresh', and has a 'Refresh data' button. It is switched off while connectors are 'coming soon'. No screen shows per-artifact usage; server limits exist but are not shown.

purpose.what_it_does: Shows which connected apps an artifact reads and whether they are ready, re-loads the artifact's data on demand without asking the assistant to rebuild it, and (server side only) counts and caps the AI calls an artifact makes.
purpose.why_it_exists: The brief requires per-artifact connected-data status, refresh and usage (S26.33, S26.34, S26.37). A live dashboard that reads Gmail or a tracker needs a way to refresh and to know if a connection broke, and an app that loops on AI must not drain the person's allowance (migration header, apps/web/db/neon/0391_artifact_runtime_usage_cap.sql:1-30).
purpose.who_uses_it: Owners of HTML or React artifacts on a plan with connected apps; viewers of published apps who are asked to allow AI and app access.
problems_solved: Stale dashboards without regenerating them.
Not knowing a connector is disconnected.
Runaway AI use by one artifact.
use_cases: A weekly numbers dashboard that refreshes from connected apps when opened.
Switching an artifact to refresh only when asked.
Stopping live updates for an artifact.
A visitor to a published app sees which apps it wants and chooses which tools to allow.

where_to_find_it: Web viewer: when an artifact is live, a strip under the toolbar shows a 'Live' pill (link to the Live artifacts page), text 'Updated <relative time>' or 'Not refreshed yet' or 'Connect <apps> to refresh', a 'Refresh data' button and a 'Live options' menu with 'Refresh when opened' or 'Refresh only when I ask' and 'Stop live updates' (apps/web/app/chat/live-artifacts/LiveArtifactControls.tsx:27-125; ArtifactPreview.tsx:3105).

Web page 'Live artifacts' (sidebar item 'Live artifacts', route /chat/live-artifacts) lists live artifacts with 'Artifacts that refresh with data from your connected apps.' and 'New live artifact' (apps/web/shared/components/layout/app-nav-items.ts:162-169; apps/web/app/chat/live-artifacts/LiveArtifactsView.tsx:205-264).

Consent card 'AI permission' (on a published app and on a live artifact): per connected app, checkboxes for each tool, notes 'Not connected. Connect it in Settings, Connectors, to use this part of the app.', 'Blocked in your settings.', buttons 'Allow' and "Don't allow" (apps/web/app/shared-artifact/[token]/ArtifactConnectorConsent.tsx).

Usage: no per-artifact usage screen on any app [searched apps/web, apps/mobile, apps/cli for artifact_subject and artifact usage display; only the server migration, a policy function and tests matched].
Desktop (Electron) follows web [inferred]. Matrix doc says desktop, mobile, CLI, VS Code and Chrome do not render published apps (doc: docs/product/surface-feature-matrix.md:402-410).
prerequisites: Connected apps must be released: the release state constant is 'coming_soon' today (packages/contracts/types/src/connector-release.ts:14), so these flows are refused.
The AI switch AGI_ARTIFACT_AI_ENABLED must be on (apps/web/lib/server/artifact-ai-switch.ts:5-9).
A plan with the 'artifact_connectors' capability: pro, max, max_15x, team, team_premium, enterprise (packages/contracts/types/src/billing-catalog.ts:341,361).
An HTML or React artifact saved in one of the owner's Cloud chats (apps/web/app/api/artifacts/live/[artifactId]/route.ts:41-42,109-110).
screens_and_controls: Live strip, Refresh data, Live options menu, confirm 'Stop live updates?'.
Live artifacts page cards with Open, refresh policy and Stop live updates.
AI permission consent card.
journey: Open a live artifact in the panel; the strip shows when it was last refreshed.
If a needed app is not connected, the strip says 'Connect <app> to refresh'.
Press 'Refresh data'; the preview frame reloads and the page asks for data again (apps/web/app/chat/live-artifacts/useLiveArtifactRuntime.ts:208-212; ArtifactPreview.tsx:3264).
When the page first asks to use AI or apps, the consent card appears; choose Allow or Don't allow.
Optional: choose 'Refresh only when I ask' so loading the artifact does not pull data.
Stop live updates with confirmation; the artifact stays in its chat.
feedback_and_outputs: Strip text, toasts 'The refresh setting could not be saved.' and 'Live updates could not be stopped.', messages 'This artifact refreshes only when you ask. Select Refresh data to load current data.' (useLiveArtifactRuntime.ts:22-23), refusal 'Connectors are coming soon.'.
No usage figures are shown.

Connector tool allow list per artifact.
Settings, Connectors (to connect apps).

working: Live binding store and routes: read, bind (PUT), change refresh policy (PATCH), remove (DELETE) with audit events (apps/web/app/api/artifacts/live/[artifactId]/route.ts:86-166; apps/web/db/neon/0380_live_artifacts.sql:27).
Viewer strip and hook with readiness 'ready' or 'needs_connection' and missing connectors (live-artifact-contract.ts:20-21,50-60; LiveArtifactControls.tsx:46-86).
Consent card shows per app 'connected or not' and per tool availability (ArtifactConnectorConsent.tsx).

Server completion and connector describe routes with plan, workspace, moderation, content safety, secret handling and managed-usage reservation (apps/web/app/api/artifacts/runtime/artifact-completion.ts:115-200,270-310; apps/web/app/api/artifacts/runtime/[token]/connectors/route.ts:43-90).
incomplete: The brief calls S26.33 and S26.34 missing; the code exists but is disabled while connectors are 'coming soon'.
Status shows only 'ready' or 'needs connection' per binding; there is no per-source unhealthy state beyond 'connected'.
Per-artifact usage is capped and attributed on the server, but nothing reads it back for display (artifact_subject appears only in the migration, the reservation call and tests).
disconnected_or_disabled: connectorsReleased() is false, so the connectors and completion routes answer 403 'connectors_coming_soon' (apps/web/lib/services/artifact-connector-gate.ts:20-25; artifact-completion.ts:121-123).
AI inside artifacts is off unless AGI_ARTIFACT_AI_ENABLED is set (artifact-ai-switch.ts:5-9; artifact-completion.ts:116-118).
Cloud-document saves hidden until release (ArtifactPreview.tsx:2448,2459; ArtifactPreview.connectorsUnreleased.test.tsx).
Migration 0391 header says 'NOT YET APPLIED : draft only' while managed-usage-request-service.ts:804 calls the function it creates; applied status is unknown.
The live binding PUT does not itself check connectorsReleased (route.ts:92-120 shows only origin and runnable checks).
not_available: Mobile, CLI, VS Code, Chrome: no live artifacts, refresh or per-artifact usage (doc: docs/product/surface-feature-matrix.md:402-410; no code found).
Public share of an artifact that reads connected apps is refused (artifact-connectors route.ts:56-60).

established.statement: S26.33: an artifact that reads connected data shows which sources it uses and whether they are connected or healthy.

acceptance_criteria: With connectors released and a Pro-or-higher plan, a live artifact shows 'Updated <time>' after Refresh data.

Choosing 'Refresh only when I ask' stops data loading on open until Refresh data is pressed.
While connectors are 'coming soon', the connectors route answers 403 with code connectors_coming_soon.
Without the AI switch, completion answers 403 with the artifact-AI-off code.
A public link cannot be set on a publication that uses connectors (409 conflict message).
Per-artifact usage, when built, equals the sum of that artifact's ledger rows in the account usage numbers.
inferred: Per-artifact usage should read the artifact_subject column. [inferred]
Refresh is a reload of the preview frame, not a model call. [inferred from useLiveArtifactRuntime.ts:208-212 and ArtifactPreview.tsx:3264]
proposed: [proposed] Show per-app status icons (connected, expired, blocked) in the strip.
[proposed] Add an 'Usage' line in the strip using the existing reservation records.

steps.what_happens: Viewer loads the live binding for the artifact and shows readiness.
When the page asks for AI or apps, the host lists the needed connectors; the server describes them and their connected state, after the release and plan gates.
The person allows or declines; the answer and chosen tools are saved on the binding.
Refresh data bumps a key so the preview frame reloads and the page requests data again.

Each AI request the page makes goes to the completion route, which applies gates, moderation, content-safety and secret handling, takes a turn slot, reserves managed usage with a per-artifact ceiling and returns text.
The model call runs on the managed route chosen by the server for artifact prompts.

execution_and_data_flow.models_and_providers: The page's AI calls use a managed route resolved on the server (ArtifactRuntimeRouteUnavailableError, artifact-completion.ts:303-305); the provider is not chosen by the person. access_and_usage.permissions: Only the owner can bind a live artifact (readOwnedRunnableArtifact). Consent chooses allowed tools; tools blocked or needing approval in settings are shown unavailable. Workspace feature gate 'artifact_connectors' via buildWorkspaceFeatureGateResponse (artifact-connector-gate.ts:44).
access_and_usage.subscription: Plan capability 'artifact_connectors' for pro, max, max_15x, team, team_premium and enterprise (billing-catalog.ts:341,361); error 'Connected apps in published apps are available on <plans>.' (artifact-connector-gate.ts:34-41). Managed compute access is also evaluated (artifact-completion.ts:150-160).
access_and_usage.limits_and_metering: Per-artifact AI call ceiling and a share of the five-hour budget from plan catalogs (managed-usage-policy.ts:194-205), enforced by the reservation function in migration 0391 (applied status unknown). Rate limits 'model-catalog' (connectors) and 'llm-completion' (complete) (runtime routes). Up to ten connected apps per request (connectors route message). Calls count toward the plan's usage (consent text).

access_and_usage.model_compatibility: The artifact page chooses no model; the server picks the route. Not model-selectable by the person.

features.summary: Every document shows a name on its chat card and at the top of its viewer. A document with no name gets a fallback: 'Untitled' on web, a kind-based name on mobile, 'Untitled artifact' in the CLI list. On web only, the person can click the name to rename it.

purpose.what_it_does: Shows the document's name on its card in the chat and in the viewer header, supplies a fallback when there is no name, and on web lets the person rename a stored document. Names are trimmed, runs of whitespace are collapsed to one space, and the result is cut to 200 characters (packages/ui/unified-chat/src/lib/answer-document.ts:2,7).
purpose.why_it_exists: The person must know which document they are looking at, especially when a chat holds several. Rename lets them label a document without making a new version.
purpose.who_uses_it: Anyone who receives or edits a generated document in AGI Workforce on web, mobile, the CLI artifact list and the VS Code artifact tree.
problems_solved: Several documents in one chat look the same without a name.
A document with no title would show an empty header.
A generated name can be wrong or too long; rename fixes it on web.
use_cases: Read the title on the card in a chat to pick the right document.
Open the document on web and rename it from the header.
List cloud artifacts in the CLI and see 'Untitled artifact' for unnamed ones.
See a kind-based name such as a document type on a mobile card when the stored title is generic.

Mobile: card title (InlineArtifactCard.tsx:223,287) and full-screen header text in the form '<title> · <type label>' (ArtifactFullScreen.tsx:1275).
CLI: the artifact list prints display_title (apps/cli/src/lib.rs:3933,3941,4012).
VS Code: the artifacts tree label (artifactsTree.ts:37).

Chrome: the side-panel artifact card title falls back to a localized 'untitled' string (artifactPanel.ts:345). Desktop: no artifact code found under apps/desktop; the public Desktop shows the hosted web app (AGENTS.md section 5).

execution_and_data_flow.models_and_providers: No model is involved in showing or renaming a title. The initial title comes from the model's output or from the first heading (documentTitleFromAnswer, answer-document.ts:14-27); which model made it is not part of this feature.

features.summary: Version history lets a person see every saved version of a document or other artifact with its time and a short note on what changed, open an older one, compare it with the one before, and restore it. Restoring adds the old text as the newest version, so nothing is deleted. Built on web, mobile and the Tauri desktop panel; not in CLI or VS Code.

purpose.what_it_does: Keeps each saved state of an artifact (document, deck, code, page) as a numbered version. The person can step through versions, open a list showing time and change size, view a line or word comparison with the previous version, and restore an older version. Restore never removes later versions; it appends the old content as the new latest (packages/platform/artifacts/src/artifact-store.ts:40-44).
purpose.why_it_exists: The assistant and the person both rewrite the same document. Without history one bad rewrite would lose good text. The product requirements say an artifact has version history (doc: docs/product/requirements.md:748) and an artifact lifecycle with preview, edit, compare, restore (doc: docs/product/experience-contract.md:43-45).
purpose.who_uses_it: Anyone who edits an artifact by hand or asks the assistant to change it: writers, analysts, students, developers working with generated pages or code.
problems_solved: Undoing an assistant rewrite that made the document worse
Finding what changed between two versions
Recovering older wording without keeping copies by hand
Knowing when a version was made
use_cases: After asking the assistant to shorten a report, the person opens Version history, sees 'N lines added, M removed', and restores version 2.
On the phone, the person steps back one version with the Previous version button to read the earlier draft.
The person opens 'Show changes' to see exactly which words the assistant replaced.
On the Tauri desktop panel, the person picks an older version and chooses 'Restore version N'.

where_to_find_it: Web (also the Electron desktop window, which shows the hosted web app: ARCHITECTURE.md:53): in the artifact side panel header, a chip with a previous arrow, a label 'v3/5' and a next arrow. The label is visible text 'v{position}/{total}'; the longer words 'Version 3 of 5. Show version history' are only the accessible name (apps/web/features/chat/components/artifacts/ArtifactPreview.tsx:2658-2686). Clicking the label opens the 'Version history' list (ArtifactPreview.tsx:2980-2987). The More menu adds 'Show changes' / 'Hide changes', 'Review changes' (latest version only, when editable) and 'Restore version N' (when an older version is shown) (ArtifactPreview.tsx:2325-2350).

Mobile: full-screen artifact view. A chip with 'Previous version', a button labelled 'Version N of M' (visible 'vN/M') and 'Next version' shows only when there is more than one version (apps/mobile/src/features/chat/components/ArtifactFullScreen.tsx:1434-1490). Beside it are 'Show changes' (:1499) and 'Restore' (:1517, accessible name 'Restore version N'). The label button opens the sheet titled 'Version history' (apps/mobile/src/features/chat/components/ArtifactVersionHistorySheet.tsx).

Tauri desktop (internal build, not the public Desktop): the shared artifact panel has its own history list with the same wording and a confirm step (packages/ui/unified-chat/src/components/ArtifactPanel.tsx:447-470; packages/ui/unified-chat/src/components/artifact-components/ArtifactVersionHistory.tsx:39). In local privacy mode a host action 'Restore version N' is added when a past version is shown (apps/desktop/src/features/artifacts/useDesktopArtifactActions.ts:56-73).
CLI and VS Code: none found. Chrome: not searched, unknown.
prerequisites: An artifact with at least one saved version. Web shows the chip when versionCount > 0 or the lineage has more than one artifact (ArtifactPreview.tsx:965); mobile only when there is more than one version (ArtifactFullScreen.tsx:1434).
Web: the artifact must be a stored artifact in the side panel variant for undo/redo steps (ArtifactPreview.tsx:1055).
No separate plan or sign-in check found for viewing history on any app (see access_and_usage).
screens_and_controls: Web chip: 'Previous version', version label button (disabled when no versions), 'Next version' (ArtifactPreview.tsx:2650-2700).

Web history list: heading 'N versions' (plural-aware), close button 'Close version history', newest-first rows 'Version N' with '· Latest' on the newest, a time line then ' · ' then change text, and a 'Restore' button on every row except the latest (apps/web/features/chat/components/artifacts/ArtifactVersionHistory.tsx:109-183). Escape closes the list (:111-118).

Change text per row: 'Created, N lines' for the first; 'Same as version K' if identical to an earlier non-adjacent version; 'Line order changed'; otherwise 'N lines added, M removed' (ArtifactVersionHistory.tsx:38-67). Time is formatted with the browser locale, medium date and short time (:69-74).

Restore confirmation dialog on web: title 'Restore version N?', text 'This replaces what you are looking at with version N, added as the new latest so the versions in between survive.' plus 'Your unsaved edits are discarded.' when an unsaved source edit exists; button 'Restore' (ArtifactPreview.tsx:1008-1030).

Web 'Show changes' view: word-level for text documents and email, line-level for other types (ArtifactPreview.tsx:3210-3217). 'Review changes': Keep all / Undo all and per-change 'Undo change N' / 'Keep change N', then saves a new version (apps/web/features/chat/components/artifacts/review/ArtifactChangesReview.tsx:25-130; ArtifactPreview.tsx:3128-3141).

Undo and redo while viewing the latest version step through saved versions, named 'Undo last change' and 'Redo change' (ArtifactPreview.tsx:530-531, 1060-1082). Mobile has the same pair (ArtifactFullScreen.tsx:145-146, 855-878).
journey: 1. Open the artifact in the side panel (web) or full screen (mobile).
2. Click or tap the version chip label to open the history list, or use the Previous version / Next version arrows to step.
3. Read each row's time and change note; click or tap a row to view that version (the latest row returns to the live version).
4. Optionally open 'Show changes' to see what changed against the version before it.
5. Choose Restore. On web a dialog asks first; on mobile the restore happens at once.
6. The old text appears as the newest version, the view returns to the latest, and all older versions remain in the list.
feedback_and_outputs: Web: a new top row 'Version N · Latest' appears after restore; unsaved-edit warning appears in the dialog text.
Mobile: success haptic after restore (ArtifactFullScreen.tsx:811-817, 827-836).

Restoring the content that is already current does nothing and returns false (apps/web/features/chat/stores/artifacts-store.ts:976-989).
settings: None found for version history on any app. Mobile keeps at most 20 versions per artifact (apps/mobile/src/features/artifacts/store.ts:45); web keeps at most 200 artifacts (artifacts-store.ts:30) and mobile 200 (store.ts:36); these are constants, not user settings.

working: Web: version chip, history list with times and change notes, open, restore with confirmation, word/line 'Show changes', per-change 'Review changes', undo/redo by version steps (ArtifactPreview.tsx:1008-1082, 2325-2350, 2658-2686, 2980-2987; ArtifactVersionHistory.tsx).

Web store: same id with different content appends a version; identical content does not (packages/platform/artifacts/src/artifact-store.ts:15-17, 69-115); restore re-publishes the old content as newest (artifacts-store.ts:976-989).

Web persists artifacts and versions in browser storage key 'agi-artifacts-store' (artifacts-store.ts:589-591) and pushes edited artifacts to the account for managed-cloud chats (artifacts-store.ts:1053-1087).

Mobile: version stepper, history sheet, restore, show changes, undo/redo (ArtifactFullScreen.tsx:855-878, 1434-1530; ArtifactVersionHistorySheet.tsx); store appends a version on restore and returns false if the chosen version is already the latest (store.ts:358-380).

Tauri desktop: versions come from stored artifacts via commands artifact_get_versions and artifact_rollback; rollback creates a new version 'Rolled back to version N' (apps/desktop/src-tauri/src/core/artifacts/types.rs:370-385; apps/desktop/src/runtime/TauriRuntime.ts:1569-1600).
incomplete: Mobile restore has no confirmation step and the sheet restore also acts at once (ArtifactFullScreen.tsx:811-837), while web asks first (ArtifactPreview.tsx:1008-1030).
Mobile drops the oldest version once more than 20 exist (store.ts:175-178). The wording 'restoring does not delete newer versions' still holds; older ones fall off the start.

Web has no per-artifact version cap that I found; only artifact count (200) and a browser-storage fallback that shrinks the saved payload when storage is full (artifacts-store.ts:564-583). How versions are trimmed in that fallback: unknown.
disconnected_or_disabled: Tauri host action 'Restore version N' is returned only when the privacy mode is 'local' (useDesktopArtifactActions.ts:42, 53-56); the cloud-mode restore path goes through ChatInterface (packages/ui/unified-chat/src/components/ChatInterface.tsx:703-790). Whether both are reachable in the Tauri app: unknown.
not_available: CLI: no command lists or restores versions (apps/cli/src/lib.rs:1359-1415 lists only list, show, open, publish, published, audience).
VS Code: the artifacts view lists, opens read-only, copies and saves; no history (apps/extension-vscode/package.json:689-719).
Chrome extension: no version history code searched for; status unknown.
Electron desktop has no separate implementation; it shows the hosted web app (ARCHITECTURE.md:53).

established.statement: The user can browse a document's past revisions with their times and open or restore one (S27.29).
Artifacts must have version history.
Artifacts are versioned objects with preview, edit, compare, restore.
Restore adds the chosen version as the new latest and keeps the versions in between; the dialog warns that unsaved edits are discarded.
History is append-only and restore never deletes later versions.

acceptance_criteria: Every history row shows a time in the viewer's locale and a change note.
Choosing Restore on web opens a confirmation naming the version; cancelling leaves the artifact unchanged.
If there are unsaved edits, the web confirmation says they are discarded.
After restoring version K, the list holds one more version than before and the new latest has version K's text; versions in between are still listed (web).

steps.what_happens: Person opens the chip or sheet; the app reads versions from its local store.
Each row's time and change note is computed in the client by comparing line counts of neighbouring versions.
Person confirms Restore (web) or taps Restore (mobile); the store appends the old content as a new version.
For a managed-cloud chat, the changed artifact is queued and pushed in a sync batch; chats that are temporary or hold on-device turns stay off the account.
On Tauri desktop the version list and rollback run in the local Rust store and database.

data.where_stored: Web: browser storage 'agi-artifacts-store' and, for synced chats, table web_artifacts / web_artifact_versions. Mobile: on-device storage (mmkv, store.ts:3) and pending cloud push. Tauri: local artifact database.
data.synced: Web and mobile push for managed-cloud chats only (0039 header: 'Managed-Cloud ONLY'). Local and own-key artifacts are never pushed (0039 header; artifacts-store.ts:1059-1063).
data.retained_or_deleted: Web: up to 200 artifacts retained, oldest dropped (artifact-store.ts:75-80). Mobile: 20 versions per artifact, 200 artifacts. Deleting a message or conversation removes its artifacts and versions (artifacts-store.ts:1002-1034). Server retention beyond that: unknown.

execution_and_data_flow.models_and_providers: Version history does not call a model or provider. Restore, compare and listing are local logic. A new version usually comes from an assistant reply to an edit request, which is a normal chat turn (see F027-08).

access_and_usage.account: Viewing and restoring local versions needs no account in the code read; the web app's own sign-in requirement is unknown. Cloud sync of artifacts needs a managed-cloud account (0039 header).
access_and_usage.permissions: Cloud rows are user-isolated by row-level security (0039 header). No role or workspace check for version history found.
access_and_usage.subscription: none found in the code for version history on any app.
access_and_usage.limits_and_metering: Web 200 artifacts (artifacts-store.ts:30); mobile 200 artifacts and 20 versions each (store.ts:36, 45). No usage metering found.
access_and_usage.local_mode: Works fully on the device: web keeps versions in browser storage and mobile in on-device storage; local and own-key artifacts are not pushed to the account (artifacts-store.ts:1059-1063; 0039 header).

features.summary: Selection actions let a person select part of a document and ask the assistant to change only that part: rewrite, shorten, lengthen, change tone, adapt for an audience, translate, or describe a change in words. On web the toolbar builds a request and sends it through normal chat; the document changes only when the assistant's new version arrives. Other apps differ.

purpose.what_it_does: Shows a small toolbar over selected text in the web artifact side panel with Edit with AI, Improve and Comment. Improve opens a menu of preset instructions. The chosen instruction, the selected text, 400 characters of text on each side and the document title are packed into a chat message asking the assistant to change only that passage and reply with the full updated document (packages/ui/unified-chat/src/lib/artifact-selection-request.ts:103-165).
purpose.why_it_exists: ChatGPT Canvas and Claude artifacts change files by prompt (doc: docs/decisions/2026-09-27-founder-decisions.md:119-122). Selecting a passage is the quickest way to aim that prompt at one place instead of the whole document.
purpose.who_uses_it: Writers, students and professionals editing assistant-written documents and decks in the web app.
problems_solved: Rewriting a whole document to fix one paragraph
Typing long instructions to point at a passage
Keeping the rest of the text exactly as it was
use_cases: Select a long paragraph, choose Improve then Make shorter.
Select a sentence, choose Improve then Executives to make it lead with the point.
Select a heading and choose Translate to a language from the supported-language list.
Select a phrase, choose Edit with AI, type 'make this sound warmer', press the check button.

where_to_find_it: Web (and the Electron desktop window, which shows the hosted web app): select text inside the artifact content area in the side panel. A toolbar labelled 'Selection actions' appears (apps/web/features/chat/components/artifacts/ArtifactSelectionToolbar.tsx:22, 146).
Chrome: right-click selected page text for 'Translate this'; right-click text in an editable field for 'Rewrite selection' (apps/extension/src/background.ts:7453-7460).

VS Code: lightbulb code actions on a code selection: 'Refactor with', 'Explain with', 'Generate Tests with' the product's code name (apps/extension-vscode/src/providers/codeActionProvider.ts:37-70). These are for code, not documents.
Mobile: no selection actions found. Whole-document 'Ask for changes' fills the composer instead (apps/mobile/src/features/chat/components/ArtifactFullScreen.tsx:147, 328-334, 988-991).
CLI: no document selection. Tauri desktop shared panel: no selection toolbar code found in packages/ui/unified-chat/src/components/ArtifactPanel.tsx.
prerequisites: Web: side-panel variant, a stored artifact, the latest version shown, not in 'Show changes', not in the pick-an-element mode, not PDF/Word/image, content not empty, and the chat must supply the send callback (apps/web/features/chat/components/artifacts/ArtifactPreview.tsx:2165-2175).
Chrome rewrite: a signed-in managed-cloud account (apps/extension/src/background.ts:7510-7513).
The selection must be inside the content area; a collapsed selection shows nothing (ArtifactSelectionToolbar.tsx:43-50).
screens_and_controls: Toolbar buttons: 'Edit with AI', 'Improve' (with menu), 'Comment' (only when comments are available) (ArtifactSelectionToolbar.tsx:22-25, 146-348).

Improve menu groups: 'Edit' (Rewrite, Make shorter, Make longer), 'Change tone' (Professional, Friendly, Confident, Casual, Empathetic), 'Adjust for' (Beginners, Experts, Executives, Students, Children), 'Translate to' (one item per supported language) (packages/ui/unified-chat/src/lib/artifact-selection-request.ts:26-100; apps/web/features/chat/components/artifacts/artifact-selection-request.ts:1-12).

Edit with AI form: input 'Describe the change...', a check button named 'Send the change request', a 'Cancel' button (ArtifactSelectionToolbar.tsx:23-27, 270-300). Instruction is trimmed and cut at 2,000 characters (packages/ui/unified-chat/src/lib/artifact-edit-request.ts:9-13).
Escape dismisses the toolbar (ArtifactSelectionToolbar.tsx:188-197).
journey: 1. Open a document in the web side panel and select a passage.
2. The toolbar appears above (or below if near the top) the selection.
3. Pick an Improve item, or choose Edit with AI and type the change.
4. The request is sent as a chat message; the side panel closes on small screens (ArtifactsPanel.tsx:655-661).
5. The assistant replies with the full updated document, which arrives as a new version of the same artifact.
6. The person reads it, can open Show changes or Review changes, and can restore an older version (F027-07).
feedback_and_outputs: If the message cannot be sent, a toast reads 'The change request was not sent. Try again.' and the toolbar stays (ArtifactPreview.tsx:2198; ArtifactPreview.selectionEdit.test.tsx:127).
Nothing in the document changes until the assistant's reply makes a new version [inferred from: the request only goes to chat, ArtifactPreview.tsx:2185-2199].

settings: The language list comes from the shared supported-language list (packages/ui/i18n/src/languages.ts:9). No selection-specific setting found.

working: Web: toolbar, Improve menu, Edit with AI form, request building with selection, 400-char context each side, optional current text up to 24,000 characters, slide scope for decks, and send through chat (ArtifactSelectionToolbar.tsx; artifact-selection-request.ts:103-165; ArtifactPreview.tsx:2177-2215; apps/web/features/chat/pages/WebChatPage.tsx:6097-6102, 7894).

Chrome 'Translate this' needs a second step (press send) and works on page text, not a document.
The brief's code references for Chrome (side_panel.ts:14710, 14725) point at unrelated attachment-menu code now; the real lines are side_panel.ts:16488-16497 and background.ts:7624.
disconnected_or_disabled: On web the toolbar is hidden whenever the conditions in ArtifactPreview.tsx:2165-2175 fail, for example on an older version or a PDF.

established.statement: Selecting text shows a toolbar of actions (S27.15); the user can rewrite, shorten, expand, change tone, adjust audience and translate a selection (S27.16 to S27.21).
Chrome has no selection toolbar by decision; VS Code has no rewrite by decision.
The request names the artifact, the passage, its surroundings and the change, and the assistant replies with the complete updated document.
If the request cannot be sent the person sees 'The change request was not sent. Try again.'

acceptance_criteria: Selecting text in a latest-version document on web shows Edit with AI, Improve and Comment.
Improve lists Rewrite, Make shorter, Make longer, five tones, five audiences and one entry per supported language.
Choosing an item sends one chat message that contains the selected text, text before and after it, and the title; the document is unchanged until a reply arrives.
The toolbar does not appear on an older version, in 'Show changes', or for PDF, Word and image artifacts.
When the send guard refuses, the toast appears and the toolbar remains.
Pressing Escape dismisses the toolbar.
inferred: Because the request goes through the same send path as a typed message, it follows the active mode and the person's plan limits [inferred from WebChatPage.tsx:6097-6102].

Mobile and Tauri desktop may be intended to stay prompt-only; the decision on phone document editing says editing goes to web or desktop (doc: docs/decisions/2026-09-27-founder-decisions.md:285-289) [inferred].

steps.what_happens: Person selects text and presses Comment; the client captures the quote and 400 characters of context.
The client posts the comment with CSRF token to the comments route.
The server validates the body and anchor, takes a per-user-per-artifact lock, checks the 500 cap, and inserts the row under row-level security.

The assistant reply makes a new version; Review changes compares it with the previous version in the browser.

features.summary: Web lets a person start a document or deck from built-in or saved templates, save a document as a template, and rewrite a document in a saved brand's voice. There is no page layout view, no print view for documents, and no citation or bibliography tool for documents. Other apps have none of these. Citations were decided out of scope.

purpose.what_it_does: Offers starting points (templates), reusable house voice and look (brands) and, as required by the brief, would offer page layout, print and citations. In the code today: 'New from template' creates a document or deck in the open conversation; 'Save as template' stores the current document; a saved brand's voice can be applied by asking the assistant to rewrite; a brand's colours and fonts apply to decks.
purpose.why_it_exists: People write the same kinds of documents again and again and want consistent wording and look. Gemini and Claude documents start from templates and edit in place (doc: docs/decisions/2026-09-27-founder-decisions.md:301-306).
purpose.who_uses_it: Professionals and teams who write meeting notes, briefs, updates, press releases and decks on the web app.
problems_solved: Starting from a blank page
Re-typing the same structure
Keeping one house voice across documents

Write a good brief, choose 'Save as template', and reuse it next week.
Save a brand with voice 'plain and warm' and apply it to a draft.

Mobile builds the file on the phone (print service for PDF, docx builder for Word) and opens the share sheet.

A cloud save (when released) sends the content to our server, which builds a Word file and uploads it to the person's Google Drive, then returns the link.

features.summary: When the assistant writes an email, web and mobile show it as a card with To, Cc, Bcc, Subject and a body that can be edited, copied or opened in the mail app. VS Code and Chrome show a read-only card with Copy email. Nothing sends the email. In the CLI, a generic approval screen shows recipients, subject and arguments before any tool runs.

purpose.what_it_does: Recognises an ```email block in the assistant's answer and renders it as an email form. The person can adjust fields, copy the whole email as text, or open it in their own mail app with a mailto link. Separately, the CLI approval screen shows who receives a connector or tool action and its subject before the person allows it.
purpose.why_it_exists: An email should look and behave like an email, not a code block, and a person must review what would be sent in their name. The brief asks for an email presentation, editable recipient, subject and attachment fields, and a review step before sending.
purpose.who_uses_it: People drafting messages with the assistant on web, mobile, VS Code and Chrome; CLI users approving tool actions that contact people.
problems_solved: Copying an email out of a code block
Missing recipient or subject
Approving a send without seeing the recipients
use_cases: Ask for a reply to a customer; edit the subject; press 'Open in mail app'.
On mobile, tap Edit, add a Cc, tap Copy email.
In the CLI, a tool call with a 'to' argument shows 'Who receives it: to: ...' before 'Allow'.
In VS Code, press Copy email under the drafted message.

where_to_find_it: Web and the Electron window (hosted web app): a card labelled 'Email' inside the chat answer (packages/ui/unified-chat/src/components/markdown/EmailBlock.tsx:56-190, label 'Email'). Web also has an 'email' artifact type shown in the panel (apps/web/features/chat/components/artifacts/ArtifactLabels.tsx:107; ArtifactPreview.tsx:1812).
Mobile: the same card as 'Email' with actions 'Copy email', 'Edit', 'Open in Mail' (apps/mobile/src/features/chat/components/DraftSurfaces.tsx:340-460; used from AssistantSurface.tsx:589-650).

VS Code and Chrome side panel: a read-only section headed 'Email' with a 'Copy email' button (packages/ui/unified-chat/src/components/markdown/assistantFence.ts:520-521; apps/extension-vscode/src/__tests__/answerSurfaces.webview.test.ts:71-99; apps/extension/src/features/side-panel/markdown.ts:406).
CLI: the approval prompt for an MCP tool or a managed connector action (apps/cli/src/agent/tools.rs:138-165; apps/cli/src/models/managed_approvals.rs:128-141).
Tauri desktop: the shared chat markdown component renders the card in the floating chat (apps/desktop/src/features/floating-chat/index.tsx uses the shared markdown); main chat not traced.
prerequisites: The assistant's answer must contain a fenced block with the language 'email', starting with header lines (To:, Cc:, Bcc:, Subject:), a blank line, then the body. A finished block needs a recipient or a subject and a non-empty body, otherwise it shows as ordinary markdown (packages/ui/unified-chat/src/components/markdown/richBlocks.ts:116-150).
The model is told about ```email blocks in the answer-UI tool description (apps/web/lib/services/answer-ui-tool-service.ts:52).
CLI approval: a tool whose arguments contain keys such as to, cc, bcc, recipient, subject, and the person has approvals turned on [approvals gating not traced].
screens_and_controls: Web fields: 'To' and 'Subject' always; 'Cc' and 'Bcc' when present or when 'Edit email' is toggled (EmailBlock.tsx:96-104). While streaming, fields are read-only and the action buttons are hidden (EmailBlock.tsx:206, 118).

Web actions: 'Edit email' (visible text 'Edit', toggles empty fields), 'Copy email' (icon), 'Open in mail app' (EmailBlock.tsx:120-170). When changed: 'Save changes' (or 'Edits are temporary in this view.' when nothing can persist) and 'Cancel' with a 'Discard unsaved changes?' dialog (EmailBlock.tsx:245-300).
Mail link is limited to 2,000 characters; if the body would exceed it, the body is copied and the mail app opens without it (richBlocks.ts:176-200; EmailBlock.tsx:106-117).
There is no attachment field: the draft has only to, cc, bcc, subject and body (richBlocks.ts:37-45).

CLI approval lines: 'Who receives it: ...', 'Subject: ...', 'Amount: ...', 'What is bought: ...', a blank line, then the full arguments as formatted JSON cut at 4,000 characters with '... truncated' (apps/cli/src/approval_details.rs:5-8, 47-56, 78-100).
journey: 1. Ask the assistant to draft an email.
2. The answer streams; the card fills in read-only.
3. When finished, press Edit to reveal empty fields and change the text.
4. Press Copy email, or Open in mail app to hand it to your own mail program; send it there.
5. Optionally Save changes so the edited text replaces the block in the saved message.
6. CLI: when a tool that contacts someone is about to run, read the approval lines and choose to allow or refuse.
feedback_and_outputs: Copy state 'Email copied' or 'Copy failed, clipboard unavailable'.
Notice 'This message is too long for a mail link, so it was copied. Paste it into the new email.' or the failure variant (EmailBlock.tsx:140-175).
Error 'Changes could not be saved. Your draft is kept here; try again.' (EmailBlock.tsx:150-155).
CLI: the approval screen text only.
settings: None found for the card. CLI approval behaviour depends on the approval mode, not traced.

features.summary: Lets a person open the source text of a generated artifact, change it and save the change as a new version. Web and the Tauri desktop panel have an editor, and mobile has a plain text box. Web adds highlighting and bracket help. Error markers and completion are not built. VS Code and Chrome do not edit in place.

purpose.what_it_does: Opens the text of a stored artifact (HTML, React, code, Markdown) in an editor. A save adds a new version to the artifact's history instead of overwriting the old one, so the person can step back. Unsaved text is kept on the device until saved or discarded.
purpose.why_it_exists: A model's first draft is rarely final. Typing a small fix is faster and cheaper than asking the model again, and it needs no model call. The brief (S28.01) says generated code must open in an editable view where the change is kept.
purpose.who_uses_it: People who generate pages, components or code in chat and want to tweak them by hand: developers, designers and makers.
problems_solved: Fixing a typo or a value without another model turn
Losing typed edits after a reload or app close
Overwriting a good version with a bad edit
use_cases: On web, change a heading in a generated HTML page, press Save, and see the preview update as version N+1.
On a phone, edit a code artifact in full screen, close the app mid-edit, reopen and get the kept edit back.
In the Tauri desktop panel, press Edit artifact, change text, press Save edit.

where_to_find_it: Web (also the public Electron Desktop, which shows the hosted web app, doc: AGENTS.md section 5): artifact side panel, More menu item 'Edit source' (ArtifactPreview.tsx:2317), after the Preview/Source toggle (aria-labels 'Preview' at ArtifactPreview.tsx:2600 and 'Source' at :2617).
Desktop Tauri build (internal): shared artifact panel button 'Edit artifact' (packages/ui/unified-chat/src/components/ArtifactPanel.tsx:779).

Chrome side panel: 'Code' toggle shows source read-only (apps/extension/src/features/side-panel/artifactPanel.ts:865). CLI: prints or writes the source, no editor (apps/cli/src/lib.rs:3917).

features.summary: The brief wants a browsable tree of a generated project's files with create, delete, rename and search. No app has this for generated projects. Artifacts are single text blocks. VS Code shows a flat list of cloud artifacts, and its own file explorer works only after an artifact is saved into the workspace.

purpose.why_it_exists: Real apps have several files. The brief (S28.02 to S28.04, S28.08) asks for a tree and file operations so a generated project can be worked on like a normal code project.
purpose.who_uses_it: Developers who want a model to build whole apps, not single pages.
problems_solved: Browsing a project made of many files
Reorganising generated files
Finding text across files

features.summary: Shows a generated HTML, React, SVG or Mermaid artifact as a live preview inside a locked-down frame, with a Preview and Source switch. Web and Tauri desktop need a separate sandbox web address to run scripts; mobile uses a restricted WebView and Chrome a hosted frame. Side-by-side view, device sizes and theme switch are not built.

purpose.what_it_does: Draws generated pages and components so the person sees the result, not only code. Runs the artifact's scripts in an isolated frame so a bad artifact cannot reach the person's account.
purpose.why_it_exists: A model's page is judged by looking at it. The brief (S28.09 to S28.13) asks for live HTML and React preview, split view, device sizes and light or dark themes.
purpose.who_uses_it: Anyone who asks the assistant to build a page, widget or component.
problems_solved: Seeing a generated page work without copying it out
Running untrusted generated scripts safely
Telling the person when scripts cannot run instead of showing a dead page
use_cases: Ask for a calculator page and use it inside the chat panel.
Ask for a React component and see it mount.
On a phone, open the full-screen artifact and use the Preview/Source switch.

working: Web: with a valid separate https sandbox address, the panel frames that address with sandbox 'allow-scripts allow-same-origin', waits for a ready message, then posts the render payload (SandboxedIframe.tsx:263-300, 399). The renderer shows HTML as a real nested document, React through a pinned in-page compiler (needs a default export or App), SVG through a sanitiser, Mermaid with security level 'strict' (infrastructure/sandbox/index.html:636, 694-810, 812, 841-854).
Web: Mermaid previews render client-side, not in the sandbox frame (ArtifactPreview.tsx:3282-3290 area; renderMermaidPreview).

Mobile: HTML, SVG, Mermaid and React render in a WebView under the shared content policy; JavaScript only for HTML, React and Mermaid, no storage, incognito (SafeArtifactPreview.tsx:99, 280-282; sandboxedArtifactHtml.ts:193-215). The brief says React is missing on mobile; the code has it.

Desktop Tauri: registers an 'artifact://' scheme for a dedicated renderer origin (apps/desktop/src-tauri/src/ui/artifact_sandbox.rs; lib.rs:220) and the shared panel routes previews there (packages/ui/unified-chat/src/lib/artifact-sandbox.ts:209-218).

incomplete: Web without a sandbox address: falls back to a frame with sandbox 'allow-scripts allow-modals' and no same-origin; the page's inline scripts are blocked by the app's own policy, so only layout shows and a banner says so (SandboxedIframe.tsx:109-127, 413-427).

Whether production sets the sandbox address is documented as not set (doc: audit/prior-audits/chat-security-audit-2026-10-26.md:62; audit/registers/known-flaws.md:57) and the brief lists a switch-on task; code cannot tell.

steps.what_happens: The panel builds a render payload from the artifact type and text.
The browser loads the renderer page from the configured sandbox address.
The renderer announces ready; the panel checks the message came from its own frame and origin, then posts the payload.
For React and Mermaid the renderer loads pinned scripts with integrity hashes from public script hosts.
The artifact's own code runs in the frame; network calls are blocked by policy.
If the sandbox frame is not ready in time, the panel switches to a local fallback frame.

features.summary: The brief asks for a panel of an app's packages, user control of network destinations, and secret or config placeholders. None exists as a user feature. Previews run under one fixed policy: no network calls from the artifact, and scripts only from a short list of pinned public hosts. Nothing is configurable by the person.

purpose.what_it_does: Today it only describes the fixed safety envelope around a preview: no network from the artifact and a pinned list of runtime scripts. As a feature the brief wants a package list, a network allow-list the user sees and edits, and placeholders for secrets.
purpose.why_it_exists: Real apps call APIs and need keys. The brief (S28.17, S28.20, S28.21) asks for those controls without exposing secrets in the preview or the chat.
purpose.who_uses_it: Developers building apps with the assistant; reviewers who must know what an app can reach.
problems_solved: Knowing what a generated app installs
Limiting where an app can connect
Giving an app a key without pasting it in code
use_cases: See that an app needs a charting package (not built).
Allow one API host for a preview (not built).
Fill in an API key placeholder privately (not built).

where_to_find_it: No control found on Web, Desktop, Mobile, Chrome, VS Code or CLI. The only related behaviour is invisible: the fixed content policy and, on web, the rule text 'Only React and ReactDOM are available' shown in an error.
prerequisites: Not applicable: no feature to reach.
screens_and_controls: None found.
journey: Not applicable. A person who asks for an app that calls the network sees the call blocked; the preview may show a script error (F028-05).
feedback_and_outputs: React import error text: 'The preview cannot load "<name>". Only React and ReactDOM are available.' (infrastructure/sandbox/index.html:760-775).
settings: None found. The policy is a code constant (packages/contracts/types/src/artifact-csp.ts).

working: One policy applies to every renderer: default-src none, scripts from self, inline, eval and four public script hosts, connect-src none, no child frames beyond the nested one, base-uri none, form-action none (packages/contracts/types/src/artifact-csp.ts:17-45; infrastructure/sandbox/index.html:54-57).
React preview loads only pinned React, ReactDOM and a compiler with integrity hashes and refuses other imports (index.html:208-226, 760-775; apps/web/__tests__/security/sandbox-runtime-sri.test.ts).
Mobile preview uses the same content policy constant (sandboxedArtifactHtml.ts:193-215).
incomplete: Published apps can ask the platform for AI and saved data through a brokered request channel, which is a different path from user-configured network access (apps/web/features/chat/components/artifacts/artifactRuntimeClient.ts; infrastructure/sandbox/index.html runtime shim line 255). That belongs to publishing features in this area, not read in depth here.
disconnected_or_disabled: In an unpublished preview the runtime channel answers 'AI and saved data are available once this app is published and opened by a signed-in viewer.' (SandboxedIframe.tsx:48-49).
not_available: Dependency panel (S28.17), network permission controls (S28.20) and secret or config placeholders (S28.21) on every app. No component, store or route found.

established.statement: A panel shows and manages the dependencies the app installs (S28.17).
The user can see and control which network destinations an app may reach (S28.20).
Apps can declare secrets or config values as placeholders the user fills in without exposing them (S28.21).
Security behaviour fails closed; collect the minimum data; never commit a secret.
Local, own-key and Cloud are separate trust boundaries; nothing silently crosses them.

acceptance_criteria: A generated app's package list is shown in a panel with name and version.
The network list shows blocked by default and each allowed host the person added.
Adding a host asks first and names what the app can then reach.
A secret placeholder shows as masked, is never printed in the chat or in the preview source, and is not sent to the model.
An app that uses an unlisted host is blocked and the person is told which host.
inferred: Any allow-list change must pass through the same policy module for all surfaces, since three surfaces enforce it from one source [inferred from artifact-csp.ts header comment].
Secrets must not enter the model context [inferred from AGENTS.md section 6].
proposed: [proposed] Treat a network allow-list as an explicit consent step with a visible host list.
[proposed] Store placeholder values in the account's secret store, never in artifact text.
